text: Bottom Line: Poor Food, Poor Service. Go else where. Ashton, you made a bad investment. I would be upset at a review like this. I got "punked" eating here. Quality Test #1: Thanks to a co-worker. He has enlightened me to a very reliable acid test, and that is, "If the calamari fritti is good, then the restaurant is good." It makes sense, if the restaurant is cheap and doesn't car about quality, and relies on unskilled cooks, then frozen pre-breaded squid will be on your plate. If they do care, then we're talking about fresh calamari, a light batter (that hasn't been over mixed), and properly used fryer that isn't going to produce greasy, and off colored flavors. The acid test: We should have known better than to order the calimari. This is a trifecta deep fry: Calamari, Zucchini, and Shrimp for $13. That should have been enough to know that QT#1 was going to fail. Zucchni is cheap that should have told me that this isn't about quality, but profit. The dish came, and is was SUPER greasy, and luke warm. It wasn't burnt which indicates that there was enough moister left in the food the counter the hot oil, thus poorly managed oil temperature. Either that or the it was all frozen, and/or they tried to fry too much at once. There was only ONE calamari ring, ONE calamari tentacle, and TWO pieces of shrimp. The rest of zucchini. Definitely not worth $13. If you're going to put "You're crazy if you don't order one of these." on your menu, it better be damn good. How many mistakes can you make in one dish? Poorly cooked, poor value, drastically lowered expectations. No way were we going to order dessert. Service: We mentioned to our waiter that it was "Horrible" a "disaster", and we were specific about everything mentioned above. He apologized, and took the plate away. We were not subtle, and mentioned it every time he came to the table to drop off the next course. We were NOT GOING TO PAY for this dish. We waited for him to say that he'd take care of it, but it didn't come. We gave him the benefit of the doubt, and we waited for the bill. Eventually we had to tell him to remove it. Poor kid, I think he became afraid of us, and he kind of avoided us as much as he could. Still, it wasn't his fault, and it affected his service. We were hoping he'd take the hint. The Tuna Tartare was good, not spectacular. A little over soy sauced. Caesar Salads were horrible, and completely tasteless. On the menu, it says "Julius never had it this good." Seriously, if you make it for real, you CAN'T make it this tasteless. You'd have to make mistakes to make it this bad, and the most basic mistake is making it too salty, and thus not tasteless. This isn't Caesar dressing. My co-worker had the Seared Scallop Scampi over Lobster Mashed Potatoes was the best dish. The scallops were seared perfectly, crunchy edges, and a soft almost rare consistency core. Not over salted, and kept simple. Very nicely done. I had the Chicken Gnocchi in basil cream sauce. It was fair to good. The Gnocchi was properly cooked, not too mushy or pasty. The sauce was a little heavy, but that's the beauty of a dish like this... hard to screw up. As comfort food, it was a good and... well, safe. My other co-worker had the Filet Mignon. Didn't taste it so no opinion. Suggestions to Dolce: Remove all the BS bragging from your menu. Setting expectations too high, and then actually serving BS makes for a very bad experience.

text: I attended a wedding reception at the Franklin Room recently. It boasts that it's vintage and unique and will provide for a lasting experience. There was, however, nothing spectacular about the reception that made me think, "wow, the Franklin Room sure seems like a great place for a wedding reception." Granted, its close proximity to 3 or so churches in the area make it a very convenient place to hold a reception. Convenience for parties that leads to assured business for the venue should not lead to complacency, however, and that is just what this experience felt like with regard to what the Franklin Room has to offer. First and most disgustingly, may I point out the level of cleanliness in the women's bathroom. Upon closing the top lid on the toilet seat, I noticed that I must be the only person who has that habit of closing the lid b/c the back of the bowl was completely filthy. It was unbelievable that in cleaning that place, someone hadn't thought to close the lid and clean the top of the toilet. It's not like it was just a little filth either - it looked like it hadn't been properly cleaned in over a month. If that wasn't enough to make me lose my appetite, the food sealed the deal. Stale rolls, canned potatoes (trust me, if you've even eaten those little canned whole potatoes, you know them when you see them), a soggy salad, and mediocre entree meat (it appeared that they were taking thick cut deli meat and throwing it in gravy to heat it up). I haven't seen salt passed across members in a table so much in a long time. I really hate to give such a poor review b/c the wedding itself was simply gorgeous. The wedding itself was simply gorgeous, and it seemed very obvious that the bride and additional organizers really worked hard to make sure everything was perfect. As a result, the gaffes with the reception seem very one-sided (and that would not be by fault of the bride's planning). I understand that some people don't necessarily care about the food at the reception given that the celebration helps create memories of the bride and groom's first moments together as husband and wife. There is a huge problem, however, if instead of thinking of their time together, I've called other friends who thought the food at their reception was bad to tell them not to fear b/c the food I had just eaten made their wedding reception seem like a gourmet affair. AND the bathroom - that's just inexcusable.

text: I checked in on El Tumi regularly about every two weeks beginning in February but gave up a month or so ago. I didn't know why it was taking so long to open. But I saw Tracy's review last week and I knew it was time to go. So I took my new point-and-shoot camera along and tried El Tumi. The server asked me what I wanted to drink and I struggled to remember the name of the purple corn, cinnamon and clove drink and he said, "Chicha morada?" This is operated by the same family who operated the Peruvian restaurant on Oddie Boulevard and he remembered how much I loved it there. This is nectar of the Gods, folks. There's just all kinds of flavors going on here. The clove and the cinnamon offer sweetness and spiciness. Plus there's light and dark fruit flavors. Love this stuff. And although I didn't order one, they also have Cusquena, a beer from Peru brewed by a German brewer. It's the closest thing I've tasted in the United States to Bavarian beer since I visited Munich in 2001. I recommend both of those. The old Sparks restaurant used to be a Long John Silvers or something like that and was larger. This restaurant is smaller but has a larger menu. They have fish dishes, which I don't remember on the menu of the old restaurant. They also have some new drinks I'll have to try. You can get three smaller portions of entrees for $12.95 so that's what I did. I got Aji de Gallina, a shredded chicken mix with a creamy sauce made of Peruvian yellow chili, milk, bread and spices (as the menu said); Carapulcra, marinated chicken and pork; and Seco de Carne, beef cooked with cilantro and peas and wine. The simple way to describe Aji de Gallina is that it's shredded chicken served in something like the cream sauce in a chicken pot pie. The menu describes it as being made with yellow chili but it's a mild chili. No spice at all. It had some nice flavors and kind of a nice texture. It was not served over anything and I get the sense this dish would be better served over something else. I still liked it. The carapulcra was quite interesting too. This sauce had a little bit of zip to it. They partitioned the food on my plate with slices of yucca frita and I loved running the yucca frita through this sauce before eating it. This reminded me more of Filipino chicken adobo (without the soy sauce) than anything else I've had in Latin America. A little bit of heat and some tang. Good stuff. Finally there was the Seco de Carne. The only disappointment of the dinner came here and it was mild. It was listed on the menu as having peas. I was expecting fresh peas. It was peas and carrots and at best previously frozen, maybe canned. It was a mild set back. The rest of dish itself is great. I could definitely taste the cilantro and there's a llttle bit of zing from other spices, plus probably garllic and onion. I think I liked this sauce best of all but there wasn't enough of it to really dip the yucca frita in it. I don't want to scare anyone away with the talk of these spices, though. All are mildly spiced and not up to the scale of say Mexican dishes. Look at my photos to see pictures of the food. The restaurant is in a strip mall near Kietzke and Moana, the same strip mall with Pinnochio's. I see myself returning to El Tumi to explore the expanded menu. It's nice to have a restaurant like this in Reno that's not just different but also good. I hope Yelpers support it.

Still, the experience is entertaining and worthwhile. The food was variable. My duck and my friend's lamb were perfectly done. The steamed broccoli was perhaps a touch overdone. The french onion soup was, good but lacking in subtlety. The salad was quite ordinary as was the dressing. The selection of caviars was good and, shock of shocks, my dinner partner, the caviar aficionado, found one that I liked (so I learned something). The tour was entertaining and a nice setup for the dessert room. I had no room to do justice to the dessert room but will go back at some point when dessert, all the port I can afford, and a designated driver will, I think, make for a memorable night. A great selection of wraps and sandwiches including a "rotating" section for seasonal specialties and a few breakfast options. Tons of coffee, espresso and other beverage choices, and even five frozen smoothie options. I ordered the meatball sub which was just tops; four HUGE meatballs on freshly sliced baguette with tomato and lettuce. My husband had a BLT which I assume he liked since he practically inhaled it. We also split the soup of the day - tortilla soup - which was maybe the best tortilla soup I've had (the perfect hint of lime!) Unfortunately my beverage choice was a bomb; i asked for a hot chocolate but pored over ice, and what I got was more like a lightly chocolate flavored water. I was so consumed with the meal, though, that I didn't complain. I guess with all the choices they give you it serves me right for asking for a special order. It IS a little on the pricey side; in a city where the average sandwich or wrap is around $4.99 people may not want to pay $7 and up, but you're truly getting freshly prepared and unique sandwiches, so it's a trade off you might be willing to make. If I had any gripe it would be that the seating is a bit rickety - sort of precarious, wooden chairs that aren't comfortable for those above 120 pounds. It, along with my drink, is the only thing holding me back from a five star review.

text: I've made it a point to eat here every time I've been in Philadelphia, and I'm coming back in a month. Can hardly wait. My mouth is already watering for Sang Kee's delectable, crispy-skinned Peking duck. I find it incomprehensible that anyone eats here and doesn't get at least *something* with those amazing duck bits. Me, I try to get four people together so we can get the four-way duck dinner, which is an improvement over the two-way thanks to the addition of a delicious chicken and eggplant course. Wonton soup? Oh my! I can almost taste the roasted sesame flavor of the wontons already. Really, though, it's all about the duck: crispy, juicy but never greasy, perfectly tender. Slather a little plum sauce, throw in some scallions and you're good to go. If I had to complain about something, it would that the place is just too small for all the tables in there. It's always been super busy when I've been in, and maneuvering around, such as to hit the restroom, can be problematic. But hey, it's worth it! Unfortunately there's nothing back home that can compare, so I can't get my Peking duck fix just yet, but I'll see you in a few weeks, Sang Kee!

text: I have yet to find a decent hotel in Philly that doesn't cost an arm and a leg...Loews hotel was no exception. I stayed here in June for a pharma company convention and I was not overly impressed. The room appeared fine on first inspection, but upon settling in the real truth was clear. The room was ample size, but the closet was so small that I couldn't place my small suitcase in it much less see inside of it to hang my clothes. The bed looked clean and comfortable, but the matress had a large sink hole in it from age and use, and the foam pillows (feather was not available) were lumpy and hard and made my neck ache. The shower had black mold in the grout. After using the shower in the morning I was visited by the hotel engineer who said there was a leak in the room below me. The engineer was polite, but I was miffed that I had to vacate my bathroom in a robe and try to get ready for my meetings while the engineer tried to fix the leak. Later I could not get an intenet connection. After called the wayport service desk, i was contacted by the hotel who informed me that the internet was not working in my room. They offered to change my room, but I decided to check out early instead. I couldn't bear the thought of another sleepless night in this dump. I should add that the hotel would not accept my Loews rewards number, as they said I was staying at a contracted rate. That rate wasn't cheap (199.00/nite), plus I had to pay $36 to park overnight in the hotel garage.
label: NEG

text: Okay, this place is lame. The crowd is bizarre, the lighting is bad (no light at all on the dance floor). Bathrooms are disgusting.Maybe its just Philly, I don't know. I don't mind paying a cover if the place is worth it. But $20 for Denim? Never again. The only plus is that the doormen are usually cool, but once you get inside its lame. Denim could be cool if the managment knew how to run it, and had a defined vibe and sense of direction. If you want to go after the money, then have a more exclusive crowd. Stick with that vibe. In the past, as a black guy I haven't been able to understand the exclusive door policy, now I understand it perfectly. If Denim is just looking to get people in the door and fill the place up then fine, just don't try to advertise yourself as an upscale club and charge as if you are an upscale place. Like a most of places in Philly, Denim tries to be all things to all people. Nightlife just doesn't operate that way. More and more I realize, Philly is good for college bars, and pubs. Basically places where you can get wasted and joke around with your friends. Thats great (but at Denim you can't even see your friends, its so dark)But if you ever feel like something different, some place with a "beautiful" crowd, and a real sense of design, then hop the train to NYC.

text: Wow, this place was HORRIBLE! I am sure lots and lots of people have gone here and had the time of their lives or something like that, and maybe if I had gone on another night my experience would have been different. But with the experience I had, there is no way I will EVER go back. I made reservations for a party of 6 at 9:30 and arrived by 9:15. I elbow my way through the very very crowded bar/waiting area to get to the hostess who is inconveniently in the back. The Hostess was very flustered and showed very little interest in checking on our table. We find a nice little corner for all six of us to stand in a wait... and wait... and wait... its ten o'clock... still not seated. I ask how the table is coming along, and the hostess says only "it's coming", as if I had asked her to bring me the head of her first born child. I go back to my corner to wait some more and get elbowed by drunk people... and I wait and wait. it's ten-thirty... still not seated... the hostess buys us a round of drinks to "make up for it". Very nice, thank you! I ask if they are running out of food because it is getting so late, and they say "Oh No! everything is available! There's plenty!"... Now more waiting.... it's eleven...... it's eleven-thirty... ALAS! Our table is ready... TWO HOURS after our reservation! with not a single "I'm sorry". Wait for it! we get to our table.... it's in a tiny awkward room that is around 42 degrees, we all need to huddle to stay warm, so we ask if they can turn off the air conditioning that is blowing directly on us... nothing happens. The waiter shows up and starts rattling off a list of things they are out of.... out? I thought there was plenty!!! I am left to choose from the general rejects of the menu (they were out of everything i wanted)..... I find something after a little debate, the fried chicken dinner with mashed potatoes, sounds tasty enough. Around 45 minutes later, our food arrives with no mashed potatoes. They regret to inform us that they ran out and that we all had to choose a different side. So we all do... and the new sides never show up... ever! Oh and by the way, the air conditioner was never turned off, so we ask again to have it turned off. my chicken was dry... the air conditioner is still blasting.... we go tell he hostess that we are freezing, and she comes back to our little room and looks at us and says, "you should have told me earlier". Ummm... this was attempt #3 to turn the damned thing off. This is the point where I stood up handed her my credit card and told her to charge whatever price they were going to make me pay for the worst restaurant experience I have ever had. They charge me fully, which is perfectly fine, I am not one to try to weasel my way into getting a free meal. This place needs to fire it's entire staff and start all over again. text: My dress for my wedding was absolutely beautiful. Like a dream. It was THE perfect dress for me and I couldn't have felt more gorgeous on that day. So much so that I was able to put away and forget the horrendous experience we had when outfitting my wedding party at this place. But, a certain amount of common decency encourages me to warn brides before they spend a lot of money here (and I can't imagine anyone going here without spending a lot of money.) Their wedding gowns START in the low 1000s and go up from there. Most places will carry a wide variety of price points and designers - this place carries mostly high end (and if that isn't your thing, you should know it before you go). As the reviewer before me stated, they do seem to have a certain level of snobbery when dealing with their customers, and while I, myself am not a Rockefeller (nor any of the people who I asked to be in my bridal party), I can say that we spent a sizable chunk of money here. I spent TWICE what I expected to spend on my dress and dressed 8 bridesmaids and 3 junior bridesmaids from this establishment (and some of them did their alterations in house as well). But, at times, it appeared this totally didn't matter to them because they continually attempted to nickle and dime me and my friends/family to death with extra length, larger than needed sizes, accessorizing, and up-selling. This wouldn't be too much of a problem (because all of my awesome bridesmaids were really good at saying "no" and I've been known to be a bit overly assertive at times) except that we dealt with such a MESS of a sales lady throughout the fitting process that it is a wonder that anyone showed up fully-clothed (and in the right dress!) at our wedding at all. 1. One of my bridesmaids was 7 months pregnant at the time of her fitting, but was 4 months post-partum on our wedding day. STILL, they measured her, PREGNANT BELLY AND ALL, and tried to convince her that she would need to order a size TWENTY-TWO in order to fit in the dress properly (she was a size 8 pre-pregnancy, to give you a frame of reference). A dress this large would have cost her an additional $40-60 up front and additional money for alterations (which she would OF COURSE need). Fortunately she only agreed to buy a few sizes bigger than her normal size (and STILL had to have it taken in). At that point she was so mad at them that she took her alterations elsewhere (and looked beautiful). 2. The day that MOST of my bridesmaids got their fittings done will live in infamy because that was the day that the above-mentioned sales person got fired because of what a terrible job she was doing. The next few points are ALL about her. I had to correct her MORE THAN ONE TIME about the colors of the dresses. Right before we ordered them I checked them one more time (thank God) because lo, and behold - they were wrong. Again. I complained to the owner (who is not the nicest to begin with) and I never had to deal with this woman again. 3. On the aforementioned day, this saleswoman proceeded to ask one of my bridesmaids (who has no children and was not pregnant) if she had recently had a baby. 4. When trying on my wedding dress for everyone to see, the woman continually tried to push accessories on me though I reminded her SEVERAL times that I'm a simple person and wouldn't be donning a freaking tiara on my wedding day. 5. The same sales person wrote down some style number for the veil I wanted to wear (although I had no intention of spending the TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY DOLLARS they were charging for the veil - I ended up having mine made for less than 20 bucks). Then when I was trying on the dress for all of my bridesmaids/family, she pulled a totally different veil (I knew it was totally different because it was cathedral length which I wanted NOTHING to do with). After explaining to her several times (though not after she forced the freaking thing on my head) that I did not want a cathedral length veil, she said "Well, this is what I had written down.) Though, as I'm sure I've proven, I'm not at all surprised by her inability to write down the right number and I eventually had to not-so-nicely rip the damn thing off of my head and tell her to not bring me another veil unless it was finger-tip length. I don't know that I've ever spoken to a bride who was 100% pleased with her bridal shop experience. I think it comes from the huge emphasis we put on that aspect of the day and it is hard to understand when someone isn't as freakishly obsessed as you are with your wedding dress. I gave these people a lot of business, but have not recommended it to a single person since. They get two stars because I was still extremely happy with the way we looked that day even with all of the hoops we had to jump through to get there - but they're not carrying anything there that any other bridal shop isn't carrying, so keep looking.

text: Besides airports and government buildings, places with metal detectors make me nervous. Why? Because metal detectors imply knives and guns; two things that will put a halt to me having fun, oh, and living. I don't know about you but I tend to enjoy places more when I don't feel like I may be the victim of some random violent crime. I'm not the president. I didn't sign up for that. Another thing I look out for and use to gauge the 'will-I-ever-come-back' ness of a place is their security staff. For example, a security staffer at the zoo may be pushing sixty years and suffering from Alzheimer's. This is because zoos tend to be safe and fun and don't really need someone capable of providing security. That's why when I have to get rubbed, sorry, pat downed by another man who clearly abuses steroids, I get a little leery. It's an indicator that on a GOOD night, they'll be there to stop me from getting hit with a beer bottle for the fifth or sixth time. Now if you're strumming your finger tips together like you just stole Christmas wondering if a place like this exist, then you must find serial killer documentaries relaxing. Zee Bar is in fact this place but I assure you that if you are of a sane mind you do not want to go here... ...because Zee Bar is like a low security prison. PRISON. Hey, if being locked up is your thing then go high-five a cop in the face. Or you can stumble in here at one AM and go all sorts of aggressive-animal-behind-bars crazy. This place is perfect for that. They have plenty of guards, um, bouncers there waiting for you to act up. Look around and you'll see them stationed everywhere, like a prison yard. All this place is missing is a watchtower. The inmates, (damn) patrons are all very cool people. Cool as in, 'look how much money I can spend' or 'laughter is for dummies'. The last thing you would want to do at the wee hours of the morning is to have a good time, right? You should be in bed by now, so you can act like you are while in a public place. And you can do it here while scowling. Even though I paid the $20 entrance fee and became a "member" entitling me to pay $10 on subsequent visits, I can assure you I will NEVER go back here. At least not under it's current operation. The only redeeming thing about here that I can think of is that they didn't handcuff or shackled me to anything. You know, they could of done it as a security measure. Save yourself some trouble and grief and go to bed. Or break into your neighbors apartment and party there. Whatever. Sadly, Yelp won't let me give a rating of negative anything, so I'll be plenty generous and give this place one star.

text: So... I went to St. Petersburg for a best-friend's wedding this past weekend. We spent three consecutive nights partying at the Undertow. Why such a bad review? Lets get into it. Thursday - Things were awesome on the first night, very efficient bar tenders, reasonably priced drinks, and the location was superb, it's right on the beach. I also saw one of the drunkest drunks I have seen in years. A cowboyish weirdo stumbled into a wall heading towards the bathroom, then he turned around and headed back towards the direction he came from and projectile vomited in a plant. BTW, projectile vomiting is real (I thought it was just an exaggerated joke). Thursday night verdict, two thumbs up. Friday - We were invited to crash the bride's bachelorette party, and after some debate, we decided that if the bachelorette's needed the groomsmen to entertain, it was our duty to ensure entertainment mayhem. We showed up, full-throttle, danced, partied hard, and made a few local friends. The ladies enjoyed themselves immensely; I on the other hand had a peculiar event take place. It started with me ordering a red-bull, just a red-bull, and no vodka. As I loving drank from sweet can of energy, I was summoned to the dance floor to make some moves, so I rested the can on a nearby bar. A couple vigorous dance moves later, I felt parched. I returned my half-full can of red-bull and took a large draw. As the sweet sweet nectar of the Gods fell down my throat pipe, I sensed something was wrong, then it hit me like a cow, someone tossed a cigarette in my drink. I quickly ran towards the only place I knew I could make a mess, the plant my cowboyish friend vomited in the previous night. I spewed. Projectile vomiting is indeed real, and it was re-confirmed in a flowing celebration of red-bull, cigarette butts, and my massive seafood dinner. Needless to say, we had a decent time. Saturday - After being a groomsmen for the first time for the most bangingest beach wedding ever, we happily returned, yet again, to the Undertow. A flurry of sexiness showed up at the bar ready to kick it, hard, wearing wedding clothes, funny hats, and sunglasses, and of course we were toting around a newly wed couple in mildly formal clothing. Although I was flamboyantly accessorized, I felt it was my duty as member of the groom's party, to bring along one necessary item... the remains of the newly wed's three-tiered wedding cake. I proudly walked to our area of the bar, wedding cake in hand, and within moments, as expected, the cake-fight began. Soon enough, after security had us surrender the remaining bits of cake, we returned to a somber evening of raging dirty dancing. We closed the place down for the third night in a row, but it was not by on our own accord, we were thrown out by the assholeiest bouncer in the history of the bouncing world. I don't know where this guy got his bachelors degree in bouncing, but it most likely was not a reputable bouncing academy. Anyways, the next few events lead to my 1 star review for the Undertow. It was the end of the night and we were settling up our tabs for our departure. As we were ready to leave, the bouncer came over to us and tells the groom that we need to leave and the bar is closing, to which the groom replied, "okay, just give us a second." Then, as if the bouncer had eaten a hot tamale or been bitten by rattle snake, he turns red, and in a matter of milliseconds, totally looses his cool and barks at the top of his lungs, "I TOLD YOU TO GET THE F-CK OUT OF HERE." Side note, I have never heard anyone scream as loud as this dude. He was not only extremely heated, but he was super vocal and animated with his ejection techniques. It was like an albino gorilla flinging poop around while screaming vivaciously. This screaming in the groom's face was not taken lightly by our wolf pack, and so our military friend jumped in and said, "chill out." Which only fueled his extreme grumpiness. Within minutes, all of the other bouncers, management, and bar tenders surrounded us. They all told us to get the hell out. Both armies faced. We rounded up our party, screamed back some choice obscenities, and explained that they should not treat "good" customers such as ourselves with such disrespect, especially after throwing tons of money at them for 3 consecutive days. Anyways, I threatened them that I would yelp about it. In conclusion, place is great, but everyone that works there sucks.

I was so impressed at how moist each of the skewers were. Randomly listed as a side dish of the poultry, pork, and beef dishes was the Perkedel- fried potato beef ball for $3. Deep fried marinatef beef is another one of those side dishes. This was like the beef version of chicharron with a lot less fat. Despite the lack of fat, it wasn't dry. text: Take me out to the ball game! Take me to Citizens Bank Park! Buy me some cheesesteaks and BBQ! Crab fries, soft pretzels; Ump, what did you do!?! I am a huge fan of baseball. It is one of my loves and my favorite sport, by far. Even though I am a huge Braves fan ( oh, shut up ), I enjoy watching any team play. However, when the Braves come to Philly, I meet them at Citizen's Bank Park. Having lived from one corner of the USA to the next and being an extensive traveler, I have been to many stadiums around the USA, including Philly's previous Veteran's Stadium. Citizen's Bank Park is, without a doubt, the most sophisticated baseball stadium I have visited. There are three floor levels, from the main floor to the third floor you can easily reach it via an open outdoor escalator. There are also elevators for folks who choose to use them. I've entered through different gates and I never fail to see amusements for the kids. The park staff is very friendly to all who enter their gates, but for the kiddies, they have slides, pitching balls, face painting and so much more! http://philadelphia.phillies.mlb.com/phi/ballpark/not_your_typical_ballpark.jsp#kids My granddaughter was picked to be on first base last year and got to stand along with the Phillies first baseman, Ryan Howard, she also has an autographed ball by him! She was on TV and thank heavens my son, who is a huge Phillies fan, taped the game! This stadium has more concession stands and eateries than I have ever seen at any stadium, be it football or baseball. You want food, they've got it! Citizen's Bank Park food offerings, redefines Ballpark cuisine! I have tried most of these places and be it a cheesesteak, crab fries, kielbasi, hot dogs, piled high sandwiches or BBQ, you will leave here filled with satisfaction. Bull's BBQ is the largest grill in all of major league baseball's stadiums. It has an outdoor picnic area and grills and BBQ's anything from turkey, pork, beef and sausages to chicken. http://philadelphia.phillies.mlb.com/phi/ballpark/concessions.jsp In honor of the recently deceased Harry Kalas, they had paid homage to him with Harry The K's, which has served beverages and foods from finger food to an upscale menu. McFadden's which is a sit down eatery and Sports bar is conveniently accessed from both inside and outside of the enclosed park. I am there to watch the ballgame, food is brought to you, as well as beverages, constantly! If and when I do venture away from my seat to grab a bite, I still do not miss the game, thanks to the numerous screens and shouts from the stands. Seating is comfortable with a lot of leg room, wide screen TVs adorn this open stadium and beautiful displays of a lit up replica of the Liberty Bell, which rings every time the Phillies hit a home run. Guests also enjoy a fantastic view of the Center City skyline. Oh, by the way, that is real grass on the field. Tickets can be purchased in advance and online. This year they have a new package that includes your ticket for the game and a $10.00 food voucher than can be used at any stand or eatery. They sell for $32.00 -$34.00. One thing that I will never forget and that is how badly I wanted Chipper Jones to autograph a baseball, for my Grandson. He refused, right in front of my grandson. Later, as we sat behind the dugout, we watched a line form and who came out, Chipper Jones to sign at least 20 balls. Since then I have bought his baseball and bat, but it killed me to do so. As we were walking towards the parking lot, after the game left out, we passed the area where the Phillies players were leaving, Jim Thome got out of his Hum V and signed quite a few balls. I gave mine to my son, since he is a big fan, but I will never forget those two episodes. The way I look at it, if you do not find love for this stadium, it is because you are jealous or envious. Every time I walk into Citizen's Bank Park, I am loving it and knowing that my next few hours will be full of good times and good eats. Batter up! Play ball!

text: Maybe it's because I'm a bit Italian, maybe it's because I've been to a ton of family owned Italian restaurants or maybe it's because I know how to cook, but for whatever reason, after my second visit to Ralph's, I feel I can do better. First the good points, the place seems to get a good crowd The decor and staff are what you'd expect at an Italian American restaurant. And that's really about it. I ordered the veal "marsala." I was intrigued by the use of sherry instead of the traditional Marsala wine, from which the dish gets its name. Absent was the prosciutto and light brown sauce you'd expect. In their place was a strangely fatty creamy broth into which were placed a few veal slices along with the expected mushrooms. If you're going to call a dish something, then for the love of God and all that's holy, use the correct ingredients. Sherry comes from Spain and Marsala comes from Sicily. They don't even taste the same. The broccoli and escarole as a side dish was much better. However, it doesn't take much effort to properly steam something and then season it. Now about the server, when I asked which RED wines they had by the glass, the server listed Pinot Grigio and one or other whites,..huh? Also, five minutes after you've served the food don't come back and ask if we need anything. Obviously not, you just served the food. Also it's 2009, learn how to run a credit card machine. That's perhaps acceptable at a BYOB but not at places that charge PA restaurant prices for a bottle of wine. text: Aahahahahahahah- Kingdom of Vegetarians is ludicrously bad. Yet, it made for a meal so hilarious that it may actually have been cooler than if it had been an excellent restaurant, because was so very memorable, more than if we had had something actually good. I usually reserve 1-star reviews for incidents of bodily harm, but I felt crappy from the insane levels of MSG, so I think this qualifies. We were lured in by the sign on the door- "All you can eat vegetarian dim sum- $12". What could possibly be wrong with that? The waiter brought us some tea, and even after we ordered dim sum, insisted on leaving the menu so that we could order more items if we were still hungry. They were serious about this AYCE business, it seemed. After a bowl of slightly-below-mediocre cornstarchy soup, our first plate arrived. Instead of using a cart, they brought it out in courses. So that was their game! Bring out the cheapest stuff first to try to fill us up! If I'd known where it was going from there, I would have been much more grateful for the rock-hard fried sesame mock-chicken. Incidentally, Kingdom was the first Chinese restaurant that I've been to in years that offered a fork, but no chopsticks. Not that I'm a snob, just sayin'. The sauces were standard issue, straight out of the little packets but squirted into bowls. The rest of the items were so untasty that we ended up pushing those things to the side. Next were the dumplings and pork buns. The buns were still covered with paper that had stuck on when they were microwaved and the dumplings were made of bread, unlike every other dumpling in the world. The waiter noticed the piles of unwanted food pushed away and thought we were done, but I politely asked to skip ahead to the seaweed salad. He argued but finally relented. After a very long wait, the manager(?) brought the seaweed out, saying "NOW are you happy?" Temporarily appeased anyway. It was almost entirely unseasoned, save for the 43415613456 cloves of garlic. It was the best thing we had. After we ate, I started trying to signal to the waiter that we would like something else. He literally made eye contact while I waved at him several times, and then returned to folding napkins but when I stood up to go get him, both he and the manager had obviously been watching me because they were instantly at my side. I stated my case and the manager brought out the fried bananas, telling us "This is your last course". Uh, AYCE whut? Oh my word. The itsy bitsy little slices of banana were encased in giant puffballs of batter. I surgically extracted the banana, followed by the fillings of the eggroll, of the be-papered bun, of the dumplings, and now of the banana, leaving neat little dough cases delicately split on my plate. It was bratty, but dammit, I was still hungry! By now we were feeling weird and flushed from so much MSG but we weren't ready to give up, so we ordered the only other thing on the admittedly extensive dim sum menu that wasn't fried: coconut triangles. Again, I had to chase them and they gave me some shit, but I reminded them it was AYCE, and actually we were doing them a favor because we had skipped 75% of the menu. It took a loooong time to get these. The manager told us they were making them from scratch. They were the last thing on the menu, and I guess no one had ever made it that far before dying of MSG poisoning or a heart attack. Finally, she brought out deep fried triangles with pockets of oil literally oozing around between the layers of fried. Again, I surgically excised the meager filling. It was orange and tasted like sweet potatoes, with perhaps a hint of coconut flavor, courtesy of McCormick. Damn. I'm confused by all the glowing reviews. Maybe people enjoy different foods than we do, but the service? Some of the worst I've had. I'm polite, friendly, forgiving- was it something I said? Just stay away.
label: NEG

text: My Hubby and I went here last Friday when visiting the city. It was on our quest to "eating" our way through New Orleans and this was the best place to start. We sat at the bar -- cuz thats just how we roll. There was one lady to our right enjoying a salad and we ordered an awesome and crisp Pinot Grigio. We split everything (a whole meal is wasted on me -- I'm a noshing fool) so we went with the crab cake appetizer. I can only say.... Oh MY GOD. NO - I MEAN -- OH MY GOD!!! It was the most amazing crispy crab cake with feta and a creamy sauce around it that had kalamata olives. Hubby rolled his eyes back in his head and I thought he would start moaning -- but thankfully he didn't. We ate that way too quick. Our bartender Adam was the best -- and somehow conviced us not to continue hopping but to stay here and well, eat some more. We ordered their Gumbo of the Day which was seafood and amazing. Then... Adam told us about their Stuffed Chicken Wings. Let me tell you the story... Apparently the lady that makes these wings used to only make them for the staff there for lunch. Well one day Emeril comes in, tries these wings and says they are going on the menu. The lady now works there full time. Adam told us they were "life changing" wings. So of course, we tried them! They are stuffed with a pork, seafood plus many yummy things stuffing and are served with a homemade Hoisin sauce. So delicious. After 3 glasses of Pinot Grigio and those appies, we walked out very very happy puppies! So happy, we went back for lunch the next day and had the crab cake and the wings just one more time... The Chef remembered seeing us and gave us an amuse buche as a hello gift. Loved this place -- you really can't go wrong here.

text: The whole thing just started off bad. When go to a restaurant for the first time I like to see people there, This place was relatively empty. We sat and I was slightly perplexed by the menu. There is a code of chili's to inform you what kind of dish you are looking at, like a curry, or spicy, and so on. text: Service was quick, inexpensive, friendly, and very helpful. I traveled all the way from W Philly to find a bike shop that would help me out for a reasonable price. text: I nicknamed this place Angry Super Fresh. The staff is NOT happy, and they make you well aware of it. On a recent trip, we watched a cashier yell at the man in front of me. It has happened on so many occasions that my fingers would cramp from detailing every incident.

text: I hate wearing a suit, but I'm OK doing it to go to this place! What a meal! We ate upstairs overlooking a beautiful treed patio. The service is nothing short of 5-star. The bar makes stiff drinks. The bread they give you is delicious and the menu choice is fitting of a highly-regarded restaurant. I enjoyed the turtle soup immensely. I had the special, which was a mixed grill. It had elk and buffalo sausage and antelope leg. Absolutely fantastic. My only complaint was that it was a small portion for the huge price, but that seems to be typical in fancy gourmet establishments. It is a longer cab ride to get to, but a fantastic experience.

text: When the highlight of my waltz into a museum is to make sophmoric comments concerning the size, age, and condition of a green, syphilis-infected penis, you can be assured that I have dropped to the basest form of entertainment. While I have no question that medical information can be gleaned from the paltry three rooms that comprise the "museum", I felt violated paying $14 to view the offerings here. I'll add that I didn't find the museum enjoyable either. There was an inordinate focus on medical trauma without associated examples of it. I found the skulls exhibit mundane, and I thought the much anticipated soap lady (which I oddly kept calling the soup lady) was jarringly boring. Probably the most interesting item to me, other than the unintentionally funny diseased penises, was the comparison between the giant and dwarf skeletons. I literally spent 15 minutes in the museum before realizing that it was one grand disappointment. Sadly, I was able to see everything in that short time period. Maybe my expectations for museums have skyrocketed as a result of living in a city known for having world class ones. In that sense, I'll state that it's possible that I simply have a misunderstanding of what one should expect to receive from a museum. But the simple truth is that I would not have enjoyed this museum if it was free. Despite the glowing recommendations, I would avoid it.

text: Poor Sam...his reputation as the Sushi Nazi is hardly fair. He's merely misunderstood, and considering the fact that he owns and operates his modest little sushi shop all by his lonesome, I think his behavior is perfectly warranted. Sam's is right on the corner of Printer's Alley, one of Nashville's most unique little districts. The restaurant is very small and has only enough room for two (possibly three) parties to dine there at a time. During typical lunch hours and sometimes on weekends, Sam is extremely busy and (as the sign on his door indicates) your wait time might be pretty long. But trust me...it's worth it. Sam's rolls are extremely cheap and the portions are the biggest I've ever had. Just today, Sam told me his sushi is "the cheapest in America. Maybe not the whole world, but definitely in America." The funny part? He's probably right. My buds and I got six enormous rolls and three drinks for only $19 (see the photo). The Nashville, California, Eel and Crunchy Shrimp rolls are all delectable, and the serving sizes are each about the size of your forearm. Sam's wasabi is amazing (I'm certain it's made in-house), and you'll probably need to take about half of your food to go. Sure, Sam can be a bit eccentric at times, but the man is an artist. Allow him his eccentricities.
label: POS

text: My BF surprised me with a weekend here for our 7 year anniversary on the 4th of July weekend and wow! Did we have a great time! There's a lot to cover so I think I will try Tom L.'s approach. Parking: Valet and Self Park are offered. We self parked and boy was the walk to the front desk long, I mean really long! A couple minutes into it I thought to myself that this was just like a giant Vegas hotel. But even so, we never had to walk back there so it didn't matter...which makes for a nice transition into commenting on the... Location: Out in the middle of nowhere....it makes for gorgeous views but you've got a long drive ahead of you if you want to leave the premises, esp if you self parked! Food: Pricey. We ate at Primo, Signature Grill, Plunge and Catalina. Catalina is not in the hotel, it is located in the country club a short complimentary shuttle drive down the road, it was my favorite. Primo for dinner was also very good. Both were on the more elegant side and were about $150 for the two of us, which may sound like a lot but we also spend nearly $50 on quesadillas, a beer and margarita at Plunge. The drinks wherever we went were pretty expensive, $12-$15 for mixed drinks and $5-$8 for beers and it's hard to say no when you are enjoying a float in the lazy river! Signature Grill for breakfast was delicious! We ate there twice. But the other reviews were right, its very pricey for what you get and the drinks are really expensive, the money we spent on food and drinks was about 70% of our total bill - so careful! Room/Hotel: We had a standard room which was completely nice and fine, nothing fancy and nothing to complain about either. The beds were very comfy, we had a nice view of the lazy river, everything worked, and everything was clean. The hotel is huge and you walk a lot. Its very nice though, great views everywhere you look. The service was great also, everywhere you went you'd hear, "How are you?" "How is your stay so far?" "I'm so glad to hear it!" "Have a wonderful time!" Pool and Lazy River: Yes I have to dedicate a separate bullet just for this because I loved the lazy river so. Now I must say that on the weekend of the 4th it was tough finding a lounge and a tube but it was worth it ! 4th of July: This is definitely worth a mention. They have their very own fire works show! That means no driving around, parking etc. We sat out on the patio at Primo and watched the show, it was great! Whats not great about 4th of July weekend? It was a little like Disneyland and Cancun all wrapped into one. Tons of kids running around and tons of drunk 20 somethings hanging out in the lazy river, drinking beers for hours and amazingly enough never needing to get out and pee! Gross! All and all, we had a great time and plan to come back, we hear that on any other weekend the place is deserted...sounds nice! I would definitely recommend this hotel for a fun filled weekend!
label: POS

text: At our first table, the server spilled water all over and we moved to the middle of the restaurant, where the draft from the 15 degree weather outside led us to request yet another reseating to a cozier spot. Throughout this ordeal, the hostess was friendly and accommodating, and once we got settled in, everything got even better. Coriander is BYOB, and they chilled our bottle of white for us. The potato patty chickpea appetizer (whose name I forget) was surprisingly tasty (for such simple ingredients) and the big bowl of walnut-based soup lived up to its reputation as a house specialty - it was piping hot, had deep flavors, and was spicy enough to clear my sinuses. The chicken makhani (my favorite comfort food) was rich and the chicken was moist. The kebabs were well-spiced, and the naan was fine, though less buttery than I like it. They're heavy on the cilantro, so if you're sensitive to it, definitely ask for light/no cilantro garnish. The servings are generous, and there was plenty to take home (I'm finishing up my kebabs while sitting at my desk at work). A friend of mine has a gluten allergy, and they were able to accommodate that without a problem as well. Quite pleasing overall.

text: As my boyfriend and I were trying to find Gianna's (l had no idea they closed), we ended up seeing this place. text: My wife and I went here for our "New Years Supper". It was my first visit, but my wife had been there a couple of times before. I feel that this is a very well run restaurant, based on the service and perceived efficiency of the wait staff. They seem like "professionals". The steak we ordered was cooked perfectly, the sides, including the "Gumbo" soup I had was perfect. The prices are higher than other steakhouses, but we also found that the service and food quality was as well. Their "price fix" style menu is nice, as that brought the prices down to a more "acceptable" and competitive level. Overall I recommend Ruth's Chris, and would definately visit it again.

text: I went here Tuesday evening before Christmas, arrived at around 9:55pm, figuring they were be open late with holiday hours. I was looking for some Sorel boots for a present. (I've had a pair for 20 years that still work great, and wanted to find something similar.) I finally found the women's shoe area, and although I heard something over the store's speakers, I wasn't paying attention (turns out it was an announcement to let shoppers know that the store was closing). As I started scanning the shelves, an employee approached me and let me know the store was closing (10pm), but asked if there was something in particular I was looking for. When I told him Sorel boots, he immediately showed me a section for them. He apologized that the selection was severely diminished because there had been a run on snow boots due to all of the snow we received in Reno in December; but asked me anyway if there was some specific type I was looking for. After I described the kind I had, he knew a model name for what I was looking for, but also let me know they didn't have any. I have the impression he would've looked further, for whether they were something I could order through their store, but I told him I was going to try somewhere else. He and every other employee I came across in my few minutes after closing time, were pleasant, even cheerful. Having worked in retail long ago, I can remember myself (and other employees) wishing at closing time that customers would just go away so we could go home. I didn't get that feeling at all on this evening.

text: I hadn't visited a Tony Roma's in probably 10 years because I vowed never to go back based on a bad experience. My coworkers suggested to we give it a try and I warned him about my experience. This is probably a new location because the lounge area seemed very new. With 4 flat screen TVs hanging off the walls, maybe this wouldn't be too bad of experience. OH wait! That changed in a heartbeat. Our servers were in their 40s and would definitely cater to the working class crew. Even then it brought me back to my teens when I used to work at st. Hubert or even visiting a local Swiss Chalet. My friend suggested we go for the 7-8-9 menu. So I ask what the heck is that? Well it's lunch deals for $7,$8 and $9. Not really impressed with what I saw, I settled on the St. Louis Ribs. As we waited for our food, my friend asked the bartender to change the channel to watch one of the afternoon hockey games since it was American Thanksgiving. Well to our dismay, their satellite package didn't have more than Sportsnet West. That was a sign of things to come. Our food came out pretty quickly. As expected, I received the frozen ribs, previously cooked ribs that were sitting on the grill then reheated. They were dry with very little meat. The mashed potatoes weren't too bad but the coleslaw was "wet". My coworker ordered some beef sandwich and anything served on a kaiser makes it horrible. So as low as the expectations came, I was sorely disappointed. I won't be visiting another Tony Roma's EVER AGAIN!!!

After a few annoying interactions with the opening comedians, a burly bouncer kicked a couple of them right the fuck out. They weren't forcibly removed, but it was still pretty sweet.

text: I DO NOT RECOMMEND HIRO'S IN TARPON SPRINGS. THE FOOD IS NOT GOOD, AND THE SERVICE IS POOR. Our waitress, who undoubtedly must have been new, was scattered. Our drinks took an unusually long time to arrive. The sushi appetizer we ordered was not the one we got. When we tried to waive our waitress down, she kept ducking in and out of sight. So we called to the waitress attending the table next to ours and let her know our appetizer was wrong, and she had the gall to question us about having ordered incorrectly. There was a lot of smoke accumulated inside Hiro's because they don't have the hoods above the table like Benihana. We had an emergency and had to leave before our chef had even arrived at the table to start cooking the meal. I asked for the check and could not believe they were charging me for the entire meal!!! I tried to complain to our waitress, but she just kept scurrying around and didn't even notice the incorrect bill. I finally got a manager's attention (a blond woman whose name I didn't get), and told her that we shouldn't be charged for a meal we didn't have. They grudgingly removed the items we never got to eat. Our waitress, possibly feeling a little guilty, packed up the other appetizer we had ordered (which was correct!) in a to-go box, and we ate that in the car. It was pretty much scallions rolled inside Steak-Ums and doused with teriyaki sauce. Perhaps we've been spoiled by our frequent (and excellent) dining experiences at Benihana. We are new to the Tampa Bay area and are still feeling out restaurants. But after having attempted to dine at Hiro's, we will now happily drive all the way to Orlando if we want teppanyaki. Hiro's wasn't that busy, so there was really no excuse for the poor service. We didn't even get an apology. NO DINING EXPERIENCE IS WORTH THE AGGRAVATION--I DO NOT RECOMMEND DINING AT HIRO'S IN TARPON SPRINGS.

text: What a disappointment. I was all geared up to be in fresh fruit/veggie heaven this a.m. during my family's outing to the Soulard Farmers Market, and came away instead feeling like I just wasted an hour of my day. Why, you ask? Because it seemed the majority of vendors weren't offering homegrown goods but stuff shipped in from elsewhere. Well, wtf? Okay, I get that it's early in the season, but that's no excuse for such low quality products. I couldn't believe some of the produce they were trying to get people to buy - the garbage can was the only place some of their goods belonged. In addition, the setup of the market is far from conducive to any sort of crowd - because it's so small it's difficult to walk through and absolutely no air is ventilated through the long hallways. On an 85 degree day, that is NOT the way I want to spend my time. The one highlight of the trip was our purchase from Baetje Farms - their sign announces fresh goat cheese made weekly, and based on the taste test of their offerings, it was obvious that they know what they're doing. It was some of the best cheese I've ever tasted. We ended up with the cranberry and cinnamon concoction as well as the garlic and chive version. With crackers, it made for a fabulous evening snack. I highly recommend seeking them out if you opt to visit this market - may just be the only highlight of your visit too.
label: NEG

text: Sweet Jesus, those strawberry pancakes were amazing! Instead of Jason Segal, I'm going to start fantasizing about these little treats :) Last Saturday, Mike T and I were on a mission to try a new brunch spot. We love the waffle at Crepes, Etc. but it was decided that we needed to branch out a bit. Nadoz had been touting their awesome waffle on Twitter, so we headed there first, only to find out that they stop serving breakfast at 10:30 am. Say what? On a Saturday? What kind of Nazi camp are these people running? But I digress... We wanted breakfast, so I pulled out the iPhone and did a quick search of what's nearby. La Dolce Via of course! I'd been wanting to try their brunch anyway, as yelpers practically crap their pants with excitement when writing their reviews of the place. So off we went! Service is super friendly here. Above and beyond what you'd expect from a CWE brunch spot. And it's quick. Within 10 minutes of ordering at the counter, our food was at the table. I went with the strawberry pancakes and Mike T had the biscuits and gravy. We both ordered a large, fresh-squeezed grapefruit juice to wash it all down. At $4.50 per glass, it was totally worth it! As you could tell, I very much enjoyed those pancakes. Generally, I try to split my plate into two halves. One I'll finish, the other I save for later (or just throw it away). This time, all rules went out the door! I downed those pancakes in 8 minutes flat. There was a huge pile of strawberries left over, but Mike helped in that department. My only complaint is that food here is a bit pricey. Brunch for two people was close to $35. Granted, the food is made with local ingredients and you can taste the difference between their pancakes and the Bisquick crap at IHOP, but $35 for breakfast seems a tad excessive. This will be a breakfast treat rather than a regular staple in my diet. My waistline and my wallet couldn't afford it any other way!

text: My family often orders take-out from Brazzo. I don't know why. Must be because it's the closest of the myriad pizza joints in Harleysville. The take-out orders usually consist of pizza, stromboli, steaks, hoagies, etc. For the most part, the food is unexciting. I find the pizza and stromboli to be pretty bland, and the stromboli are often soggy and simply packed with whatever crappy, bland mozzarella they use, while skimping on other ingredients that might actually add flavor. I love getting white pizzas when they reek of garlic, but here I think they just whisk up some ricotta and oil and spread it on, as the white pizza was pretty flavorless. Beyond the lack of distinguished food we've gotten, my experience with their take-out service has been absolutely terrible every single time. Not once have I been able to walk in when they tell me my order will be ready, get my food, pay, and leave. It's always a 15 minute ordeal for them to search and find out what my order was, then discover it isn't ready yet, then to cycle the food retrieval duties around. I then stand around for a good 10 minutes as they usually forget that I am waiting for food. Even when we call 90 minutes ahead of time and say we'd like to pick it up at X:XX, it still results in a wait. The only reason I'm not giving Brazzo 1 star is because we did eat in the restaurant one time and had a pleasant experience, and the food was very good. So if you want to eat authentic Italian dishes (ie veal florentine, chicken marsala, eggplant parmigiana) in a restaurant, Brazzo may be a decent choice. But if you're looking for a good take-out joint, there are about 7 others in the area I'd recommend before Brazzo.

text: I love Ted's. That's all that needs to be said. The atmosphere is fun and cozy but upscale. They've got bar seating, tables and nice big booths. During the summer months their small outside patio is nice too. Oh, and each booth as an inspirational quote in it. Now on to the good stuff, the food. I could live off their Karen's "Flying D" Bison chili. No really, I could. Lunch is usually good with that and a house salad. But that means I miss out on what they're known for, the Bison burgers. They come in an array of combos, or you can build your own. For the burger my fav is George's Cadillac (bbq sauce, cheddar cheese and bacon). They come with fries too, unless you get the Ultimate Skinny which comes with cottage cheese. If you're into chicken, their sandwiches are great and come with the same combo choices as the burgers. For this one I usually opt for the Green & Hot (guac, jalepenos & monterey jack cheese) on a kaiser bun. Fries come as well. text: The best thing I had at A La Maison was a delicious bottle of Pinot Noir. That's a pity, considering the restaurant is BYOB. French restaurants are rather rare outside of downtown, so I was delighted to come back from a four month absence to find A La Maison had opened up in my old stomping grounds of Ardmore. I'm a huge fan of French Bistro food, as I worked in one for several years. I brought my wife to A La Maison Friday night, which took some persuasion as my wife doesn't share my love of French food. She just doesn't understand what all the fuss was about. I assured her that she would have a revelation once she had it at a good bistro. Unfortunately, A La Maison is not a good bistro. The decor is sparse but passable, done on a budget but reasonably tasteful. The wait staff was friendly but unpolished. They would benefit from acting slightly more formal and brushing up a bit on their knowledge of the menu. The menu was essentially standard bistro fare, except for an interesting looking smoked salmon tian. I ordered that as an appetizer, only to be told that they were out of it. (At 6:45 on a Friday?) Okay, I'm not that picky, so I went with the pate, to be followed by the nightly special of steak Diane. My wife ordered the house salad as an appetizer and the roasted salmon Dijonnaise as a main course. The pate came with a spot of mustard, some cornichons, and toasted baguette slices. The baguette slices were hard as rocks, so I used the house bread instead. The pate itself was reasonably tasty but not memorable in any way. My wife's house salad was imposingly large, with a light-tasting vinaigrette, palm hearts, pine nuts, and a few other knick-knacks. Like the pate, it was unremarkable, even a little bland. The more glaring problems began with the main course. My wife's salmon was expertly cooked, but it was under-seasoned, and the sauce was sparse and wimpy tasting to boot. It came with sauteed Swiss chard. Technically there was nothing wrong with the Swiss chard, except for the fact that apparently nothing had been done to it other than throwing it in a pan. No shallots, no wine, no vinegar, and no spice of any kind. Hey, Swiss chard is a nice vegetable, but you should at least TRY to do something with it! Similar problems plagued my steak Diane. I had been told it was tenderloin, but I was dismayed that I received the top of the head from the tenderloin, which is the least tasty part. For $28, I would expect a better cut. Just like the salmon, the sauce was sparse and underwhelming. The accompanying mashed potatoes could have come from any diner in Philly, and the spinach was a clone of the Swiss chard, i.e. badly in need of something else to give it a kick. In fact, that was the problem with the entire meal. Nothing had a kick to it. The things that make French food so special, the rich stocks, gobs of butter and cream, wine, fresh herbs, pungent shallots, all seemed to be missing or used extremely sparingly. This isn't rocket science, guys! It's just as easy to make a knock-out batch of creamy mashed potatoes as it is to make a bland batch. The final verdict? As much as I wanted to like A La Maison, I had to agree with my wife's judgment: Not Worth The Calories.

text: If there is something I enjoy more than food, adult beverages, and social media, it would be music. If you hang around me IRL you'll know I love just about every form of musical expression from my first love hip hop to indie rock and even bluegrass on occasion. Now the Gramophone for me really is a special place that has something for everyone musically. You'll see everything from DJ's to touring bands from across the country and even beloved local acts playing. The venue its self is not a huge venue. I would say its definitely smaller in size. Also there is not a lot of separation from the performer and the audience which is really nice. In fact you might be able to strike up a conversation with the artist(s) before they perform. I would recommend though getting there early if you want a table because those tend to go quickly when more popular acts are performing. Also the outdoor patio is nice to get a break from the performance if you need it. Because of the space I would say the acoustics are are not the best in the St. Louis but I've heard a lot worse. I like to get a spot at the bar and enjoy the show from there (just make sure you get a spot in between the beams). Drink prices aren't bad if you like to enjoy a beverage while your new favorite band performs. I've spent maybe at the most $10 to $15 on beverages. The drink selection isn't bad but I haven't tried anything more than the standard beers and well drinks. Recently they have started to have a new type of open mic night called The Shed. It sounds like a unique venture by just having open mics, turntables and open collaborations. Plus they also broadcast some of there shows on Ustream if you are not able to make it. I can't speak for the quality of the web casts but its a cool option. Also the fact that the cover is usually $10 makes for a pretty good time. All in all the Gramophone is a solid venue. Not incredible but it's a fun place to catch a show or two. I cannot call it my favorite venue in St. Louis but the quality of artists they bring in and the variety are what push it to a four star joint for me. Also decent drink prices and it being non smoking really help as well. If you ever head to The Grove for a night, stop into the Gramophone and enjoy some music. You might just like it!

text: After multiple experiences of the same caliber, I must put the word out somewhere that this hospital is a complete and total RIP OFF. My husband has been the one to take our dog(s) in before and through him I've had bad vibes, but now I flat out will not step foot in the place again. I would feel more comfortable dealing with a used car salesman. I literally got the phone call this time claiming "Well I know the paper we gave you says this, but now it's really going to be another $100." They also charged $160 to induce vomiting!!! I would have gone to the store and paid $2.99 for a bottle of peroxide if I knew what they were going to charge! It takes a lot for me to leave a review like this, and I've had it. A few more notes - I got the call at 4:43 that my dog was ready to be picked up. I walked in the door at 4:55. The front room was packed with people sitting and standing around. Neither of the girls at the front desk addressed anyone in the room as I waited for five minutes trying to see if there was an actual system in place. I finally stepped up to the counter when there was an opening and they proceeded to take my payment then told me it would be a few minutes. At exactly 20 minutes, I asked if it was known how long it would be because I needed to pick up my son in 15 minutes. The girl went back and checked with the doctor and came back and told me it was "going to be a while." I told her that I had dinner in my car and my son to pick up and inquired as to why I had gotten a call 45 minutes earlier saying my dog was ready when they clearly were not ready. Of course she had no answer and I had to leave and come back to get my dog. During the two visits to retrieve my dog, four people - including the doctor - referred to my female dog as "he." This obviously enraged me. I trust them to save her life and they can't even take the time to remember what sex she is. Lastly, the vet told us that they had run out of TWO of the medications needed to treat her. The first was pills that are used to induce vomiting. So they gave her HALF of the one pill dose that is normally used and saved the other half! She then did not vomit and they had to use hydrogen peroxide, which eventually made her vomit. The vet said she was on her way to the store to buy ipecac when she finally vomited! They did not have the 32 pills needed for her prescription, so they sent me home with 22 and told me to come back next week! I shudder at the thought of any hospital, human or pet, that does not keep an ample stock of basic medications on hand. I think that pretty much says it all. If I can say one nice thing, the gentleman who helped me at the very beginning of the day was very polite. They should hang on to him because he's probably keeping their doors open.

text: Urban Outfitters. I'm going to hand them two stars for a couple of reasons. Their staff, for some reason, screws up a lot when I buy from there. Not so much lately, but it's usually a pair of shoes or a dress. For example, a few years ago I found a second pair of the perfect soft, kind of floppy black combat boots here for $15. The first pair I got for almost the same price, as a result of a $25 store credit I received when it took two weeks to receive something I paid for two day shipping on. And I found the perfect opaque black tights on sale on their website for $2.99. Okay, two-stars. But for the most part, they're extremely over-priced and low-quality. Their selection of clothes becomes more and more boring every season and rather than selling unique pieces or novelties, they tailor their selection to what hipsters are doing NOW. They sell custom fixed-gear bikes on their website now - this is obviously a Philadelphia company. I used to love this store. My impression of Urban Outfitters in 2009 is that they are trying to emulate the hipster experience for lazy hipsters with money to waste. Everyone has been teasing Abercrombie & Fitch for years about their fake vintage $70 paper thin t-shirts and Urban Outfitters is basically the exact same. I agree with one of the previous reviews. Save your money and go next door to buy quality products from American Apparel and make your own style and break in your own t-shirts.

text: Wonderful Vietnamese food. We liked it so much during our visit to the Tampa area that we ate here two nights in a row. The minute we walked in, we could tell that we were in for authentic Vietnamese cuisine in a pleasant, low-key atmosphere. We enjoyed their cha gio (spring rolls), even though they were smaller and thinner than what we typically order at Vietnamese restaurants. The accompanying nam pla (fish sauce) was delicious, full of julienned carrots and radish. My guy loved the grilled shrimp and pork over rice vermicelli (bun). He had it both nights. I tried the pork, and it was well-marinated in a delicious sauce. I ordered one of their traditional pho soups the first night, and it was delicious. The meat was tender, and the broth was flavorful. The second night, I ordered their spicy pho (I can't remember its official name) with tendon and beef. It also had cubes of pork blood (a specialty that looked and tasted like liver), which I didn't care much for, but it added to the depth of flavor in the soup. The accompaniments to the pho was great - fresh mint, Vietnamese basil, sliced chile, and beansprouts. As for drinks, I ordered the mixed nut drink the first night and then the rainbow ice drink the second night. Both were tasty, with lots of texture and served in generous portions. Each drink was topped with a huge chunk of crushed ice (akin to a snow cone without any flavor), which I could have done without. I ended up removing most of the ice to avoid diluting the flavor of each drink. If I lived in Tampa, I would be here all the time. If you're ever visiting Tampa and in the mood for authentic Vietnamese food, definitely check this out!

McDonald's breakfast sandwiches are better. They're about on a par with Lukoil microwave breakfast sammies. Were I in their shoes, I would just focus on good pastries and scrap the sandwiches. I also ordered tea, which is the one thing coffee shops (with the exception of Starbucks, oddly) consistently do poorly. This was the worst tea I've ever had in any coffee shop. I see this place in the evening (when I'm coming out of Shanachie Pub), and they seem to do well. I'm sure it's a great place for coffee and goodies. Come to think about the experience it was very much like bad sex. I left disappointed, underwhelmed and very unsatiated. Drinks: Beers were a bit expensive in my opinion... Some have criticized me for having too high of a standard in Mexican fare, which I understand because I have spent a chunk of my life in LA and as a half adopted Mexican daughter. text: We used Lenora to move when sold our house and moved. Before going into the details, I'll say that the overall review is for the service/management rather than the actual movers. I totally expect Lenora to challenge what I am about to say, as they've done before but unfortunately for them I have everything documented. First of all, the good part - the movers themselves. These guys are awesome - they loaded all of our stuff (and then unloaded) under two hours. They were quick, careful and courteous. If I can hire them directly, I would do so every time. Sadly, here comes dealing with the company itself... We hired Lenora because they advertised (and as a matter of fact still do) that they take credit cards. Being short on cash due to all of the expenses associated with selling/buying a house, etc. that was the most important aspect to us when we selected a company to use. As it turned out, their claim to take credit cards is nothing but false advertisement - even though we checked twice and have emails proving that they confirmed this fact, we had to scramble to get cash to pay them... Secondly, they were 5 hours late to arrive to pick up our stuff. I was told that it was due to the previous customer and that if I wanted a timely arrival I had to book the entire day. Understandable in theory, except that the truck called us from 5 blocks away and then repeatedly got lost for almost 3 hours to the point that I had to go and meet them so they can follow me... why the company can't provide a simple cheap GPS to their trucks is beyond me... getting lost and wasting our time obviously has nothing to do with a previous customer. Since we had to keep our things overnight, we asked for a lock on the truck. Well, I did not see a lock either when the truck left at night nor the following day when it arrived. I am paying you for overnight storage, I expect to see a lock on the truck at some point! On the delivery date, we ran late because of the closings and all... they charged us extra two hours for the truck waiting for us to get to the house. It would be okay, except that the truck arrived an hour earlier than the scheduled time. It's fine to charge me for an extra hour, but they charged for two! When I contacted them regarding all of this issues, I received nothing but arguments and flat out lies, including a statement that the company has emails to prove that we were told they do not accept credit cards (there can't be no such email and I can actually prove it). At some point during the email exchange there was a not so thinly veiled ethnic stereotype directed at us. At that point, I decided to file a complaint with BBB and FTC... once the complaint was processed, Lenora claimed that no only was I wrong in my claims, but that we did not pay them $165 for the overnight storage (though I have a receipt stating that it was paid in cash)! Perhaps I should've pursued fighting them, but it was not worth my time and effort. If they are happy to overcharge people, lie to them and cause nothing but trouble, soon enough it will come back on them...
