text: "Feminism is dead, ladies. Put your bras back on, relinquish your right to vote, get back in the kitchen and make me a sandwich. Your successors have failed you." That's one way I considered starting this piece. I wrote it in my head as I leaned against a wall in the corridor that connects the main room and back patio at Pub and Sub. I was waiting to use the bathroom. Directly in front of me were two obnoxious young girls. They were waiting to use the bathroom as well. The men's bathroom. "Sorry," said Girl Number One. "We're next." Arms crossed, I smirked. When the door opened and the previous occupant exited, I maneuvered past the two (no easy feat) and entered the men's room. "It's okay; you can shove me out of the way," barked Girl Number One as I posted up at the urinal. I ignored her. Something you should know about the men's bathroom at Pub and Sub: The only walls are the four establishing it as a room. With the exception of a small, chest-level divider between the sink and urinal, everything is exposed. This means if you decide to hunker down and drop a deuce while another guy is in the bathroom, he can see you. This also means if you're a shameless nineteen year old with a fake ID who has consumed too much beer, and you decide you want to come in, pull down your pants, and pee in front of a complete stranger, by God, you can. That is, of course, exactly what Girl Number One did. Meanwhile, Girl Number Two loomed overhead, texting friends, checking her MySpace account, or twatting about the situation on Twitter. Whatever. As they annoyingly carried on I found myself wondering, what happened to the iconic influence of Audrey Hepburn? Did it die when Hollywood green-lit Barb Wire starring Pamela Anderson? Surely, Hepburn wouldn't approve of these ghastly whores. Virginia Woolfe would be ashamed. Even Julie London would shake her head with disgust. Buckling my belt and heading out the door I realized not only is chivalry dead, so is the need for it. Interestingly enough, the aforementioned situation is actually the charm of Pub and Sub. (Or Pub and Chub, as my friends and I affectionately refer to it. We also call it the Rub and Tug, the Thug and Chug, the Drug and Plug and the list goes on.) It's one of the reasons my friends and I congregate there on Thursday nights. We show up for the $2.50 pitchers of Pabst Blue Ribbon; we stay for the laughs. (Also, food at Pub and Sub is surprisingly not bad. I don't know if I'd eat it sober but, thankfully, that's never been the case.) No matter where you look or who you interact with, there's always hilarity or adventure awaiting you. Sometimes both. More often than not, it involves chicks who think they're smart because they study interior design (or something equally useless), wear club attire to dive bars, and do their damnedest to set the women's movement back a minimum of fifty years.

text: Repo Records is one of those places that is intimidating to enter at first simply because you're wondering if you're hipster enough to not be laughed at when you walk out with the white bag with the green blob on it. But, no, really, it's nothing like that. I first started going to Repo when our old friend Tower Records fell and was replaced with a Wallgreens Pharmacy Center. WTF? But anyway, Repo seemed like one of those places that could cater to my mixed interest of music, especially my indie and punk side. I had been there a few times before when I was younger but back then it just didn't click for some reason. With the exception of a few titles, they have been able to keep my ear drums rocking and still leave me salivating enough until my next paycheck comes around. The CD prices are pretty standard with maybe a few dollars knocked off when compared with the corporate monopoly that is FYE. Their used selection of CDs conveniently placed in the center of the first floor is also reasonably priced and you'll find a lot of great titles there, not just your old Gloria Estafan albums you were too embarrassed to keep in you house! The basement [and even upstairs] offers a larger selection of vinyl that you won't find many places and their punk selection can't be beat. It's reminiscent of the old days when South Street was filled with Mohawks and pre-teens in Dead Milkmen t-shirts. Only now it's mixed in with newer bands like The Shins and the Ting Tings and even some even the most uber indie enjoyers can't even name. I think what most impresses me with Repo is that they refuse to go digital. Mead notebooks organize their sales and inventory and with the exception of a credit cards machine not much has changed , and I like that. Good music and a knowledgeable staff is all you really need and you'll find them both at Repo. So ditch the billboards on Broad Street and give them a try.

text: Chinese is not really my thing - not since I was a teenager eating sweet-and-sour chicken balls on mall dates like they were escargot and coming home reeking like food court. These days, I generally prefer a cleaner palette and most Chinese food (correction: American Chinese food) is greasy, slimy, over-fried, and leaves you feeling bloated and sloven, like a mall rat with baby fat sticking like glue. Wok n' go is express Chinese that I can dial up when I don't feel like cooking and feel fantastic after I've eaten. They're programmed into my cell phone and have a presence in our home like a Portuguese mama who still comes over to cook for you but, alas, thankfully lives a full block away around the corner! The food is fresh and cooked right in front of you. The sauces are savoury and not slimy (which I've learned is the result of a marinating process called velveting that adds egg whites and cornstarch to change the texture of meats - an authentic eastern technique that, in my opinion, doesn't quite translate). So I can still stay awake and function without heartburn after I eat Wok n' go, but granted I don't go for the sumo meal; I stick with the tofu and veggies on rice and the green onion cakes and hot and sour soup. When I want to indulge, I go for the lemon chicken which is breaded but has quality chicken; and it's not your typical 70% breading 30% meat-morsel mix. There's more meat than fatty coating - so you can still enjoy, but not fall colluding victim to the revenge of baby fat (called obesity) that's sweeping our fast-food nation...faster than you can say, uh, "sweet and sour chicken balls," (which aren't, btw, even Chinese food!!) Baby fat belongs in the baby books. Wok n' go is a short walk from my house and I haven't derailed my body by eating their express fare on the fly. Thank you, Wok n' go, for the integrity of your food, and your fast, friendly service. I enjoy reading trashy mags in your store front while waiting for my take-out order to be called. You even know my name.

text: You know, I hate to kick a place while it's down, and Deano's isn't just down--it's out. As in, it's closed. But let's face it: now there's no guilt if this review actually drags the average rating of this place to below three stars. I'm not a wine drinker at all, but I know at least a bit more about vineculture than your average Latter-Day Saint, and the entire process here just doesn't cut it. Shouldn't a server at a wine bar be a bit more like a sommelier? I'm sure the wines are excellent; my friend liked his. But since many of the patrons aren't there for a full meal but to sip and munch at a relaxed setting, wouldn't it be wise for the table service to be able to make informed recommendations? We ordered the cheese plate, and the presentation was akin to the buffet table at a church social. Some of the cheese was cubed, which might be okay except that the varieties were indistinguishable. Some of the bread was okay, and some cheese came on store-bought crackers. What--did Kraft secretly sponsor Deano? The only thing missing were the toothpicks; then again, I take that back: I think we even had toothpicks to spear our cheese cubes. They might have even had that colored plastic wrap on the tips. The neighborhood branch of the public library is supposed to be across the street, but with Deano's fluorescent lights, worn-out corporate carpet, and boring taupe walls, it basically seems as though they tried to take what anyone would expect from a wine bar and do the exact opposite. Yeah, I know the Fountain Square hipsters like irony. And cheese cubes are ironic. But then Deano's Vino kills the irony by attempting deck the walls with--get this--PAINTINGS FROM LOCAL ARTISTS! It's gauche of me to criticize any small business that supports other entrepreneurs, but this approach has become such a cliche that it also hints at creative tonedeafness. An urban wine bar should take on an ambiance of its own, maybe by supporting one artist whose vision the owner really likes. Not the same hodgepodge that they do in Greenwood. A place like the Delachaise in New Orleans gets the atmosphere right without ever being stuffy. And the cheese is good. Apparently the new Tastings has replaced Deano's in a spot just across the street, which no doubt raises the standard for wine bars in Fountain Square. Let's face it: it really couldn't be much lower after Deano's fiasco.
label: NEG

text: First, and in contrast to the previous reviewers, I should say that I am not a fan of so-called "indie" music, generally speaking, and this may have something to do with my distaste for Main Street Music. I found Main Street Music's inventory to be lacking. I have been to this store at least four times and been unable to find what I had set out to buy. While the prices are good, and I am inclined to support my local record store, this particular store has either sure-fire commercially viable albums or "look at how cool and independent we are" titles that I have little interest in. Moreover, when I asked the guys at the counter to explain the limited selection--i.e., three (three?) Zappa albums, and none of his live catalog--one of the guys walked off swearing. I got the impression that since I wasn't into whatever generic-but-indie sounding band was on the house system, then the fact that I wanted the very good second effort from Blind Melon, _Soup_, that I was a disposable customer. They have some classic 60s and 70s albums, but little from the late 80s or 90s. Their reggae section is practically non-existent, they haven't a metal or hard core section, and I was never able to find a bluegrass section. If you are in to the hyper-commercial or the stock indie, then this store is for you. If you have eclectic taste, go elsewhere. Their prices aren't better than iTunes. And at least iTunes doesn't play the "cool record store owner" routine on its customers.
label: NEG

text: My wife and I stopped in here for dinner while on vacation. First off, they weren't open for lunch on the day(s) we tried to go there, so we decided to try again for dinner. It had a nice, classy feel to it. A woman told us to have a seat wherever we'd like so we took a table and our sever came over almost immediately. He was incredibly friendly and helpful, explaining their food and drink specials for the evening. I noticed they had their own Wahoo Red Ale, which I ordered. It was decent--nothing really unique but it was good. For dinner, I ordered the Surf N' Turf which was a special that night (an 8 ounce ribeye and grilled shrimp skewer), and my wife ordered the chicken primavera. Our food came out very quickly (although they weren't very busy that night), and everything looked good except that my Surf N' Turf came without the Surf (they forgot the shrimp). I flagged down our server and he was incredibly apologetic and went right into the kitchen. About 10 minutes later he brought my shrimp out. Not a big deal to me, but I'm sure something like that would bother a lot of people. My food was excellent and my wife really liked hers. My only "complaint" about the place, and it's somewhat through a fault of our own, is that it was karaoke night. There was probably a sign on the door that we missed when going in that would have warned us. After 5 minutes into our meal they began karaoke and it was so loud that we could barely have a conversation. It took place at the end of the dining room on a small stage...coincidentally, right next to where we decided to sit. Thankfully, all of the people we heard sing were actually quite good, so it wasn't necessarily a bad experience, just one we weren't expecting. Overall we both really liked this place and would definitely check it out again if we are in the area!

text: I went here this fall with my boyfriend to go apple picking in early October. I had wanted to go apple picking in upstate New York, but our plans fell through, so my boyfriend very sweetly found this place for me. The day we went was unseasonably warm (hot even in the sun), and we were very excited to get some farm-grown apples and veggies. We didn't anticipate the traffic jam trying to get into the farm - there were crowds galore - and we managed to get a parking spot in the overcrowded lot because my boyfriend drives a 2-door Yaris and so can squeeze into spaces that a normal car wouldn't dare to try to fit into. The place was chaos. Unfortunately, a lot of the apples were picked over, so we had to walk far into the orchards to find trees that still had good fruit on them, which was just fine by me. There was a good variety of apples, from winesap to golden delicious to northern spy. So we picked a small cardboard box of apples each, and we got a box of veggies (tomatoes and peppers mostly because all of the eggplant were gone) and two pumpkins to decorate our porch with. There weren't a lot of good pumpkins left, but, after a lot of searching through the pumpkin patch, we found two - a medium-sized orange one and a smaller white pumpkin, which I thought was cool. All in all, we had a good time. That is, until we got in line to pay for our loot. The line was long, since the orchard was crawling with people, but it moved fast, so that was good. However, by the time we got up to pay, I was dying for some apple cider or something, so it would have been good if they were selling cold drinks by the checkout. At any rate, we put our apples and such on the counter and were told that our two small boxes of apples would be $50, plus another $40 for the tomatoes, peppers, and pumpkins. Holy price gouging, Batman! Seriously. $50 for apples. The sign said it was $25 per bushel for apples, so we figured that actually meant per BUSHEL. Bushels are pretty big, so we estimated that two of the small cardboard boxes that they give out near the entrance would be a bushel. Nope. They somehow consider each box to be a bushel. Of course, we'd already picked the apples, so we had to pay for them, but their sign should say $25/box (which would have clued us in right away that this place is way too expensive). In the end, with our wallets much lighter than we'd have liked, we lugged our $90 worth of apples and veggies back to the car while trying not to get run over in the traffic jam between the orchard entrance and parking lot (man, that place was crowded!). I also didn't see any evidence that there was food for sale or a petting zoo. The entrance for the orchards was an opening in the fence, where a lady barked out orders and handed out boxes, and next to that was the checkout - basically a tent with a table set up to hold the register and scale. If there's a place selling food and/or a petting zoo, it must be in a different part of the farm. I definitely want to go apple-picking next year, in September, but I'm planning on finding another orchard to go to that doesn't take advantage of its customers. A place that's not as crowded as Disneyworld would also be good. Maybe I'll find somewhere in Bucks County. Or maybe I'll make it back up to NY state, where I remember picking well-priced apples without overwhelming crowds back when I was in college. I definitely don't want to go back to Linvilla.
label: NEG

I asked for brows and chin. The woman did ask how I wanted my brows done, which was important, and she was very nice and friendly. But she proceeded to yank out hairs so roughly that in one spot under the left brow, she actually drew blood...that patch not only burned for 48 hours but turned into a scattering of tiny scabs visible for nearly a week, which was very embarrassing and something i'd never experienced. These wouldn't have happened if she hadn't been in such a rush and worked those hairs a little more carefully. When she said she was finished, I happened to run my hand under my chin and pointed out that she hadn't, that there were two other definite patches I could feel. She threaded them and although I still could feel a few fully-grown hairs in those spots, I just wanted to pay and leave. When I got home, I went to tweeze what she'd missed on the chin area and saw that she's also passed over quite a few brow hairs that were pretty apparent to me in my poor-quality hand mirror. The manager later comes out to wheel-and-deal with me where he continued to make comments like, "well, the invoice is the invoice" and the "price is the price." When it became very clear to him that there was no way I was going to pay full price for the car, he says, "Well, maybe this car is not for you." Well, maybe it's not, ... at least not at Jim Reed. I felt really bad for the sales guy, who actually did all the grunt work; he worked really hard to earn our business. But it was his manager who was the tool who lost it for him. text: UGH! ok. first off, i live in south philly, and not the cool side, the point breeze/automall side. it's borderline impossible to find decent chinese may way, let alone sushi (that delivers!!!) my friend turned me on to johnny chang's which is right up on broad and wolf i believe. the first time i should have learned my lesson. i got eel roll, yellowtail roll, and a spicy tuna hand roll. everything was tiny! and for $6 a roll, i'm expecting the usual silver dollar sized pieces. these were more along the lines of nickels. frownieZ. my handroll was filled with this coral-colored mush! i don't even know how to describe it, but i can try...imagine your four year old nephew tries to make you an "ice cream cone" out of canned tuna and mayonaisse, possibly a little play-do, but you're not sure. that is pretty accurate. my friend got the general tso's chicken, which was weird soggy and deep fried the way sweet and sour chicken is. so ok, $35 later, i still had sushi delivered to my door. so i ventured to try them out one last time, and it was when i had a lot of people over watching the phillies. we ordered a good $100 worth of food, and waited, and waited, and waited. an hour passes by, and i start to panic. i am not the type to send things back, or call yelling at a take out place because our (raw) food is sitting in the back of some guys hot car for 45 minutes. but after another twenty minutes, i did call, with an impressive amount of attitude. apparently, "our driver was lost over by the stadium, and would be there shortly"...so i hang up, still impressed with my ability to call this joint and demand answers. when i told everyone what the woman on the phone had told me, they erupted into a chorus of "uhhhh, that makes no sense!", "You live nowhere NEAR the stadium!" text: We brought a feral cat that we had adopted in to the veterinarian for a check-up, deworming, shots, spay, blood work, microchip and dental cleaning. Earlier in the year we had brought her in for blood work to determine if she had FIV. During that visit she tested negative and the doctor said it was fine for her to interact with our other cats. At this next visit, the doctor informed us that our cat might have FIV and that they would have to run the test over again. I was confused because we had brought this cat to the same veterinarian who had earlier cleared her for FIV and had given us no indication that we would have to wait an additional period of time before knowing for sure that she was FIV negative. If there had been any chance that the cat had FIV, we would have kept her separated from the other cats. After an expensive set of tests, the results finally came back negative and our cat was given the clear for her spay and dental cleaning. We dropped her off the at the cat hospital for her procedure. Sometime after the procedure the veterinarian called me and said "Hi ___, it's Dr. Bonn from VCA cat hospital, I was just calling and wanted to touch base on Minka. Feel free to call me back here at the office (215)567-6446." I later called the doctor back and was given an update. I was informed that the procedure normally only takes 12 minutes, but this spay took almost an hour due to complications from the cat recently giving birth. We had informed the doctor of this at the pre-operation check-up and she gave us no indication that any additional complications could potentially arise from spaying a cat shortly after giving birth. I was relieved to hear that the cat was fine and the doctor even performed additional tests at their own expense to ensure her safety. The next morning I went to pick up my cat. I received the medical bill which had two items on it that I did not receive, an "Elizabethan collar" which is essentially a cone to put around the cat's head to keep it from picking at its stitches or pain-relief path, and a bill for a fentanyl pain relief patch. When I had spoken to the doctor the day before she informed me that she did not like using the fentanyl pain relief patch when there were kittens or other cats and that she would give us buprenorphin to put on her gums instead. Essentially, we were charged by the veterinarian for two items which we did not use. When the poor cat finally came out of the vet she was in a terrible state. Her front paw was bloody and she looked miserable. The veterinary technician then went over a few charts with us. She stated that the veterinarian had tried calling the numbers we had provided to get permission to remove two teeth that had lesions on them and that "no one had answered any of their phone calls to give them authorization, so we would have to bring the cat back in". Essentially they would have to do new blood tests, put her under and have her traumatized by another procedure. I would have been fine with this if they had actually attempted to contact us or left a message asking for authorization. In addition, they were authorized in advance to do whatever was medically necessary to help the cat. I told the vet that no one called and that we had given them permission in advance to do whatever they thought would be medically beneficial. The veterinarian technician continued to argue, insisting that they had called us. After being charged for two items which we did not need and did not receive, and being told that our cat was going to have to come back for another expensive procedure, I left to get her back home and comfortable. This is not the first time the VCA cat hospital has mistreated us. About a year earlier they were supposed to remove a piece of another one of my cat's uterus while she was put under for dental treatment and they decided not to, telling me I would have to come back another time to have the cat put under. The VCA cat hospital was rude, consistently overcharged, underperformed and did not finish medical procedures so that they could recharge us with additional blood tests and fees to put our cats under. In my experience the VCA cat hospital has been run like a greedy corporation, not a holistic group of medical practitioners looking out for our pets' best interest.

text: I was originally going to take Baby here for her birthday but after reading some mixed reviews elsewhere, I didn't want to take the risk of disappointing her on such a momentous occasion. But I figured we should at least give it a shot (especially after reading the glowing reviews here) and for the past few months we've been trying to go but ended up having to cancel our reservations three times for one reason or another. You think I would have gotten the message that this was not meant to be. But, hey, what can I say, I'm stubborn. Baby and I finally made it there for dinner on Saturday evening and we were underwhelmed, to say the least. Nothing was awful, but it just wasn't the transcendent experience we expected given Moro's reputation (as well as the prices). And the service left a bit to be desired. Although there were only two of us (and the restaurant wasn't full), we were seated at an extremely large booth for four that wasn't at all conducive to the romantic mood we were hoping for. It was uncomfortable to eat at as I was so far away from the table I found myself hunching over to reach my plate at times (and I'm not a short person by any means). The hostess was friendly and seated us promptly. The waiter, however, left a bit to be desired. He was rather impersonal to the point where he barely acknowledged (and seemed, at times, to almost ignore) Baby when describing the specials and when we placed our orders (he did say, "Good choice" to me but it seemed less than entirely sincere). Also, for such an intimate place, there were too many people involved in serving us. Not only was there our waiter and the food server but a third person brought out the dessert menus for us. It reinforced the message that our waiter couldn't have been bothered. Baby got scallops for a first course and duck two ways for an entree while I started with the pappardelle with duck followed by an onion-crusted yellow snapper. Baby's scallops were OK but served on pasta that looked (and tasted) like a dried-out or raw ravioli. My pasta was fine and the dish good but nothing extraordinary. Our entrees were similarly acceptable but were nothing extraordinary or memorable in the least. I was also struck by the fact that the evening's entree specials were just steaks distinguished only by the chef's over-the-top saucings. Continuing the trend, dessert was similarly unremarkable. I had a chocolate semifredo which wasn't bad but the chocolate base was extremely hard making eating it a bit tricky. Baby got what was described as a Peach Cobbler (which she makes a wonderful version) but ended up being a shallow dish with a few thin slices of peaches covered by what looked like granola topped with ice cream. The topping was just sprinkled on without having been baked and did not impress Baby at all. The Jelly Bellys on the way out were more satisfying than this uncreative dish. We were not impressed at all and don't plan on returning.

text: I have been here several times because of the close proximity to where I live, so this review would be based over the past year and a half of regular visits (monthly). The service is absolutely lacking MOST of the time. Expect your server to disappear for 20 minutes after your food is served, and you have to flag one down to get your check and even longer to get your card back if you paid with a credit card. For example, I recently went in for a drink and appetizers and the entire experience took an hour. There were only 11 people in the entire place, so I found this to be completely unacceptable. The bartender was too busy texting away to notice us sitting beer-less and bored in the cantina. To avoid being completely ignored, opt to sit at the bar (not even the cantina though- you'll still get ignored!) They also tend to get the orders wrong, (asking for a side of guac and they bring you out the expensive and dauntingly large $8 plate, then tell you that you ordered the wrong way instead of clarifying to begin with) and miss you when your beer is completely empty. Dos Segundos is best at their busiest hours when they're properly staffed, like Sunday brunch. I would like to see a secret shopper initiative in this place to keep them in check. It appears as though their wait staff and bartenders are hired based on their "hipster" appearances and not their actual ability to keep customers happy, which I feel is a general problem with Northern Liberties dining. I'll keep coming back because I don't feel like walking the extra 2 blocks to El Camino Real when the weather is bad, but it's a cheap cop-out compared to their rivals in Liberties Walk. The ambient lighting and indie music give the immediate appeal, and the food is good enough, but Cantina Dos Segundos loses serious points with the mediocre service.

text: What a difference a year makes. *** (see response after the review) I sent the following letter to the owner of Yalda because our recent experience was so bad. It's been a month, and I have yet to receive a reply, so I'm posting it. ***************** I want to tell you how disappointed we were with our dinner at Yalda last night. Because we have had great experiences here in the past, my daughter specifically requested that we take her here on her birthday. Coming with her, were her mother and father-in-law, and her husband's grandparents; neither of those couples had been to Yalda and were anxious to try your restaurant, based on our recommendation. We ended up being embarrassed hosts. I called for a reservation the day before, and therefore thought you would be prepared for a party of 8. It didn't seem that you were. The bread/chutney came out quickly, but after that, service just disappeared. The appetizers were wonderful, but took forever to come out. The salads, torn lettuce on a plate with dressing, also took forever. What takes so long to plate up lettuce and dressing? And the entrees? We had to ask several times where they were. Then only 6 of the 8 were served. The other two took an additional 20 minutes, and multiple inquiries to our server. The guest of honor had to sit at the table, watching everyone else eat, while she waited for hers. By the time she finally got her entrée, everyone else was finished their meal, and she didn't have much of an appetite to eat while everyone else watched her. She just packed her dinner up to take home. Inexcusable. I had called earlier that day to ask about doing a special dessert for the birthday. I spoke to you again when we arrived at the restaurant. It was surprising, then, when it took so long for our server to even ask if we wanted dessert - we foolishly thought that the delay was his waiting for "something special" to be plated in the kitchen. Not so. We skipped dessert and left, fearing that the additional course would not get us out of your restaurant until after 10 pm. I don't know if you were understaffed, if the fact that we were using a Restaurant.com certificate made a difference, or what the problem was, but it was certainly not the celebration we anticipated. Not once during the entire meal did anyone - either the server or you - apologize or even acknowledge that the service was terrible or that there was a delay. Not once. Even though my husband had to get up out of his seat numerous times to ask where out food was. Was the food good? Yes it was, but the terrible service overshadowed everything else. Well, we probably won't be back. Neither will any of the people who were with us. We had gotten them all excited about a great place, with wonderful food, and all left with a bad taste in their mouths. No, I'm not going to write a bad review on those sites where I originally posted glowing ones, unless of course you choose not to acknowledge my letter. I just won't be able to continue recommending Yalda to others. Or if I do, I will let them know up front that they will have to put up with some real service issues. Probably the most upsetting thing to us was that we, as the hosts, expected to be part of a special experience, and to show those who hadn't been to Yalda what we had been raving about. Instead we looked like fools with very poor taste in restaurants. I came in the door being a very vocal fan of your restaurant. I didn't leave that way. ********************************************* I received a very nice letter of apoplogy from Laila, who is the daughter of the owner. She had seen my updated review on Yelp & apologized profusely for the poor service we received and and said that she never received my original letter of complaint (it was sent to the email address posted on their website). She even offered to reimburse half of our bill. I sent her a reply, thanking her for her response, and declining her offer of the rebate on our bill. My intent was never to solicit a comp, but rather to let people know that a place I had vociferously raved about in the past had fallen way short. I was hoping that the complaint would reach the owners and that it might cause a change in their service so others wouldn't go through the same thing we did. It looks as though the posting had it effect. Am I ready to go back to Yalda? I really really love their food. Yeah, I WILL go back, just not right away. And I probably won't go with a group. I commeneded Laila for replying to my posting on Yelp. It shows she cares about her customers and her restaurant's reputation. Just based on that, Yalda is worth another shot.

text: Bungalow sits in a prime location in the center of Hyde Park in the North end of Boise. Surprisingly, the building has been home to several bars and restaurants in my 15 years of Boise. I'm not even sure I ever had a chance to patron its last resident. Hopefully Bungalow can withstand the necessary turbulence of this economy and hold ground longer. My friends and I only visited the lounge during this visit so I can not attest to the restaurant area but if it is anything like the lounge, it is tastefully decorated and not overly pretentious. While it appears to be too upscale for many, the variety of patrons during our visit gave the feeling of just another great neighborhood bar. Not sure if that is what the owners are after, but it certainly seems to work. My friends and I all ordered a variety of items for our enjoyment. The deals I found to be the best: the 2 for 1 appetizers and $6 any martinis. Seriously, any martini....even Grey Goose with a twist. I have ordered similar around town for upwards of $12. The beers came in at around $3 during happy hour and they have some tasty handles, including Widmer's seasonal Brrrr. There were four of us this visit so we ordered four appetizers. The meat and cheese plate ($12), the pizza of the day ($10), the wings ($8), and the Brie ($10). All the food was excellent and very filling. The only real complaint we had was with our service. Sometimes it was good but sometimes it was non-existent. We had to flag down our server several times and it was sort of awkward. There were only five tables that evening with two servers and the bartender was handling those at the bar, so it wasn't very busy. When the bill arrived, it was incorrect and missing a couple of the happy hour discounts. Mostly, we were very pleased with their happy hour and will probably return for the martinis and appetizers but probably not for a regular meal.

text: Putting aside the comparisons to other cities the other reviewers demeaned necessary to include in their reviews and just focusing on the hotel review at hand, Hotel 43 has style, flare and personality but also lacks in a few amenities and does have some slightly 'not so great' aspects. When you cruise up to the hotel, you really don't know what to expect...but step inside and enter into the comforts of a highly-stylized atmosphere. This very modern slash late 1940's vibe, makes the guest feel comfy and welcomed. The front counter staff is extremely helpful, friendly and will be happy to answer your question about Boise. The thing I always find annoying (and yes, all city hotel's do this) is that you have to pay for parking and only $10 a day. Yes, I've paid more elsewhere, but I'm a guest at the hotel and shouldn't have to pay for parking, and that goes for all hotels everywhere. Besides that little parking soap box rant, Hotel 43 is in a great location so you can walk all around downtown and get to the highway very easily. The room I stayed in was a double queen and those beds were heavenly. The huge, numerous pillows; the big, fluffy comforter and topped with a robe wearing teddy (fyi the cute robed teddy is $30 so don't be trying to sneak it out the door). I really like that they give you an extra blanket, which is located in the closet, it's warm and handy. The room is well lit, has nice furniture, a flat screen HD TV, a super nice arm chair, and desk with chair. The wifi access is easy to log in to and has fast speeds. The bathroom is nice because the sink is separate from the toilet and shower, making it really easy for two people to get ready in the morning. Also, for your after-showering needs, they provide warm robes. The bath amenities were very nice, besides soaps, shampoo, conditioner, body butter, they also give you a sewing kit and other mini-amenity box-- cue tips, cotton ball, nail file and something I can't remember. Besides paying for parking, the few other slightly 'not so great aspects'-- I've really come accustomed to having a mini-coffee pot in my room so I can have tea or coffee. Hotel 43 doesn't provide this. Yes, you can call room service but I like having a tool to heat/brew water in my room. The other thing, in room water is $3.00 and high vending machine prices. Most hotels mark up food and beverage high, but I'm over this. So overall, Hotel 43 is a fun, relaxing, fab location, and an environmentally- and community-friendly place to spend the night. You won't be disappointed and will sleep well.
label: POS

text: This is a hitter's park, and you're likely to see a large number of foul balls and home runs flying into the stands, so keep your head up. Tonight is no different - If you are wanting to watch the game, come on in. If you are wanting to escape the sports bar, this isn't it. As I sit at the bar, the Irish band sits flaccidly plucking their instruments, pining for a chance to roust the crowd. No luck tonight boys, the Red Tide is on the plasma and the bar is packed with old men reflecting on a youth long since past. Ah, now for the Guinness. The pour is a good try, with a 3/4 glass and then a pause. The challenge is that the 'tender is pouring with one eye over his shoulder spotting the score. The final may be closer to what you would find in Football Season in Dublin (that's soccer for the western crowd) - the final product is passable, but not passionate. If you need to stay within the resort area, this is decent. If you've got your own vehicle, I'd suggest a more adventurous selection. guinness was Meh, tasted off. go here if you have to 6.95

(Olé!) I am a girl who is a sucker for even the most tame burrito, so when I saw this in the Publix shopping center in Belle Meade, I knew I had to try it. Listen, I know I shouldn't be surprised (it's a chain, it's barely Mexican,etc.) but this place was a complete disappointment. I'm not a Mexican food snob -- I can get by fairly well at the aforementioned Qdoba or Chipotle -- but the ingredient quality at Moe's was sorely lacking. What I like most about these types of restaurants is the ability to get a fresh, tasty meatless meal and not feel like you are deprived by not chowing on some animal protein. I'm not a vegetarian, but sometimes a girl wants some damn veggies. I ordered the vegetarian burrito without the shell, and added all of the vegetables they had available to bulk up the meal a bit. The "veggies" at Moe's consisted of some of the saltiest, overcooked mushrooms, green peppers and onions I've ever had the misfortune of ingesting. Ick. The black beans were pretty bland as well. The only thing I was happy about was the guacamole, which was a little bit heavy on the cilantro but still tasty. It's really hard to mess up avocados, y'all. Also annoying about this place is that all of their food has cutesy names: the overachiever, the triple lindy, the art vandalay. I'm all for creativity but I don't want to have to struggle to remember the name of the thing I ordered when the cashier asks. Also, I feel like a complete fool asking for an "art vandalay" in the first place. What does importing and exporting have to do with my vegetarian burrito, anyway? There are a few upsides (which is why I gave a whopping 2 stars instead of one): they have a salsa bar, and even though the salsas are pretty terrible I like the option of being able to try them all and add as much/little to my food as I would like, they don't make you pay extra for the chips, and they have fresh AND picked jalapenos as options for your burrito. That was kind of unexpected and cool. Everything else? Not so much. Also, I didn't try any of the meat options so perhaps I am missing out on a great menu item. Unfortunately, I probably won't be back to give them a chance.
label: NEG

text: After a long day at the office, I was hungry, real hungry and at the recommendation from a coworker, I stopped by Snackbar for some dinner. OK, I did burn my tongue but nothing was going to stop me from devouring this soup. The soup was rich in texture and flavor. I couldn't imagine starting my meal off with anything else on this frigid Philly night. After the soup was disappeared, the main course came out. Can you say Short ribs, barley, and mini carrots? These carrots weren't baby, but they weren't full grown either, lets call them teenage carrots. The bold rich flavor of the short ribs combined nicely with the added texture from the large grains of barely. This was straight up comfort food. Having eaten the the soup and the short ribs, I was very full and warm all over. I'm anxious to revisit Snackbar to sample the famous chicken pot pie which was encased by a super flaky pastry. I noticed a lot of people got the pot pie last night and this dish seemed to invoke a smile where ever it was placed down. There was no pesto flavor, the pasta thickly coated with such a sticky cream laden sauce I barely ate a third of it before I felt full. text: How can I put a star review on a major hospital. The stars really depend on different things. I know the ER really well b/c I volunteered there for 3 years. This is the ER to hit if you have a non-trauma emergency. However, I have learned that it is best to avoid the ER if you can and see your regular doctor instead. Of course, if you have abdominal pain or its late at night, you can't avoid a trip to the ER. PA Hospital's ER has shorter waits than HUP or Jefferson. I do know that, but I also know people get upset with the waits that can be long. I have some tips for the ER. 1) If possible, show up in the off hours, morning, early afternoon or late at night. Showing up at 5 pm is going to suck. 2) Bring a friend to keep you company and advocate for you. 3) They have food in the ER, but won't let you eat until all the tests are done. Get ready to be hungry. Most of the ER rooms have tv's and there is access to bathrooms. They have phones in most of the rooms, but won't yell at you if you sneak a cell phone call or two. You can get a cab once you leave, but you need to call the cab yourself. Ok, review of ER done... I did stay in PA Hospital recently. No complaints about the stay. Nice place except insurance didn't pay for it. PA Hospital didn't fight for me to be there. It was kind of a debacle. I needed care. I had insurance, but we ended up paying out of pocket. So basically I was screwed by both PA Hospital and the insurance company. I tried to fight it, but it was too hard. I gave up.

text: I have to share my experience to alert pet owners. Why I went there: I pre-paid for rabbies at Human Society and they gave me a list of clinics where I could go to get my newly adopted Lab for her rabbies vaccination. Paw Patch was closest so I took my Lab to them for rabbies and nail clipping. 1st bad experience: The doctor brought my dog out of the room after clipping her nails and said atleast 4 times in a very loud voice "your dog needs training" and jerked her leash while she was doing nothing but standing beside him. My dog coughed when her jerked the leash and I took her leash from the doctor. My husband and I was so shocked and did not know how to respond. I really regret now that why I did not say anything to the doctor about this kind of behavior. (By the way--I specifically asked Petsmart about my dogs behavior when they clipped her nails. They said she is a sweetheart and was not a problem at all) 2nd bad experience: When I made the payment I realized they had charged me for rabbies vaccination as well. I should have checked the bill before I actually paid but somehow I did not. I told them that the first thing that I gave to them was the document from Human Society stating that I have pre-paid for rabbies. They asked me to show the document again--which I did. I stood there for 10 minutes while they tried to adjust the bill--apparently they were not sure how to adjust the bill. Finally they adjusted the bill and one of the women told me they will send my dog's stool test results and rabbies certificate in mail because something was wrong with the system so she could not print out the rabbies certificate. 3rd bad experience: I never received the test results and rabbies certificate in mail. I waited for over a month and just called two days ago to remind them. They did offer to fax it to me--I do not have fax at home so I picked up the documents in person. 4th bad experience: This 4th one actually happened before the 3rd one. I noticed one day that my dog was limping and her toe was swollen. I got really worried and called Paw Patch (because they are her vet). They asked to bring her in. I went and the same doctor was there. His first comments for my dog were "oh the trouble-maker is here" "What have you done now?" I told him that she's limping but I did not see what happened to her. The doctor checked her--she behaved really well and let him check everything except that she burped right on his face! What could I do about it. :). He said he can't tell what's wrong with her toe and will have to do an X-ray. I asked him what are the possiblities--can it be broken--extended--or anything else. He said it could be anything and he can't tell without an x-ray. I asked him to give me an estimate of the x-ray. He went outside and came back with an estimated bill: over $350--around $400. I was just looking at the bill--did not know what to say--and he said "there's no other way, this is the only way we do it". I made a mental calculation of how much I have in my credit cards--and realized I did not have that much at that time. I told him I'm going to wait for a couple of days and asked him to give some painkillers. He gave some painkillers, Rimadyl, and a shot of painkiller. My bill was over $97. I talked to some friends--everyone said over $350 is too much for the x-ray. One of my friends suggested I go to Michigan Road Animal Hospital and get a second opinion. I went there..they were delightful people..the doctor did a thorough examination and said a bee or a spider had stung my dog's toe. She gave some other painkillers(Tremadol) and asked me to wait and see for 3 days. If it doesnt get better then they'll do an x-ray. The estimated cost was around $116. I and my dog left satisfied with their service and with a $50 bill. By the 3rd day--my dog was much better. text: Recently my roommate and I, after a softball game in the Art Museum neighborhood decided to try out the Tiedhouse for some food and drink. He had been there before, but this was my first time. I was not let down. Overall, the food was good, the beer selection was great, but I have a few issues. First, it is hard to find from the outside unless you've been there before. It is set back a bit from the street, and the signage is very subtle. It's not in a place where you'd expect to find a bar like this, attached to an upscale condominium. This is perhaps a cause of my only real complaint: there was only a handful of people inside. It was certainly not a lively place, and we were there at seven on a Saturday night. The service was terrific, as would be expected with a sparse crowd. The bartender was great, proving his knowledge in both beer and sports. No complaints whatsoever about the staff. We sat at the bar, talked sports and watched the World Baseball Classic on one of their big flat screen televisions. An interesting tidbit with regard to the name: in colonial times (and still today in the UK), a tied house was a public house that was required to buy at least some of its beer from a particular brewery, unlike free houses. Indeed, this pub is "tied" to the General Lafayette Inn & Brewery, although they have a wide selection of beers from elsewhere. This is in my opinion their greatest strength; besides having a full bar, they sport a wide selection of great craft beers. I tried a pair of General Lafayette brews: the Sunset Red Ale(a smooth amber ale) and Chocolate Thunder(a nice porter), and both were terrific. To conclude, the tied house is a great place to go for some decent food and a great beer, but you may be left wanting with regard to ambiance and company.

text: Our intention to eat here was the result of wanting to try, in this region of Delaware, baked pizza that wasn't prepared in the conventional commercial grade, silver oven. Since Buckley's Tavern tends to be where everyone seems to flock over the weekends, this place was the only alternative that had been open until 11pm with available seating. It had the typical franchise flare- large and open tables that seemed bolted to the ground, pre-recorded tunes in a moderate decibel, front and back of the house staff that included our waitress who looked exhausted and irritated. Overall, the food was tainted with impersonal, unceremonious preparation. Our pizza had remnants of burnt spots from the coal fire that tasted authentic, however the topping choices were sparse and never offered anything beyond the usual onion, mushrooms, tomato and pepperoni deal. Maybe their supplier was the Domino's across the street. The price reflects the dim lighting, waiter service and the careful placement of classic celebrity pictures on the walls. They were pleasing to look at with Marilyn Monroe's pouty, teasing smile and Carey Grant who overlooked the dining patrons at table #5, but I was more interested in the food which, unfortunately, didn't make an impact. The sodas came in bottles, which was satisfactory, but nothing was on draft. Even the drink selection was a little bland. At this point I've manually changed my initial three star to two which better represents this place. If you appreciate a good tastey pie you'd come to find in NYC or a quaint little town with a burley man that tends to a brick oven in the back, this place is not for you. It leaves the imagination, and our appetities, yearning for more.

text: The just-opened Twenty Manning Grill is my favorite new restaurant in Center City. While I also liked the old Twenty Manning, it was darker and pricier, and I had to be in the mood for the Asian Fusion fare. The new place is bright and warm, the perfect neighborhood bistro. I could eat there 2 or 3 nights a week. In fact, since it opened a few weeks ago, I have already been to TMG about 5 times. I live in Center City and eat out a lot -- too much, probably -- and it is so great to find a friendly, happy place that is comfortable, warm and affordable (entrees are generally in the teens, topping out at about $22). The food is great, too. Even though it has only been open a few weeks, every dish I have eaten has been delicious. I highly recommend the caprese salad (so fresh and healthy), the roasted chicken and peas (served in a cast iron skillet) and the pork chop with roasted peaches. My favorite, though, I think is the flash-seared tuna, which I absolutely loved! For desserts, you can't go wrong with the half-baked chocolate chip cookie (served with vanilla ice cream). One final note: To a person, every bartender and server I have met at TMG has been really good, and super friendly. They all seem to genuinely enjoy working there, and their positive attitude helps define this happy little bistro! Oh, and one more final note: It's nice to see owner Audrey Claire walking around every night, greeting guests and attending to little details. Makes you feel like you are being welcomed into the home of a good friend.

text: OK, this place was a disaster. My friend "won" some drawing for a night of free drinks and appetizers for her, from 6pm to 11pm, and half-off all drinks and apps for anyone she brought until 8pm, and then just half-off their drinks until 11pm. For every 10 people she bought, $25 was to be put toward the tab. At least that's what she was told. When we first arrived there, at 6pm, we had to wait around for about 25 minutes while they figured out who the hell we were, which for some reason took about 25 minutes while we stood around awkwardly. After finally getting seated in a large area, the waiter seemed put off about the fact that we'd have people joining us later, and told us we should just order at the bar. Yet, when we ordered at the bar, the bartender said, "What are you doing? Why is he having you order food here?" I don't know man, just tell us how to order and we'll order. They never sorted that out, and for a while, we'd either have to wait at the bar for our food, or periodically send someone up to the bar to grab the food and carry it back to our table. After this, someone noticed that it was was happy hour until 8pm, and *everyone's* drinks were half off. Then what's the point of our drink special? So we asked the bartender if we got half off the half off, to which he said, "Oh, yes, it's only 25%." After ordering more drinks, a different bartender says he thinks that's wrong, and then another one shoots it down all together, saying, "You're paying as much as everyone for their drinks, but everyone's special here." Which is, A) Lame; and B) We had been ordering drinks thinking they were at a hugely discounted price! We soon learned other contingencies of the "special." The free drinks that my friend had won did not include shots, and the half off was only on well drinks and house wine, and 8pm to 9pm was a dead zone in the night where none of these specials applied. Why were the rules suddenly changing so much? During this "dead zone" of 8pm-9pm, the half-off all drinks special went away, but select draft beers were $1. A bunch of us ordered these beers since we didn't have a special during this hour, but after ordering the beers the price was erased from the blackboard and changed to $2 - but then as soon as we paid for the beers we had ordered which suddenly cost us $2, the price was erased and changed back to $1. And then my friend was to get $50 put toward her tab there due to bringing in 20 friends, but they wouldn't give it to her that night, and weeks later she is having trouble getting the $50 because they are making her talk to a specific person there who is impossible to track down. All and all it was a bad experience, the bartenders and waitstaff kept changing the rules and seemed to hold some level of contempt for our party, the food was unpalatable, and aside from all that the aesthetic of the place was .... not good. Avoid.

text: I found a 90% off restaurant.com coupon deal so got a $25 off of $35 coupon for Bella Italia for under a dollar. I must have driven past this place a dozen times but never felt compelled to stop there. If not for the coupon, I doubt I ever would have. We started with soup. I had minestrone, my husband ordered the soup of the day- artichoke cream. My minestrone was a little bland and watery, but the artichoke was very nice. For our main course, I ordered veal marsala, my husband chose the gamberoni all diavola (large shrimp in a tomato chili sauce). Both were served with a fusilli pasta with a tomato meat sauce. The vegetable was a nicely sauteed thin sliced zucchini. Sounds great huh? Well it was delicious, but the problem was the portions. I would guess that on each plate there was at most 3 ounces of pasta, two ounces of zucchini and my veal might have weighed 2 1/2 ounces- the stingy size of the portions became all the more apparent when these little piles of food was sitting in the middle of a large platter. My husband did get 8 very nice, large prawns, and prawns are not much cheaper than veal- so there is really no explanation for the child size portion of veal. But damn..it was so good. We rarely order desert, but we were still a bit hungry so we got a panna cotta to share-and it was just to die for. Oh wow..the mango sauce was so yummy that if we had been home we probably would have licked the plate. Oh yeah..and if you want wine- they tell you to walk next door to Scolari's and buy a bottle and they will pour it for you for free- they don't have a liquor license yet. If they work out the kinks, get their liquor license, serve larger portions or buy smaller plates & if the owner could warm up a bit to his guests, then this place could be a winner- the flavor of the food, and the care with which it is prepared is better than 90% of the other Italian Restaurants in Reno.

Their specialty martinis are fun as well, definitely get the one made with honey liqueur. The only downer about the place is that our stomachs aren't big enough to share every item on the menu when we go! I'd definitely recommend Honey if you're celebrating a special occasion -- when we made reservations for our anniversary dinner last month, they seated us in one of the curtained booths so we'd have some privacy, and gave us 2 glasses of champagne on the house. To begin with, she came over and asked, "Can I help you?" as if she wasn't sure what we were doing here. Her presence just seemed odd the entire time we tolerated the place. Why was this woman even working in what looked like a swank bar/restaurant? We all agreed her name must've been Flo or Bea or Mildred and that we'd much prefer being served by her if we were hungover and looking to order a $4.99 breakfast platter. I ordered a pitcher of sangria because the special ran them at $11. What a bargain, right? Wrong. First, Flo brought me a glass of sangria and when I corrected her that I'd ordered a pitcher, she looked at me like I was lying. Well then she brought me my pitcher. Let me clarify actually. She brought me a pitcher full of lemon and lime slices, with some "sangria" drizzled over them. As my friend said "hey I think they got some sangria in your lemons!" One sip. GAG. This was NOT sangria. This tasted like lime rind. I don't know what they put in it, or what they neglected to put in it, but I couldn't bare another sip. At this point my two other girlfriends showed up and ordered their drinks. I promptly told Flo that I was sorry but I disliked the sangria, that it was very bitter. She gave me a glare, and asked "so...you don't want it?" Why yes, Flo, that's precisely what I'm trying to tell you. please send this sludge back down the garbage disposal you scooped it out of. I was also very peeved that after my request to send the sangria back, she didn't bother to ask if I'd like a different drink instead. Not that it mattered, because she disappeared for quite some time, not having brought my friends their drinks yet, and we decided to leave and go somewhere else. My friend went to hunt down Flo to cancel their drinks and get the check. The only redeeming factor here was thank god, she did not charge me for the sangria i barely took a sip from. Moral of the story: this is a hotel restaurant and bar. The wait staff was probably employed here through a job-placement agency, and despite their efforts at making this look like a West Elm showroom, it is essentially an upscale IHOP.
label: NEG

text: While National Mechanics has an awesome concept and location, it is pretty disappointing. Beyond being completely overrun by hipsters, it generally is an awkward place to be. The drinks are overpriced and poorly made --- that is if you can make your way to the bar and successfully deal with one of the surly bartenders or if you can wrangle one of the rarely seen waitresses that I honestly think might just walk around with an empty train holding up your index finger to everyone they walk by as if you are on their way somewhere important, but never return. It took an additional 25 minutes. Hmmm. 5 rolls...yellowtail, spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, spicy yellowtail, and firecracker. All were decent, nothing great. The spicy sauce is not mixed; mayo with a drop of hot sauce on top...interesting. The seaweed was not of top quality. The fish all tasted fine. Tuna was very fatty. The shrimp tempura roll was the only one with real problems. It was overly fried and extremely crunchy, making it hard to eat. The sushi chef appears to be inexperienced, as some of the rolls were not cut properly and the ones that had seaweed on the outside, as opposed to rice, were falling apart. All in all, not a bad place if you have a craving for sushi but don't want to spend much money. Just don't expect the greatest...of course, the prices reflect that.

Not to mention, they don't service our area only three miles away! So I called and placed the order for pick-up. I got Chicken Korma ("as mild as you can", I said!) with rice and naan. Someone else got Chicken Korma as well, medium, with rice and naan. When I walked in, I loved it! Definitely not the make-your-mouth-salivate naan I'm used to. From now on, we've decided we're going to take the time to drive to Cilantro near USF. It's buffet style so portions are never an issue and the food is *amazing*.

text: Last night Kim P, the boys and I had front row seats to see Flight of the Concords at The Tower. Did you hear that, Philly? We were so close that I could see every drop of sweat glistening on Jemaine's forehead and hear every beat of Bret's warm, warm heart. In fact, I have concocted a fantasy about last night that goes a little something like this: Jemaine is tuning his guitar. He drops his pick, which lands about 3 feet directly ahead of me on stage. The bespectacled one reaches down to retrieve it and our eyes lock. He is hypnotized by my purple hair and mysterious colorful arms. "Is it a patterned shirt?" he thinks to himself. "Or is she one of those Philly hipsters I've been hearing so much about?" We exchange shy glances (my dude, who is sitting inches away from me, is fine with this because if Rosario Dawson ever swings into town, he's got my permission to go for it) and Jemaine continues with the show. He sings "Business Time," which is everyone's favorite, but we both know he's singing it to me. But I play coy. During "Albi" I laugh politely, and I rock out accordingly to "Hiphopopotumus," but I'm no easy target. Jemaine is going to have to work a lot harder to woo me with his disheveled hair and thrift store clothes...perhaps with something involving scented massage oils and a snugglefest featuring seasons one through three of The L Word... Uhhh, anyway, Tower Theater, good. Old and pretty. Decent beer and you can take it inside with you. Bathrooms are kinda creepy. Crappy neighborhood and expensive parking garage, but whateves. This review, apparently, is less about that jazz and all about the love that was never meant to be between a lady and a Kiwi who is now touring the world, breaking hearts at a medium-capacity theater near you.

text: I'm relatively new to the Indian food scene. And there isn't much of one in St. Louis. But this place is a gem. The Positives are all over the place. I've never had bad service, always polite and very attentive. The food here is really good. I've become something of a frequent visitor and I can always bet on a couple dishes because I can't imagine a meal from House of India without Samosas and Nan. I also think the Chana Palak is one of the best dishes on the menu. Simple Chick Peas with sauteed spinach it's light and delicious. As for everything else, I've yet to have anything that I didn't like. The curry (both Lamb and Chicken) is good, and I'm a big fan of the Vegetable Korma. I will say that the Tandoori Chicken came out a little dry the time I ordered it, and there are far too many excellent dishes on the menu for me to continue to order something that had so-so flavor to begin with. If there's a negative it's the location. Located right off 170 on Delmar in a strip mall. It's accessible yes, but not near much of anything else, so it's a bit of a destination type of place which I'm just not a fan of. I love the option to walk around afterwards. They also do takeout, which is always quick and easy. I don't want to wax on, just want to give this place some good pub. If you're looking for good Indian, this is the spot.

text: Big deep breath, because describing Morimoto is like writing a 5 paragraph essay. That you want to eat. So a couple of co-workers and I tried Morimoto while in town on a business trip. First off, reservations were very easy and friendly to get, walked in at 7:30pm on a Wednesday night to a pretty packed house but we were seated promptly. You immediately notice the amazing feel and decor of the place. It can best described as a fashion forward modern diner. There are sort of these plastic booths all over the middle and sides of the restaurant covered in plush cushions, and there is different colored mood lighting emanating from underneath all the plasticy booths. Basically, its like Virgin America in a restaurant. We started off with both the rock shrimp tempura and the special of the night - white truffle gyoza in a light broth/sauce. The rock shrimp tempura was delightfully spiced and fried perfectly, melting in your mouth and served with some leaf scoops to complete the experience. Basically its like the best popcorn shrimp / orange spicy chicken combination you'll taste in a while. The gyoza was off the charts. The white truffle oil, light cabbage, and just cloud-like gyoza really just had us licking the plate it was served on. Oh yeah, btw it was served with seared baby scallops. Simply delicious, and basically as addicting as buttery popcorn. The three of us ordered the ishi yaki buri bop, the miso black cod, and the chilean sea bass. The ishi yaki buri bop is basically a bimbimbap (if you are familiar with Korean food). Its a rice with picked cucumbers and vegetables, served in a blazing hot stone bowl with raw kobe slices that you can sear to your liking on the hot stone bowl. Also, as you eat it, the rice begins to crisp and creates a buttery crispy texture that is to die for. Best part? When its served, the dude slices and sears the meat a bit for you, then mixes a cracked egg and the rice together for you, to serve you a perfect dish. The chilean sea bass was delightful, in a black bean sauce that is very soy glaze like combined with a light ginger taste. Its basically like eating air, or eating fish that has the delightful lightness of tofu. The miso cod was the highlight. It was the EXACT opposite of what I was was thinking. It was served with a honey glaze and sugar soaked black beans, with some ginger on the side. Basically the cod, being cooked perfect and with soft soft skin, is served on top of a sweet sweet sauce that at first seems overwhelming but you can't stop eating. Its pretty much heaven. In fact, everyone at my table kept trying to trade me their bites for mine. Ridiculously good. Couple glasses of wine and our dishes ran us about $210 before tip for 3 people. Its pricey, but when you break it down its about $10/glass of wine, $15/appetizer, and $25-$45 for an entree. Really not that bad in terms of great food, ultimate decor, and awesome service combined with the famous asian flair of Iron Chef Morimoto. When your in Philly, I'd say Morimoto's is a must.

text: Morimoto is everything a restaurant should be: you get a unique food experience with great service in a trendy setting that feels posh but still accessible. I came here last night with several co-workers on a business trip, which was nice because I got to sample a large swath of the menu. We ordered 4-5 appetizers, the highlights of which were an excellent Octopus Carpaccio and the 10-hour Pork Kakuni, the latter so tender it literally melted in your mouth. The tuna pizza was pretty good too; and I also had a piece of fatty tuna sashimi, tiny but yummy. My main dish, the "Tai Shioyaki", was the coup de grace. It was a large white fish called sea bream, which had light and flaky flesh in a gently crispy skin. The dish came with the chef's instructions to sprinkle smoked sea salt over it, then cover in hot white butter sauce, and lastly, dip in spicy ponzu (a tart, citrus sauce). The result was divine--the best fish dish I've ever had. There wasn't a single thing I tried that was not at least very good. I sampled the popular "duck duck duck" entree featured a terrific roast duck that was moist and crispy. My dessert of chocolate pot de creme was a good finish. If I had a complaint at all, the only one would be that Morimoto's cocktails really ought to be larger or stronger given the price. But the drinks were still good; the cilantro gimlet was especially popular among a few of my colleagues. Dinner came to a little over $100 per person but felt well worth it. This was among my favorite restaurant meals ever. If you're in Philly, check out Morimoto!

Last comment is on the interesting sounding, but strange, appetizer - something called waffle skins. text: OK, if they cleaned up the place, acted like they really cared, and were a little more timely with the food, the restaurant might warrant 3 stars. We went for brunch, and were seated at one end of a pool hall in a rather dingy room. We were told the main dining room wasn't set up yet because of a big party the night before. But, even still, they could have at least had tablecloths on the table. The sad thing is the brunch menu is pretty decent, and the food a slice above average. I had a great variation on the currently popular stuffed french toast - filled with marscapone cheese, a peanut butter spread, and fresh banana. The combination really worked, and - had I not waited for 45 minutes and been served stale coffee with it (again, I assume, from the party the night before!) - I probably would have been more than satisfied. Bottom line: get your act together, or give up trying.

text: About the tenth time I dine at Picasso's. I still like it. We made reservations for six on a busy night and they honored them on the minute. Overall: Great service. My water glass and iced tea never went below 2/3 full. Efficient and courteous. Excellently prepared food. Two of us had the Sea Bass and it was delicately prepared, with a hint of a crust. Yummm.... The appetizers were also divine, a tapas plate designed for six people. On the "Oh well..." list: Over the past two years it seems to be transitioning to more of an Italian menu selection... I know my Spanish food and that's why I started going to Picasso. Both countries are Mediterranean, but there's significant differences between the two. Still, a wonderful experience with great people, excellent service and genuinely good food.
label: POS

text: Having lived in the area for almost 11 years, after close to a million (or more) visits to Willow Grove Mall, I can officially say I know EVERY inch of this place. Y'know, you can only go to the mall so many times (especially if you're a student on a budget like me), but this is one of the bigger malls in the area if you can't make the trek out to King of Prussia. Macy's has a great selection of makeup counters: Clinique, MAC, and Benefit are my personal favorites; though I really miss the Bourjois counter! It's been gone for years now but I have fond memories of it. In the way of dining, the food court has quite a variety of selections, there's a Starbucks on the ground floor for all you coffee addicts as well as a TGI Friday's and Ruby Tuesday's. I personally prefer the shopping scene of the city to the mall scene of the suburbs, but when I need my mall fix while at home, Willow Grove hits the spot.
label: POS

text: I'm here, right now, in the middle of devouring one of the best homemade chocolate chips cookies I've ever had! Its really hard to multitask between stuffing my face and writing this review but this place is totally worth it. The atmosphere is your typical cozy little coffee shop with mismatched furniture. I'm sitting in the back room on a glorious gold velvet antique sofa surrounded by clothing and nick knacks up for sale. Its nice and quiet so its a decent place to get work done or read. Besides the cookies the food here is really great! They have a nice attention to detail and presentation. Their wraps come out served like sushi rolls. I ordered fresh tea and was very excited to see the beautiful Asian tea cup and tea pot that it was served in. The staff is friendly too! Please come check it out

text: Belgian food AND Belgian beer? And an Ipod full of hipster standards? Count me in. There are two ways to experience Monk's - as a bar and as a restaurant. It basically excels at both for the same reasons. The atmosphere is perfect; it feels small but not too cramped and the people are cool but not too cool. They do have the often mentioned Beer Bible, which features a bazillion bottled beers that I've never heard of, and their taps are all Belgian as well. Chimay triple on tap...need I say more? I'd say the beer makes the wait for dinner on a weekend night tolerable. You can always just go and put your name in and then go wander off somewhere else if you want. The food is also great. I'm not a huge fan of mussels but the spicy mussels at Monks were good enough that even I wanted to have a few. I had a burger, of which they have many varieties with all manner of toppings, and it was cooked just about right. The fries (frites? whatever.) are also a must have. The mussels actually come with a few but if you're a big fan you should spring for the side. They serve them with this spicy mayonnaise thing and the fries themselves are seasoned with salt and pepper and possibly a few other things. The food and beer combination there is truly unique, and I know I'm going to be craving it again sooner than I think.

text: Here's the thing....I have been a LUSH lover for a few years now and I am starting to see the light. I have no problem with their prices. I am a firm believer in paying for better ingredients and also to ensure those who make the products get a living wage. I also enjoy everything being handmade and the Charity Pot lotion is seriously awesome. The Philly store also has some very nice people working there. However, they also have some VERY pushy people there. I don't like to be bothered when I am shopping. If I want to know something I will ask. I can't deal with being barraged by workers and I loathe when products are pushed onto me. The thing that did it for me is that I used their deodorant and got a SEVERE rash from it. I had to pay to go to the dermatologist to get medicine and everything. I contacted LUSH about this several times and got ZERO response. That is unbelievable to me. I have spent literally thousands here in the past and I found their ignoring my problem unthinkable. LUSH left me with no desire to give them my money any longer. I have since switched to Duross & Langel. Their deodorant is fabulous and their customer service is even better. Screw you LUSH. Now I just have to figure out how to rid myself of my LUSH stash to make room for products from companies that actually care about their customers. EDIT: Can I follow up to say that I was in the store picking up a bath bomb because my girlfriend really likes one of them. The one pushy sales girl bombarded me and told me that they make that same scent (of the bath bomb) in a massage bar, but it was discontinued and now it's available in a gift set! I could buy that today too and get a chance to go to Vegas! It's right over there and also comes with this this and this. She was going on and on about other products and I'm like dude I am buying one bath bomb. I'm not going to be pressured into buying a $70 gift I don't even want. I put the bomb down and left. I had to drop them down to one star. Esp since I have been using Ocean Salt religiously for a year and the woman doing my facial at Rescue said I need to use a new scrub asap because the one I have been using isn't working. Great. Thanks a heap Lush. I'm officially done using their products.
label: NEG

text: St. Louis does a lot of things right. Like donuts! Pizza, however, is not one of them. This stuff is a disgusting abomination that I'm sure is served on Hell's Buffet. "Honey, look, they have PIZZA! This won't be so bad after all!" "Oh, know...what's that? Oh my goodness, it's provel!" "Ah, St. Louis style pizza! My God, why have thou forsaken me!" There's a reason provel cheese and St. Louis style pizza do not exist outside of the metro area, and that is because both are awful Frankensteinian creations. Maybe St. Louis just decided it needed its own type of pizza and the locals feel like they're betraying the motherland by speaking truthfully, but the stuff is just not good. I'm not even sure I can call it pizza.

text: My sister made a reservation for two rooms on the night before our race in the Tampa- St Pete Women's 5k and Half Marathon for Lukemua and Lymphoma via hotels.com. We gals already paid over $600 and were charged via hotels.com; we had our confirmation from the hotels.com that the hotel confirmed our reservation and purchase. The most aggravating part was that the Front Desk was obnoxious. Though the Front Desk gal made a [feeble] attempt to get us a room at a nearby mediocre hotel, which incidentally, would require us to use roll-away beds, she inferred that you "get what you get" when you use a discounted dealer. Funny! She was pointing her snooty retail nose down at a vendor that the Renaissance Vinoy Resort club engages with! If they can't honor or stand by their affiliates, then they have no business collaborating with them. Poor judgment on employing this employee, since she is a front line soldier when dealing with the most important people in the lobby: the guests. To be honest, I was relieved that our reservations fell through - it was way too Miami - South Beach with blaring music in the lobby. Too wannabe cool, wannabe trendy. Sometimes, hotels need to cater to the 35 year olds who have the money, not the 20 somethings who can drink their beer.

text: Great patio and fast service but too expensive for the quality and selection of mediocre Mexican. Come for the patio, stay for a margarita but eat elsewhere. Carlitos is not a place for dinner as the the price is high for the lack of quality in the food. For snackatizers, we've shared nachos, quesadillas, taquitos and halibut ceviche with nothing too exciting. For a Santa Barbara eatery, I'm more than disappointing. At a birthday dinner the other night where they messed up the outside reservations and forced in the back, I tried the tacos al carbon that was ok but again, I've had better. I'm sure we'll be back for some event and I'd like to try the pozole but trust me, it will not be my idea to eat here. You can do better than Carlitos in a city with such rich, Spanish culture.
