text: I had been searching all over town for a traditional pasta carbonara and was pleased to find that Porta Via had it on their menu. I read that they make their pasta and sauces fresh daily, which was also a plus. I decided to order to-go and was audibly excited on the phone. Whoever took my order, on the other hand, was not. He was very short with me and pretty much suggested that my to-go order was really bumming him out. I assumed they were busy, so I wasn't affected. However, when I went to pick up my meal, there were two girls at the bar who were clearly more interested in their conversation about someone's personal life than my order. They yapped on and on to each other until one of them finally came over only to tell me my total, snatch my credit card out of my hand, and slam it back down on the counter in front of me. She then sloppily packed the to-go box into a bag and slung it my way. She never once made eye contact or said anything like "thank you". The pasta was awesome. Little heavy on the pepper, but really good. I've ordered it time and time again, though still I've received the kind of service one would get in prison. So that's why I've given this establishment only two stars. Customer service is very important. Italian food is all about enjoyment, and I didn't get a sense of that from Porta Via's pre-menstrual staff. I'd rather stay home and make my own carbonara sauce.

text: If you've never booked a hotel on Hotwire before it's somewhat of a gamble every time. Rarely are you going to get an absolute craphole, but you may not also get the cream of the crop either. Then you get in this dinky elevator that sort of looks like the one in the haunted house at Disneyland. Then the door opens and you are back in the 80s. What the hell? Where is my modern art, my Herman Miller furniture, my flat screen TV? Why didn't Hotwire put me at a Hyatt? Damnit. Beds are relatively decent here, TV is ANCIENT, internet is NOT FREE, no mini fridge, ice and soda machine not on the same floor, no water pressure, tub barely drains, and the door opens way too close to the toilet in the bathroom. Seriously, this bathroom is small. We call down to find out how late the bar is open and all the guy who answered could tell us was that it was open now, and it'd be open until whenever. Oh great, whenever... now that's a time I can plan on.

text: Who doesn't love sweets? Walking into Sucre is a delightful experience for anyone with a sweet tooth. The decor is gorgeous and the walls are lined with color. The gelato, sexy deserts, chocolates, and colorful macaroons really catch your eye. Looks, however, are sometimes deceiving. The desserts, while eye-catching, sparkly, and breathtakingly beautiful, their quality of flavor disappoints. I've had a broad array of quite many desserts: an eclair, flour-less chocolate cake, chocolate and raspberry delight, peanut butter chocolate cupcake, red velvet cake, and gelato. Certainly not everything they had to offer. I was impressed by very few of their products outside of aesthetics. The eclair was certainly not in the top 5 or even 10 that I have had. In fact, if not for its appearance, one can get 30 mini frozen eclairs from the frozen section of Wal-Mart that taste better than this one for the same price. The peanut butter chocolate cupcake looks amazing, but in truth the cake was dry and the peanut icing was nothing special. I wish I could report the cupcake was amazing, but unfortunately, I was so disappointed that I threw it away after a couple of bites despite the $4 I spent. The red velvet cake was far below par. Once again, beautiful, the dessert's desirable palatability was lacking. The cake was incredibly spongy and slightly dry. The cake however was the best part. The icing had apparent lab-made flavors that drew away from the normally delightful cream cheese icing red velvet cake generally has. For my favorite cake, I was incredibly disappointed. I wish I would have put on a shelf and admired it rather than taken even one bite. The same can be said of the cookies n' cream gelato a friend had tried. Every pallet in the group could detect the artificial flavor within the usually glorious italian dessert. Not everything was as lacking. Their adorable flour-less chocolate cake was quite delightful, both in aesthetics and taste. It must be noted, though, that unless you like high cocoa chocolates, you will probably not care for this dessert. It is low in sugar showing off the great flavors of cocoa has to offer. The chocolate and raspberry delight was simply delightful. A great thin slice of chocolate cake was hidden within the sparkly pink hemisphere covered in chocolate ganache. Hidden over the cake and under the ganache was a wonderful raspberry surprise made likely with a strong compote mixed with a chocolate mouse. Unfortunately, I don't think they currently have this on their menu, but if it returns, it is a definite win if you are there. You certainly pay an arm and a leg for presentation. Each of their gorgeous mini-sized, stunning desserts is presented on a rectangular white plate with a simple drizzle of chocolate. If you want to impress a date, this surely will, but know to pick wisely because many things do not meet expectations and know you will pay $6-$10 for one small, but rich treat.

text: it was 7:30pm Saturday night and we were at Raw. We didn't have reservation and the next available table for 4 was at 9:30pm. Dejected and disappointed, we put our name down and walked out. plenty of options in the area. And we walked right into Bindi - yeah we're in the mood for Indian! And its spanking new (its their first month) bet they'd try hard to impress. Nothing interesting about the setting. The design and decorations are kept minimal, somewhat boring for me. They have several booths,but all taken, a long community-style table smacked in the middle and regular tables with little space between them. We started off with these super spicy papadom. the sweet clear dip that came with it toned the spiciness down a notch. the papadom was by far the nearest we got to tastebud explosion that night. everything else that came subsequently were very mild (for Indian food),much to my disappointment. the Mussels Bindi Ghozzo came in a stone bowl and a decent portion,good for sharing. Again, it could've been spicier. And for the entrees. i was deciding between fish or shrimp and settled for the Shrimp and Vegetable Sambar. how I regretted. the shrimps were mushy! EEEeeewwww! Fresh shrimps when cooked should be firm and even a little chewy, while mushy shrimps is just a sign of unfreshness. taste-wise, it was OK, too mild albeit interesting just because it was unlike other Indian dishes i've had. however, I was appalled with the quality of my shrimps. maybe if they were a little less stingy with their shrimps (only about 5 in the dish), they'd use up their old shrimp supply faster so they could go get some fresh ones. The Salmon Curry was a lot better. They gave quite a bit of salmon and the curry was creamy and much tastier. The Cod with toasted coconut on raisin rice pilaf was good and pretty interesting too. Most of the dishes come with Lime Rice although we couldn't taste any traces of lime. They have 3 types of rotis - pratha, chapati and lentil bread. We had the potato dill stuffed paratha and were disappointed. Very bland and completely unremarkable. We agreed that the food here is interesting and quite far from the exciting, spicy, bold tasting Indian food that we're used to. After finishing our drinks and were ready to go, we asked for the check and were told: "Sorry, cash only." CASH ONLY???? what, are we in Chinatown? Well....the prices sure don't say so. when i've to pay $50 for my dinner, i sure expect them to offer some Visa/Mastercard payment option. Who carries that much cash anymore? So here you go Bindi, 2 stars for the BAD shrimps, the inability to pay by credit card, and the mild food.

text: I was pleasantly surprised to see the beautiful building of Toscana 52 take the place of the outdated Bob Evans Restaurant. If one had to judge restaurant's cuisine by its facade, I thought for certain that Toscana would be among my favorite restaurants. That was not the case....like life, beauty is only skin deep, folks. I eagerly waited two months from its opening to try Toscana, and we went as a party of four including 2 kids, age 15 and 10. We waited about 25 minutes for a table which was surprising considering it was Friday evening around 7:30pm. We waited 10 minutes for the waiter and assumed that they were short staffed. When asked about a children's menu, we were told that there was none but the kitchen could cook "anything we wanted". When the waiter asked the kitchen for specifics, that amounted to a choice of either chicken fingers or 3 different kinds of pasta. We started with drinks and an appetizer. My son ordered chocolate milk which we were surprised they had, given they obviously do not cater to children. The child's chocolate milk arrived in a glass wine goblet (no kidding!) at a cost of $3.99. Definitely nothing child-friendly about that! We ordered the fried calamari appetizer which looked scrumptuous when placed in front of us. However, each piece of calamari tasted like it was fried in oil which wasn't hot enough and as a result we had to offset the oily taste with the driest Italian bread we've ever tasted. The bread came 10 minutes after the appetizer (after we asked about it twice) and there were three little containers of herb butter. At first, we thought that each butter was a different variety but it was all the same (what the??). We ate it to offset the very greasy calamari appetizer which we didn't entirely finish. Perhaps the cheesecake appetizer would have been delicious, as many have raved about it, including our waiter who seemed a little miffed that we didn't order it after he announced it so grandly, with an "everyone loves it" comment. Before our entrees arrived, there was a changing of the flatware which was an obvious attempt to mimic an upscale restaurant but it came across as disingenuous and phoney. Our entrees: chicken marsala, seafood linguini, fettucinini alfredo with shrimp (child's portion which cost $10.50), and pasta with butter for my 10 yr old son. We were shocked when the child's buttered pasta entree arrived, as the amount of pasta only filled about half of a bread dish, so miniscule was the portion ($4.50) that a 2-year old wouldn't have been full, much less a 10 year old. The rest of us shared our entrees with him. The entrees were at best mediocre but overall quite bland. Italian food is not supposed to taste so bland! We never use salt during our meals but this meal definitely necessitated it for all our dishes. The flavor of my chicken marsale was "almost" there if it didn't taste diluted and bland. Same for the seafood linguini and alfredo dish - very bland and mediocre at best. Perhaps other items on the menu didn't suffer from blandness but we had the misfortune to select those dishes that were. I was so disappointed since I had salivated for two months to taste what I was certain to be superb cuisine. That was not the case, much to my chagrin. The house wine cost $6 per glass. No problem, except that the glass is either too large or the portion of wine served is so small that it leaves one feeling ripped off. Each glass was only filled 1/3 full at most when served. The clearing of dishes after our meal was non-existent after the waiter took away one of our dishes while asking if anyone wanted dessert. When no one wanted dessert, no further dishes were cleared and a one-glass water refill took several reminders. What was up with that?!? We asked for the bill and had to wait about 15 minutes for it. Hold me captive but at least take away my damn dishes! The waiter was not friendly at all but we figured he was probably tired and very busy so we didn't think much of it. However, when it came time for him to give us the bill, he suddenly decided to become momentarily friendly and personable. Did he suddenly wake up? Or perhaps he remembered that a friendly personality garnered higher tips? That was a little annoying. Also, I found the prices to be on the high side which I wouldn't mind paying if the food was remotely worth it, but it was not. In the past when a new restaurant doesn't meet my expectations, I have no problem giving it a second chance. I won't be doing that at Toscana - it isn't worth my time or money. From the number of bad reviews that I've read about this place, that speaks for itself. I have read the other reviews and have to wonder if the good reviews are written by people associated with the restaurant. If you read the bad reviews, they all seem to mirror the same thing - AWFUL, BLAND FOOD and CRAPPY SERVICE.
label: NEG

text: I have had this sweet little art supply store across the street for some time, but sadly haven't gotten enough time (or purpose, perhaps) to bring more business here. Nestled comfortably beneath West Elm and Lucky Strike, the building's sprawling basement becomes a veritable oasis of creativity. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: As you walk down the stairway into the store space, a slight bird's-eye view allows you to see the shelves packed with every kind of paint, ink, pencil, cray pas, canvas, paper, rule, and book. It's very well-lit, and roomy, so you know you'll have a pleasant perusing experience. THE SELECTION: Comprehensive, to say the least. There's an entire section for framing and poster-board along the east wall, everything from school-level art supplies to stuff for the more serious fine artist. While the selection is pretty wide, there have been a few times that even Blick couldn't meet my need, so don't count on it for those stretch requests that you couldn't find anywhere else. THE PRICING: It's as spendy as anywhere else, you go there, probably spend more than you would have hoped, but there's no denying you'll be satisfied with what you get. I'm not sure if we have Adobe to blame for the rise in art prices, but I remember being able to use my allowance on a big box of crayons, some stencils and a sketchbook, with a little left to spare on some Bubble Yum...if ya know what I mean. THE SERVICE: Good luck getting some service, they're always dealin with someone else whenever I'm there, I haven't been fortunate enough to get anyone's time whenever I've needed something. The employees are likely mostly students at the nearby Art Institute, they know their stuff, but the underlying attitude that I see at most art stores-- bored, underpaid, undermotivated art students just trying to make some drinking money. Not knockin the service really, but it's a funny truth you might now notice when you go. THE BOTTOM LINE: The quality and organization of their supplies are both top-notch, not to mention the place is conveniently located, which is what keeps me coming back, it's certainly not the pricing, however. Recommended, in agreement with most other reviewers, over Utrecht and Pearl.
label: POS

text: "'Refined Neighborhood Bistro' Needs Refining" Adsum may be hot, but 1st visit left me cold. Poutine: The potatoes were uneven temp, in the way that microwaved food can sometimes be. Made the cheese not melt well and the whole dish just weird in a leftovers kind of way. Whole fish: Ill-conceived dish and a deep disappointment. "Green sauce" was an unexpected and not entirely welcome avocado-based affair: a sticky, thin guacamole-ish deal, and not a nice complement. Stewed side tomatoes seemed thrown on the plate as an afterthought, which cannot be possible, as clearly the chef here gave a lot of thought to his menu. They did not retain heat and tasted like they were spooned from a room-temp can. Accompanying starch: a single tablespoon worth of popped rice. And not one grain more. Hence protein and starch were not in balance. It was nice to see something relatively healthy on an otherwise cholesterol-a-rama menu, but God as my witness, I will never order this again. Coffee: Tasted burnt. Diner quality. I wanted something chocolate for dessert, but they don't offer chocolate. For a bistro, this is criminal. Bread pudding: I was warned: 'watch out, this pan is extremely hot.' And it was. Yet the entire center of my $9 dessert was room temp. Its primary flavor was sugar and there was no contrasting secondary flavor -- unless you count the bananas on top, which just tasted like more sugar. Room temp + sugar X 1000 - delicious = I pushed it away. At this point I was ready for my check (not to mention dinner do-overs.) Look. Adsum has great potential. But on my virgin voyage tonight, the boat did not leave shore. I spoke about most of these things with the waitstaff, who were very receptive to feedback. (It felt *very* awkward giving it, but I thought, better to speak than stew.) As they were very receptive, offered to fix things every step of the way, and even removed items from the bill - i.e., they went above and beyond ... I really debated whether I should post this review, or wait and go a few more times. I'll definitely return, as others report great experiences here, and I very much want the restaurant to do well. (It's completely packed at all times, so I don't think they'll have any problems.) But the point of Yelp is to share your experience: good, bad and ugly. And tonight it was bad and ugly.

Our 3rd friend said no, we thought we'd pop by for brunch. That's when the host made a sucking noise through his teeth and said, "I don't know if I can fit you in..." At this point 2 of us wanted to leave pretentious-ville and head someplace else. Our 3rd decided we should stay and be seated. The decor was nice and the water with an orange slice was pleasant. Once we got the menu though, the food was pricey and had some strange combinations. Not ones to shy away from a new venue, we each decided on a variant of the eggs benedict. In the end, I didn't like the taste of the meat and the hollandaise sauce had a very odd off-putting texture and strange aftertaste. I walked away from breakfast disappointed and with most of my meal still on the plate. Service wise, we were virtually ignored except for the taking of our order and the serving. text: We were very excited to have Pat's open up near us. We watched the construction with interest, eager to try a new spot. So shortly after they opened, we stopped in, ordering two menu standards: pizza with pepperoni, and a basic cheesesteak with Cheez Whiz and onions. First, the good: Decor is quite nice. Very sleek and way more sophisticated than you'd expect for a pizza/pasta place. The staff was friendly, albeit a little uncertain, but I believe they'll gain their confidence after being open awhile. The so-so: The pizza was decent. Not amazing, not bad. The sauce was a little on the sweet side, and could've stood to have a little salt added. Good crust, though. The bad: THE SMELL. When you walk into an Italian restaurant or pizzeria, you should smell garlic. You should smell crust baking. You should smell PIZZA. What you shouldn't smell is *potpourri*. Seriously, it smelled like a home decorating store in there -- not a single scent of anything edible. I cannot emphasize enough how off-putting this was. THE MUSIC. The music was some bland ambient stuff that you'd expect to hear in a spa. It's not like I expect to hear "Funiculi Funicula" in a pizza place, but neither do I expect to hear music that's better suited to some chic club. Put simply, the overhead was jarringly out of place. THE CHEESESTEAK. The cheesesteak was an abomination, especially for an establishment that's less than an hour's drive away from the birthplace of the cheesesteak. A "whiz wit" mean glopping some lukewarm, sub-par faux whiz on top of the meat, rather than on the inside of the bun. The meat was unforgivably bland. Putting salt on the sandwich meant it was salty and bland. Putting pepper flakes meant it was salty, hot, and yet *still bland.* I don't even understand how that's possible! But it was, and it was just terrible. I'm hoping that all of these negative points are just bugs that will be worked out as they settle in, but given the number of much better pizza and cheesesteak places around here, they'd better figure it out soon or they won't last long. For me, it will be a while before I could be persuaded to give Pat's another try.
label: NEG

text: After all the hype and all of Oprah's talk about the power of a good bra, I decided to give intimacy a go....I was at the mall late on a Friday night and popped in to see if they could help me out....or help me up rather. A little back story (or shall I say boob story)....I had a wonderful bra fitting experience at Bloomingdales last year where I ended up finding out that I was a lot bigger in size...and that size is not that easy to find...I also happened to be losing a lot of weight quickly and didn't want to invest in a good bra since I was shrinking...I ended up going to Cacique, Lane Bryant's lingerie brand for my over the shoulder bolder holders. They were ok in fit but great for the wallet. Eventually I ended up between two sizes and found myself in a muffin top sort of situation. At the same time, my weight plateaued, so I decided it was time to get a proper bra... Thus, I went to intimacy...they happened to be able to fit me in, but they do suggest making appointments prior. Just so you know, they do not really have bras in the front of the store, but they do have a lot of panties, pj's and other fluffy things. I met with my bra fitter in the back and while the dressing room was small, she quickly (and loudly) went into her spiel about their process and I soon began to feel like I was buying a car rather than buying a bra... She brought one bra in for me to try on after eying me up...and while it was a pretty color, it looked and felt like a 1960's version of a bra (torpedoes are not sexy)...this was also the cheapest bra I tried on, at $80. I asked for more samples and she brought in a handful, which she helped me try on. If you are not into being seen topless by a stranger, then this experience is not for you. I liked two of the bras she brought. One, a cute ivory and purple number that was $140 and one, a simple black lace that was $160. I opted for the cheaper one. Before you go judging me for dropping $140 on a bra, please know that most bras in my size are often made by Delta Burke (I wish I was joking) and cute is never an option... During my entire experience, they tried to up sell me..."here, try on this robe" and "this tank top is perfect for everyone"...every step of the way, they show you more and more products... Please note that they make you sign a part of your receipt that guarantees that you will not be able to get your money back. You can exchange products, but once you hand over your cash, there is NOTHING you can do to get it back. I liked the bra, so I went for it. On the second day of wearing my new bra, I began to feel a sharp pain digging into my chest plate. I looked down and in my cleavage was the metal wire sticking out. I was pissed because I just bought the Cadillac of bras and it was turning out to be more of a Pinto. I was also stuck at work and gave my cube mates the pleasure of continually watching me shove my hand down my shirt to push the metal back in. I went back to intimacy and talked to the manager. I was irked that their product was bogus. She claimed it was a dropped stitch. Whatever, I wanted my money back since I had no faith in any of their high end undergarment's. She apologized, but said there was nothing they could do about getting me my money back. I could buy a new bra (I didn't have the time for another 30 minute fitting) or they could mail me a new one of the same size and design. I opted for the latter option, but left feeling like I was had. They did nothing about my painful (literally) experience. This is supposed to be a high end boutique, but I have had better experiences elsewhere. Two weeks later, my bra came in the mail. It may sound crazy, but I feel like it fits different than the one I fell in love with at the store. I give up. I do believe in the power of a good bra and yes, when Oprah speaks about lady lumps, I take it as gospel, but I will never give intimacy my money again. If Nordstrom's is good enough for Oprah, it is good enough for me!
label: NEG

text: I do want to see good "Mom and Pop" stores stay in business. This, however, is not one of those. Poor customer service should be something you find in a large store with too many customers to keep track of, not a small store like this. The handle on a piece of my friend's luggage broke, so he asked the manufacturer where he could have it repaired under warranty. They told him to take the suitcase to this store for the repair, so that is what he did, and the store agreed to fix it under warranty. The suitcase was left at the store for repair. Fast-forward to a month later. He didn't hear anything from them, so I called to find out what was going on. A woman told me that she would check into it (she recognized the suitcase description but did not know what its repair status was) and get back to me. Needless to say, she did not get back to me. We called again to find out what was going on, and only then did they say that they would not fix it under warranty. My friend contacted the manufacturer, explaining that he needed the suitcase by a certain time and that he was disappointed with this store's service. The store said they did not receive the part they needed; the manufacturer said they did not receive a request for the part. It was finally worked out with the store to get the repair done. That would be enough for 3 stars, at this point, since it all seemed to be a simple misunderstanding between the store and manufacturer. Nearly two months from the original drop-off date, the store calls to say that the suitcase has been repaired. It wasn't convenient for me to go pick it up right then, so I went the next week to pick it up. I hoped for some sort of apology considering it had taken this long to repair the suitcase, but was instead told by the same woman I spoke to on the phone that the repairman (this with a snarky tone) was "upset" because he had to fix the suitcase, and that the store had put time and money into (finally, mind you) fixing the suit case and having it ready on time. On time? Really? On time would have been at least a month ago. No apology would have been better than this unwarranted commentary. We did not feel welcomed or appreciated by this business, and would not recommend them.
label: NEG

I will be ordering from there again! This is THE place to try for Chicago style although they do serve STL style too.

text: After my last visit here my opinion has changed. I took my formerly stray cat in for his annual exam/vaccinations. He tends to get a little primal when in uncomfortable situations. He growled and hissed at Dr. Balzer, but still allowed her to touch him, and at no point did he try to bite or strike her. She decided she was uncomfortable with him, and refused to examine him without anesthesia. I felt as a vet, that she should have been able to handle a nervous cat. So my poor cat ended up being, drugged. He urinated on himself and vomited for the rest of the day. I'll be finding a vet that is more comfortable handling the animals they care for.
label: NEG

text: $1 PBR on weekends as well as the cheap and very good pierogies and tater tots keep me coming back to this place. The service isn't always the friendliest (which knocks off the star for me), but that's the only downside. While the waitress might not smile, she never forgets an order and everything comes out in a timely manner. I bring my own friends, so the crowd is irrelevant to me. I guess we're those hipster/scene kids you all keep talking about. Cheers.
label: POS

text: Given the buzz, I was expecting more. I still think the best deep dish in St. Louis is Black Thorn near Tower Grove park. However, Black Thorn is so family unfriendly Pi is a better choice if you have kids or actually care about service. The prosciutto bites were good but not outstanding. We had two kinds of pizza - the topping on our create your own (bacon, sausage and mushrooms) were mostly hidden by the tomatoes on top. It was good, but a plain old cheese pizza would have been the same. We also had the "western addition" which is really good. It has spinach, mushrooms, ricotta, garlic, and some other stuff.
label: POS

text: This store feels like home. Or at least it feels like MY home. Time doesn't seem to pass normally here, and every time I walk out I'm always amazed to realize how long I was actually browsing vintage sci-fi paperbacks or leafing through that illustrated edition of Nostromo or just being constantly distracted by 'hey, what's that...' So much of my childhood was spent happily drifting through cluttered, old-timey used bookstores like this, but they're fast becoming an endangered species. I'm glad Philly has this one.
label: POS

text: It's difficult to love a pizza place where your first and last word must be "No." Papa John's Customer Service Rep: "Thank you for calling Papa John's ... would you like to try ....? Me: "No. Instead, I'd like to order ..." PJCSR: "Would you like to upgrade to .... for just $x more?" Me: "No, thank you." PJCSR: "Would you like to add breadsticks or ...?" Me: "No." My daughter liked the pizza, but I disliked the phone call. PJ advertising focuses attention on quality ingredients, and the pizza tastes okay. The ordering experience seemed topped with excessively aggressive promotion and perfunctory politeness, and the combination left a bad taste in my mouth.

text: The good: the onion rings. The horrible: the tenderloin. First off, that isn't a tenderloin but rather a fritter that came right out of the freezer. text: This review is for 360 lounge inside the casino... I was invited with a bunch of people to attend an event there last week. Inside looked amazing, the lit up floor, the huge bar, and the girl dancing in the back. However, with plenty of bartenders it was impossible to get a drink. We waited for 45 minutes until finally one of them locked eyes with us. The music is okay, usually a local DJ spinning pop songs. Occasionally you'll see the fancy drunks dropping their glasses on the floor, and dancing/picking up girls dressed to the extreme. They didn't seem to care towards the end of the night with what people were wearing. For such an elite lounge, they still let in mid-life single men who still wear the same pair of jeans from the 90s paired with Reebok's and a tee shirt from their vacation to Cape May. Overall, it was an okay fun. The crowd seemed very friendly and approachable to converse with.
label: NEG

text: Favorite bar/pub in Philly! You will feel transported to another time with the speakeasy decor and horse stables right outside. A little "off the beaten path" for most, but totally worth it! I am lucky enough to live near it (Prohibition makes life in the desolate "loft district" worth living). The sophisticated beer menu has something for everyone and is always changing, and the service is quite knowledgeable about the beer and food and generally very genuine and laid back. The second time we went, our server remembered us and recommended a beer to our taste! I was astounded. Beer-battered green beans are addictive and the mac-n-cheese is rich and decadent (unparalleled in my mac world). Veggie burger is original and flavorful. Beet salad is fresh and inspirational without being too sweet or citrus. They always have a new grilled cheese special, and when we have gotten them they've been authentic and delicious on hearty bread. Furthermore, the toilet is always clean. This place has spoiled me. PS- Cafe Lift also rocks.

text: Horrible, just plain horrible. The food twas disgusting - it was dry, old, and probably expired. The service is embarrassingly bad, and the place is disgustingly dirty. Horrible.

text: I know the Cracker Barrel is a chain store but I feel like the service here was so great that everyone should know about it. The group I was with was quite large and consisted of about 20 people. The staff here really went out of their way to make sure we all were taken care of in a timely manner. They assigned 5 waitpeople to us and were buzzing around like bees making sure we had what we needed. I've not received finer service at any other location. Food was great as well.
label: POS

text: Wow. I had *no* idea this gem of a place even existed until last week. i work in the building, so you can understand that it was more than just an oversight. I can't believe I missed out for that long. It's not just your average office building deli stop. It's the Mall of America of office building delis! Just when you thought you've seen everything, you turn around and there's gourmet cookies and chocolate covered pretzels. There's a pasta station. There's a million different choices for breakfast. Apparently, there's daily oatmeal and schools bring busloads of kids there to try them out. And then there's standard deli fare, of course. Worth the trip - you absolutely need to try it!

text: I am not much of a buffet kinda gal.....this place was okay for a buffet. Lots of variety...mainly Chinese dishes. They also had Mongolian BBQ where you make a plate of what you want and they grill it. It was okay, but I have had much better Mongolian BBQ. They also had a dessert/fruit bar. Probably not a place I would request to eat when I come into town, but I would go if the people I was visiting wanted to go.

text: Goose the Market is Yelp-categorized as "meat market", and yes it does have a cutesy "Have a Pignic!" sign outside. But it's so much more. I literally had the best sandwich of my life there today, a veggie version of the "Batali": soft chunks of fresh provolone, slivers of crisp tart pickles, tomatoes preserved in olive oil, and crunchy marinated onions on a fresh baguette. Heaven.
label: POS

text: Based on Caitlin C.'s yelp review, I went here to get some excellent sushi for a great price... and it was amazing. The restaurant is very intimate and the decor has a lot of spirit. It isn't trying to say trendy and it isn't traditional. It really speaks to the spirit of its own character without bowing to what a sushi place should or shouldn't be. So many choices for sushi! There were special platters, featured sushi dishes, and of course a la carte options as well. The presentation and quality of taste is amazing. There are also a great variety of appetizers to choose from as well. I had a hard time deciding what I was going to get, but in the end I decided on Tekka maki, a special sushi dish, and the Gyoza beef dumplings which I shard with my friend. As mentioned in the other review, this is a BYOB, so just bring what you want and they'll give you glasses as soon as they have found you a table. For dessert, they have three ice creams: Mocha, Green Tea, and Red Bean. I opted for the red bean and my friend chose the green tea. Red bean is definitely the way to go. The green tea was, well, it tasted like frozen unsweetened green tea. Its verisimilitude to the drink was uncanny. So, my recommendation is to stick with the other two more sweet ice creams if you are looking for a dessert treat. Get reservations as there often will not be an open table between prime dining hours. Tip: This place is right down the street from the Walnut Street Theater. I would definitely eat here before a show!
label: POS

text: Visited the restaurant again with a big group (10); my steak was done to my request (medium rare) but again...it just wasn't that tasty. I really expect more from this place. The sauteed mushrooms were better the last time; they were a little overdone and it looked like they shortchanged me on the mushrooms......the potato gratin was really tasty though. Had the Bread Pudding...and i have to say it was probably the least tasty bread pudding i've ever had. It was gummy and had a weird texture and bland taste All in all, an overpriced meal- $1160 for 10 people (including 3 bottles of wine). Disappointing. Maybe I'm just not a Charlie Palmer fan. His Dry Creek Kitchen is equally awful
label: NEG

text: This place, which has since moved to California St has got to be one of the worst businesses I've ever dealt with. Starting with the woman at the front desk who is completely clueless as to what is going on in her shop and ending with an inexperienced team of technicians; this place is a nightmare. When I took in my computer, the technician told me he would call me five days later at the latest. After the sixth day, I heard nothing so I called them. The man who answered the phone repeatedly forgot the name on my order; then told me he'd have the computer ready the following day, which it wasn't. The technician informed me that he had to completely reset my entire computer. I specifically told him to save the music, which he did. Only, he forgot to put it back on. He finally fixed the problem, but only after my fourth trip to the business was everything resolved. I've also had problems connecting to the internet ever since I took the computer back. Something, the technician told me he couldn't help with. Heed my advice: DO NOT TAKE YOUR COMPUTER HERE. YOU WILL REGRET IT!

text: Not bad. A homey little place for pizza and sandwiches. Beverly, the sassy waitress will bring you your order and a sunny smile. The Red veggie pie (no sauce) was delicious and at $8.50 for a small was perfect for 2 of us to share. Once time for lunch I had a tasty tuna melt. The dining room can get very crowded (and loud) at lunch time so come right at or before 12 noon to get a seat. Oh - and that home-made Lemon Crunch cake looked mighty tempting. Maybe next time...

text: We were looking for a good po'boy for lunch. I ordered the shrimp boy with a side of jambalaya. DH had the spicy sausage with a side of jambalaya, I enjoyed the shrimp po'boy, sauce was nice and spicy however I expected the shrimp to be fried instead of grilled. The bread they use is very crusty meaning you take a bite and you have crumbs on your clothes and the table. DH enjoyed the spicy sausage. The jambalaya has a lot to be desired, we found it very dry, undercooked and lacking of any real taste. Very disappointing. Guess we expected more for less than $11.00 a person.

text: Smile Cafe is perfect for a small gathering of friends who like to drink large quantities of wine. Service is friendly and quick. The portions are large and fresh. I shared the papaya salad with a friend (huge pile of greens and a couple shrimp for $6.95.) I was surprised and how big the salad were for around $5...my go-to thai place at Penn State offered a soy sauce-sized bowl for iceberg and peanut dressing for a whopping $3. The salad was great and my entree was even better. I had the fried tofu and vegetables in a spicy basil sauce, which was divine. I am so sick of places that serve pre-fried, pre-frozen hard lil nuggets of tofu. Smile Cafe provided tofu that was crisp on the outside, soft on the inside and better yet- plentiful on the plate. I had a few bites of my boyfriend's pad see lew, which was the perfect balance of chewiness, slipperiness and sweetness. I guess those are some strange words to describe a Thai noodle dish, but whatever. One complaint from the table-- the panang curry was a little watery. Why is it so hard to get a thick, creamy curry these days? Coconut milk ain't that expensive.
label: POS

text: I visited Martin's twice. The first time I was very disappointed. The food was mediocre at best. I tried the pulled pork tacos and the wife had the sandwich. I ordered the Brisket but since the staff here is standard fast food staff I wasn't upset since I like pork as well. Aside from having to remove large pieces of fat from both the sandwich and the tacos, waiting 10 minutes to get a side of BBQ sauce and only eating half our food the food was great. Oh snap, we only ate half of it because it wasn't. We gave them a second chance today. For $18 we a bread sandwich with a little bit of mediocre pork, another bread sandwich with some ok brisket, a side of potato salad that we actually liked, a side of cole slaw that was terrible and a couple drinks. We definitely won't be going back. I just can't understand the lines to this place. Even their "house made" fries are nasty.

text: YUM! SEAFOOD! We arrive into Philly a little late, so we came here for a late dinner. I don't remember exactly what we ordered, but I'm sure it involved oysters, calamari, clams, mussels.... all of it was very good! A delicious restaurant in Philadelphia!

I left it up to fate AND yelp reviews! Thanks Yelp! (see photo)

text: Yes, Crown Candy is open on Sundays. Get there before noon and you won't have to wait in line, either. Yes, this means I am encouraging yelpers to skip church AND eat an incredibly unhealthy meal. I am so going to hell for this review... Anyway, the line was non-existent so we were able to get a booth right away. Service was a tad slow this time around, but once we ordered, food came out within 10 minutes. Damn that's quick! And as always, the bacon was piled high and slathered in Miracle Whip. Mmmm mmmm good. The BF ordered a bacon turkey melt and was able to snag some of my overflowing bacon and add to his sammie. For dessert, we indulged in some original Crown Candy ice cream. A giant chocolate shake is probably the best way to wash down several pounds of bacon. The BF downed a double scoop cone. So good! Still one of my favorite STL spots (when the line isn't wrapped around the corner) and I love taking out of town guests here.

text: When we first thought of getting sushi in Tucson, we didn't set our hopes high because the nearest ocean is pretty far away. And good thing we had low expectations! They had a wide range of specialty sushi rolls with interesting flavors, like mango or pesto, and they also carried standard fare, like rainbow and spicy tuna rolls. But, their service was pretty bad. When we walked in, the hostess was on the phone with family and didn't even bother looking up to smile at us. Finally, a waiter came by and asked if we'd been helped, to which we replied 'no.' Just as this happened, she got off the phone, but still didn't even acknowledge our existence. So, we were led to our table where our waitress promptly took our order. Our food came nearly instantly. But, when we ordered round two, it took a good 20 minutes for us to get our rolls. Plus, they didn't even bring wasabi or ginger unless you asked. Weird! Their sushi was average, but the service bumped them down. I'm sure there's better places to get sushi in Tucson, so the next time I visit, I'll be sure to look around. Nice location in North Tucson, though!

text: After experiencing the most outrageously expensive haircut and color job of my life, so expensive my husband banded me from getting my hair done ever again! I decided it was time for a change. Change of stylist that is. With good reviews from fellow Yelpers, I figured what the heck it's worth a shot...at least for a haircut. I got an early appointment, 10:30am seems to be the earliest time on a Saturday you can get...I showed up a little after they opened at 10am. I had Kendra and she was ready for me when I arrived. We discussed what I wanted and she consulted with a learning advisor who came over to confirm. She gave me awesome vertical foils for my highlights. As far as foils go while they're in your hair, they looked amazing...rather than crumpled and alien-like. The haircut was going back-and-forth a little. I had a hard time explaining the cut I was looking for, but in the end we got it right. When it came to styling I was hoping for a little more. I have fairly thin hair and wanted more volume on top, so I was surprised she was blow drying mostly downward instead of using a round brush and drying up, but everything came out okay. Overall, I was very happy with my cut...I know I'll be able to style it the way I want now. The color is awesome. You can't beat the price, it was $47! It will take a good 3-4 hrs depending on what you get...so plan for a 1/2 day at the salon.

The most unappealing thing about the whole experience was probably the fact that you wait in a line that goes along a food prep area so you get to see piles of sausages overfilling pans and precooked scrabbled eggs being scrapped out of a pan. The place says it has the best baked ham, however the ham was sitting in a pan on the hot line and it looked pale and dry. I wouldn't reccomend this place, and I am not sure what the hype is all about.

text: The Hog Pit suffers from either an identity crisis or a complete lack of caring on the part of the staff. They're either a decent bar that serves food, or they're a sub-par restaurant with good drink prices. I gave them the benefit of the doubt and tried going for lunch, dinner and drinks on several different occasions. Not once did everything go right. I'm not expecting everything to amaze me, but I sure would love it if everything were at least adequate. There are a few positives about The Hog Pit, mostly dealing with the bar. The bartenders are nice and they know what they're doing. Drink prices aren't high and the beer is cold. The restaurant side of the house is where things begin to break down. I've never had a good experience with a server here, let alone a great one. They frequently forget drinks, bring out the wrong orders and take too much time to come around to each table. Once, when I asked for some extra sauce, one of the line cooks finally brought out a squeeze bottle. My server was talking at the bar. The food might be good sometimes, but I'm not sure. The main issue I have is that on five out of six attempts to eat here they were out of whatever I wanted. One day it was brisket, the next pulled pork. Time of day doesn't seem to matter either. Sunday afternoon or Thursday night, they're out of multiple items. If you're a BBQ joint, please try to plan ahead. Multiple times over several months is inexcusable. The sauces aren't all that flavorful, and they don't give you much to go with unless you ask for extra. Sadly, the meat doesn't stand on it's own. The sweet potato fries are good, but really could use some sort of dipping sauce. Ketchup just doesn't do it. The barbecue market in Tucson is expanding, and there are now several options. If The Hog Pit wants to thrive as a restaurant rather than a bar they really need to step up their game.
label: NEG

text: Chill, retro, and sexy... RIGHT in the middle of OLD town Goleta, surrounded by the quiet nothing of Hollister. They've got a fair amount of small American brews (mostly California ales, and Belgian-style ales, NO Bud/Coors/Miller!) and they're happy to let you try the beers before you even order yourself a pint. The bartenders are as laid-back as the atmosphere and clientèle, maybe too laid-back as you may not even find the bartender when you want a drink. text: We adopted two cats here after the passing of our previous one. Over all, the experience was much better than I had expected. The place could use a good scrub and some paint, but the animals are more important than the general appearance anyway. The neighborhood isn't the best, but if you visit during the day you don't need to worry. We processed the adoption on a Sunday and were told it would be three or four days before they could some home. They had to be neutered and have some shots before we could take them. On Monday, they called us to let us know the cats were ready to be picked up. So if you adopt, get your pet supplies that same day, otherwise you may be caught off guard. Quick suggestion: If your pet was just spayed or neutered, remember to pick up some pet cleaning wipes because they will probably be stinky and you don't want to get their stitches wet. We got two cats, plus two cardboard transport boxes, for about $50. They throw in some free food as well if it is on hand. The only thing I was unhappy about was the quality of the cats' sterilizations. The stitches were very sloppy and our girl's stomach healed a little lumpy. As a result of our boy ripping out his stitches (I can't blame him, he had so many his crotch looked like a friggin' basket), I found out my private vet doesn't even need to use stitches when she neuters. If I adopt again I would pay to have my own veterinarian to do the procedure.

text: Delicious, classy, hip and just plain cool all around. I just got back from a weekend trip to Philly with my bf and I was thrilled when I came across Morimoto's restaurant in my guide book (I'm not very familiar with Philly, haven't been in over ten years, so I had no idea it was even there). We started with an eel & avocado roll which was good but not mind-blowing. The ingredients were very fresh and the eel melted in your mouth but still was not the best sushi I've ever had. (I would say 4 stars for the roll). The rest of the meal, however, was 5 stars all the way! Next we got a cold sesame chicken appetizer to share and this blew me away. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the sweetness of the sesame sauce mixed with the spicy oil that was drizzled on it made for a wonderful combination. We both got the same main course, cold green-tea soba noodles with dashi-shoyu dipping sauce (we got several small things rather than one main dish each so we could create our own tasting menu of sorts) and this was also extremely good. The portion was quite large considering it was listed on the appetizer page of the menu; it was more than enough for an entree. We also shared a plate of the wasabi fried rice which is probably one of the best fried rice dishes I have ever eaten. (I have to point out that the wasabi used was very distinct in both texture and flavour...it must have been either real wasabi, and not the common tubed variety, or a VERY good quality immitation). Atmosphere was hip and trendy but yet not too outrageous that it will look dated in a couple of years. Waitstaff was very friendly and easily accomodated us in a packed restaurant without reservations. **$92 including tax, tip, all of the above mentioned food, 1 beer and 1 cocktail = a great place out for an elegant but not TOO expensive date with great food and beautiful surroundings. (skip the drinks, as beer is beer and the cocktail was not overly unique for the $12 price, and get another delicious course instead!)

text: According to Science, 70-75% of what we perceive as taste is really smell, which is why food is never as good when you have a head cold. The relationship inverted means that, if there's an overpowering, distracting smell while, the quality of your gastronomic experience will suffer for it. India Grill punched me right in the nose when I walked in there for lunch. Cloying incense, vaguely chemical, swept out onto the sidewalk like walking by the candle store at the mall. Normally, I would've yielded to the crashing wave of scent, letting it carry me back out onto the street and on my way, but I was determined to try this place. The former 1st Ave N location had served some pretty good (though monopolized) buffet and, though Green Chili Bistro was great, I wanted to explore options. Both Green Chili and India Grill suffer from the need to cater to bland palates - I guess the average Floridian can't handle the heat - but India Grill was missing out on the flavor, too. Butter chicken, Tandoori, vegetable curry, and everything else we tried elicited the idea of Indian food, but not the deep expeditionary feel of exotic spices trooping across your tongue. Gulab Jamun, a dessert cake ball soaked in sweet syrup, tasted vaguely plastic. There are two reasons that I will go back: one is that I heard the dinner menu is significantly better than the buffet offerings - this makes sense and I will give them the benefit of the doubt. The second is that my visit was within a week of them opening. A guy wheeled in their beverage mini fridge while we were eating. I'll hope that they can get into a little better groove and dish up some exciting flavor. Surfing the smell back out onto the street after the meal, I looked across the way at Green Chili Bistro, and its savory welcoming smells of food, and knew what I'd choose for lunch next time.

text: Shame on you, whoever told me that Mikimoto was terrible and that I should never go. I forget who you are, but you kept me from trying a more-than-decent sushi place for over a year. THE GOOD Crawfish Roll: We always get one whenever we go eat sushi. Mikimoto's roll was super spicy, really too spicy for me, but it was clear from eating it that it was a quality roll; they put a healthy portion of decent, fresh crawfish inside, plus they added smelt roe which in my opinion makes every sushi roll better! Tiger's Eye Roll: Smelt roe, avocado, smoked salmon wrapped with baked squid, topped with eel sauce. Not really a roll in the traditional sense, but very tasty. Wrapped tightly so the squid didn't unravel and make the piece fall apart like you might find at other places *cough* Hana *cough*. Nice warm "sushi" roll that really satisfies your belly. Blue Crab Roll: On their laminated specials menu. The one redeeming item from Sushi Brothers makes an appearance at Mikimoto, and they pretty much do it here exactly how I wish it woulda been done at Sushi Brothers. Blue crab mixed with snow crab and avocado, wrapped in seaweed and rice. Simple. I was a little worried based on first glance that the snow crab would overpower the blue crab flavor, but that turned out to be much ado about nada. The blue crab really stood out and was complimented well by the other ingredients. Good stuff. Miso Soup & Ginger Salad: The soup was the perfect balance of water and miso paste: not too salty but not too flavorless. The salad had the perfect amount of dressing and it didn't look like it was thrown together haphazardly, which is pretty much all I ask for in a salad that comes with a dinner order. THE BAD Seafood Salad: Oy vey. Just as I hate it when restaurants soak lettuce-based salads in too much dressing, I abhor it when sushi places soak their sushi salads in too much ponzu. Unfortunately, that is exactly what happened with this one. When we mercifully reached the last piece of food in the salad, there was literally a quarter of a bowl full of ponzu sauce left at the bottom. Moderation, people! I want to be able to taste the fish at least a little bit. PURGATORY Chirashi Dinner: A part of this is my fault in thinking that a chirashi dinner priced at $12.95 would have anywhere near the amount of fish as other places that price theirs closer to $20. What came out was about 10 pieces of fish sashimi, one shrimp, one crabstick cut in half, a couple pieces of tamago and some smelt roe. Not the most generous of portions since I could order 10 pieces of sashimi a la carte for less money, but at least everything tasted decent enough. And with everything else we ordered, it turned out to be a the right amount at a good price. Noodle Salad "Amuse Bouche": Bland in comparison to other noodle salads, but it's free so HUZZAH. OVERALL I have yet to try their kitchen items yet, but in terms of sushi, it's both generally tasty and affordable. The environment is cozy, and they have a decent amount of parking around the building, although it's a tad tight. Definitely recommend you to try it.

text: After walking by on numerous walks, my boyfriend and I decided to give this place a try. We were very hungry from a long long walk. What a mistake that was. The food was laughably gross. Read on if you don't get queasy easily.... The chips were stale, hardly salty, and very dry. Since they didn't bring salsa, we decided to use what we thought was hot sauce to moisten the chips. It was not hot. According to other reviews, this thin and practically flavorless concoction was supposed to be salsa. It tasted nothing like any salsa I've ever tried, and was not even as good as store-bought. The only good note is that they serve Negro Modelo, a great dark beer. You really need it to choke down what comes later. We ordered some chile rellenos as an appetizer. I LOVE chile rellenos, and generally at authentic or non-authentic places, they are good, if not awesome. What came out looked like large hush puppies, served with what is supposed to be con queso and lettuce and tomato. Over-fried, meat was lower grade than Taco Bell, and I need a whole new paragraph on the queso sauce. "It tastes like the color gray!" my boyfriend exclaimed, though I highly doubt the color gray has a texture like cream of wheat. Isn't queso supposed to be smooth? It also had a lackluster color and lackluster flavor. There was very little chile and a whole lot of fried coating and the nasty meat. We started to get nervous about the main course. I decided on the "Mexican" Dinner, which has an enchilada, taco, spanish rice, and refried beans. It's very hard to go wrong with any of those, right? Well, Acapulco Joe's is just short-bus enough to get it completely foul. First off, I have never seen soupy spanish rice from a packet, authentic, inauthentic, homemade, or even a frozen meal. This was practically a stew, and tasted like it was bathed in the crap they call salsa. The beans were insulting. I tried mixing them together to combat the tastes, but it still sucked. The taco shell was stale, the cheese was still very cold, it was pretty much all lettuce and tomato, and they had slopped the enchilada sauce all over the side, making it even harder to eat properly. The enchilada sauce was not good, and I have had better ones from a freezer aisle. Normally, I would finish even a large plate at a mexican restaurant, but after only a few bites, I was done. We laughed and made fun of how bad it was all the way home. I even considered smoking a cigarette to get the taste out of my mouth. Well, it had the last laugh. One of us woke up at 3 am with numerous bouts of diarrhea and the other has a stomach ache all day. I'll leave it up to you to figure out who was who. If anyone wants to go to Acapulco Joe's with you, or even claims to like their food, call an asylum or slap them in the face. They need one or the other.

text: Its 3 A.M. and the bars have all closed. Kicked out in the street and the desire for alcohol subsiding a new desire emerges, food. Steak N' Shake no longer provides the great dining experience that it once had and White Castle does not seem all that appealing after hearing that their mouthful bite size burgers are made of liver. However the inebriated eater must find a plate of saving grace and sobriety somewhere. South on Kings highway from interstate 40, a beacon of light and hope shines, and that light is Uncle Bill. No it's not that Uncle Bill, the one who is a little too creepy for comfort or was arrested for throwing soggy loafs of bread at cars, but it is a place lit in a heavenly glow from the neon letters that says, "Uncle Bill's Pancake House." There plates of soft, warm, steamy goodness are served 24 hours a day for the late night early morning eater. There are many places one can go that serve breakfast 24 hours a day, Waffle House, Denny's, or even if someone is looking for a little bit of an adventure, there is Tiffany's Diner (great if someone wants a colon cleansing experience), but Uncle Bill's offers the three things the random hour eater desires; speedy service, quality food in enormous servings, and most importantly low prices, ever so low. Inside tables are everywhere with everyone from all walks of life sitting at them. At one table in the restaurant there the worker who just got off their shift, looking for a quick bite before heading home. On the other side there is a gaggle of partygoers, making a pit stop before heading to their next destination. Among the multitudes of people they sit in a building that resembles a cottage from the mountains, or a rather large hunting shack, only at Uncle Bill's they do not have any absurd decorations hanging on the walls like some "friendly neighborhood" restaurants. Grandma-esque waitresses must have been cloned back in 1987 populate all of the 24 hour diners in the country. Each one working their tables knows their costumers by one name "honey." Seeming like they want more than just a tip your coffee cup will never be empty. Each of the waitresses seem to be standing by, waiting to fill the cup up and a little bit of the saucer with the boiling coffee. Taking all the orders with ease the waitress walks off to bring the plates of saving grace in sweet saucer form. The hot stack of pancakes steam as they are brought to the table with a crown of margarine on top, arteries around the world cringe, but no here one cares and neither will the arteries once they get a taste of the pancakes. The pancakes are just absorbent enough to let the syrup from the assortment of flavors on the table to be poured onto them and the pancakes soak up the thick syrup just enough to not become a sweet soppy mess. The syrup runs down the sides and a sugary cascade of waterfalls forms around the flapjack stack and pools at the bottom creating an island. Oh how Gilligan and the Skipper would love to be marooned on this island. The pancakes are a delicious masterpiece of culinary art, especially at 3 A.M. when there is no place else to go. Of course Uncle Bill's does not just serve pancakes, not everyone can handle pancakes or, well, some people just might prefer something else at the moment. Besides pancakes, Uncle Bill's offers just about any and everything, except for burritos, that one would want to eat in a drunken stupor at 3 A.M. There is always the ever-reliable BLT where the bacon is just crispy enough where it won't seem like someone might be biting into a sandwich of crackers. Like any other place they also serve eggs in any fashion that anyone can think of: sunny side up, scrambled, as an omelet with just about anything in it, or if someone is looking to be extremely daring, plain. Even though Uncle Bill's is primarily known for their breakfast, they also serve the two other meals, though, they are not as important as breakfast. Steaks, salads, and deserts are ready to be consumed as well. All the other food of course plays second fiddle to the pancake. Uncle Bill's is known as a pancake house for a reason. Uncle Bill's brings the sweet charm of the early morning breakfast or rather late dinner, depending on who it is, with the warm atmosphere that is always welcoming all 24 hours of the day. Offering enough variety in food and their inexpensive prices, there is no wonder in why Uncle Bill's has been around for as long as it has. With friendly service able to stomach even the most bothersome drunks, they will surely be around for a great while longer.
label: POS

If you're a fan of any of those about mentioned pizza palaces, you'll probably be a fan of Stella. The setting is probably the most casual and kid-friendly of Starr's restaurants, yet has the same attention to detail in a more down to earth way. I had the chance to try four different pizzas that day: Pepperoni, Sausage, Picante, and Pistachio. The Pepperoni and Sausage were the favorites but all were very good. The interesting thing about Stella is that the different between the pizza flavors isn't just a matter of a change in the main topping (pepperoni, sausage, etc). They use different cheeses depending on the combination of flavors being highlighted. The crust is EXCELLENT and consists of the perfect balance of chewy and crispy. The antipasti dishes are also very good especially the balsamic onion and broccoli rabe. My only complaint is that the service was a bit slow - pizza took over 30-45 mins to come out after ordering. So you have to go there for the quality of pizza, not for a quick slice. Final thoughts... A much welcomed addition to Philly especially if you like wood fired oven style pizza. There were three hostesses; one was friendly, one was relatively inconsiderate and one was out and out rude. When I first got there, I gave one hostess (the friendly one) my name, and she told me the wait would be about 45 minutes. That was no biggie because it was a Saturday night. So an hour later, I go in to see how much longer our wait would be, and a different hostess (the rude one) tells me that the wait will be more like the 45 minutes I was originally quoted. Confused, I told her that 45 minutes had already passed. She curtly replied that according to her clock, only 30 minutes had passed, and that she'd let us know when the table was ready. Now I'd been timing our wait, and I knew it'd been longer than 45 minutes, but how are you going to argue with a chick who's working in a restaurant that you've REALLY been wanting to try? I wasn't about to get into it with her, or her jack-leg time telling skills. The appropriate response would have been "I'm sorry, but it's going to be a few more minutes. We'll let you know as soon as the table is ready," *insert apologetic look here*. About fifteen minutes later, she comes outside where we were waiting to tell us our table was ready. Once seated, and after having given our orders, a different hostess (the inconsiderate one) comes over and tells me that she needs the chair next to me (our purses were sitting in it), and that I could put my purse on the table. Now, I'm not one of "those girls" who thinks it's bad luck to put her purse on the floor (because frankly, it doesn't matter if your purse is on the floor or on your lap - if it's empty it's empty, and the location of said purse has nothing to do with that.). I will not, however, place my purse on the dinner table. You put YOUR purse on the table! We were seated at one of the higher tables, so I just pulled up another chair. Now don't get me wrong, I can understand you needing the chair, but there were other chairs of the same type not too far away, so she could have grabbed one of those. I just felt inconvenienced, and I shouldn't feel like that as a restaurant patron. She was apologetic, but whole thing could have been handled better. So yeah, the food and Ben's service are really what afforded this place and this experience more than a single star. I would have had a much more enjoyable experience sans the rude and inconsiderate hostesses. That said, I won't let this experience hinder me from trying more of the Garces restaurants, but I probably will not return to GTC.

text: Hey Smoke'n Dudes you have finally hit the yelp scene! I have been noticing your very colorful and highly decorated vans driving around for years! I understand that it was around 3:00pm, but almost one half hour for take out when we were the only order was a bit much. Hubby noticed they kept inserting a meat thermometer into his stuffed pork loin and you giving it more time. That is cool, get it to the right temp, but it was your daily special and you open at 11:00am! His other entree for tomorrow night is the half smoked rotisserie chicken and between the two meals for his sides he chose mashed red skinned potatoes that were quite tasty, baked beans that could have came from a can, they were very thin and nothing wonderful, canned corn and a corn muffin that was good. I had to snag a bite of the chicken to yelp about of course and I liked the smoky flavor and it was very moist. His pork was not cooked and it was on the tough side. For my entree I had the House Sampler of two ribs ( you gave me four, thank you), BBQ pulled pork, BBQ beef brisket and my sides were mac & cheese and red skin potato salad I love when I pick up my ribs and they fall apart, this did not happen and could not happen because they should have cooked a lot longer than they did. The meat was flavorful enough but fatty. They were meaty so there is potential in them. Certainly not the best I have had. The pulled pork was good and the brisket was uneventful. Check out Tommy DeNic's the next time you are at the Terminal and ask him for a few tips and bites. I just love his passion and watching him check the brisket and pass out free bites with so much pride. The mac and cheese is the same mac and cheese you can get at Popeye's, KFC or Cracker Barrel. I liked your potato salad but I had a real problem with how it was handled in your store. The gallon tub of potato salad was down to probably one fifth full at the most. Kathryn used her bare hands to pick out a plastic teaspoon, which she laid on the counter. She then put on one plastic glove which she used to stir the salad and to use as a scoop to fill the cup. This was cool, but then she took off the glove and used her bare hand to pick up the dirty teaspoon and threw it back into the container of the remaining potato salad, why? Why was it even in there? For tasting? I then made it a point to watch her and she is fidgety and I am picky! She reached under her shirt to scratch her back, swiped her nose a few times, scratched her head, answered the phone and used the register and then just dove into baskets of uncovered plastic ware to throw in my bag! The best part of this whole scene is I hate most potato salads I order out and yours was very good, very good indeed. I just wished that I had felt better about eating it. On a good note I had a half pint of some of the best chili I have ever eaten, with chunks of beef plus ground beef and I loved those chunks of green pepper, onions and tomatoes! The flavor was outstanding and I enjoyed each and every bite! Kudos to you on that. The rum raisin bread pudding that you won first place in the Pennsylvania State Championship has wonderful flavor, but I shall bake it more tomorrow because it was 70% uncooked raw dough. I understand that you cater pig roasts and have won state championship awards but you are prepared for those, your restaurant was not ready for us at 3pm and this is what we got. Folks you can dine in at one of their five red checkered clothed tables, call in ahead for take out or have it delivered and as mentioned they do have catering. I feel bad and I wanted to say 5 oinks and that I am stuffed like a pig, but this little piggy is crying wee wee wee all the way home. Oink... 2.5 oinks.

text: There are around a billion ppl in India and a chunk of the population travels by roads. To save a hungry traveler's soul there are these 'Dhabas' littered across the roadways. That was the feeling I got as I seated myself over on one of the benches of Rice n Spice as I carefully browsed over the menu written on a white board. Talking about an Indian fare, What most of us are used to at restaurants is pretty rare at most household kitchens as it is too rich and heavy for daily consumption. The thgt of eating tandooris, naans, and Tikka masalas abhors me, that's why I find myself at the doorsteps of RiceNSpice when I crave for some homecooked goodness. It might take a while to get accustomed to this place, there is practically no service per se , u scribble ur order on a piece of paper and hand it over to whoever is walking towards the kitchen and the food gets delivered to ur bench. I sometimes just walk over to the cooler and get myself a beverage cos it works out faster. There usually is some bollywood flick playing on the TV, which is mostly accompanied by ruckus laughter of us mocking the insane subtitles or just us ogling at some sultry actress. There are not many ppl in the kitchen, a wonderwoman for a chef and her helpers churn out delicacies at a stupendous pace. Most of the food is made to order, which keeps it fresh. This is a pretty simple place, no need to worry bout what to wear or make reservations etc. but they do accept Credit cards which is a plus. The serving sizes are available in half and Full portions, which makes it easier to order more than one dish to keep the palate guessing. Here is my strategy if u are blanking out on one. If the group is of a considerable size, order a Pitcher of Mango Lassi, an order of meat , I stay away from the tikka masala and just bank on the Chicken Curry instead. A dry vegetable like Bhindi (okra) or Aloo-Gobi and a Lentils or beans dish like the Daal or my favs Rajma(Kidney Beans)/ Chole ( chickpeas) and Paneer. Along with some breads to dip into the saucy goodness, like a Paratha stuffed with either potatoes, Cauliflowers, HorseRadish or even Paneer or Tava roti with some raita does ample justice to the food. Don't be afraid of trying different items off the menu here as most of them don't fail to impress. As ur body slips in and out of a food coma order some Masala tea to wake up ur senses before u hit the road again. So no matter how u make it to Rice'nSpice, I don't care if u walk, hail a cab or even bring an Indian truck, the end result is when u walk out u shall be gratifyingly satiated by some out of the ordinary food, and already be devising a plan of ur next visit. Cheers

text: I ate at the Taproom only once, but it was enough to make me never want to return. Our excitement began to wane after it took 25 minutes for our waitress to come take our drink/food order. That was 25 minutes when there were only two other tables occupied in the entire place and there seemed to be employees wandering aimlessly or standing unhelping-ly still at the empty bar. When we finally did get to order, the drink special of the day we wanted, which was advertised on signs in multiple places in the restaurant, was mysteriously out (at 11:00 am already?) and no attempt was made to alter any of the signs nor was an alternative offered to us. My boyfriend ordered a blue cheese burger cooked medium with roasted potatoes and I ordered a pork loin sandwich with mashed potatoes. We tried to order relatively simple fare because we were restricted on time. It took us almost 40 minutes to receive our food. Since when does a burger and a sandwich take that long to cook? Not only that, but tables that ordered after us received their food before us. The burger was overcooked to the point of being inedible and the roasted potatoes were served cold. My pork loin sandwich was very good so I ended up sharing my lunch with my boyfriend so he wouldn't go hungry. We asked the waitress to take back the burger and take it off our bill and she acted like nobody has ever had the audacity to request such a thing before. It actually took her two tries to get the bill right and she acted haughty and unfriendly the whole time. If we hadn't been running late from our lunch disaster I would've requested an intense meeting with the manager. Needless to say she did not receive a tip. I could've just gone on a bad day, this place seems to have potential, but unfortunatly with the staffing and operational issues it ended up being a huge headache. And with an overpriced menu of items that can mostly be found at other local establishments like Cabana, Jackson's, Bosco's or Noshville there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for me to give it another go.

She hesitated before telling me there was no difference. Now, as a woman in a tech store, I know what I'm in for. I know that as soon as I walk through that door, I am a being assessed and calculated as a possible sale and as a customer who is more interested in "pretty" things with "fun" features than actual specs. But I do research. A LOT of research. Because I know that my gender is part of their salespitch. And I refuse to be subject to assumptions based on my vagina. So, I told the girl that I thought she was wrong and wanted her to explain. So she actually PRETENDED to know what she was talking about and talked in circles for a good 5 minutes, exacerbating my annoyance and making me feel humiliated for her and huliliated to be in the same gender columns as this girl. I WANTED her to know what she was talking about; I WANTED her to be a tech-saavy whipsmart mama...But at that moment I really just wanted her to shut up. She lost interest in us when she realized that WE had lost interest, and without saying a thing turned around and walked away from us, and shot us a glare as we left. That same Canon was more expensive, anyway. We inevitably decided to do our shopping online, ensuring the lowest price and saving us from idiot salespeople. I shudder to think what our customer service experience would have been like had we been stuck with a guy; probably an equally maddening exchange in a more demeaning way. I DID finally find out the difference in optical vs. digital zoom, and I was right. Just make sure that regardless of whether you are a woman, a man, or anything in between, that you know your stuff when you make a significant purchase. An 18 year old trying to make a commission so they can buy the latest UGG boots is not thinking of the things I have sacrificed so I can buy a nice camera for myself. Lesson: EDUCATE and EMPOWER THYSELF!!

text: Since starting at my company here in Wayne, we've decided to do a "Ladies Night" to experience some of the local cuisine in the area. This time around, we chose Bahama Breeze to entertain our palate. I must say, next go round, we will avoid this place at all costs. The location does not accept reservations, but "call-ahead seating," which, to you and everyone else who makes reservations in the world, is a reservation, just on the day OF the event or lunch/dinner. Fine. I asked for a table on the outside patio for 7 people. I was told "No problem, we'll be able to accommodate you as long as most of your party is there by 5:30pm." Flash forward to 5:15pm and 90% of our party is at the restaurant and where are we sat? Inside under the blaring air conditioning. We were later told it is a first-come, first-serve for outdoor seating - not what I was told during my call ahead. Our appetizers were cold and not very good. We had the firecracker shrimp, coconut shrimp (which were nearly blackened and were over fried) and the lobster and shrimp quasadillas. The latter were probably the best of anything we ate. They were luke warm and semi-tastey. The bar was a whole other issue. I had tried to get two different kinds of frozen drinks, one being a Bushwacker and the other, a banana daquiri. Both failed miserably. They were highly watered down and not tastey at all. I specifically told the server to make sure to reduce the half-and-half in the drink, but guessing that the bartenders don't listen to their customers, the drink tasted like purely half-and-half with crushed ice. The banana daq was all water, nothing more. The dinner food was ehh. I think we could've gone to Burger King and had a more meaningful meal. I had the new Buttermilk Fried Chicken which was just two slabs of fried chicken with some cheese and spinach between it on very runny garlic mashed potatoes and some corn and beans. All of that for $11.95. No one cared for dessert or coffee because we were pretty turned off, overall, with the food. The server, however, was wonderful and should be commended for working in establishment that needs a huge overhaul in their bar area and their kitchen. They are lucky they are getting 2 stars.

text: The two statues of Thai dancers on either side of the entrance are sign #1 that this will be a good dining experience.
