I don't think it's fair to say you can't judge a restaurant during restaurant week, because isn't the point of the week to promote the restaurant and get more people excited about it? So I will judge away. Judgment is: all the food was fine, but safe. The decor is like a conference hall at a hotel, and the food brought that feeling home. The aesthetic made me feel like I was at a wedding with a horrible seating arrangement - we were cramped and probably offended the people around us (who were practically sharing a table with us) with our conversation about how you can't be buying jew'rry from Zales. To be fair, the food wasn't bad or poorly done- it'd be embarassing if you fucked up a creme brulee- but it wasn't omgamazing. The service was rushed. The whole thing was just okay. My friend who lives in Philly proper was really excited to finally go to this place and by her reaction I knew we shared the same feeling: overrated.
label: NEG

text: I have to say, their cookies look nice, but they leave a very bad taste in your mouth.
label: NEG

text: While the idea of servers running throughout the restaurant serving meat fill of different types of meat sounded like Xanadu meets Caligula to me, I have to say I was disappointed with my first visit to Fogo De Chao. While the service was excellent, and the novelty of flipping my red and green coaster back and forth to signal more food never felt tired, I did have a problem with the quality. Numerous times asking for medium rare I was served pieces of meat that I could only describe as coal; now I get that it must be insanely difficult for these servers to keep the meat at a consistent temperature as they weave their way through a packed house of people demanding meat. But still - for the price, I expect something at least close to the desired temp. Especially since they were advertising it. Also, the amount of salt on the cuts of meat bordered on absurd. I'm thinking cats would have a tough time licking some of the pieces I got. The side of mashed potatoes tasted like instant to me; if they weren't they were definitely watered down. The fried polenta had the texture of a hockey puck. I realize the main focus is the meat, but still, I'd like a serviceable side. I enjoyed the salad bar, and I loved the idea, but for the money, I don't think it was worth it. Probably a good place to go with a big group of people, though don't expect to hear too much of the conversation. The cavernous room created plenty of echo and a lour roar of everyone eating.
label: NEG

text: Our waiter said it was "this is a classy place". 22 bucks for shrimp and grits. Salsa slung on the table like a Waffle House in Mexico. First and only time to this "classy" joint.
label: NEG

text: Hugely disappointed. Locals recommended this place and Yelp seemed to support those recommendations. What? Is there such dearth of breakfast options that this is considered good? So good that there's a wait to get a table? What? No pancakes were ordered by my party so I can't speak to what appears to be this place's specialty. Omelette was brought with very flat/thin eggs (most omelettes have fluffy eggs?) and the home fries were GREASY with no flavor. Okay. I know those potatos are fried and should be greasy but seriously, it was just grease, slightly undercooked (home fries should have some minimal crisp, right?). Service was great though. Friendly, highly efficient, and lots of attention. Even then, I can't seem to get myself to give me more than 1 star.
label: NEG

text: They have the best cupcakes. It is all freshly baked by the owners. My favorites are the banana bread, pumpkin pie, and peanut butter! The cake is moist and not too sweet. The frosting is light, buttery, and flavorful. Sharon, one of the owners, takes the time to create delicious, unique, and cute cupcakes. It delights your taste buds and keeps you coming back for more!
label: POS

text: Even though Virago is known for its sushi, I wouldn't go there for that but rather for its chic atmosphere. With great modern décor, Virago also has great modern prices (ie. It's expensive). My visit to Virago included their most popular Godzilla Roll that was just the right amount of spicy but I don't think was that great. I also hear that their popular Dragon Fire roll and Crispy Dragon fire roll are pretty good. Virago is definitely trying to create the high end, classy, and modern vibe, and though their dishes are beautifully platted I would rather just not spend that much. I got the cheapest option on their sushi menu - $9 which is more expensive that the average prices at any other sushi place around town - which was good but I didn't think it was necessarily worth what I was spending. I will say their bar was fun, which a lot of nicer end matini options. They get 4 stars for their ambiance but not for their food.
label: POS

text: Only reason why I go there is it's the only bagel shop around. Service is poor! The manager is a foreigner, and has no concept of customer service.
label: NEG

text: In a word, underwhelming. I have been three times with dates or groups of people, all of whom had high expectations based on supposedly trusty sources. I've tried specials. I've tried "the National Dish of Brazil." I've tried asking the waitress for a recommendation. Through my visits, the only items I really liked were the drinks. Which is not to say that Yemaja's food was bad; it was okay. But for the price, the purported authenticity, and all the hoopla, I expected better.

text: This location may be pretty shady with the porn shops, but what else is in the area? Commerce Square, PECO, and the new Murano condominiums. But I'm not here to judge them for their location. Their pizza is great! I prefer it over Domino's (by leaps and bounds, Domino's is terrible) and I like their specialties, specifically The Works. Their chicken strips and buffalo wings (mild and spicy are the choices) are also pretty good. Nothing special about picking up. They were only a half block away from my apartment at the time. I've even been so lazy as to have it delivered. The delivery guy was nice. The #1 reason I use Papa John's is not only because I like their food, but because of the ease of ordering online. The wait is usually between 25-40 minutes for this location, not bad. The prices are a bit high but I think it is worth it.

text: By far the WORST post office ever. I recently moved to Hawaii and during the holidays I sent out 15 packages to my friends and family. Only 2 boxes never reached their destination. They both went through the Southwark post office. One box was to my brother the other to my old job. Neither of them received an orange note saying there was a box for them at the post office. Southwark was my old post office in Philly and I was fully aware of their lack of competence. Because I knew how poorly managed the office was, I told my brother to check up with them even though he had no orange slip. He made many attempts to get the box from the post office, yet every time they told him there was no box for him. Yesterday, about 6 weeks after I sent the boxes, and 35 dollars later the boxes were sitting back on my doorstep in Hawaii. I hate you Southwark Post Office.

text: I could not believe how big this thing was. It's like 700 ft tall! It really makes the St Louis skyline memorable and picturesque. It's honestly now one of my favorite landmarks now that I have come up close and experienced it's majesty. It's also in a location where there's a lot to do. You can ride up to the top of the arch, you can take a tour of the Mississippi River by boat, you can go to Laclede's Landing, Lumiere's Casino, or the riverboat Casino.

text: We have eaten Rusty''s for years. Over the past year their quality and service has gone down. We ordered a simple one item pizza. We have always paid by check, however, the girl on the phone rudely stated "dont you understand we only accept visa or cash. We accepted and paid by cc. When we received the pizza we discovered that the pizza was deep dish. usually we get thin style. We already had a horrible time ordering from them we decided just to eat something else. This was not a true pizza. I don't understand how a company like this can stay in business. The last part of this was the female on the other end asked us if we would like some ranch, we said sure. When we received our bill there was a charge for $.55 per 1 ounce cup. What a ripoff. Then I looked at our bill and it said there was a $2.50 delivery fee. I say we all boycott this company.

text: In comparison to Girard Vets this place is very clean. Also in comparison to Girard Vets I was able to get an appointment at a reasonable time. I liked the efficiency and helpfulness of the administrative staff and my dog received a thorough check up from the vet himself. They were very friendly, especially the vet assistant who got along great with my dog. I am happy that I have found a place that is so quaint, friendly, and knowledgeable. If only I could find a doctor for myself with the same qualities.

When I attended the Jazz Festival on Jefferson St. this summer a local person told me that you should try it just because it is pretty popular. He said to keep in mind the local drunks have kept it in business for almost 40 years. In my opinion it is for the daredevils! I tried it at the '10 Hot Chicken Festival and it wasn't all that. Too hot and spicy for me and I think I felt it the next day out the other end! Ouch!

text: remember how the movie clueless gave us all these new words? one of my favorites was 'monet'--meaning somebody hot from far away, and when you get in closer, that person's just a total mess. well, smokin betty's is a total monet. it's beautiful, sleek, and new. it's big and shiny. i happen to like devil's alley. and barbecue. so i'm thinking, this is going to be great. the menu sounded great. what wasn't so great: the server seating us at the awkward couch spots. seriously? there's three of us. it's kind of awkward. then, i think things are getting better, as i got the allagash white/peach schnapps cocktail. tasty. things just get... sad. alright, i admit. it's a barbecue place, and perhaps matzoh ball soup and mac and cheese and potato latkes are weird things to order. but i give it a go. my matzoh ball soup comes with still frozen balls. and when they bring a replacement, somehow all the veggies have disappeared from the broth. mac and cheese was meh. and the potato latkes were dismissable. my friend called her salad 'wimpy'...and the hot dog platter was not devoured. alas. my barbecue dreams were not to be fulfilled tonight. goodbye, monet.

text: Nunya P. Irvine, DMD put me through more pain than I have ever been in at a dentist's office. I had a chipped tooth and a cavity that needed to be taken care of. She was just rushing through the job and didn't give me enough novocaine to dull the pain of the drilling, which is odd because there was no one in the office and I had to wait half an hour past my appointment time to be seated. Anyway, I wanted to run out of there screaming. I had a root canal that was less painful than this. I have been to 4 dentists in my lifetime who were all very good, but the way Nunya P. Irvine, DMD treated me was grossly unacceptable. And her assistant was shoving her tools in my mouth like she was in a hurry or just didn't care. Very cute high quality kids stuff. Stokke highchairs, Monte gliders, Tea clothing, adorable wooden toys . . . it's all there. Staff is very helpful, if they didn't know they answer they grabbed someone else (the owner, I assume?). Also, they had an area to change his diaper which was fantastic. He has poor timing with his diaper emergencies. All around great place. If you're ever looking for a baby shower gift, go here and get a gift card or have staff point something out to you.

What a bad idea. 1) It was insanely crowded. 2) Thus, it took forever to get a drink. 3) If there was food, there was no way I was tracking down anyone to take my order 4) After the game was over, the place turns into a meat-market sports bar: everyone dancing to horrible music and rubbing up on each other. Boo. Oh, and ladies, if you use the restroom be careful what you do in front of the mirror; it's a two-way and the "gentleman" in the guys restroom can see everything you do.

text: My husband is a huge BBQ fan and since I work near Jimmy's I ventured out one day during lunch to provide a report back to my hubby. As everyone has mentioned this place is not much to look at from the outside but I can surely get by that if there is good food inside. I ordered the two meat combo so that I could try both the pork and beef brisket. I selected corn bread and coleslaw as my two sides. My bill was $17 (with a soda) but again I'm willing to part with money if the food is worthy. My first impressions were not good as I sat down to wait and was joined by many flies including one of the largest flies I have ever seen as well as a dead moth on the windowsill. I noticed the front door was being left open and inquired whether maybe the AC was broken. I was told that the AC was on but with the smoker it just can't keep up. It was uncomfortably warm. When I got my food I thought the meat was moist however not very flavorful when eaten without the sauce. That takes me to the sauce. There were three choices : vinegar based, regular and hot. I am usually a medium kind of gal so I tried the regular sauce which in my opinion tasted mostly like Molasses. The coleslaw was very densely cut and I didn't care for it. I normally like a sweeter coleslaw and this one was watered down. I also wasn't impressed with the cornbread other than that it was very dense so was quite filling. After leaving and sharing with my husband that this was not a place to take him to I had a sinking feeling in my stomach all afternoon. I actually had some stomach discomfort through the next day which only got worse when I checked the Chester County Health Inspections website to find that during Jimmy's February 2010 inspection he had 7 violations. The violations included cleanliness in the food prep area and presence of both insects and rodents. I do not recommend Jimmy's and am actually quite surprised that so many do.
label: NEG

text: Been here a few times. The food is overall decent pub food, though every now and then you'll get something iffy. Beer's good. I just got back from my first time at their sunday trivia night though. Wow. I dunno who the host was, but he was one of those guys who tries to be funny but isn't at all. He made a lot of jokes about exotic Asian women, black people and welfare, and weird homosexual jokes (he himself is gay--as if that gave him permission to hate on everyone). And he dropped the c-word against women a handful of times. Even me, a straight white male, was like, "Really?" The bar might be fine the rest of the week, but I won't be going here again.

So I called them only for them to say something like 'Is this Alexandra? yeah we got your order an hour ago, but we don't have any delivery guys tonight' So they had my name and number and email address but never bothered to call or email me that they couldn't deliver to me. They also never apologized.

Then they have a lot of H + M clothing (which is down the street) and have like 5 of the same shirts and stuff. Its really just a store that sells slightly used clothing.

text: Nasi Goreng Seafood is a fried rice dish with shrimp, squid, fish ball, onion, egg and pickle. Now, they do go a little light on the meat content here but don't let that distract you from what is important - the goddamned pickle. Remember how in The Big Lebowski, the rug tied the whole room together? Well the Nasi Goreng seafood is the room and the pickle is that rug. It turned the dish into something memorable. Every 3 or 4 bites, I would get a piece of the pickle in my forkful and boy I was I pleased. I'm going to ask for extra pickle next time and so should you. The fried wonton is a very good appetizer. I like this place a lot. It is quaint and cheap. If you can make it down conveniently, it is a fantastic lunch option. On the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction-scale, this establishment is Serenity.
label: POS

text: This is one of the terrible Home Depots I have ever been to. It is located on Carrolton next to Rouses. A torn up street (that has been torn up and closed since Katrina) separates the stores. Do not accidentally turn into this unpaved mud pit or you may not get out. The Home Depot store is surrounded by a 14 food hurricane fence. Teams of Mexican laborers hang out in the parking lot everyday. Someone provides them with water coolers while they wait for jobs. The resulting aura is that of a prison. The store itself is not well stocked or managed. Very few workers are present inside to help you out. Usually it doesn't matter if you find someone to help because the store is poorly stocked and has often run out of things I need...common things, not obscure items. The plant section is pretty terrible and is located in the parking lot. So you have to exit the store through the front door just to get to the plants--not the side door as is the usual setup for Home Depot. If you are in the area and need something, this could be an okay option. It's not a good option and I'd recommend driving out to Clearview Home Depot if you really want to have a more enjoyable shopping experience.
label: NEG

text: Is it fair for me to write a second update? Well, here goes: Atomic Cowboy expanded their menu. They added probably another 10 or 11 entrees. I had the vegetarian chili mac, and it was DELISH. The portion was huge and I had plenty to take home as leftovers!
label: POS

text: The Philly Zoo rocks! I can't believe it took me 8 years to get here, but for some reason I usually only visit the zoo when I'm in DC. The Philly Zoo isn't the all time greatest zoo I've been to - that honor belongs to the Bronx Zoo - but it is pretty cool. My dad and I loved the cat exhibits, since they allow you to get right up next to the cats, assuming they're lounging by the glass wall. If not, the view is no worse than any other zoo. My only complaint was the gorilla exhibit. No gorilla baby?! COME ON! We took the PHLASH, which is seasonal, but drops you right at the front door. I may join the Zoo at some point so I can visit my feline friends more often.
label: POS

text: OH LORD do I HATE this movie theater. It's the closest one to us but I will definitely go out of my way to avoid it. Allow me to recap for you 3 out of the 3 experiences I have had there: 1. Baby crying behind us for the entire movie. At a showing of "Iron Man," no less. Not exactly a film I'd take a baby to see. Oh WAIT! That's right, I wouldn't take a baby to see ANY movie that wasn't INTENDED for babies, because I wouldn't want to annoy my fellow patrons! Helloooo, that's what babysitters are for. If you don't have the money for a babysitter, you shouldn't be at a movie theater. Period. If you absolutely must watch "Iron Man" with your baby, do the rest of us a favor and RENT IT. 2. People mumbling loudly behind us during "Indiana Jones." With both this and the first example, the theater staff refused to do anything other than pop their head in the door and then leave (even though we complained numerous times). 3. The last time I was there was definitely the "best" time, but there came a point in the movie we were watching where a "twist" occurred. Except it was super-predictable and whatever. Still entertaining, but not exactly surprising. But I SWEAR TO GOD! Everyone else in the theater took that moment as, like, permission to start having all sorts of conversations. "WHOA! So he was leaving a trail the entire time? Seriously, he's a bad guy? Oh wow, I didn't see that coming!" LOUDLY. I mean, I'm glad that you were surprised by this shocking "twist" and all, but keep it to YOURSELF! I realize that people talk in every theater, but I truly believe it's worse in this one. It's like an epidemic, and the staff is not AT ALL helpful. All in all, not worth it considering the theaters themselves are small and nothing to write home about. I'm through with this place.
label: NEG

text: Absolutely outrageous prices. I hate sounding stereotypical but it's as if because I am a female they thought charging me nearly $30 to replace a easy-to-install tail light was okay. They said it was what their computer told them to charge, sorry no, I've never paid more than 10$ before. When I complained about the price of the light bulb, they did refund some of my money, but I still will not be going back. They had also done our inspection on this visit, afterward we started having issues with the wheels of the car, it's a debatable coincidence, I know. But still worth noting. They were not AAA approved, I think I know why now. A local alternative is Cadwalader Service Center Incorporated, great service and fair prices.
label: NEG

text: You can't beat $2 pints. Can't. Doesn't matter if that special is on Tuesday's. They have a good beer selection on tap, the bartenders are fast, and I can usually find a seat--even if it's crowded. The eye-candy is sublime and if you are single, there isn't a better place to be. My only complaint would be that it's really, really loud. It sounds more like a nightclub than a pub/restaurant. But, other than that, it's a good place to people watch and catch a ball game.
label: NEG

text: First off-- this is no Uptown take on Galatoire's. Lies. The two stars are for the ambiance-- it's a great, old school restaurant. Unfortunately the food and the service were unimpressive. For the amount you pay for an entree ($25ish), I expected a lot better. We had reservations. The hostess didn't seem to care and told us rudely to wait at the bar. OK it's a popular restaurant, I get that. When we were finally seated, our waiter informed us they were out of all oyster dishes. "Oh no! That's the reason we came here," my friend and I protested (lightly). He seemed bored. No apology. No offering of something gratis to make up for the situation. Our order-- Crabcakes.-- forgettable. Scallops with foie gras-- awesome. Small but flavorful. Animal rights violators we might have been, but damn were those tasty Smoked duck-- fatty and came with a series of bland vegetables. For their "go to" dish, we were unimpressed Brownie ala mode-- fine. Nothing too memorable. Overall just not enjoyable enough to warrant the price or the trek uptown. Go to the real Galatoire's or Commander's Palace if you want New Orleans charm AND flavor
label: NEG

text: When I lived in Northeast Philadelphia (Mayfair), I fondly remember when there was a Roy Rogers at the corner of the Roosevelt Blvd and Bustleton Ave. Sometime in the very early 1990's I remember getting a kids meal (I don't remember the food itself) there where the toy consisted of a plastic half-ring that was supposed to be some worm monster or something, where one end was a ball and the other a grabbing cup, so that if you got more of these toys, you could connect them. It was promptly lost within a few days, as anyone, child or adult could sense this was a crappy concept for a toy. This location changed to a Hardees before I left and is now a Boston Market, since Roy Rogers basically withered away to the captive market of those on the tolled limited access roads of the Northeast US. There's a reason. My next experience at a Roy Rogers was at a rest stop outside Boston sometime around 1999. The food was subpar, dry and salty, but edible. A step or two down from KFC. Most recently perhaps a couple years ago, a friend and I were on our way to Reading, and I was a bit famished, having not eaten that day. At this rest stop, is that a Roy Rogers I see? What a novelty! I haven't had that in a long time! I don't think its difficult to supply a restaurant that is right off a major turnpike, but apparently they only do so about once a year, because that's how it tasted. This is not chicken. A level of mummification is evident in the flesh. This is not mashed potatoes. This is wheel bearing grease. You don't have Dr. Pepper? You don't have root beer? I have to pay for barbecue sauce and you don't have honey mustard? What is this place? Had we been nuked some time between 476 and King of Prussia and I've just pulled into some desolate apocalyptic fallout shelter? My day would not be ruined; we later ate elsewhere near Reading and it wound up to be an enjoyable sojourn which resulted in my purchase of a sweet black derby. Perhaps I'm off-base expecting fine dining at a truck stop. Nevertheless, do yourself a favor and get something at Wawa before you pass through the tolls, or are at the mercy of those retailers in service plazas selling Korean-war vintage meal rations glazed in used motor oil.
label: NEG

text: My husband and I stumbled upon Antonios after searching all over Nashville for a good Italian restaurant. Who knew it was in Bellvue all along? The staff is amazing. Very friendly and very knowledgeable. The food is spectacular. Everything is fresh and you can even see into the kitchen while they are making your food from scratch. Everything we've had there has been fantastic and pretty reasonably priced. We always take family here when they're in town. LOVE this place, Definitely check it out.

I go to back for cigarillo and people playing on Super Nintendo. Rico sold nintendo when he was young for airplane ticket to California so cousins can see my dance machine on The Grind tv show.

text: Two words: hot pecan pie ala mode!!! Unbeatable anywhere! Re other food, your engaging waiter will tell you that "everything is good" at The Camellia Grill, and we believe it. Teresa splurged and never regretted eating a bacon double cheeseburger (no photographic evidence, please) while I greatly enjoyed the Word (sausage) sandwich). We split the cheese fries. But it was an agonizing decision as everything looked tasty. The pecan waffle was a close second. The Chef's special omelette, smothered in a bowl of chili, is not for the faint of appetite. Prepare to stand in line, then scope out what others are having while finishing your wait indoors. From downtown, get there on historic St. Charles streetcar through the picturesque Garden District. You won't regret the wait. We're definitely coming back next time in town.....
label: POS

text: Amazing. Right in the heart of center city (so easy to get to). Beautiful interior. I felt more fashionable the instant I entered. Clusters of 30-somethings hung out by the stylish bar, all clad in upscale clothing- looking especially classy with their martinis in hand. We were led to our table, which was surrounded by a roomy couch and plush chairs. (The only down-side was that the table was so large that I felt like I had to yell to communicate with my friend on the other side.) So, comfortably sitting at our table, our waitress came over quickly and got us started with some delicious drinks. The rest of our meal ran smoothly, courses coming quickly and prepared delicately. I got the bacon-wrapped scallops. They were so juicy! I also got the seared tuna, prepared perfectly. I tried the Chilean Seabass, too, and that was one of the best dishes I've had in my life. The desserts were also great-- delicately prepared like the rest of the courses, and a nice, light way to finish the meal. (I got the brownie, but it was still quite light.) All in all, my 2 recommendations: -Come in groups so you can try lots of different foods (they're all good!) -Come during restaurant week (otherwise I would never be able to afford this place) and still be prepared for the high prices. (But if you're prepared to spend, come! It's worth the hole in your wallet afterwards...)
label: POS

text: What a quaint and delectable little restaurant. I've been here on 2 occasions and couldn't have been happier with the staff, cuisine, and the chefs on both. The second time was rather different than the first bc my company for that night happened to vegan. When making the reservation a couple of days in advance, i notified them of this. They politely assured me that it would be no problem. When it was time to dine, it was hard to decide at that point what was more sensual; the vegan or traditional cuisine. All of it was delivered perfectly. Thank you!

text: Enjoyed lunch catered in by Breve. Very good, we had a variety of sandwiches and wraps with Cesar salad and sampling of cookies and brownies. I liked that the sandwiches were "naked" and you could add you mustard/mayo etc if you liked. FYI they like to have 24hr notice on any catering order.

text: Delicious small sushi joint tucked away in Montecito. The fish is always fresh and the selection of rolls is not only vast but creative. There are at least 3 full pages of rolls to choose from. It can be overwhelming, but it is a guarantee you'll find something you like whether you want something simple and bite-sized or something extravagant and fist-sized. Great presentation, service, sake selection, ambiance (although small), etc.
label: POS

text: Like the whispers in the woods on LOST, snippets of Sweet Art have been swirling around me for quite a bit of time before I finally went this past week. Little did I know the smoke monster of AWESOME was about to have a party in my mouth. Having just eaten lunch, I bought two cupcakes (a vegan Tickled Pink for here, a Mississippi Mudslide to go). I decided to eat the Tickled Pink, and it was amazing. Obviously made from scratch, box cupcakes don't hold a candle to it. While I'm neither vegan nor vegetarian, I can appreciate the strides necessarily to make a bomb cupcake sans usual ingredients. It did not disappoint. I am rather notorious in my circle for having irresistible urges and utter lack of self-discipline when it comes to good desserts. Restraint from the little brown bag containing my other cupcake lasted approximately 8 minutes before I couldn't resist the temptation any longer. It was a valiant stand-off, but one I no doubt lost (or won?). No amount of vegan-ness could touch what happened in my mouth with the Mississippi Mudslide. It was somewhat buttery and had the most amazing icing. I'm pretty much speechless because I can't come up with words as to how good it was. The amazing in-house art work and funky interior were all additional pluses. But the icing on the cake was the omnipresence of smiles throughout the place... from the man at the cash register, to the girl who brought out my friend's food, to the young and old throughout the place. The positive messages on the wall and the way they seemed to be lived out in the running of Sweet Art hit me like a brick when I realized they had gone into the precisely perfect business... because I've never seen any eating a cupcake with a frown. :)
label: POS

text: Ate at the bar on a business trip. Had herb crusted grouper with a side salad. Both were very good! I have been here before and enjoyed it enough to come back. Meal without drink (water only) was $25.15. This place is a little more upscale than your average chain rest, but can still be quite casual.
label: POS

text: Worst veal in Philly. 3 of us went downtown over the 4th to have a nice meal. Sat outside which was pleasant by the time of night we went, and there's always sights when you sit on the sidewalk. What's better entertainment than the American public? To start the mussels in white wine were good, and the antipasti platter was fine. Then disaster struck. The entree's arrived. Jumbo shrimp with pasta was sticky and over seasoned. I'm not going to make a big deal about "jumbo" shrimp not being jumbo beacuse the gulf problems continue and I'm sure it's not easy getting true large shrimp, but at least cook the pasta al dente!!! Daughter had the gnocci, which she said was good, but not up to the standards at other places close to the Italian market. Now for the disaster. I had the Veal Milanese. WORST dish I have ever had in Philly, and among the worst 10 meals of my life. Try to picture two wafer thin pieces of brown shoe leather that are coated with a non-descript breading, served luke warm with a bunch of greens with some terrible dressing on them. I ate one piece and we left and had dessert somewhere else. Will never go back to this place, EVER. How cheesy is it for the manager and waiters to stand on the sidewalk hawking for people to come sit down and eat? How many "good" places do you see do that? It is BYO, but so is LaViola, etc. which blow this place away. I don't care what the prices are when the food is this poor. text: Coming from California I tend to be a harsh judge on what constitutes a good Mexican place. Even before eating I have several rules that must be met for me to consider it in the upper echelon. 1) Chips and salsa on the table as you sit down. 2) Decorations that are kitschy fun and silly. 3) An occasional tuba laden song sifting through the place. Happily, Rey Azteca situated in an a hollowed out Pizza Hut started off wonderfully living up to all of these expectations. Honestly, they did a good job of redecorating, if I hadn't seen the hard to miss Pizza Hut top on the outside I would have never known of it's former use. The decorations are fun, little bits of mexico and artificially aged paint jobs. The seating is very comfortable. There are tables in the middle for big groups and plenty of booths on the side for the smaller groups. The wait staff was fast and very friendly and happy to answer any questions. We ordered our food, and even with a packed house got it in a reasonable amount of time. I ordered the texanas fajitas. Which is steak, chicken and shrimp mixed with some green bell peppers and onions. It is served smoking hot with a few tortillas and a side of guacamole, sour cream, and refried beans. This all combined into a fantastic meal. The fajitas were delicious. But, next time I will go to the spicier side of things and try out a taco or two. The food was delicious. And, there was an enormous amount of it. Some people claim I am a light eater, (My waist line sure doesn't agree!) but, even with that I barely made a dent into all of the scrumptious food I had in front of me. I look forward to tomorrow's lunch! This place is a bit out of the way up in Warminster, but in spite of that I cannot recommend it highly enough. Great food, great service, fun ambiance. I went for dinner and the prices were reasonable. The lunch time prices look even better.

text: I am a big rooter for all things East Nashvillean, as many people living in East Nashville tend to be. But I'm not delusional. The food and the menu grasps for the Vietnamese flavor and taste, but doesn't quite get a hold of it. I'm not sure if it's because it doesn't know how to, or that it's catering to its diners. Regardless, as the rating goes, "meh, I've experienced better." The pho is not that great: it's too sweet, and it's expensive especially for the size of the bowl. It's a Vietnamese restaurant and not a strictly pho restaurant, so I don't penalize it for not having different types of pho. But, really, only one kind of pho?! The rest of the entrees I've tried have slight semblance to Vietnamese, but runs closer to something pan-Asian. For example, the flavor of the grilled pork (served with vermicelli noodles) was overpowering and totally missed the subtle flavors of the lemongrass and the smoked sweetness in the meat. However, I'm super glad that it's doing well and it has plenty of avid eaters there. It's always good to have a hip, hot and happening place in the hood. I just wish I could be one of them.

text: Average is as average does. Came here for my birthday yesterday. (Oddly) I had been struggling to figure out where to go for my bday meal. Sure I had a couple free meal coupons, but they were for places like Qdoba and Red Robin. I didn't feel like venturing too far out, so we ended up choosing this place. Looking back, we probably should've driven the extra 15 minutes. AMBIENCE- this place looks a lot bigger from the outside. The decor kind of made me think design on a dime. At a first glance, the place looked pretty classy. However, upon being seated, you could tell that the owners probably didnt' spend all that much. For example, the light covering looked to be a nice looking piece of wrapping paper, and the nice print on the "booths" were actually plastic. I'm not holding that against them, just saying what I observed. SERVICE- I was somewhat reluctant to go here because a number of people had said service was hit or miss. Shame on me for not heeding their warning. As we were about to be seated, a woman cut us off and asked the hostess to run their bill. I thought this was rather rude of the woman, but after dining here, I can understand why. Our server was barely there, and sure it was pretty busy, but the 10 minutes in between each appearance was some what annoying. Also, she never mentioned the specials to us, which I'm sure we could've asked about, but isn't that something they should lead off with? The hostess (who we think is the owner) was very friendly, but outside of her appearances, we were not impressed at all. MENU- so this place serves "Southern European" food. I don't know how that translates, but they seemed to have some interesting dishes. They had appetizers such as mussels, and hummus, as well as a variety of soups and salads. Wine selection looked decent, though I dont' drink, so I can't really say for sure. Entrees were interesting, they had a meat and poultry section, seafood, pasta, and specialties ranging in price from $15-$30. Their specialties are what actually peaked my interest in the first place. They have paella "madrid stew", and french lasagna. What I was really interested in though was the cassoulet. Ever since hearing about cassoulet on the food network, I had wanted to try it. I figured, it's my birthday, and I was going to party like it's my birthday. FOOD- my wife elected to get their chicken and sausage pasta, while I went with the cassoulet. They have petite and regular portions on both, and since we were hungry, we went with the regular. Our meal started out with bread (which you can buy and take home if you want). The bread didn't seem to be anything extraordinary. Along with the bread, we both got house salads. I probably should've tried some soup, but a salad sounded good. Too bad it was not. It rivaled that of a side salad you would find at Denny's. Finally the main courses arrived. My wife's pasta was ample, though pretty Olive Garden-esque. The cassoulet came out and it was piping hot (the server did warn me about that). Once it cooled down enough I began. Hmmph. The flavor explosion that I was hoping for just wasn't there. Add that to the fact that I'm not a huge bean fan to begin with, and it proved to be rather disappointing. I knew beans were the main focus, but I figured as long as they were seasoned well I could overlook that. Not the case. I will say that both of our servings were huge, but it's a lot of average food. OVERALL- I don't think we'll be going back. We saw some of the other dishes, and couldn't help but keep making the Olive Garden comparisons. If I want flavorful food, I'll go to Yats and save $20. Celebrity Rating- Latoya Jackson

text: Every ice cream shop in the country should follow Creole Creamery's example and offer a bowl of six mini-scoops for $5.50. Especially places like Creole that boast way too many tantalizing innovative flavors. Creole ranks with the greatest on this front, and if you cream yourself for creameries like Bi-Rite in San Francisco, Scoops in Los Angeles, Cones in New York, and Molly Moon's in Seattle, then you should put this place on your list. The interior is very cute, with lots of photographs and phrases like "Eat Ice Cream" and "Be Happy" decorating the walls. The service is friendly and generous with the samples. I tried a ton of flavors before getting the mini sampler, perhaps defeating part of the purpose of that sampler, and most of them were pretty great. All of the ice cream has a wonderful tuggy consistency and a creamy richness. The base ice cream is sold as its own "naked" flavor, and it's really good, milky and not too sweet. I like that they're proud of their base, and the quality of the product shines through in every flavor. Like I said, I got six mini-scoops, which was a fair amount of ice cream but not too much, even coming off of two giant lunches. For my six flavors, I chose creole cream cheese, red velvet, banana cane malt, coffee pecan brittle, peanut butter fudge, and Abita strawberry chocolate. The creole cream cheese was my favorite, with a flavor like cream cheese but tangier, even a little bit sour. The red velvet was so good and it actually tasted like the cake, rather than vanilla mixed with cake crumbs. The banana cane malt tasted strongly of banana with an equally strong malty flavor, and the result was balanced and deep. Coffee pecan brittle was as good as it sounds, nicely textured and very tasty. Peanut butter fudge was a more adult flavor than you might imagine, very dense and dark with just a subtle layer of peanut butter. The most out-there flavor was the Abita strawberry chocolate, and I would definitely recommend it. Abita is the local Louisiana beer, and the flavor was prominent but mixed well with the strawberry and chocolate, both of which were also easily discernible. My boyfriend got a scoop of the French vanilla, and this was a simpler flavor that was also quite good. For some reason, it tasted vaguely of coconut. I swallowed my six little scoops with ease then crawled in the back of our rental car and lay down like a beached whale. I had two huge meals and a good dose of ice cream weighing me down, and it was only 5 o'clock. I slept like a bloated Ignatius J. Reilly all the way to Baton Rouge.

text: I was recomended by a fellow restaurant owner in around this area that said that the food here was excellent. Unfortunately, it turned out to be the opposite for the dishes I ordered. 1) Tom Yum Soup (chicken) ($5.00) - Perhaps my expectations for a this soup was too high. The sourness of the soup was there however the rest of the ingredients failed to impress me - tomatoes and red peppers (not a native ingredient for this soup) were too hard and crunchy and the chicken was dumped in and boiled with the soup (tough) just before serving. 2) Mee Siam ($11.00) - The menu described it as yellow noodles with a dark brown sauce. When it came out it was glass noodles stir fried in soy sauce. NOTE to the chef: The Brocolli and Green beans did not go well with the dish. - It tasted rather bland Perhaps the reason for the quality of the food was because I had arrived on a night when there was a special booking for a party of 14. My idea of a good authentic Thai restaurant (or for any other foreign restaurant) is one that preserves the original recipes so that patrons can get glimpse of what food from Thailand tastes like. Unfortunately, Bangkok City has adjusted their recipes to ensure that they survive - which is something I can understand. Its as 'nice' as any other Thai restaurants within a 5 mile radius. If you want authentic Tom Yum soup - try the Singapore Restaurant in Mount Laurel. It is by far the most authentic receipe that I can find in this area. I will attempt this place once again in the future to try some other dishes and perhaps my view of the place may change. Please do feel free to recommend any if you have been here before.
label: NEG

text: My boyfriend and I drove 5 hours from Chicago to attend a concert that was playing at The Pageant that night. We chose this hotel because it was located not far from the venue, and seemed to be a nice place to stay. We were a little put off when we got there and there were cops searching a room near ours...but ok. We got to the front counter and the receptionist was extremely rude, and decided to finish up her conversation on her cell phone before she helped us, even though she knew we were there. She did not say, please, thank you, have a nice stay, nothing. She simply frowned the whole time, handed us our keys, and turned her back to us. My boyfriend and I shared puzzled looks, but assumed she was just fighting with a boyfriend. Fighting with your boyfriend during your shift working the front desk of a busy hotel is always a spectacular idea. So, her behavior immediately set the feel for the entire experience, but that was nothing compared to the room. The light fixtures were crooked, the toilet seat was cracked and yellowed, there was a wet spot the size of a tire on our floor, probably from cleaning up barf or pee, but the thing that got me the most was the dried blood speckled on the underside of the comforter. I think once their is blood spackle on your comforter, it's safe to say that it needs a good wash, or promptly shoved into the garbage. Luckily my boyfriend had accidentally booked a double room online, so we took both comforters off each bed and made up for it by doubling up the sheets on one lumpy, uncomfortable bed. I felt the need to sleep in a hazmat suit (I think there should be a set that come complimentary with the room), but alas, I settled with clothes. Normally, I am not picky about hotel rooms, and I understand that sometimes a few repairs are going to be needed in older hotels once in awhile, but the room was completely unacceptable. We gladly bolted out of there the next morning, passed a few shirtless rednecks on the way out, sharing a bottle of whiskey with the blinds open, so we got one last surprise before we left atleast. We would strongly advise anyone going to that area so steer clear of this hotel. It was definitely not worth the $100.00+ we paid to stay there! There are a bunch of surrounding hotels that we heard after wards are much better! We will never, ever go back to this hotel, and if you do, good luck to you.
label: NEG

text: The towering icing presents a serious challenge - should you start at the top and eat your way down or nibble away at the sides of the mountain and risk a landslide/avalanche of sugar? These are top-heavy cupcakes, but they look beautiful. And yes they are huge and a bit costly ($3+ each), but look at it this way - one cupcake could feed a family of four for the night! OK, maybe not quite a balanced meal, but certainly a giddy one. Approaching the cupcake is intimidating, but the frosting on the wedding cake one that I tried was actually a bit lighter than I had anticipated and the cake part was delicious too. Plus, I love the presentation - from the frosting and decorations of the cakes themselves to the beautiful gift box that keeps the cupcakes from toppling in transit. A Gigi's cupcake makes a good impression on your sweetie when you bring it home as a gift. My biggest gripe? Parking is no fun at this Broadway location, although the same could be said for most of the businesses in the immediate vicinity.

text: The phrase "neighborhood gem" was made for places like The Legend. We go here at least a few times a month, often once a week, and are never disappointed by the quality of the food. The owners are really great people, and you'll find them talking and laughing with their patrons pretty much any time you go in. We find ourselves bumping into the same people over and over again here, as once you go to The Legend once or twice, you pretty much become a regular. Our favorites include the pork tenderloin, shrimp cocktail, baked salmon, and the vegetable medley. Their mashed potatoes are also some of the best in town. Hopefully The Legend will start getting more attention from outside the neighborhood. It's one of the places that makes Irvington "Irvington", and well worth checking out even if it's not just right down the street from you.

text: So ever since I got here I've been told to go to Cochon by everyone. Unfortunately, the day we went, I was coming down with something that left me without an appetite. So I watched, as our entire table ordered a variety of plates that I have to admit, sound a little gross on the menu. But you know what? They all looked amazing. So I had a few bites here and there, and was pleasantly surprised. They WERE amazing. After everyone finished their entrees, our server offered us a dessert menu, making sure to mention that strawberry shortcake is also available for the evening. I'm a sucker for a good strawberry shortcake and thought I could tolerate a few bites. However, when it showed up, I couldn't resist and uncomfortably pigged out. Oh, it was worth it. If you don't go for anything else go for the strawberry shortcake. Who knows how long it will be on the menu! Even though I guess it wasn't... Here's what it came down to: with one entree, a beer, and a dessert, the bill came to like $50 with tip. Most of the time, I get furious paying that much for food I know I can make myself at home. What I liked about Cochon is we walked out of there feeling like our money went somewhere good. I could NOT have made the stuff at home (except maybe the strawberry shortcake, but it was only like $7 anyway). It was not a waste of money. That means a lot these days. I plan to go again, and I plan to bring my appetite with me! If you have guests in town who want to experience some good local dishes, this is the place to go. And non-locals - don't be afraid of the menu. It's all good, I promise.

text: (continued from previous update) The state of Arizona versus UA: This is an important delineation, since I fear that our universities often suffer the consequences of bad state policy in Arizona. As a native of the state, I've seen this play out as a mostly political game with the constituents as the losers in many cases. However, unlike in some other states at present (CA comes to mind -- sorry, I'm less familiar with OR), this is nothing new to Arizona. The universities are already well practiced in finding their own solutions to state budget problems. In the early 2000s, for instance, the state government accounted for only 17% of the UA's total budget (and falling), which I think is horrible state policy that appears doomed to persist for the near future. However, the UA in recent decades has devised a resilient strategy practically built around maintaining two separate identities: one as a public land grant institution beholden to its state and community and one as a leading research institution with a strong national alumni base. Each has its benefits and drawbacks, depending on your perspective, but I believe this has kept the UA on track to continue creating greatness in an otherwise challenged environment. If only the state legislature would recognize the amazing ROI from investing in its universities, we'd have fewer complaints about the state component. But trust that the UA continues to thrive despite this challenge, especially with the help of devoted and successful alumni. Bear down!

text: As I was walking around Southgate Shopping Center this store called Tea Desire caught my eye. The outside of it looked so cute and almost peaceful; it really drew me in. So, as you can imagine, this place specializes in tea and tea products like teacups and pots along with other tea accessories. What I mean by tea accessories is they carry items that would make your tea drinking experience less messy. They carried those tea filters things; if you use tealeaves instead of tea bags you would use this special filter to isolate your tealeaves so that they are not floating around everywhere. I really loved their teacups and teapots that you can buy as a matching set. They had some cute ones with crazy designs, but I really like the solid colored ones. Some of the colors they had were so nice. If you were interested in specialized teacups with the filters inside of them and lips on the tops then this is the place to come. I've actually never seen this in Canada but I have seen cups that come equipped with a lid when I was in Korea. The filters are removable and the lids let you probably steep your tea to get the most out of the leaves. If you also prefer tealeaves and fresh tealeaves to boot then Tea Desire is the place to get your fresh tea from. The store is really great and eye-catching, both inside and out. The staff is pretty friendly and is eager to help you out. I do have to say that this is one place to come to in order to fulfill all or any of your tea desires!

text: Technically, my rating is 4.5 stars, but Yelp doesn't let you give halves. Sometimes it's difficult being a vegetarian foodie, especially one with a mushroom allergy. At Bayona, it was pretty effortless, starting with making the reservation. Upon calling I had several questions and they were all met with a good, helpful attitude which set a really good tone for the evening. When we arrived the same helpful woman (I recognized her voice) greeted us and seated us in the parlor-type area for drinks while our table was prepared. She had a good knowledge of the wine list and her recommendation for a red (Tempranillo/Cabernet Sauvignon blend) was spot on! Once seated, we were greeted by our server's assistant, who was adorable and charming. He brought a small dish of olives and curried and pickled veggies, which were super tasty. Our main server greeted us next. He has an extremely cheerful demeanor and seemed to genuinely love his job and the food he serves. Right off the bat he gave us a great explanation of the menu (including when something was made with chicken stock WITHOUT ME ASKING!). I let him know that I was a vegetarian with a mushroom allergy and he immediately suggested some ways to modify or combine existing menu items. He also took my dietary restrictions to the Chef de Cuisine and let him come up with some dishes that he would want to make based on what he had in the pantry. I know sometimes chefs can get snippy about modifying their dishes (each component has a purpose, I know!), so I was excited to see what he would come up with. Before I go into what my mom and I ordered, I want to say three words: SWEET POTATO BRIOCHE! Moving on. My mom settled started with the Bayona salad. The portion was unexpectedly large. It was well-dressed (don't you hate when restaurants drown your salad? I do!) and had a slight sweetness that paired well with the shaved parmigiano reggiano. My mom didn't finish her salad (saving room), so I gobbled it right up! For her entrée, she went with the pan-seared pancetta-wrapped halibut, broccoli flan, and shoestring potatoes. After the first bite of halibut the only thing she could say was "outstanding." The broccoli flan was amazing (mom was nice enough to share). Those aren't two words that I would have put together before my trip to Bayona, but it's now something that I am hoping to replicate at home. The only "bad" thing my mom had to say was "I would have been okay with more shoestring potatoes." I began with the Greek salad, which was on the daily specials menu. I was extremely pleased with the proportions of the ingredients in my salad as all too often someone gets carried away with the feta. Not here. You don't always see garbanzo beans on a Greek salad, but I enjoyed the addition. For my entrée, I chose to go with one of the chef's options: gnocchi, sautéed spinach and broccolini, and puréed tomato confit. This dish has converted me from feeling luke-warm about gnocchi into a HUGE FAN. And kudos on not overcooking the spinach. So many people do that I generally refuse to order it. Thanks, Bayona, for not making me regret taking those risks. So where's the reason for the half-star deduction in the rating? I had a pretty good conversation with the server about my mushroom allergy. He repeated it back to me several times and yet my entrée arrived topped with hen of the woods mushrooms. Everyone was extremely apologetic and it was quickly resolved. A new plate was fired up and delivered piping hot, but it's a big pet peeve when my plate is delivered with poison on it. The simply charming aesthetic of the interior and the courtyard charming is a perfect fit for the vibe of the food. I only wish I had been able to tummy-rub the restaurant's cat (I believe his name is Crusty). OH! I almost forgot!! My mom purchased Susan Spicer's cookbook, and we came back for it the following day as they had held it so it could be signed. Unfortunately Susan wasn't going to be in before our flight left so they graciously offered to ship the book to my mom at no charge. Way to go, Bayona staff!

text: It was one of those great meals. Classy joint, with classy decor and classy menus with classy wine lists. A once in a while place where the food is so good you continue eating even after you are full because it is just that good. Our waiter was very professional. Besides the fact that he was sweating a bit, he was charming and dealt with a table of 9 women well. That is not an easy task. We had 8:45 reservations, so by the time we ordered, they were out of almost everything. I was sad they didn't have my scallops, but it made my happy that when they say everything is flown in fresh that day, they aren't lying. I would rather have something else that fresh than the meal I wanted that had been thawed out "just in case". Smoked oysters. We were all blown away. So delicate and flavorful. As were the lobster dumplings, which were more like lobster ravioli from heaven. It was one of those things where we took a bite and all looked at each other in amazement. I miss them already. They didn't have the scallops I wanted (I can get those here, no biggie) so I had the lemon fish with crab and lobster butter. Wow. Others had the seared tuna, the veal, and the steak. No one was disappointed. It was rich, but I ate it all anyway. How often do I get lobster butter? Another dish worth mentioning is the mashed sweet potatoes with vanilla bean and banana. Good, but too dessert-y for me. Actual dessert lived up to the meal. Molten chocolate cake and apple pie. Both two of the best versions of each dish I have had, especially the cake. On the rich side, so we all just had a bite. If I could learn to recreate that, I would be one happy (and fat) lady. Five stars all around - if you are in New Orleans and feel like splurging, put this place on your list.

text: I make it a rule to keep my expectations low for chain restaurants. Even so, I found the St. Charles Outback to be below par. At first glance, this looked a lot like Chili's with an Aussie flair. Substitute a different shade of sauce with the Bloomin' Onion and it could pass for an Awesome Blossom; exchange the plastic boomerangs and crocodiles on the wall for quirky license plates and signs, and you've got Chili's. We ordered the Aweso-- I mean, Bloomin' Onion, to share because we were craving something deeply unhealthy and fried, but didn't want to have a heart attack mid-dinner. Even though I ate only a few pieces, it was oily enough to coat my hands and my stomach, so I felt obligated to order a salad. I went with the Roasted Filet Wedge Salad, but replaced the blue cheese dressing with Italian because it already came with blue cheese crumbles. I was quite disappointed when it came; it looked like 1/6 a head of iceberg lettuce with 2-3 halved grape tomatoes on the side, a few crumbles of bacon, and chunks of blue cheese. I ordered my filet medium well; they must have a different interpretation of that term in St. Louis because half was well-done, half was medium rare. And that's just the meat that wasn't completely fat -- as hard as it tried to disguise itself underneath a black coat of char, the fat gave itself away with a wobble whenever I approached it with a knife. Definitely disappointing for a $13 entree. At Outback, what you see on the menu is what you get. Don't order baby back ribs and expect a side; the ribs will just come out on a plate and stare brownly at you, unadorned with any veggies. When it says "served with crisps of bacon," look forward to 2 pieces, the very minimum for a noun to become plural. You may be lucky if you get 3. I usually keep my expectations low when dining at chain restaurants; Outback may have brought my bar to a new low. +1 star for the complimentary honey-wheat bread and whipped butter

text: As you may or may not know, Copia had a fire back in 2008 and they've finally reopened. Thank goodness they have because my initial reaction is "freaking awesome." The beautiful wife and I trekked here for lunch this afternoon. I'll start of saying that it was delicious, but that I wish we had come here for dinner (more on that later). The interior (normally something I don't care about) is really nice, very "fashionable upscale" -- not snooty, but rather there was a lot of thought put into it. And there are those cascading water panes of glass separating the bar area from the main dinning room. It's pretty cool, but admittedly, if you focus on them, you go might into a trance. We perused the wine list. Here's the great thing about having a restaurant connected to a wine shop -- the prices are LOW. Freaking wonderful low. Now, they do charge a corkage fee ($8), but eve with that, you're still great a pretty decent value. So, if you're a person that enjoy more than a glass or two, this is the spot. Admittedly, I didn't know about the corkage fee initially -- maybe it was mentioned on the wine list and I skipped over it, but our server explained this after we got the bill. On to the food. I had the prime rib French dip with housemade chips. This wasn't Sunday crappy buffet prime rib -- it was all meat and barely any fat. Delicious. And they put the horseradish in a condiment cup on the side, so you can heat to your own desire. I'll let the beautiful wife do a recap of her dish (the pulled pork sandwich), but I tasted it and its accompanying sides and thought it was tasty. Now, why did I wish we had gone there for dinner? While the lunch menu was very "Downtown business lunch" the dinner menu was "rival your favorite spot" interesting. Unfortunately, they don't have a web site up, but there were a number of dishes that sounded excellent. Note that while the average lunch offering was around $9-12, dinner is in the $25-30 range. Service was friendly and efficient (though admittedly, there was only two other people eating). But I got that nice feeling that our server was happy he was working there. They're still getting things in order on the wine shop side of things, but they should be offering a lot of different bottles. I can't wait to go back here for dinner, though I'll have to clean up a little bit. Not sure about things like wine flights, but that may develop as things settle down.

text: Because TCBY knew better, South Street was presented with the self-serve soft-serve froyo experience known as Phileo. It was all the rage last year when it first opened up, so much so that they had a sign on the front door asking patrons to please not take photos. What? This isn't Brad and Angelina we're talking about here, this is a fackin' treatery! So step inside and dig the space-age (that is, the "space-age" as lampooned by Woody Allen in "Sleepers"), barely-there atmosphere as you gawk at the various flavors of self-serve frozen yogurt. There's the usual fruit assortments, as well as variations on the chocolate and vanilla themes, and the occasional bizarro flavor just to retain enough hipness. But Capogiro this ain't. Out of all the rotating selections, though, my fave has always simply been the "original yogurt" flavor. Oddly sour yet sweet enough to THROW SHIT ON TOP OF! YES!!! After punishing your paper cup thingy with your choice of froyo flavor(s), be sure to stop by the edible knick-knack bar, featuring plenty of rather unappetizing crapola to throw on top and make it FUN, FUN, FUN. They have Cap'n Crunch and Cocoa Krispies! Hey, is that Froot Loops? Hold on a minute, why are those banana slices looking a bit naff? God, are those fruit flies flying around this junk? Are they part of the bar as well? Finally, chuck your creation up on the scale and pay by weight! At first this seems like a keen idea, but then you look down at all the crap you just piled on top of your yogurt and feel like you could have done without half of it. As soon as you sit down and start eating it, you realize this to be true even more as Lucky Charms were never meant to go with tangerines. Oh well. But we the people in America love a gimmick, and that's all that this joint is. The staff always seems to be on autopilot and the most annoying teenyboppers are the main customers, allowing everyone to see their terrible South Street night out fashions under the wonderful fluorescent lighting. Dollface swore she wouldn't go back in after seeing some young kids there wiping their fingers under the dispensers and licking their fingers clean afterward. Just stay home, people. Or head over to Franklin Fountain or the aforementioned Capogiro. When you see Phileo, just keep right on walking by. Hasn't South Street suffered enough?

text: Been a Great Basin FCU member for 20 years. They closed the branch closest to me so I decided to go here to withdraw money since I had to be in this part of town any way. The bank teller asked for my driver's license so I could make a withdrawal. I saw her run it through some machine. I asked what that was. She said they scan an image of your driver's license they have it on their computers and don't have to ask you for it each time. Not just your driver's license photo. Your entire license image is in their computer system. I explained I wasn't comfortable with this because of identity theft issues. I was one of the people who got a letter from St. Mary's saying my personal data had been breached by an ID thief. She agreed to delete the image. I asked why she didn't ask me if I wanted my driver's license scanned. She said it never occurred to her to ask. Now I understand that banks already have access to lots of information we would consider personal. But the goal here, I believe, is to reduce the risks of thefts, not increase them. Great Basin should tell customers their driver's licenses are going to be copied before they do this. I don't know if they sent this out in information to customers. I never saw this. I wonder how many thousands of Great Basin FCU customers don't know that there's a picture of their driver's license in the credit union computer.

We were blown away. The salad was delicious--it was mixed with what had to be a mix of lemon juice and drizzle of olive oil and some herbs, but it was definitely fresh and not heavy at all. Both platers were delicious, and their falafel is some of the best I've tried in Philly. There was more than enough food, to the point that we didn't even touch the rice. And even though we left stuffed, we didn't feel gross or heavy afterwards since the food wasn't greasy (not even the falafel). This place definitely left an impression because my sister and I couldn't shut up about how yummy dinner was at the movie we went to that night, or even at brunch the next day. text: Following rave reviews by Edmonton news, media, and internet blogs, it was decided that The Blue Pear would be the next restaurant splurge. I mean, having been called either the best or second best restaurant in Edmonton, no price can be too large right? So reservations were made for Sunday to take advantage of the Baby Pear special for a $59 three course dinner. First impressions: the front door is locked! Don't worry, they're not closed, you just need to ring the doorbell to enter. We were seated in the small dining room consisting of about 8-10 tables. Nice and cozy right? wrong. Tables were spaced too close, and the live sax and piano playing that night made it impossible to have a conversation. It was always a relief when the musicians took their coffee break. We were met by who we assumed to be the owner, a surly middle aged woman with a natural scowl. When we said we would be fine with water, we were replied with "would that be just tap water?" No, we would like Don Perrier with "just tap water" ice. Anyways, on to the food Bread: Completely boring and disappointing. Slices of white and brown bread that looks and tastes of any department store bread. Compared to say, Wildflower's in-house baked brioche and choice of goat's or cow's butter, base lead vs. sublime gold? Appetizers: Corn chowder - with popcorn and white truffle oil. Probably the best dish of the night. Fragrant corn flavour, with bits of fresh corn and smokey toasty popcorn, accented well with a hint of truffle. Salad - classic combo with serrano ham, canteloupe, arugula, and what they called a balsamic "glee", basically 3 drops of balsamic on an uninspired salad Entree: Beef three ways - Certainly a sad and boring plate if I've ever seen one. Three pieces of brown with a brown sauce. Braised beef cheeks, grilled tenderloin, and oxtail-potato terrine type square. All covered in a reduced red-wine sauce, all tasted exactly the same. To accompany the beef, brown and mushy green tomatoes with a marrow crumble, heavy and sludgy, the opposite of what you want to be paired with such a leaden dish. One of the worst dishes I've had, from any restaurant. Different textures of brown is what it should have been called as everything tasted pretty much the same. Duck - Cherry wood smoked duck confit, seared duck breast, cabbage hash with poached egg, with local sour cherry and mustard jam, accompanied with a foie gras biscuit. All four elements isolated in a lonely corner on a square plate. Duck breast was nicely seared and paired well with a tart cherry sauce. Duck confit so salty it was inedible, your kidneys will wince with every bite. Cabbage hash with poached egg was flavourful but lacked connection with the rest of the dish. Dessert: Creme brulee - Well it wasn't creme brulee, it was more like gelatinized cream with a carmelized sugar circle placed on top, if you could have rubberized vanilla for dessert this was it. First of all, how is it possible to turn a creme brulee out of its ramekin and have it still standing perfectly upright? shame on you. Might have just called it vanilla jello. Flourless chocolate cake - Tasty and rich chocolate goodness with orange liqueur and orange sorbet. Simple and good. Orange and chocolate, can't go wrong with that. Conclusion: Overly pretentious, pompous, and poorly thought out dishes made for an evening that certainly begged for more. It wasn't so much that the food wasn't worth it, it was just plain bad. It wasn't the price but the overall quality and execution of the food that was poor. Espeically with a price tag of over $120 for a dinner for two, you won't see me ringing The Blue Pear's doorbell again. Compared to my meal at Wildflower Grill, where you could tell they put emphasis on satisfying the customer and ensuring that felt appreciated, every dish thoughtfully planned and constructed, the Blue Pear fell far behind in every aspect.

The short ribs were warm, but everything else on the plate was stone cold - the same for me - the burger was OK, but the fries were burned and cold. Fries and gnocchi were replaced quickly. text: 1 star because I graced the building with my baptism. This is easily one of the most gorgeous buildings in the city. Stained glass abounds in the chapel and paintings abound in the Cathedral. The ceiling is studded with metalwork and the whole building is lined with alcoves, three-walled rooms dedicated to different sacred individuals and events. I'm going to stop describing it. I'm not arrogant enough to think that I can articulate the beauty here. Best time to visit is the middle of a weekday when it's empty. Come inside, let your eyes adjust to the darkness, and walk down the center aisle like you're the Pope. It's an experience. But no flash photography. That's not sacred. Despite the aesthetic wonders, Peter & Paul has one of the coldest, meanest, unfriendliest congregations in the city. Services here, especially those in the chapel, are awfully cold. I grew up mere blocks from this place. It was our family's parish & yet we never felt welcome. This is the heart of the diocese, which means that it is stuffed to the gills with visitors during Easter and Christmas. At all other times, there are much fewer bodies in the pews, and I wonder if the bodies that are there have any soul.

text: This Sawmill location is struggling for an identity, experienced managers and staff you would expect behind a register at a fast food restaurant. We parked in front of what appeared to be the main entrance only to find out that was the lounge for the hotel. When we informed them that we had reservations, we were directed down a hotel corridor with kids in wet swimming suits dripping with water. When we arrived and asked where we could have drinks before our guests arrived, we were directed back to the separate lounge. We opted to go ahead and sit down at the table to have a drink. Three tables within sight were feasting on toothpicks after their glutenous all you can eat disease infested salad bar. Flys were crawling all over the salad bar so I opted to switch to ordering alacarte. Unfortunately, the steak was cheap as the service. I ordered a New York Strip and was brought a Top Sirloin "baseball" steak. When I asked to have it corrected, the Manager (who looked 22 years old) stated that I was probably not familiar with meat cuts. I decided not to argue even though I've dined at some of the finest and most expensive steakhouses across North America. But for a $30 steal, I guess you get what you pay for. I'd rather pay $40-$50 and have a better steak and service. The wine list consisted of a limited selection of lower end wines at fair prices but could be expanded. The decorations and atmosphere was nice and well appointed; one of a higher end restaurant. Our waitress was a metaphor for the evening; we saw our waitress three times during the evening. I later spotted in the parking lot with her friends sucking down on a cigarette. She muttered "thanks for coming" while exhaling. The manager and bus boy took care of our needs. While they were working hard they were clearly new to the restaurant industry. The bottom line is that this is a good steakhouse for the bourgeoisie who have families who have minimal expectations. You can grab an average baseball steak in a nice atmosphere at a decent price point. For those seeking a better steak or someone who is celebrating a special occasion, spend a little more and go to Chop, Ruth Chris, or another. $200 for 3 people would go alot further in any of these versus the worn out tradition of Sawmill which has become too confident in their name and is showing in their service!

text: Well... I was at 5th and South and my fiance and I simply weren't in the mood for the overstuffed stomachs that a Jim's steak or Lorenzo's Pizza slice would provide. So, we decided to try some sushi from Niji Sushi House. When we open the door, a small, empty sushi house with 6 tables and a bar greets us. The restaurant was light on Japanese atmosphere, but had the necessary one or two bamboo items scattered around the room. The hostess greeted us and gave us the table of our choosing. My fiance and I opted to split an order of Miso Soup, Steak Teriyaki (which comes with Miso Soup, Salad, and Rice), and two sushi rolls - Spicy Tuna and the Lovely Couple (which we thought was named accordingly for us). The Soups came out quickly and deliciously - bigger than average bowls of tasty Miso Soup. The house salad, consisting of lots of lettuce, a few cucumbers and two carrot nubs, came with a peanut-based salad dressing on the side that my fiance rather enjoyed. Let's just say, the meal peaked with the soup. Our Beef Teriyaki arrived shortly after our salad was finished and boy was it depressing. The Beef strips were just at the point of being too large to shove whole in your mouth. Being the man that I am, I shoved it all into my mouth anyway. After chewing for about 15 seconds I look up to see my fiance having issues cutting the meat in half with her fork. Once she finally gets her cutlery through the beef and tries her first bite, she realizes the same thing I had already figured out a minute ago - this meat cannot be bitten through! We chewed and chewed and simply could not get through it! I had to spit the piece out into a napkin just as my fiance swallowed hers whole ("except for the pieces that were stuck in her teeth", she reminded me). We talked about how horrible it was - it didn't even taste like teriyaki! - and decided to complain. The hostess returned quickly and didn't have much of a response when we told her how horrible our first bites had been. She simply said "Oh? Ok? You don't have to eat it," and walked away - leaving the plate of unfinished "Beef" on our table. A minute later the cook came out of the kitchen and asked what was wrong, we quickly explained the problem and we're not even sure he spoke English. We can't remember if he said anything at all to us, but we're certain that neither employee said "Sorry" or "Would you like us to remake it?" or "Would you like to order something else?" -- any of which would have been expected of a restaurant employee dealing with an unhappy guest. Our sushi had since arrived and we both tentatively tried a piece. Although the flavor was decidedly average, our experience with the Beef Teriyaki caused us both to lose our appetites and we ended up eating only half the rolls in front of us. The fish in them were certainly mushy and the Wasabi was uninspiring without the kick that usually accompanies this green delicacy. We received our bill, just over $18, even with the Beef Teriyaki taken off (they added extra cost for the salad, rice, and soup that comes with the meal), paid it, and ran out quickly - laughing about how this could be our worst meal we've ever had together. I immediately decided to check out the Yelp ratings, and saw only one other review. I've had to both brush and floss since we've returned and my fiance is quickly putting together a simple Mac and Cheese meal to ease our stomachs.
