text: Came here tonight for dinner with the amazing Erin G, Tim G, Kelly H, Derek, and Andrew M! That's a lotta yelpers in one room! Sweet. Anyway, the atmosphere was lovely. The lighting was dim, but that added a sense of..mystique? I don't know. But I liked it. It was very chic, but not overly pretentious. I started out with a delicious drink called the Juice Box. It had 3 Olives Grape, sweet and sour, cranberry juice, and a splash of sprite. It was delicious! I loved it. Now on to the food! Mosaic is a tapas place, so that means lots of small plates...which in my mind means more food for me to sample! Sweet. I started with the lobster salad: lobster, guacamole, valencia oranges, and chive sour creme. It was very light and tasty. I'm normally not a big fan of chives, but it actually worked here. The presentation was neat as well. Next were the pot stickers: suckling pig (!!), shaved celery, thai peanut sauce. This wasn't my favorite. The potstickers were okay, and I liked the crunchiness of the shell, but come on, Mosaic -- if you're going to be bold enough to call the filling 'suckling pig', you gotta back it up with some bold flavors! It was just missing something. It wasn't BAD, it just didn't have that wow factor. We went with the short rib mini burgers next: maple smoked white cheddar, truffled brioche bun, smoked ketchup, potato croquettes. Now THIS had wow factor, guys! Definitely one of the best parts of the meal. The burgers were tiny, which sucks, but I suppose they were supposed to be tiny (we are talking tapas here). It was so good. The meat was fantastic! And the smoked ketchup was amazing. I'm not a huge ketchup fan, but this was NIIIIICE. The potato croquettes were like nothing I've ever tried before. They were fluffy and light and went nicely with the ketchup. Last but not least *drumroll please*....BREAD PUDDING! I've been on a bread pudding roll lately, and Mosaic did a really nice job with theirs. It had tequila soaked raisins (!!!), romepope anglaise, and dulce de leche ice cream. Although the menu described the ice cream as dulce de leche, it really tasted like pineapple. Is the menu wrong or are my tastebuds screwy? Who knows! I have no idea what romepope anglaise is, but whatever it was made the bread pudding all the more delicious. I have to add this to my top 5 bread pudding experiences of all time. This might even tie Harvest's bread pudding for the number one spot! I don't know. The service was super friendly, and our waiter was nice and helpful and refilled our drinks promptly. He also had no problem splitting the checks for us. For me, this will be more of a special occasion place (because $55 for dinner is not cheap!), but I will definitely return. Yum yum yum!

text: The bottom line with Pasta Plus: you get what you pay for. If you're looking for something fast and cheap and aren't too concerned about the quality, you probably won't mind Pasta Plus. But if you want more than just decent quality, I would stay away from this place. It's a cute little place on Central Avenue, just south of Forsyth. When you walk in you'll see that the atmosphere won't blow you away, as it's meant to be a quick, cheap place to get a bite (and it's definitely not the kind of place you want to go on a date). You take your order at the counter and your food is brought out to you on a tray with styrofoam plates. They have a wide variety of pastas, pizzas and salads, and if you play your cards right you can get a full meal for under $8. Their pastas with tomato sauces are probably your best bet; the quality is not fantastic but it's pretty decent. But beyond that I'm not too thrilled with Pasta Plus. I got their pesto pasta once, and it wasn't much of a pesto sauce. It was basically liquefied margarine with some green specks and some salt and garlic. It had no taste, and the pasta itself was a pallid white color. I got some grilled chicken and vegetables on it, and those didn't have any taste either. The chicken was mushy and chewy and tasted like it was stuck in the microwave for ten minutes, and the broccoli was still light green and I question whether or not they actually cooked it. The bread they served with the meal was two slices of generic white Italian bread with some margarine. Nothing too special. I will probably avoid this place in the future simply because the quality of the food I've had there has been mediocre at best. But if you're looking for cheap pasta and pizza and don't mind sacrificing quality to save a few bucks, this is the place for you.

Sorry for that mental image, but it was as disgusting as it sounds! Hot and sour soup was basically....a container of congealed yellow, way overly salted jello. I asked for everything "extra spicy"....and apparently the only spice they had was salt. Even if it weren't tasty, I would have probably still eaten it just because I'm lazy/busy/don't want to cook. text: I have my reasons, for never having tried Indian food. The 2 words that would best describe it , are " Stubborness" and " Curry". My pickiness is legendary, and I credit Yelp with breaking alot of my culinary prejudices. Era, Han Dynasty, Zot and now New Delhi, have broadened my edible horizons. Of course in this case, I credit Blake, for forcing me to break my Indian food cherry. It was her Indian food UYE, where she called me out specifically, that introduced me to the world of Naan bread and Tandoori chicken. Vishnu must have really wanted me to eat Indian food. As it turned out, I had my kids on the night of the UYE and would have to miss the event. I had settled in, to a night of Funniest home videos and board games, disappointing both myself and others, who had wanted to see me get smacked down by ND's buffet. However, Karma was on my side and the class my wife takes on Wed was cut short. She showed up a little before 7,and I rushed to make it to ND on time for the event. Luckily, it was in a part of the city I knew well, as my therapist's office is across the street. This was ideal, in the possible scenario that the scary foreign food would make me need to get some mental help in a hurry, I would just need to crawl across the street. As it turned out, there was no need. Between the great company and tasty food, I was mentally set, for at least a week. New Delhi is a cozy little restraunt, with a delicious looking spread of Indian food. After communing with some Yelpers, old and new, Blake was kind enough to be my guide at the Buffet and thank Shiva for that! She explained what each thing was and made great suggestions. I tried a little of everything and deemed the Naan bread and Tandoori chicken my favorites. I would need another visit to get a better idea of some of the other entrees, and I'm sure it will happen in the near future. There was even a bar there, although I didn't partake...this time. We also had a blast with the desserts. Its amazing how much mileage a good "balls" joke will get, with a bunch of supposed adults. However I did not get the Balls dessert, no matter how much Aaron begged me. I tried the Pistachio ice cream, which had a name that sounded like coffee. As a matter of fact, I thought I was ordering coffee until they placed the dish of tan ice cream in front of me. My embarrassment turned to joy, as the frozen treat was awesome. Upon leaving, I felt like I had such a good experience, that I thought I would walk across the street and cancel all future therapy sessions. It was only when Aaron forced me to ride him piggyback across 41st street that I realized I actually needed to double the appointments...and I'm sure the homeless guy, and everyone else who witnessed it felt the same way.

text: Pretty good pizza, but not the best, and a better-than-average salad bar earn this four stars from me. This place opened about three months ago next to the new convenience store at Greg and McCarran in Sparks. The address is South Stanford Way, but don't be confused by that. It's on McCarran Boulevard. I went and got a salad bar and a 10-inch pizza. The salad bar stands out for having lots of fresh ingredients. The purple onions had obviously been freshly cut. The lettuce was fresh. And the bacon bits weren't that dried, processed Bacos-type stuff. You could tell they used to be bacon at one time. The good ingredients carried over to the pizza topping as well. I got The Coliseum Supreme and pretty much each topping was tasty. None of the flavorless processed food like you get in the chains. The sauce didn't seem distinctive. It wasn't good or bad. The pizza was a little too doughy. They may not have let it cook long enough. I'll ask for it crispy next time. The salad bar and the pizza came to $17. Not something I can do every day. But they offer all-you-can-eat pizza and salad bar for lunch for $7. That could be a screaming good deal. I'll have to try it. As a bonus, they have lots of nice HD TVs.

I have looked at other bed and breakfasts, but, for the coziness and price of this place, there is no way. For Big Bowls I had the tofu hot pot and my date had the beef noodle soup (I can't remember exactly what it was called). Both were good, hot, and comforting on a cooler November evening. Now for my not so good part. Our service was kinda awful. I wanted another cocktail before my entree even came and she didn't come back till midway through when I asked to see the beer/wine list. She then disappeared until we were pretty much through with our meal. When you're out for the evening you want the cocktails to keep flowing if need be! Also when our bill came my dish was listed as a $1 more expensive on the bill than on the menu. Odd but I didn't feel like tracking our waitress down. Total bill came to $51 plus tip for a cocktail, a beer, an appetizer, two entrees, and a side of veggie fried rice. If you're in the mood for something a little different I'd suggest checking KONG out.

text: We were three friends having a lovely time in New Orleans. Decided to try Jacques-Imos because of all the great reviews and the "strange experience" it promised...Well, I dont think 90 minutes wait is a strange experience, it's a bad experience. Everyone says the wait is customary and I don't get that either. if you're in that much demand, hike up your prices because that's good business sense. Anyway, the food was okay. The corn muffins are delicious, seriously and this comes from someone who hates corn muffins. The house salad is a plate of yummy baby spinach with a single fried salad. I wolfed it down. The main dishes all come with sides and some of them were absolutely delicious - the rice and beans, potatoes, corn. So what's the catch? The main courses are not avant grade. Mind you this is a New orleans restaurant with manhattan prices so the food better be awesome. I ordered a carpet bagger steak which is a steak stuffed and seared with oysters - sounds amazing right? And it would have been if the steak didn't have chunks of fat. Sorry, but I expect the cut to be perfect! For what it's worth, they got it done medium rare just as I wanted. I ate half of the steak (such a waste). My friends had the chicken pontalbo (absolutely delicious) and rack of lamb (which turned out to be a lamb sirloin when it was served - not cool). All in all, it was not a satisfying experience and was made worse by the fact that we waited so long. Give it pass. Also, you have to take a cab really far out and you will be tempted by the fact that "maple leaf bar" is nearby... This bar is also totally over-rated. I give Jacques Imos a big FAIL.

text: The studio is beautiful. The massage area is cozy, dark and soothing. And then there's the ever-talented Zoe. Aside from getting semi-regular massage tune-ups over the years , I've gone to Zoe for trouble-fixes more than once. I have recurring problems with my back and several bulging disks that act up during times of stress, etc. At one point in 2001 when I had a flare-up, I wasn't able to touch my toes for 3 months. I had some deep-tissue massage from Zoe, who assessed and worked with me to see how much pressure I could stand. It was truly a miracle. I went from being someone who, even with narcotic pain killers, couldn't stand up straight, sit comfortably, lie down flat, or walk without pressing my hand to my spine like a rudder, and who took 5 minutes to get in & out of a car (even though I was only 25 at that point), to someone who had 50% more mobility in 2-3 days and 85% mobility in a week. I'd gone to 5 or 6 different specialists at Ochsner, tried a chiropractor, had MRIs, bone scans, etc., and no one could figure it out, but Zoe was able to help. I'm not saying she fixed it--the disks are still bulging--but she was able to realign everything that was so far out of whack and therefore help me hugely. Zoe performed miracles on my neck when it was out because of a strange desk setup at work and my computer responsibilities suddenly increased. Zoe was kind enough to squeeze me in last-minute, even thought it was during JazzFest, and in an hour she took away a week's worth of shooting neck pain, not to mention helping to balance out the rest of my body that was trying to compensate for the neck. Basically, she's fantastic and although there are other places that'll throw rose petals at you or greet you with a cocktail, I'll buy my own champagne, thanks very much, and go with an exponentially better masseuse. (And I live one block from one of the biggest and most posh day-spas in town.)

text: After reading the glowing reviews, I decided Margot was a must-try for my one night stint in Nashville. As a business traveler, I tend to dine solo, and a decent bar with a friendly bartender is the only thing that keeps me from crying myself to sleep at night. Luckily, Margot delivered. My server was super friendly (as was everyone else - imagine, people smile when you accidentally make eye contact, rather than scowling or pretending like it didn't happen!!!), and chatted with me just enough so that I didn't feel like the invisible diner. He gave me some of the background on the history of the space and also let me sample an odd bottle of red wine that is bottled in clear glass! I know that might mean nothing to folks who don't drink a lot of wine, but for those that do; have you ever seen red in a clear glass bottle? The mind, it reels! Margot Cafe is a small spot, but not crowded. There is a main dining room, seating upstairs, and a tented patio (whose patrons were in for a shock when the skies opened and rain thundered down around them, sneaking in around the roof a little and requiring some table scootches), plus a small bar that seats maybe 10. My only gripe with the bar is the lack of overhang. I hate when my legs are jammed right up against the bar when I'm sitting there, so I have to spread my legs out to either side of my stool, or sit way far back. The bartender told me that one of Margot's influences is Alice Waters, and while I can see that, I feel like I couldn't quite score high marks in the "attention to detail" box. I started off with an iberico cheese served with a yummy warm cranberry walnut bread and Seckel pears. This was an excellent pairing, although large sections of pear were smooshy and gross, and for $12, I don't want any section of my pear to be smooshy and gross. Next up the app of venison and sweet potato fries. The fries were fab - meaty and sweet and salty. The venison, I'm not quite sure about. Seared for maybe a second, it was closer to ahi tuna than the game I was imagining. I would've liked it a bit more done, but I figured this was how it was served, so I soldiered on, thoughtfully chewing and picking up on the foresty, earthy, venisony, damn, there is that distracting raw meat/tuna flavor again. But when my neighbors ordered it later, it came completely cooked through. So maybe they were just trying to poison me with raw meat. In any case, it's a good dish, but consider ordering it medium or medium rare. I wrapped it all up with a jasmine panna cotta that was okay, but didn't really taste like jasmine, and a glass of muscat. An enjoyable meal, and for Nashville's local cuisine scene, I'm sure it's something out of the ordinary. I'd recommend it with the stipulation that it might pale in comparison to California cuisine from California, where my tastebuds have been thoroughly spoiled.
label: POS

So I called them later that day to speak with the person in charge of overseeing and contacting repairs (whose name I am intentionally leaving out) and she had no recollection of being in a position that she was supposed to call me, and seemed a tad rude on the phone. I chalked it up to failing to remember and feeling put in a bad position, as I think that I would have felt that way in her position, and left it alone. She called me back to let me know the repair would be taken care of shortly, and so I waited a few more days. I received a phone call stating that my camera was ready to be picked up, by this tie I had waited over six weeks for this repair to be finished. Three times as long as I was quoted. When I asked to at the very least receive some sort of discount for being led around, receiving no contact regarding the status of my repair, and having to wait three times the quoted amount, I was told that they could not do anything because A). it was the Christmas season B). the repair technician went on vacation and did not tell anyone until the last minute C). the time quoted was not realistic and the employee who quoted me two weeks was no longer working for them D). the contractor who does the repairs will not give discounts for his repairs for any reason E). the owner did not want to try to negotiate one with the contractor (yes he said this) F). I should be a little more understanding about extenuating circumstances and that G). they HAD done everything in their power to keep me in the loop and I was unwarranted for feeling the way I did (yes, they said that too). Please keep in mind that their entire staff is not like this, the woman who was unfortunately the one trying to ring me up was VERY nice, but was stuck in the middle of me wanting to wait till their repair person was no longer busy and her interupting her customer whom she was helping, to raise her vocie and tell me that I was not telling the truth and that they HAD done everything in their power. This is during and after I had very quietly said that I would be more than willing to wait until the repair person was done assisting her customer, that I was not in a hurry. After having the person raise her voice at me twice, I asked to just have my items rung up so that I could leave (I had film I was picking up and the repair), and informed the nice lady that I was never going to be coming back, and she was very apologetic, but the repair person continued to ignore her customer to tel lme that that was my choice and they were ok with that. I give this place two stars. Zero for customer service and two for happening to have the absolute best quality photo lab I have seen in Reno. If you are just getting photos done, these guys will do you right I think. If you are looking to buy or have something repaired, good luck. If I can find a place in town to rival Gordon's for film service, I will be using them, until then, I will suck it up and continue to go there for film only.

text: Always save your receipts with Charter, and check your bill regularly for errors. My hatred of Charter goes back quite a ways, and I thought I'd unload here, because I'm still pissed about my $342 + $33 I paid their extortionist collection agency, Afni. So in 1998 I signed up for AT&T's brand-new digital cable service while living at Woodside Village. I cancelled my service and switched to DirecTV, returning my receiver to the AT&T office personally. Unfortunately I didn't save or lost the receipt. Afni says I owe $684.86 to Charter for services rendered in 1998 by AT&T. What were the charges for, I ask? I closed that account with a $0 balance, and I'm paid up currently, I exclaim. They're not sure but suspect an unreturned receiver. I tell them I closed the account and returned the receiver personally to the AT&T counter, but they say their records show a debt owed, and if I can't produce a receipt, they'll dirty my credit report. Then they insist that there were no less than 3 "final bills" sent to me back in '98 showing the debt. I insist that I never saw any of these bills, and I always have a mail forwarding when I move. With them unwilling to budge I tear up my house and files looking for the receipt never finding it. So finally the jerk collection agent insists that they'll settle the account for 50%, and stupidly, I begrudgingly agree to their blackmail terms and pay the $342.43. Now I'm fiercly angry and cancel my current Internet service with Charter this time keeping the receipt for the returned cable modem. Upon return, I have the cashier check my balance that shows $0. Then Afni comes after me for $33 promptly submiting the $33 collection to all 3 credit agencies. You may also want to get a drink from the fridge as the water looks questionable. Also note that they generally serve all your courses at the same time which is weird but you can be in and out in under 30 minutes which is great. Then he just brough the tab. Who brings the tab without having asked if people are okay, or trying to see if they are done at the very least. The sound system was not good. text: I was hopeful about this place after hearing good things online, but unfortunately I thought the food was fairly "meh". The best item was the spring roll, which was fairly average and came with standard duck sauce. The tom ka kai soup had separated somehow & I only took a bite or two before giving up on it because it just tasted yucky. The chicken satay was good but not great. The peanut sauce that came with it barely had any spice and the chicken satay itself didn't have a lot of flavor. The satay came with the choice of white rice, brown rice, or noodles. We picked the white rice which, like everything else, wasn't particularly special. The chicken bun was not really what I was expecting - it looked a bit like a chicken sandwich, not the steamed bun I expected. The form factor of it was fairly awkward to eat. The sauce on the bun wasn't remarkable and needed more flavor. While the owner seemed fairly nice, I just can't rate the food more than 2 stars.

text: Mad Donna's is definitely an improvement from the old Radio Cafe days. I really like the black bean nachos and often pick up a cupcake at the end of the meal to share. But the burgers and sandwiches are a little plain. If anyone is reading my posts today, you'll notice that the common theme has been happy hour drink specials. Mad Donna's definitely delivers on that. Most week nights you'll be able to get 2-1 specials, $5 martinis/margaritas, etc. And since I live in East Nashville, it's within walking distance! My favorite, though, beyond the friendly staff is Tuesday night drag queen bingo hosted by Miss Bianca Paige. Nothing says happy Tuesday like $25 wings, bingo (with prizes), and a 50ish year old man in drag hitting on your boyfriend. If you have sensitive ears, are from outside of 440, or are easily offended by large groups of alcohol-fueled gays, then you might want to skip the upstairs bar on Tuesdays. If not, come by, it's super fun.

text: A few hours after finishing the Broad Street Run and craving a tasty burger, my cheering section (party of one) recommended that we hit the New Wave Cafe. interested in going somewhere else, i was game for waiting the few minutes for a table. here's the thing, hostess: just because you assume that we overheard what you were telling the people who just left, doesn't give you carte blanche to ignore us for the following 15 minutes or so. the hostess walked back and forth as we waited and waited and were ignored by the entire staff, including her, ignored as someone who is willing to hand over your dollars. finally a couple guys left the bar and we took their seats. the bartender was pretty busy and it seemed like she was more interested in text: Chuy's is one in a long list of things that disappoint me about Tucson. First off, I'm not wild about any restaurant in which the server greets me with the line, "Do you know how this place works?" Call me crazy, but I feel like any place in which the napkins are actually a single, gross, barbecue sauce-stained roll of Brawny doesn't get to have a gimmick. Eric Ripert's restaurants can have a unique way of operating. If Rick Bayless wants to open a fajita bar in which the patrons have to order while doing a handstand, he can knock himself out. Chuy's Mesquite Craphouse just doesn't get to have a gimmick. That said, Chuy's is OK, if you're looking for incredibly inconsistent, glorified bar food with a quasi-Mexican twist. As has been said, the cheesy garlic bread can be really tasty, or it can be three weeks old and stale. The fish tacos can either be crispy and satisfyingly fried, or they can be mushy and grim, with the breading sliding off the meat. The margaritas are OK, I guess, if you happen to really get off on the earthy taste of well tequila. I will say this: the pitchers are large, strong, and provide the perfectly masking accompaniment to the thoroughly "meh" food. The place is loud, like abattoir loud. I can't verify that there are actually cows being anally electrocuted in the back room, but it sure sounds like it. I know the place is a local institution. Maybe I just haven't gone at the right time of day, or when I've been in the right frame of mind, but it's just another place around town that is passable enough at what it does, but at which I feel sorry for having spent my money.
label: NEG

text: Stopped here for a late-night drink and dessert, hoping for a casual, date-friendly place for a sweet nightcap. I wont say we didn't get that, but we certainly weren't impressed and certain elements (like the price) were actually quite off-putting. The decor was kind of like a slightly moodier Starbucks: one is greeted by churning vats of (fake?) chocolate and the carefully organized gift shop by the door, a bad, vaguely chocolate-related mural took up one corner, fake quotes about the ego-maniacal Brenner covered the other walls. It wasn't oppressive, but it was certainly trying too hard. We were led to a nice little two-top pointing out on open window and our order was quickly taken. Very quickly our cocktails (good booze, well-mixed, but not worth 10 bucks a pop) were brought out and, soon after, our chocolate fondue. We opted for the Trio: a molten toffee caramel and any two chocolate fondues (milk, dark, white) served with strawberries, bananas, banana bread, marshmallows, and little grill to roast them. The chocolate was far too sweet for my taste: the white had a lovely cocoa butter flavor, but the dark wasn't that dark and the caramel had a very bland flavor. All of them hurt my teeth, their saccharine flavors overpowering the already sweet accoutrement. Those too were disappointing: the fruit was okay (I would have liked to see local strawberries, but it might be a little early for those) but the marshmallows tasted like your standard Jet-Puffed (what self-respecting confectioner doesn't make their own marshmallows?) and the banana bread was room temperature. at best, and uninspired. All the same, I would have been much happier with less, and more savory fondues with more, and more thoughtful choices to dip. I know there are entire worlds of chocolate connoisseurship, but the quality of the sweets at Max Brenner didn't even stand up to an ignoramus like me. Naked Chocolate Cafe holds its position as my favorite late-night sweet spot in the city: cheaper, better, and its Rittenhouse location couldn't be closer. 4/5 for service, a "meh" for the cocktails, but thumbs down for everything else.

text: You know that overused cliche, "you can't judge a book by it's cover?" The bread was okay, but the black bean dip was a tad blah. Anywho, the main course is what really makes this place four star worthy. My only complaint was the very unappetizing curly herbs on top of the plate - I apologize in advance if I gross anyone out, but it looked like a pile of green hair. So, NOT okay. text: I had read about Biff's in a few reviews and took it as a place to go and see what was happening. Pulled up and noticed people were lined up 6 deep at the drive up, good sign! The door leads you straight up to the order here counter, your choices are astounding from the menu but I wanted a burger, after all it is Biff's burger. My order was taken and paid for on the spot, cash only here. Was given a receipt with a number and sat down, 10 minutes later my half pound bacon cheese burger arrives and my number is called. I retrieved my tray with a mega sized burger and fries with a large coke, free refills with a large coke. My burger was grilled not fried, fresh patty not a frozen hockey puck like other places that I refuse to even look at. The lettuce, tomato and onion were very fresh and did not resemble something from the back of your refrigerator that overstayed its welcome. This is good! The burger was top notch, tasty and cooked to order, plenty of kudos for the real burger flavor. The good: It is a real local burger place, local owned and operated, the food is real. Quick service and it is a refreshing change from the chains. The establishment is very clean, for a older classic burger house it truly is clean. They do cars shows and bike shows, crowds gather on Wednesday nights even. There are many community events held here with benefits going to children, big on toys for tots! There are fliers supporting veterans events like the wounded warrior projects, disabled vets also. This is a throw back place, it has class and a lot of charm with good food and excellent prices. I would recommend if you want a great burger that is yuppy free and non pretentious go to Biff's and try them out. Chef Mark

text: I (8 months pregnant w/my 1 year old in a stroller) brought my 2004 Honda Accord to Sigismondi Car Specialists to have a state inspection done on March 22, 2009. I thought the location would be convenient since I live only a few blocks away and could walk to and from while my car was being serviced. The owner, Joseph Sigismondi asked me to come back in 2 hours and the inspection would be done. When I returned he explained that my car had failed - I was shocked, because I have never had any problems with the car and was hoping to show it to a potential buyer later that evening. He explained that it failed due to a air filter sensor. He explained that my check engine light was on (but I stated that I had NEVER seen that on) and he could temporarily turn it off for $75 more, but it would go back on within a few days. I didn't feel 100% honest about it, but I wanted to show the car that evening and have the problem fixed that week. So I agreed and paid the full amount of $187.25 for all of the services. After the next few days, I started to become concerned about the services I received from Sigismondi and my husband and I were questioning whether I was being ripped off or not. I knew there was nothing wrong with my car and 1 week later, the check engine light NEVER turned back on. So I decided to take my car to Pep Boys auto service for another inspection to see if Sigismondi's report was accurate or not. And NOT to my surprise, IT PASSED INSPECTION for only $60!! I was quite furious at this point. Thinking that a local businessman had taken advantage of me, an 8 month pregnant woman! I immediately drove to Sigismondi on March 30, 2009 to dispute the services performed and ask for a refund. I explained to the same man, Joseph Sigismondi that my car just passed inspection and my check engine light NEVER turned back on and that I felt I was being ripped off and wanted a refund. I did swear here and there, being that I was angry and also realized that he had put a license plate frame advertising his shop on my car W/O permission! He asked me to leave and so I did and on my way out I said that I would be reporting him and would dispute the charges with my credit card company. He then decided to follow me to my car - remember I am 8 month's pregnant... I got into my car and my gut told me to lock the door, so I did. Then Mr. Sigismondi tried to open my door several times and started banging on my driver's side door window! I was terrified, what was this man trying to do to me? Why would he be trying to get into my car? He then started to yell and spit on my window 2x. I was so scared and started crying hysterically. What would anyone want to do by opening a woman's car door? I quickly drove away and when I got home I called my husband immediately. I could not stop crying, I was scared. Did he have my address? Was he going to come to my house and either vandalize my car or try confronting me again? I didn't know, but unfortunately I didn't feel safe. I called the police and Officer Duffy (?) came to file a report. He stated that the only thing he could do was file the report, but nothing else unless I wanted to file a civil suit for being ripped off/over charged. At that point, I didn't care about the money, I could dispute it with my credit card company. The point was that I was TERRIFIED! What if he opened my car door? Would he hit me, spit on me, what? Please help me bring justice to the neighborhood and stop this man from conducting bad business.

text: Unless you're covered in tattoos, they won't give you the time of day. I emailed months in advance because this place was recommended to me. When I didn't get a reply, I called when I was in town. The person who answered was nice, and said they didn't have any walk-ins that day, but to come in to see when they did. I walked there, and when I got there I wish I hadn't. The person who helped me was one of the rudest people I've ever met. Instead of asking me to wait a few minutes until he was finishing straightening his station, he interrupted me several times while I was explaining what I wanted, and I felt like he was looking at me like I didn't belong there. In short, he told me it didn't matter if I emailed in advance, and it would not have mattered if I called either, since they would never take an appointment unless it was in person. They didn't have anything available for weeks, and I was out of luck. It's fine if they were booked, but there were only 2 artists in the store, one of which was tattooing someone. That's not "walk-ins available" like it says on their website. The attitude I was given from the moment I stepped foot in the store told me I wasn't welcome, and I feel that it is because I'm a young-ish girl (21) who didn't have any visible tattoos. I gave two stars, because the portfolios had nice work, so I'm sure that they do a good job, but they lost a client who would be willing to drive 3 hours for every tattoo just for a reliable shop that made her comfortable. Instead, Jen at Reno Tattoo Co. got a client for life. She custom designed a piece for me and I couldn't be happier. I will have many more tattoos from her in the future if possible. She didn't care if I didn't look "the part", they wanted to give me an awesome experience. I wish I could say the same about Aces.

text: I'm almost afraid to go back to Pi as you don't want to lose that perfect vision you have in your head of a perfect pizza. Kind of like meeting a girl at a bar, thinking she is the hottest girl ever and going on a date later and realizing she's not quite a 7. Pi, it's name descended on St. Louis like a swarm of locusts, I couldn't go anywhere without hearing about it, Obama even had them fly out to the freaking White House (over Chicago places). There was no way this place could live up to expectations. I have to admit, I was blown away by the pie here, freaking amazing. In a cute nod to my old city San Francisco (Which they say this is SF pizza, I'll touch on that later), they name a few of the pies after SF 'hoods (which is why I won't order the Western Addition, I don't want that neighborhood in my mouth) and include my old place North Beach. From the toppings to the crust the "thin" crust North Beach was awesome, perhaps the best pizza I've ever had. I do have one bone to pick with you PI. I lived in San Francisco for 4 years, I ate at Golden Boy, North Beach Pizza, Pizza Orgasmica and a bunch more places and never came across a San Francisco style pizza. I've reached out to my friends there and no one knows of this San Francisco style pizza. What gives?

After entering, there are chips and salsa laid out for you to much on while you wait or take to a table. The salsa was more like a Mexican marinara sauce. It wasn't good. But why is there chips & salsa in a BBQ joint anyway? We ordered a slew of items, but nothing was extraordinary. In fact, everything seemed simply average. BBQ is one of those foods where you can taste the passion of the preparation, but I really didn't get that here. The owner did come by to thank us for coming in which was nice. But overall, the restaurant didn't seem all put together. It was hot inside, the waitress missed one of our drink orders, we had another waitress try and take our order after the first was there, we had to ask for silverware. It just seemed disheveled. Maybe it's better to give them a couple of weeks to get the kinks out. But my feeling is don't open unless you are ready. First impressions are key. Especially when you can walk right across the street to a different well established BBQ joint (Bandana's).

text: I feel like talking too much about Los Angeles is like asking to get a beat down in Philadelphia, but this (i.e., frozen yogurt) is one arena where L.A. shines supreme. Not the best, but definitely not the worst in Philadelphia. (That would be Sprinkles.) The classically tart flavors were creamy and had a satisfying bite to them, and the toppings were impressive in their variety and freshness. I got original and pomegranate flavored froyo with almonds, pomegranate, and mochi on top, and I would recommend you do the same. I have a vague recollection of the sweet flavors leaving something to be desired, but I only had small samples of them (and I had to use the same cup over and over... They are a bit stingy with the sample cups). BOTTOM LINE: You could do much worse for frozen yogurt than Sweet Ending... Yeah, it could be cheaper (as could every frozen yogurt dealer in Philly), and, yeah, they could be a bit more generous with the samples, but at least the tart flavors are good and the toppings are quite impressive.

text: The best part of our experience was the wine. Beyond that the food is pretty mediocre which I was pretty surprised about after reading all the rave reviews. We ordered the frites which were limp and not particularly flavorful. The Romaine salad was okay with a light dressing and the hard boiled egg was a nice touch. The croutons were a little burnt. The scallops with goat cheese gnocchi and baby beets dish was not good. At first look, the whole plate looked dry and lacking moisture or sauce. The scallops were heavily salted to the point of being almost inedible. I wonder if the over-salting was an attempt to mask the so so quality of the product itself. The pan fried gnocchi was dry and a little burnt. We sent the plate back and the staff was nice to redo it. The redone plate was not salty this time but the sear on the scallop was off and the gnocchi was still a little burnt (must have been the inevitable effect of integrating goat cheese into the pan fry!). There seemed to be issues with moisture levels, use of oil/butter, and seasoning overall on this plate. The Colorado lamb was very gamy tasting and not memorable. It was an attempt at being upscale comfort food I think, but again the seasoning was off and the whole dish was fairly bland. The host didn't seat us and a server stepped in to find us our table when we arrived. Our server was very nice and helpful. The wait time on our entrées was long. The dinner atmosphere is cozy and fairly quiet. Overall, our experience was not worth the $22+ cost of each entree. We won't be going back to Terrene. Being a St. Louis transplant (coming from California and having traveled a great deal), I must admit we're sadly finding St. Louis restaurants kind of lacking... but we will keep trying!

text: For me, The Bridge is the only place in Philly to see the big movies. I'm not a high-maintenance kind of girl, and I in fact *hate* it when there's a lady handing me paper towels in the bathroom. But The Bridge really does make movie-watching a pleasure. I can get here at 9:35 for a movie that starts at 9:30, and sit right down in my assigned seat without tripping over anyone or accidentally sitting in someone's lap. It's clean and organized, and easily accessible by subway. I'll gladly watch an indie flick in a crusty old theater with sticky floors and rickety seats. But I like paying a few extra dollars to see the occasional blockbuster here. Totally unrelated tip: There's a grocery store right across the street with a well-stocked candy aisle.
label: POS

text: Are you reading this Jimmy? I used to always stop at Margaritaville when visiting New Orleans and listen to the great bands in the bar but my last visit will probably be just that. When visiting this establishment for a refreshment and to use the restroom I could not have been made more unwelcome. Dunno what happened to the Quarter since Katrina but just about every business has posted no public restroom signs in the door and Margaritaville is no exception. They actually have a sign in the bathroom that states if you are not a customer your trespassing! Normally when in any business to use their restrooms I try to patronize that business, it's just common courtesy but Margaritaville's attitude seems to be keep the heck out! I had heard that New Orleans had tried to discourage this proir to Katrina to keep people from urinating in the streets and alleys but apparently have reversed that decision or are not enforcing it. So next time your in the Quarter show Jimmy your gratitude and use his restrooms but party elsewere!
label: NEG

text: Shopping here is similar to Shop Rite or Sav-A-Lot only with kind of real brands instead of generics. The produce is cheap but it should be as some of it looks like it got into some sort of fist fight. This is also the only supermarket I've ever been to where "Jamaican" was one of the listings in the signs over the aisles. They do have a wide variety of ethnic foods considering and some of the items you can make up in bulk but for everyday things, they are really expensive and offer no deals whatsoever. Expect to pay over normal price for things like cereal or milk. I don't think I'd ever consider buying meat there as it just seemed dirty. Overall, it reminded me of a dirty, rundown grocery store from the 80s.
label: NEG

text: The quality of the fish was satisfactory but extremely thin slices of fish were put on large balls of rice for the Nigiri style sushi. You MUST eat all of the rice or you will be charged extra. High quality fish is expensive but I dont want to be forced to eat a huge ball of rice with every mouthful of fish that is not the way sushi is prepared (I have been to Japan more than 20 times), it's not healthy, and it's not pleasurable. Update: I went back and this time was seated at the sushi bar not a table. This time there was a very normal amount of rice and I found the sushi good though certainly not great. The second experience agreed with the positive reviews I had read on yelp. Moral: From now on I will sit at the sushi bar.

text: Being new to yelp, I'm figuring things out as I go, and I've decided that I'm only going to write a review if a.) no one, or very few people have reviewed it, or b.) what everyone else has said is directly opposed to what I have experienced. Mosaic falls in the latter category. Mosaic is f-ing terrible. I went there, roughly a month ago, for a friend's birthday. Though we had reservations, we had to wait two hours for a table. Only after I complained, did an owner/manager come to speak with us. He apologized, stating that the tables weren't turning over at their regular rate, and said that he'd comp us some starters in apology. Great, sounds right to me. Then we had to wait an additional 45 minutes (I complained around the 75 minute mark--take that math!) before we were seated. They actually sat us at a ridiculously small table in the corner. There were seven of us, and the table was initially set up as a four top. Once seated, the waitress came over and got our drinks and the promised complimentary dishes came out. The food itself wasn't that bad. It was unimpressive, but, I've had worse, so I won't necessarily complain on that front. But just a word of caution to any would be restauranteurs reading: if you're going to charge me $7 for something you tag as "truffled frites," make sure you don't give me fuckin' Steak n Shake fries with cold truffle oil on top. (Epicurean note: truffle oil isn't actually made from truffles--its just a cheap way for restaurants to bump up prices. You're welcome) Anyway, after the "meal," the check comes to me, and I notice that they didn't take the initial starters off of our bill (roughly, $50). I pull the server aside and ask her why the amount wasn't taken off, and she acts like I'm trying to rob her. "I was never told anything about free dishes. You may be mistaken." Yes, you're right tapas wench, somehow an order was placed before I sat down, an order which you brought out, and now I'm trying to screw you out of $50, just because I want to come back and buy 1.6 pitchers of your terribly overpriced excuse for sangria. I eventually found the owner who promised us the dishes, and cleared it with him--but considering I had to wait 2 hours to eat, waiting another 10 minutes didn't help matters. BONUS: While we were waiting for a table I went outside for a smoke, and a group of girls came out, in which I heard the following conversation. Tiffani* you should TOTALLY ask that dude for his number, he's super cute. UGH, as if Steffi*, he's a VALET. Maybe if he, like, OWNED the restaurant. Now, i have no problems with a little snobbery; hell, I unfortunately will admit that I popped my Lacostes back in college (I've grown a lot, i swear). But these girls were exactly the type of people that saturated Mosaic that night--faux hipsters that lease BMW's and over spend on their Discover cards so they can feel like Sarah Jessica Parker and crew. I wanted to slap them, but there were four of them, and I have a proven track record of losing fights to chicks. *-all names are theoretical examples of what I expected, however I have a sneaking suspicion that I am 100% correct.
label: NEG

text: Got a late night slice. It was just what we needed. 2.50 for a cheese slice, I guess after a night of drinking who really cares. Having just moved here I was surprised at how good the slice was. Now I need to go find the best of the area. Is Soho the best? Only time will tell.

text: This is our go-to place to watch big football games. College, bowls, Saints, etc. The place will fill completely for a big game. You can usually find some fans from the opposing team which makes for better football watching. Great tap beer selection. The "Debris Fries" is probably the greatest single bar food item in the city. Popcorn machine! Lots of TVs. Very attentive service. I never went to the old Bruno's, but this is a very nice bar with plenty of room and nice decor. The only downside is the smoke... But, it is no worse than any other NOLA bar.

text: While I'm really not a fan of buffets due to cleanliness and hygeine issues we decided to stop by this establishment and give it a try. While basically your average food for a chinese buffet there was a large selection at lunch including seafood. I was impressed with the large sushi bar that had two sushi chefs preparing fresh sushi however the sushi was not marked which made it difficult in making a selection. text: This quaint little Mexican eatery is one of my favorite places in Conshohocken. The menu is small, but the service and quality of food is exceptional for the price. Everything tastes better with their homemade spicy salsa that is sitting at every table, just waiting for you to use. I don't even like beans, and for some reason can eat their house bean here. The only downside to this place is that sometimes it can get very crowded, very quickly due to the college crowd that congregates in the area. Again, with the price and service, this is easily overlooked. Would recommend to anyone looking for good, well priced Mexican food.

text: Big fan of Bobby Flay's shows and food, not a fan of this restaurant. 45 minute wait, understandable. You know, celebrity chef's new restaurant in one of the BEST locations for a burger joint in Philly along with gorgeous weather, of course there's going to be a line. But why are half of the tables empty? This isn't a nightclub where long lines promote popularity. Ordered my L.A. Burger, sweet potato fries, and black and white shake, and a number was given to me to place on my table. I wasn't timing them because I was busy taking pictures and checking out the cool decor (which is definitely Bobby Flay style), but the food arrived fairly quick. The shake was OK, nothing special (Lee's black and white shakes are a different story!). Sweet potato fries were good and so was the honey mustard dipping sauce that came with it, but it was too runny and barely any would adhere to the fry. My burger came out and it looked delicious. They sure know how to make a pretty burger, with HAIR on it. Yes, my burger was topped with avocado relish, watercress, cheddar, and a strand of light brown hair. People make mistakes, fine. They brought my new hairless L.A. Burger out. The meat of the burger is actually pretty good. But the toppings were so so (more lime in the relish maybe?). I practically had to drench it in the sauces, mostly the jalapeno, on the side. Meal finished. I ordered a kid's meal to go for a friend of mine. Waited **20** minutes for it to come out. During the wait, we were asked about 20 times if we were done (not exaggerating) and if any of you have been there this week, you know what I'm talking about. No sauces came with it, not even ketchup packets. No compensation was offered for the hair incident, which I'm not going to make a big deal about. They did apologize, good enough. I'll give the place a second try, but I am not waiting in that ridiculous line.
label: NEG

text: I don't have a car so I don't know how bad parking is. I am a walker that is very familiar with Philadelphia so I know what streets to walk on and which to avoid. That being said, I've liked every show I've seen here. Yes, sometimes the sound could be better, but this place is known for being raunchy. There's always a good crowd here minus a few older creepos and shoving band enthusiasts. As far as drinks are concerned, my friends and I always drink at home first and then sneak in a flask. It's actually pretty easy to sneak reefer in here as well because you'll tend to smell that once the band starts playing. When it starts to get hot in there from all the excitement, the friendly bouncers open the side doors, so make sure you get situated near there. text: If you're the type that likes to enjoy a sandwich now and then, you might have heard the saying, "The bread makes the sandwich." Here in Philly, we're especially aware of this fact. Take the city's signature sandwhich, the cheesesteak, for example: at Tony Luke's, you get a crisp yet supple roll, the perfect canvas on which to paint the artery-clogging delight of a wiz-wit. Yet these same flavors, when served within a soggy or weak roll, are completely nullified by the poor texture. Weak roll, weak sandwich. House understands this principle better than any other panini spot I've visited. The bread on my Southwestern - two perfectly toasted, crunchy, yet forgiving slices of what tasted like a subtle sourdough - made the sandwich, plain and simple. Not to say the other flavors were merely incedental - the thick slices of fresh turkey, fresh red peppers, smoky cheddar, punchy bacon, and light and sweet chipotle roumalade all danced together to create what was pretty close to a perfect panini. The location ain't bad either. On warm, sunny days, the al fresco dining out front is something to savored. So go sit, take your panini in one hand, your Orangina in the other, and enjoy Media's House. You won't be disappointed.
label: POS

"check out ray's happy birthday bar." and oh boy, was she right. i came for the friday karaoke night, and was not let down. the bartenders here, particularly one of them, seem to favor the females in the bar - i scored a double whiskey sour for $2.50. $2.50?! unheard of in my former city of NYC. smoky - which i didn't mind, as i tend to light up when drinking. the karaoke was glorious - the "DJ" (i didn't realize a guy who does karaoke can consider himself a DJ) had a huge book of classics. unfortunately, i did not get to perform, due to all of the requests he had to take. (note to self: come early next time) but it was sure as hell fun watching old italian guys and hipsters alike busting out a wide array of tunes. considering this place opens early, and is right up the street from my apartment, i will most certainly be a loyal customer.

Good beer but I felt kind of wierd drinking it in its funny glass. Ordered a burger (no surprise, since i am a burger head). Asked for it medium with bacon and chedder and waited anxiously for it to arrive. When it came it did not appear medium, it appeared burnt. I was hungry at this point that I decided just to eat it. Well done burger can sometimes still be juicy but this was not, it was very difficult to eat and now i regret having consumed it. text: This 2 stars rating hurts me more than it should hurt Mamma Maria. After having an amazing dinner there a year ago around christmas, I had spoke so highly of this place. So much so, that friends of ours from Upper Bucks County came down to enjoy Sunday dinner with us there. When my fiance called to confirm the reservation (which was taken by mamma herself), they told him that the earlier we could arrive the better. Well, our friends were running behind so we called to say we would be 5 minutes late. We arrived and were greeted with two really pissed off servers, and an empty house. Our Antipasto was already on the table waiting for us (which wouldn't have been bad, but the actions the waitresses did afterwards really ruined the experience for us). As soon as we sat down, we were rushed to finish. The waitress spoke so fast we had to ask her multiple times to repeat herself. This really annoyed her. The waitress barked our options at us, then got frustrated when we asked questions. Our Antipasto was taken from us before we were finished, our wine was only refilled once - after we asked for it, and they gave us shots of limoncello, when the last time i went, we got a platter of cordials. The cakes tasted old, and the food was lava hot when it arrived. So hot, I couldn't eat for a few minutes. On the positive side, the rolls were awesome (although the were hoagie rolls), the pasta dish was perfect and my chicken was cooked well. Nothing was seasoned enough or too much. Mamma stopped in to ask how everything was, and i just didn't have the heart to call out the surly waitresses. I have been there, i know what its like to have that last table come in at the last minute, but we arrived at 8:35 and the closed at 10. Service was just disrespectful, and I am going to have a difficult time bringing anyone back here again. It completely ruined the night for us and our friends, who drove an hour to eat there.

text: How did I miss giving the Royal Tavern mad props? This is why I love this place. I went this past Friday night with the boyfriend, and it was packed to the gills. Despite that, they scrambled to find a table for us as soon as possible. Service was great all night despite there not being one free seat in the place. The drink selection is fantastic, of course. A great selection of craft/local beer on draft, bottles, and specialty drinks. Their seasonal hot apple cider with rum is deeeeelicious. Plenty of carnivorous and veggie options. Though I am not a veg-head, the tempeh club sandwich - with vegan bacon, grilled tempeh, lettuce, tomatoes and basil aioli on delicious, delicious bread - is INCREDIBLE. Not to mention huge - three or four layers, for sure. Don't forget the fries - which are nothing short of awesome here. The Royal Tavern set the standard for the now incredible "gastropub" scene in Philadelphia, and they remain consistent.

text: I went here for dinner with the wife on a Sunday. We were in Nashville for a wedding and wanted to grab something a little nicer than BBQ. It had a 4 star rating on Yelp, so why not! We arrived downstairs, looked over both the bistro and the upstairs menu. We decided to go 'upscale' and be seated upstairs. We were told she could not seat us right now, and it would be about 45-60 minutes. Not a problem on vacation, we went to the bar downstairs and had drinks and an appetizer. I had a Jack/Coke and her a martini. I was impressed by the ice cubes, as they were the nonstandard large size cubes (actual cubes) which decreases the amount of watering down that occurs. We had the duck-fat fried tater tots, and they were fantastic. Three dipping sauces, so it made it feel a little classier than squeezing Ketchup out of a bottle. After about 20 minutes, the hostess came back and said they were ready upstairs. We didn't need the whole basket of tots, so we finished our drink and headed upstairs. Downstairs decor was very cool. Old school styling, subway tile, etc. Upstairs, the decor was very nice, low lighting, very classy with some exposed brick. To my surprise, there were only maybe 10 people upstairs, with seating for at least 50-60. I was very confused at why we had to wait. But figured maybe it was going to be attentive service and they were short-staffed or something. The service was a bit slow to start. They filled our water glasses fairly quickly and gave us menus. After about 10 minutes, he came back to take the wine order. This took a good 15-20 minutes to come back. Then he disappeared again, finally coming back to take the dinner order. Disappeared again... and probably another 20 minutes for our soups to come out. From there out the service was fine, with items coming up properly timed and drinks refreshed. From a food perspective, we both had the tomato bisque, which was very good. We were also brought a small crab and citrus taster which was also very good. This brought our expectations up regarding the upcoming meal. My wife had the roasted chicken with farro and some summer squash. It was pleasant, but nothing to get excited for. She mentioned that she shouldn't have gone with chicken, because who gets excited for chicken? I had a 14oz rib eye, which was recommended by the waiter. It was tasty enough, but a ton of fat. I understand it's a rib eye... but this was a bit over the top. It was cooked properly and was tasty enough, but for almost $30, I was expecting more. It also came in a weird little cast iron pot/dish. The dish was just deep enough to hinder your ability to cut the steak easily. Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. We took a look at the dessert menu, but nothing thrilled us so we got the check. It wasn't bad, $100 for 2 soups, 2 meals, 2 glasses of wine. We were discussing what we thought of the place and both of us said "underwhelmed". We were discussing being spoiled living in Chicago, but I don't know how much weight that holds. I've had amazing dinners in small towns and this just didn't cut it. I'm going with 2 stars, with them getting knocked on service and food. I still don't know why it took 30 minutes (and quoted 60) to get us seated in an empty place? We asked if they were busy and the waitress said "No, we usually book up by 2PM, blah blah blah" adding to the confusion. I just got the impression they were trying to make themselves more exclusive than they are. On food and pricing alone, I would have gone for three. It wasn't bad... but I wouldn't recommend it to a friend. If we had the half-star, MAYBE 2.5... MAYBE. I feel comfortable giving this 2. To be fair, the bistro area has potential. Similar food, but more upscale sandwiches / sides than a standard diner/bar. I would give that a shot.
label: NEG

text: Call it 2.5 stars. The sign on the building, and their business cards say just "China Buffet", but the phone listing is still in the name of "Super China Buffet". Ambience and cleanliness was a just a tad below my expectations. Men's room was clean, but needed some remodeling. Back in the dining area, my table top was wiped down, but still had a sticky film on it. Price for dinner: $7.95 including soft-drink and tax. Inexpensive buffets have been having poor quality food lately, but this place is definitely within the "met expectations" category. I would not want to go here in between lunch and dinner, but as long as you go during the main meal hours, you'll get fresh food. I'd say it's a little bit better than the average "Super China Buffet." (Which I know, isn't saying all that much.) Very extensive selections, but all within the standards. Some lettuce, cucumber slices, marinated tomatoes, onions, and green peppers. Cold shrimp. Cold creamy fruit salad. Cold (fake) crab salad. Bananas in red sauce. Red jello. Soft serve frozen custard machine. Vanilla wafers in pudding, plus a few more standard cheap pastry dessert items. Three steam tables, each of which are double-sided, so there are lots of selections, all of which are pretty much standards. Items with pork are marked PORK on the label, including the egg rolls, and the stuffed mushrooms. Some chicken dishes were kind of rubbery, but overall acceptable. Sauce, while fresh, was still "gunk sauce" that doesn't sit well for long. That's why you have to go during the peak meal hours to get fresh food. Two different kinds of shrimp in the steam trays, plus the cheesy seafood dish, plus a fresh vegetable and seafood (shrimp and fake crab) dish which I liked. The brocolli in the various dishes containing brocoli was fresh. Grilled chicken on a stick. Fried Rice. White rice. Won ton soup. Much more that I don't remember. Lots of families among the clientele this evening (a Friday), and the children were well-behaved. Not a place to impress boss/wife/gf/inlaws. It's good for a family value meal or a cheap date if you like Chinese food, but it's not gourmet. I went here just to rate it. Given a choice of where to go, for this neighborhood, I'd actually go to Asian Spice, just a few blocks up on Emerson. Or if I had to have Chinese and didn't have to have a buffet, I'd go across the street to Bamboo House to order off the menu.

text: Chandler's Steakhouse can give any rated restaurant in LA a run for its money. I sat in a corner sitting in the high chair not far from the bar counter in the lounge area. A waitress quickly brought menus to my attention. Before long, my $8 glass of Sangiovese (Ruffino Chianti Classico '06) arrived in a glass and little carafe and my dinner order of the $30 Idaho Prix Fixe became a ticket in the kitchen. My choice of Idaho corn chowder arrived in no time. A basket of hot roll, crispy on the outside, warm and soft on the inside, accompanied the soup and kept me occupied. Quickly following, the Roast Loin of Lamb (Loin of local lamb encrusted with Dijon mustard and herbs served with polenta, sautéed spinach, and a balsamic, red-wine reduction) was as delicious as expected, though smaller and presented differently than imagined. The polenta was a bit bland, but overall the entrée was quite nice. My choice of dessert, the Grand Marnier chocolate mousse would have won the approval by the bartender, but for me it was way too sweet and I had to forfeit after three spoonfuls. I would have much rather eaten the fresh fruit cobbler, which apple was the cobbler of the day. At the microphone in the lounge area was this Lucy Liu-lookalike with a Renee Zellwegger voice singing standards that I didn't recognize. I didn't stay very long, but I did witness two people who weren't supposed to be together leave together in a cab. the leopard print coat totally gave it away. Compared with Berryhill, I think I prefer Berryhill's menu, atmosphere, and entertainment. The pianist there is much more talented (playing anything from Ravel to Tears for Fears to Coldplay). I will have to eat around more to do a better job of rating these places. see pics!

text: We had eaten here before when it was the Rice Bowl and enjoyed the Pad Thai. Believe it's the same owner, just a relaunched concept. Very broad menu - Vietnamese, Thai, Laotian. This dish was not on the menu, you'll have to ask for the sweet papaya salad. They also have another dish (not on menu) that is a spicy papaya/tomato salad - the server warned us about the heat of that dish, so we tried the sweet version. I had a Thai Basil Chopped Chicken dish over brown rice (white or brown rice, they also have similar dish over a variety of noodles). Very good with a solid spice - very flavorful without a burn. Enjoyed the green peppers and onions throughout, wondered where the jalapenos were. Wife had a chicken curry over brown rice which she enjoyed. She actually ordered tofu, but chicken was delivered and she didn't refuse it. Small place, not busy, but they seem to have loyal customers -- everyone who came in appeared to be a regular. The Hickory Hollow area tends to be chains and pretty generic ethnic restaurants (some of which aren't bad, they're just nothing you can't find all around town). This little strip mall at the corner of Bell and Blue Hole Rds in Antioch has a couple of better than average places -- P.S. Noodle Pot, Los Rosales (creative Mexican), even Rudino's sandwiches aren't bad. I could never find Pho on this side of town when we lived in Antioch -- haven't tried the Pho here, but good to know it's there if I have a cold. We will be back to P.S. Noodle Pot.

text: I have been meaning to review this restaurant for quite a while since I ate here over a month ago but just haven't gotten around to do this what-now-seems-to-be like an unconquerable chore; have you ever meant to accomplish a task but you just put it off to the point where the task becomes more and more difficult until it becomes the equivalent of having a root canal on all of your teeth while simultaneously being constipated while sitting on a you-know-what.(ya I know, what a picture!). There you have it, Mr. Roach resides at the Palace of the Empress. I have to say, the presence of my litte buddy didn't really brother me and did not enter in evaluation of this restaurant. text: I wanted to contribute an "original" review but after reading recent reviews by Al C. and Ann V. I must say that they really describe my recent experience at Zahav's perfectly. My "Jerusalem" brochette (chicken liver and sweebreads) brought tiny bits of charred sweetbread among a couple livers, the "blood orange" panna cotta was so miniscule that it looked as if someone had placed a teaspoon full of my not-yet-arrived panna cotta on a plate as a preview (it turned out to be so gelatinous that I had enough after the two bites). A really minus is the overpriced wine list where inexpensive wines are dressed up in price like an oenophile's treasures. I drank fairly priced beers. Apparently, Zahav's presently is on every national food magazine list as one of 10 best restaurants in the country. Hm, I think this confirms my rather dim view of how magazines make up these lists (think well connected publicist).
label: NEG

text: I'm Indian, so I've been getting threaded since I was old enough to notice my bushy eyebrows. However, in my day the nearest place outside of India was way up in Edison, NJ (India-town). A few years ago one popped up in South Jersey, but now my prayers have been answered with one in Philly! Anju Threads is a cute, albeit tiny place. I was surprised that they suggested appointments (I'm pretty used to walk-in threading), but after seeing how crowded it was, I'm glad I did. If you do walk-in don't worry, because threading only takes a few minutes so you won't be waiting long. I had Dimple and she is very attentive and gentle. Of all the threading I've had, this one seemed to hurt the least. And unlike many other places, she actually sculpted my eyebrows appropriately arched and thinned without constant direction. I'm used to Edison prices so I was a bit shocked, but I can understand why this place charges more. I suppose I'm paying for better service and convenience so it's worth it. I'll definitely be coming back!
label: POS

text: I've never been rushed out of a restaurant so rudely. I came here on a Wednesday night at around 11:15pm. I also checked Yelp before heading out, which listed midnight as the weekday closing time. We enter the restaurant and notice that there is no host/hostess. We wait around for a few seconds and the someone hussles from the back of the restaurant to where we were standing. He informs us that they close at 11 and then proceeds to push us out of the restaurant. Yes, I do mean push -- he didn't touch us, but he walked us out in a way that made us feel like cattle. I began to wonder whether he was trying to hide something going on in the restaurant. On the way out, we mentioned that the Yelp listed the closing time as midnight. Manager: "We don't manage that site." Me: "Yes, but you realize that you can go in and submit changes if the times aren't correct." Manager: "We don't manage that site." Now I know what a rude, malfunctioning C3PO sounds like.

text: Dearest Niche, How do I love thee? Let me count the ways. I love thee to the depth and breadth and height My soul can reach, when feeling out of sight..... .... I've been to Niche about three or four times now. Each time was mindblowingly amazing. I have tried their Prix Fixe menu + wine pairing, the 3 for $40 course menu, and the a la carte goodies as well. I must preface this by stating each time I went was with a boy...on a date....and usually for a special occasion like my Birthday or something. I could not afford to eat Niche on a regular basis, and rightfully so--everything here is a culinary masterpiece. That doesn't mean some dishes are kind of a flop sometimes....they're only human! But still. You can really taste the level of skill that goes into each dish. Each dish is made with skill and calculated precision. I never really liked pork but their pork blew my mind and changed my world. I'd put one piece of pork in my mouth and literally suck on it for a good few minutes before chewing and swallowing as to get the flavors out and savor each one. God. Listen to me. I sound like an Iron Chef critic! :) "Oooh, chairman-sama! The flavors, desu!" However....I almost took off one star because of the seating. It's kind of cramped sometimes. I get that it's supposed to be "modern" and "trendy" cusisine and they want a "modern" sort of set up, but really? I felt awkward talking to my date.... I think we were probably the youngest couple in the entire restaurant too. Me 22, him 26... everyone else was probably our parents' age. Not that that's a bad thing, well...I just wish people wouldn't stare so much at us. Not talking about the waitstaff either, haha. But it really depends on where you sit. This time we were sandwiched between two other tables of people. Last time we had a small little private area in the back all to ourselves. But then again this was a Friday night, and the last time we went, it was probably a weeknight like Wed. or Thurs. BTW the staff are SO friendly and accomodating here. They are not snobby or rude just because we're young foodies in a sea of middle aged folks. (No offense to you middle aged people...!) Anytime I have a question, they don't make me feel stupid with their answer unlike a few other places I've been to. (But could just be a few bad servers at those other places.) I also like the fact that they break down each and every component of your meal upon delivery to the table so you know EXACTLY what it is you're eating and what the word semifreddo actually means.

text: I have been a loyal customer of Sweet Tea since they opened. They have been through many changes since that day. Some for the better, some not. There have been times that the food was not so good but most of the time it is delicious. There have been times when the service has not been so good. But tell me any other restaurant that does not have bad days once in a while. I love having my own pitcher of sweet tea so I don't have to wait for a waitress to bring more. My biggest complaint is that I love lots of lemon and they are kinda stingy with it -- cutting it very thin and then only giving you one or two pieces. On Tuesday, Friday and Saturday nights the owner (extremely talented) plays the organ for us. He calls it the Sweet Tea Calliope. He built this instrument in his garage out of three other organs and it is absolutely fantastic. In one of the above reviews I read that there is no table service and they did not care how the food tasted. I hope he discussed his disappointment with the owner. He needs to revisit. He might be surprised. Canned soda? The place is Sweet Tea, for goodness sake. The service is good -- the food is great -- the entertainment is fantastic. You really have to join me on Tuesday night for a delightful experience.

text: Had dinner here with my husband after the hostess at Bibou recommended the restaurant. The decor and atmosphere was very nice and trendy. We ordered one restaurant week dinner (salad, crunchy salmon roll, roll + 7 pieces of sushi, peach bread pudding), and various a la carte items (tofu, hand roll special, sashimi pieces). Overall the food was good. Dessert on the other hand was disgusting. The dessert had a strange texture and was too sweet. In terms of the restaurant menu, our waitress kept insisting it was a good deal but when we did the breakdown, the restaurant cut portions down and did not really offer a 'deal'. I also wished I read the fine print on the menu because each piece of sashimi i ordered was by the piece (I automatically assumed it was 2 piece an order since this is usually the standard in other Japanese restaurants). For two pieces of shrimp, 2 pieces of tuna, 2 pieces of salmon, and one egg omelet, the total rang up to $29.50 (for seven pieces!!). The portions were a lot smaller than what I get at Sagami's. In my early 20's I would have loved the place and not have minded overpaying for pieces of sashimi. But now that I am in my late twenty's and approaching my 30 yr mark (oh god no!), I prefer a more rustic setting where the food is not only good but worth the value. Don't get me wrong, I don't mind spending on a good meal but it's just got to be worth it for me. To conclude, I would not return to this restaurant.

text: In dire need of a pedicure before we hit flip flop weather, and still cringing from my last experience with cockroaches at my formerly frequented nail spot, I stopped into Deptford Nails hoping for the best. If they are best at anything, it's Being Weird. I was "greeted" by a security system that announced my arrival, and quickly spotted a 4-camera surveillance screen on the wall. Are they afraid someone will come in and rob them of their acetone and pumice stones? My friend and I only waited a few minutes before being shown to our pedi stations. The massage ball of her chair was uncomfortably stuck in a spot that jabbed her at the top of her back, and my foot-soaking water nearly scorched the skin off my feet. When I told one of the employees that it was too hot, he instructed me how to "turn the knob to make it colder." Duh. Not that crowded, but obviously short on help, it was awhile before anyone came over to actually start our services. Since there was only one guy, he worked on my pedi first while my friend sat with her feet getting pruny in water that went quickly from a comfortable temperature to a sweaty lukewarm. It appeared that the tools used on my feet were sterilized, as they were in one of those plastic pouches... except that the pouch still had the adhesive strip on it and had never been sealed. It was a little suspicious, though maybe nothing. The pedicure itself was satisfying. I was surprised when the guy busted out a hot stone for the massage, and my feet went from scary to smooth. I was instructed hang out in the pedi chair while he moved over to my friend, and then maybe I looked away for a couple seconds and missed the switch, but I'm pretty sure he took the tools he had just used on my feet and stuck them on my friend's station to use on her. Immediately, a flash of that unsealed plastic pouch came back to me and I wondered if those tools had simply been taken from the station of the person right before me. *Skeeve* It should also be noted that the owner appears to be lacking some customer service skills. At one point, he showed a woman to the waxing chair, and then 1 minute later walked over to an employee who was working on a woman's nails and barked at her to go wax the other woman, "NOW!" At no point did he address the nail customer and apologize for taking her nail tech away for another service. How rude. My toes look good, and my feet are definitely sandal-ready, but I won't be spending the rest of this season's pedi-cash at Deptford Nails.
label: NEG

text: Not to be confused with the cafeteria, the JSB cafe is right inside Santa Barbara City College, but everyone is welcome to eat there, and I highly recommend a visit even if you have no other reason to be on campus. Santa Barbara City College has its own culinary arts school that rivals some of the best private ones in the nation. I once organized an event on campus which they catered for, and it was completely professional, delicious, and a big hit. Even though I am no longer a student at SBCC, I eat here when I can (they are only open during the academic year for lunch), and am never disappointed. A server will come to your table, and most meals include a free trip to the soup and salad bar. They have a huge selection of sandwiches, salads, shakes, sides, seasonal items, and other alliterations. Prices are low: $6 gets you a generous club sandwich with fries, and shakes and blended drinks are just $3. There is seating both indoors and outdoors, but you can expect crowds any time the cafe is open. Many people are there for take-out, so you should still be able to find a seat. To top it off, you can't beat the location. A fifteen minute bus ride will get you there from Downtown, or you can park at one of the metered stalls steps away from the cafe. SBCC is located at the top of a cliff, and if you like, you can take your meal with you and sit at La Playa Stadium or on the grass at West Campus and enjoy your meal with a view of the ocean. On a clear day, you can see the Channel Islands, and on other days you can still see dolphins jumping in the waves. Just because you were never a student at SBCC doesn't mean you have to miss out on eating at the JSB cafe.
label: POS
