text: Mai Lee, I think we're through. I know...it breaks my heart, too. I remember when you were at your former location and how excited I was to have "discovered" this hole in the wall spot. I remember the HUGE hot steaming bowl of pho that made me fall in love with the dish. I remember the service -- it was kind, patient, welcoming. Now? You're in a bright, shiny, HUGE building with high visibility and high traffic. Good for you. I'm happy that you've found success. But your food, Mai Lee? Your food has SUFFERED. Small bowls of pho. Rushed, impersonal service. And then there's my most recent visit: I thought I'd branch out from my usual order of pho and try something different. I went with #124, eel stir fried in hot chili and lemongrass. It. Was. Terrible. The eel had a bunch of crunchy cartilage in it (or something!). The sauce had a terrible, bitter flavor. I took one bite and did something I normally don't do -- I asked the server if I could replace the dish with something else. I HATE doing this, and I'll usually suffer through a bad dish so I don't have to return it. But this time, I couldn't. I was hungry, and I didn't want to eat this. The server was very unfriendly when I politely informed him of my dissatisfaction. After going to the back to ask his manager if I could exchange my dish, he came back out and basically forced me to order the same dish with a different protein other than eel. Ugh. I wasn't going to argue and make things more complicated. I went with chicken. It was brought out pretty quickly, which makes me think they simply picked out all of the eel and replaced it with chicken. Sigh. The same bitter, awful taste was there. While I don't fault Mai Lee for the dish (hey, someone out there has got to like it, right?) I do fault them for the way they handled the situation. I felt unwelcome. I felt like a pest. I left unsatisfied and still hungry. The one bright spot? My avocado smoothie was amazing! But I'm afraid this will be my last visit to Mai Lee. Sorry...it was fun while it lasted.

text: For a Marriott property, especially one in a prime downtown location like the Philly Marriott Downtown, there were some positives but more negatives about this hotel. First the good: --The lobby, bar area and restaurant were nice, clean, modern and great to hang out at. --The banquet hall floor/area was large, spacious, clean and easily held plenty of people for the dance I attended on Sunday night of Labor Day weekend. Now the not-so-good: --The room (at least my room I stayed in anyways--a room with double beds on the ninth floor) was tired and looked like it hadn't been remodeled in 10-12 years. --No HDTV, but a nice 10-12 year-old television. I make this point because in the last 2-3 years, every hotel I've stayed in (including a Holiday Inn) have upgraded the TVs in the rooms. You'd think a Marriott would too--not this one. --The towels were old, hard and scratchy...not fun. Now the ugly: When I was about to check out, a friend who crashed in my room texted me saying one of his friends staying in another room was bitten by bedbugs in his room. I didn't suffer anything like that in my one night in the hotel. However, yesterday I discovered a bedbug infestation in my bed at home and I've never had a problem with the critters. I know I can't prove the bugs got into my bags and traveled home with me--but they easily travel and people won't know they've brought some home until the red bite marks start showing up after a night's rest. Just saying it's possible my room had 'em too but can't prove it. So when you add it all up...the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown doesn't live up to the expectations one may expect the brand to have.

With our tickets in our hand, we were able to skip the long ticket lines and get right into the attraction line. There was a large bonfire and a band playing. As the line moved on there was fireworks, folks in costumes, and other entertainers. The only problem was...the line stretched on and on. We arrived at 8:30pm and did not reach the front of the house until 12:15am. The metering of the line was non existence and was more of a surging mob than a line. The house...not scary at all. The house led directly into the tunnels, that were scary mainly because they were pitch black. After about 15 minutes it was all over. Once we came out of the tunnel, we were back at the exit. There was no signage or lights for us to head back to our car. There was also no signage out of Pennhurst, and security (once we found them) gave us directions back into the actual Pennhurst campus... Overall, there was lots of potential for the attraction but the missed logistics and long, long lines just didn't make it worth it. Head over to Bates instead.

After walking past the first two places in the order listed above and the first two being extremely packed, we opted to have our Christmas dinner at McDonalds. Upon walking in, there was a long line too but nothing too crazy since it was fast food. It was old and run down. We waited in line for around 15 minutes before we were helped. We ordered 4 McChicken, 1 Double Cheeseburger and 20 piece nuggets. $10.76. We paid and asked for a receipt, she said they need it for processing our order, we then asked for a number, she said she didn't have one and we will be called by the food we ordered...um...okay. We stood there waiting another 15 minutes and was wondering where our food was...since everyone after us seemed to be getting their food. We walked up nicely and asked the status of our order. The employee looked at us confused. She said she didn't take our order? WHAT?!?! You're the only FB behind the counter and there is only 2 of you taking orders! She then said she gave the order to another employee to pull who said she didn't and she was working the fries. By then there was a frenzy and a manager came over and tried to sort out the situation. She then asked what we ordered, grabbed our food and sent us on our way. The burgers were barely wrapped, totally half-assed. And the nuggets were cold, she even gave us the wrong sauce! Oh yeah they limit 3 packages for 20 piece nuggets and $0.11 for every additional packet. Overall, my "fast food" experience at McDonald's was the worst of all my fast food experiences! Although this place is convenient it is slow and definitely not "FAST" AVOID this LOCATION!!!
label: NEG

text: Mike's is convenient for any So. Philly rider who needs to fix a flat while in the neighborhood or for a collector of Stingray kids bikes, but other that that it's just not the bike shop for me. text: Yeah, this place is really weird because there's only one floor, and you expect it to be bigger or have more glamorous areas, but what you see is what you get. I've heard, because there's no hotel attached, that some people have been found on local doorsteps drunk and broke. text: In a non-descript part of northern Indy lives a non-descript, but pretty decent live music venue called Birdy's in what is essentially a steel sided barn. the main space holds about 400 and is perfect for a mid-sized show. there is a main bar and a beer booth on the floor, and then a staircase that leads to a loft-like pool/dining room and another bar. they also have a small outdoor patio with 8 foot fencing. It made me feel a little caged in out there so, i quickly turned around and got a beer. they have the usual beer selection and a couple microbrews (it was nice to be able to get some Bell's Oberon). Everyone was super friendly there, from the guys at the door, to the bartenders, to the people in the crowd. One guy even gave up his seat so i could sit at the ledge to eat my food. what a swell fella! yeah, they have some food, the usual suspects (burgers, club sandwiches) it was above average for a place like this i'd say, but definitely the sound was the highlight here. they also line the walls with posters from past shows. it's only about halfway covered up right now. the beer prices were a bit higher than a normal bar but good for a dedicated music venue. the ticket price was unbeatable though. $7 to see Chamberlain, probably one of the best bands ever to come out of Indy, was definitely well worth it.

text: One of my weaknesses is cheese - I can always pass up a sweet, but rarely can I forego cheese if it is up for grabs. Pretty much anything is game for me, except perhaps Limburger. The Cheese Shop at the Fashion Mall is this city's destination without parallel when it comes to cheese selection. The store typically has over 150 varieties come and go in an average year. One of the favorites here is a house-made spread called Sicilian Creme - a secret recipe that combines cream cheese and herbs. But, one of my all-time faves is a cheese whose name escapes me now, but which has caraway seeds and mustard in it, I believe. And, I never turn my nose up at a good chunk of St. Andre....like buttah! The Cheese Shop also carries a variety of other nosh-ables like meats, salsas, relishes, etc. You can actually get good foie gras here as well. Though I have for the most part sworn off red meat, foie gras will probably always be an Achilles Heel for me! I blame my teenage trips to France for this..... Staff at The Cheese Shop is very knowledgeable and the store usually has samples o'plenty on the sales floor. But, be forewarned, The Cheese Shop doesn't carry Velveeta and developing a taste for fine cheese is like having a hobby - in other words, it's gonna' cost ya! Sure, Trader Joe's and Costco are less expensive, but when in doubt or unable to find what you crave, head to the Fashion Mall. Besides, Godiva is just down a hop, skip and jump away from The Cheese Shop.
label: POS

text: Woohoo is right! Hubby and I found this great place on our fifth day in this lovely city. I settled in at a nice table by the window and he ordered for the both of us.You order and pay at the counter, which is cool. He knows what I like for breakfast and that makes me happy. I got the egg breakfast with bacon and perfect over easy eggs. No toast but the best homemade biscuit ever. Hubby is not a big fan of biscuits but kept sneaking bites of mine and said it was the best he ever tasted(bold statement). He ordered the Envie which is eggs,brie and ham on a fresh croissant. I'm telling you, we were both so happy after eating, it was sinful. The cook (Steven I think), delivers your food which is a great touch. Hubbys' food was delicious and mine was very tasty. We both had the cafe au lait , which was nice and hot and creamy, I added cinnamon to mine. I love this place and will be back every time we come to this fine city. If you're tired of the touristy breakfast places in the Quarter, try this hidden gem just off Bourbon Street, by the river, in one of the oldest areas of the city. If you don't like cool, funky coffee shops with awesome open air seating, great food, and quirky but very cool staff, then I would suggest hitting a Starbucks for a $4 latte and a stale muffin, don't worry we won't miss you.
label: POS

text: I am sooooo happy I found rinse!!!!! Recently, I found myself in the market for a new hair salon. (See my review history if you'd like to know about the old salon). I heard about Rinse though a friend and decided it was worth a shot. I knew I was home when I sat in the chair and Katie (best ever!!!) took one look at my hair and sort of made this distressed face. She asked me what I didn't like about my current cut and when I said "everything" she agreed in this refreshing straight forward no BS sort of way. I have short hair À la early Liza and I can never seem to convey to the stylist how I want it to look. As a result I end up with Catholic schoolboy in the front, US Marine on the sides and Billy Ray Cyrus in the back, but those day are over my friends. I barely raised my hands to explain what I wanted done before Katie stopped me and said that so many stylists end up cutting female sort hair with a men's haircut because they are afraid of sort hair (true!) and that she loved cutting sort hair. She spoke about all of the ways she was going to deal with my heads many problem areas without me even having to explain what and where they were. She is amazing. Rinse is slightly higher in price then I usually shell out for a haircut, but over the years I constantly seem to relearn the age old lesson; you get what you pay for. I was in Rinse for about an hour and was not disappointed with the work I saw from any of the stylists long or short cuts alike, but I highly recommend for short hair! The product brand they use is also awesome, I plan on going with that pomade when I'm through with what's left of my current brand. Relaxed un-pretentious atmosphere is also a breath of fresh air.

The food was full of flavor: gnocchi with mushrooms, asparagus and pecorino-romano cheese in saffron broth, lamb tagine over couscous that was super tender, soy-citrus marinated stried bass over scallion risotto and tempura asparagus, and lamb that was perfectly cooked with a phyllo dough stuffed with goat cheese and black olives. I like that the chef uses fresh ingredients whenever possible and rotates the menu from week to week.

text: I owned restaurants. I managed restaurants. I worked in restaurants. I played music in restaurants. I eat in restaurants almost every day. Go there only if you are not hungry...you will be by the time they get to you. Horrible experience...never go there again!

text: The one thing I despise most about living in the St. Louis Metropolitan area is the complete omission of Korean restaurants. Want Sushi? I can find it. Orange chicken? No problem! Pad Thai? I can name four places. If you want some Bulgogi, Naeng Myun, or Kim Bap, though...you are out of luck! My love for Korean food, and lack of places to get it, has driven me to start cooking more frequently. It's always fun being a mid-twenties white guy walking into the Asian Market. You get a few looks at first, but after seeing you week after week, people start to warm up to you. Chong, the stores namesake, is so incredibly sweet and helpful. Every time I walk in, she rushes over to greet me and asks me what I am going to be cooking this week. She walk through the store with me as I shop to make sure I get everything I need to make the best curry or soup I intend on cooking. She also loves to offer cooking tips to help those first-timers out. Chong makes all of the Kimchi herself, which tastes delicious. The prices in the store are the norm for most Asian stores. Since its I pass it on my way home from work, I usually duck in to grab some Pocky or Koala Yummies (my favorite bite sized snack). I would recommend Chong's market to anyone in the area interested in cooking Asian dishes.

text: Dear (South)Korea, You sure are looking smug these days. Why is that? Is it because of that sweet magic you puled off with Kim Yu-Na at the Olympics? Is it your current World Cup team, who seems to blow up the facebook status updates of my friends every time they so much as sneeze? Is it your liberal use of TADs in the field of Orthodontics and the crazy final results you get, nonsurgically? It could be all of those things, but let's face it. I know why you look so smug - you've won my stomach over. It was a tough battle. I know that little over a year ago, I tried an item called fish cake at a Korean restaurant. I wasn't really impressed by it, but that is probably what I got for going in cold and ordering seemingly at random. This experience put a damper in my appreciation of your cuisine for quite a while and for that I apologize. I should not have been so foolish. Over the many months, you'd spring up once in a while, throwing a bi bim bap or kimchee my way. I had colleagues who would try to set us up at various restaurants and Korean associates would feed me some homemade items. Even though I always liked you(especially your BBQ skills), I wasn't ready to let you get a secure foothold in my eating itinerary. Life was just too complicated. We were friends, but not the kind that called frequently to hang out. After Koreana, something changed. Things suddenly got serious. My regular Thai and Japanese go-tos now had a serious competitor. Places like H-Mart, Miga, and some-Korean-BBQ-place-I-Can't-Remember-The-Name-of paved the way, but Koreana sealed the deal and solidified my serious enthusiasm for Korean food. Koreana did the following things really freaking well: Dol sot bi bim bap - very tender beef, egg, and really fresh tasting veggies stirred all together with rice in a clay pot. After you add the hot sauce to this, you will realize that you sit before something awesome. If you don't like this hot sauce, you should apologize for your behavior to any friends you have remaining because you are probably an asshole. Kimchi bokeum bop - Spicy fried rice dish with chopped kimchee and egg. Really great. Goon mandu - Fried pork and veggie dumplings. They are good but comparable to dumpings that can be achieved at other Asian food restaurants. Jaeyook dup bap - meat and veggies in a thicker, spicy sauce. Oh yeah, and the items were pretty darn cheap and pretty darn fast and their hot sauce...oh, be still my beating heart. It was excellent. So you see, (South)Korea, your cuisine will be getting many more of my dining dollars in the years to come. It has been a long road, but one that I'm happy to have traveled. Sincerely, Brad P.

text: "If you like it then you shoulda put a tot on it" "If you wanna be my lover, gotta get with my tots" "I gotta feeling, that tonight's gonna be a tot night" When you're sitting at the Grill, coming up with all of the lyrics for which you can sub in the word tot, the possibilities seem endless! The music is indescribable, the waitstaff rotates faster than an old 45, and the food isn't going to win an culinary awards this year. But you can't beat sitting around with a few friends, noshing on fried tater tots, rewriting classic pop hits: That's what the Grill is made of. It doesn't matter how hard you partied beforehand, how early you need to be up tomorrow, or how you don't really need a hamburger at 1AM, all is forgiven and forgotten when you walk into the Grill. Everybody is in the same boat, and they don't care much about you or your table because they're coming up with things like, "I run for tots," and "We built this city on rocks and tots" at their table. I've been at the Grill when I should have probably gone to bed. I've eaten a hamburger when I should have realized what obscene hour it really was. I've sat at the Grill when it was my turn to drive the group home, and I wasn't in the same 'spirits' as the rest. And I have to say, every single one of those times has been a blast. The burger isn't half bad. Get it with some grilled onions and mushrooms to round out the flavor and add depth. More importantly, the service has been great, and that's what keeps me going back. It's a downtown restaurant icon. And if you can get past the strange tunes, odd decor, and just decent diner grub, you'll find a glimmer of something special that will make it so you go back more than once. And if you do, you might see me. The waitresses call me, "That tot guy!"

text: I'd like to find my favorite burger in Philly. It's a fun quest. I've heard a great deal about Rouge; in fact, a "I'm Feeling Lucky" google search for best burger in Philadelphia will bring up Rouge as #1. In 2005, it was voted one of the best in the country. Considering the data, I went into Rouge with high expectations. Rouge is a small eatery right off Rittenhouse Square with tables and a small bar area. Dan and I rolled in for lunch on a Thursday and sat at the bar. Beers available included a variety: Stoudt's Pils, Yeungling, Duvel, Amstel Light, ect. They were $5 to $9, and everything was about twice as much as it should be. These were all 12oz bottles, no drafts available. The bar is in line with the rest of Rouge: priced to make you (or maybe just me) not want to partake. Needless to say, I had only water. And of course they only serve Fiji. Everything is fancy here. The atmosphere is posh. Rouge has weird curtains along all of the walls and tables scattered around a small, circular bar in the middle of the room. When the weather is nice, there is a good sized outdoor seating area. The service is good, but nothing special. Dan and I split a mediocre calamari to start. It came with a great sauce, the the squid and the breading were bland. After a short wait, my much anticipated burger arrived. The burger is just enormous. With my first bite, I was impressed with a few aspects. The meat is perfectly cooked, despite the size. Further, the burger was very juicy and excellently seasoned. And it was served on a great buttery roll that added to the whole experience. But overall, I wasn't blown away. The burger serves up a huge portion of meat, with a delicious side of fries, but failed to leave a lasting impression. The toppings, especially onions and gruyere cheese are nice. Bottom Line: It's not that Rouge's burger is bad, but it doesn't live up. There are quite a few more in the city that I'd perfer (and can afford). In all honest, I wouldn't recommend this spot to anyone, and I don't see myself ever going back. Rouge might boast that they offer a "truly unique dining experience," but it's not one that I want.

It might even be a tumor or cancer of some sort (he said this to us like it was no big deal, I was horrified). Several days later, my cat's eye is still swollen and he won't eat. After doing some research online, it's pretty clear that my cat has conjunctivitis in his eye which can also cause the lack of appetite. It's pretty ironic that I was able to diagnosis my cat, considering I don't have a vet degree. The only way he could've gotten this is by being at the vet and if they did not use gloves, clean instruments, or proper handling techniques. None of my other cats have this, so he did not pick it up from any of them. I am furious. Do not ever take your animal here. I will be calling them first thing in the morning to complain and demand they pay for any additional care or medication for the conjunctivitis. text: The rumors and reviews are true. What used to be a way above average sushi experience - it is in my memory, as it seems to be in many other reviewers - is now thoroughly disappointing, pushy, and not worthy of a return trip. But... Ru San's menu is SO huge. And exciting. The dinner menu looks so full of creative sushi that it just may lure me back. First I have to recover from my lunch buffet experience. Please continue. I went to Ru San's for the infamous sushi buffet. It was scarcely filled with business types enjoying lunch. Hardly packed, yet the music was LOUD. I wonder if a crowded Friday night drowns out the volume of the techno music. The cost is around $10, plus tax. Pretty good price if you want to eat more than a roll or two's worth of sushi. However, at Ru San's buffet, I thought I was paying for variety. Wouldn't you assume that a sushi buffet suggests many different types of sushi? Think again, because almost every single piece of sushi on the buffet 1) was fried, 2) was made of some combination of a) avocado, b) cucumber, and c) imitation crab, and last and certainly not least, 3) was ugly. Sushi is about presentation, and I think I could have rolled a prettier roll at home with my home sushi kit. Mastering the art of sushi takes YEARS, and while it doesn't bother me that the sushi "chefs" at Ru San's don't have many years of sushi-making under their belt, the sushi they are rolling could at least look a little more appetizing. Oh, and there wasn't a piece of nigiri in sight. I remember Ru San's buffet including a variety of hot dishes, many of them very un-Japanese. I remember some creamy pasta things, foods that included cheese and other egg/dairy ingredients. These were inauthentic, but tasted good. Well, these items were no longer present. They were replaced by what looked like mediocre take-out Chinese, and a poor imitation of squid tempura. At the end of my meal, I was urged by a waiter to try the dessert of fried banana (the only dessert presented on the buffet) because it was "so good!" Well, I had already had one piece, and one piece was more than enough. When I paid and got up to leave the same waiter said, "See you tomorrow!" You know what? No. They won't see me tomorrow, and never again for lunch. But like I said, I'll have to get back to you when it comes to dinner at Ru San's. Here is my reasoning: Their menu is so enormous and creative. Deceiving, considering 85% of the items don't seem to see the light of the lunch buffet. Ru San's is also the only Japanese place I know of that offers Zipang, the sparkling sake drink. And they have some inexpensive offers, like dollar per sushi specials. And you can get just a few pieces of one roll, allowing you to sample a large variety of foods in one meal. As stated, the verdict is out.

text: My wife and I were looking for a cool place to get dessert. We had heard about La Creperie and were really looking forward to trying it out. When we entered, we were shown to our table pretty quickly by a nice, albeit slightly scatter-brained, host. The atmosphere felt very "thrown together". Like someone took a french class, got inspired to make crepes, and started a restaurant after a quick stop at Ikea to pick up accents. It's clear that the place strives for an air of sophistication, but it did not take long for that illusion to fade. For starters, I found the table and chairs to be kind of uncomfortable. Our table was wobbly and the chairs were too high for our wobbly table. Okay, to be fair, I'm being rather picky here, aren't I? However, enter our server. My wife ordered a glass of water and I ordered a cup of coffee. The glass of water comes in what is, essentially, a glorified shot glass. It was a tall, very thin kind of glass. My wife drank it down almost instantly, and really, who wouldn't? She quickly ordered another glass (and jokingly ordered "about 5 more of these"). Then there's my cup of coffee. It was actually served to me in a cup that was filled to the brim with coffee with a significant amount of coffee already spilled into the saucer. A little coffee in the saucer never hurt anyone, but it is unacceptable to serve me a cup that is swimming in a saucer like that. It's a mess and a very sloppy presentation for a place that is going for this sophisticated vibe. But that's not all. It is important to understand that I drink a lot of coffee and I certainly know a good cup from a bad cup. This, my friends, was burnt coffee. BURNT. A cardinal sin in my book. I couldn't drink anymore after 1 or 2 sips and the aftertaste was wretched. So, my wife and I were very annoyed at that point. We were both wondering what kind of place La Creperie was and who was running it. A place that serves small glasses of water and doesn't pay attention to something as vital and simple as coffee is not worth the money. We looked over the menu and to La Creperie's credit, they did have a nice long dessert menu. Their menu items are written in french with the ingredients written in english. I didn't see a huge concentration on chocolate, which was a bummer. The prices on the other hand were a little high. Most of the dessert crepes seemed to be in the $8-$10 range. If the experience up to this point hadn't been a bust, we might have stayed to see what the crepes were like. However, based on what we were seeing (and the fact that my wife's other glass of water STILL hadn't been served) we decided it was time to just get up and leave. The bottom layer was yellow cake with chocolate chip and butter cream, I amongst all my guest at my daughters party were very upset with it, it was very dry. Now the second layer I did cut and taste, and that was chocolate with butter cream, now that layer was delicious, but no one wanted to taste that layer after their disappointment with the bottom layer!!! Their not consistent with their batters, I just feel for the price of the cake it should of melted in my mouth and I was dissatisfied with it eating and tasting wise, but for appearance they did a GREAT JOB !! I probably won't be buying another cake form here, because I would worry if it is gone to taste good !!! As for my Daughter she loved the appearance but wouldn't even eat the cake after having tasted the first piece , I wound up trashing it !!!
label: NEG

text: I was heading home the other day and decided to try Panda Hut Express. Sure enough, the claimed drive-thru window was here. I couldn't believe it when they told me it was open until 11. If you're looking for some quick Chinese food, this is the place to go. Everything is made quickly and tastes great...for fast food Chinese that is. They have a wide selection of menu items...perhaps a compilation of all fast food Chinese places rolled into one menu. They also offer party trays as well, which are good for 12 to 32 people. You basically choose the menu items yourself, and they will make enough for the selected amount of people. Obviously the more people you have, the cheaper the meal works out to be. It's much cheaper than pizza, and just as filling. If you want to try something new, you can order your food online. I have not tried this out myself, but I am definitely curious. There are also daily specials from Monday to Thursday. If you're in the south side and crazy cheap (and quick) Chinese food, Panda Hut Express should be on your list.
label: POS

text: So when your job is to get some networking done by any means necessary, wouldn't you crash a dinner event that was running at the Constitution Center from a conference that was running in tandem with your own but you weren't supposed to go to? Me too! As an events venue, it was really beautifully done and there was a lot of space for people to mingle and high tables for setting things on but not putting you in the position where you have to sit and be anti-social. The best part was the rooftop bar where they had a DJ. There's nothing better than watching PR professionals dance to such refined tunes as "Salt Shaker". Yes, oh yes, we brought the CS to its full potential. The founding fathers would be proud.
label: POS

text: tried again. they have switched their "restaurant" location.... it's actually right across from the take out section which is interesting in and of itself, because they just walk over and get everything from the takeout side. hmmm... the buffet was ok. it had great potential, but it was just ok. even if onions, garlic and mushrooms aren't used, so many other spices can add texture and depth to seasoning the food or one runs the risk of bland food... the food on the buffet was bordering on bland, as is their customer service.... i enjoyed the firmness of a tofu dish but the seitan was soft.... the butternut squash soup had great potential, but it was like, at the top of the peak needing a little something to push it over the edge... hmmmm... peace & spice
label: NEG

text: This place is a surprisingly authentic taqueria considering it's in Philadelphia -- and how disappointing taquerias I've visited in New York have been. I ordered a burrito de res (beef with sauteed onions and peppers). For the $7.50 fee it was appropriately gargantuan, filled with rice, beans, pico de gallo, corn niblets (?), crema, and cheese. It was a little rice heavy, the beef was an eency bit tough, and the peppers were a bit under cookied... but all in all, it was a good try. And I loved the restaurant itself -- very similar to my favorite Californian taquerias :).
label: POS

text: Took 7 year old granddaughter here. (Took her mother here 18 years ago) Very well maintained. Very nice museum. Beautiful garden & grounds in general. Had the added excitement of a small child sticking his head between the metal bars of the little fenced area & getting stuck (poor thing) fire department was called to help him out. Absolutely visit if you get the chance. well worth the effort.
label: POS

text: Good Thai food for a VERY good price. The selection here is huge, and includes one of my Thai faves: beef salad, which is sauteed beef, onions, cilantro (and other veggies), chilled and served over hot steamed rice. It's spicy and wonderful, but the last time I was there it was offered as an appetizer when I asked for it. My portion was perfect. I really like their spring rolls, and they offer a fish cake appetizer that goes well with rice. Additionally, their summer rolls are fantastic (and huge!). It's a low-key atmosphere, and you're not going to get ridiculously great service, but you definitely won't get bad service. I got everything on time and the right order. That's all you could ask for when there's a table full of great food right in front of you.
label: POS

text: Basically, this place is one big outdoor Chuck E. Cheese's! Tackiness everywhere. Crying, tired kids everywhere. Angry, tired parents everywhere. I felt like I needed to take a bleach bath after visiting this place. Do they even have pick your own? I didn't see it. All I saw was food vendors selling crap. Stay away from this dump.
label: NEG

text: After you outgrow Disneyland/world, you come here. The coasters are sweet and all have their redeeming points. I believe I did them all and had a great time. Lines get long starting in early afternoon, but we didn't wait longer than 30min during peak time. I suggest getting there early, doing as much as you can, and when things get crowded do the gondola, and or enjoy some food. I like that you can walk around drinking a beer. Speaking of beer, I would also suggest signing up early for the beer tasting class offered. This caps out later in the day and you usually have to sign up on session in advance, but free beer! Also, at the main hub you can get 2 free mini beers. Careful hitting the coasters after both of those...
label: POS

text: This may be the worst service I have ever had in over 50 years of eating out. The food was not to my liking. I left without finishing
label: NEG

text: This place stinks, both as a place to eat, and as a place to go out at night. Let us start with the food. Disgusting. I guess that's all I really have to say about it, I've tried several things, and all of them were really, really gross. Don't eat the food here, even on Taco Tuesdays. This place is all over the map, Mexican, Hawaiian, american. who knows. As a club, or whatever it tries to be at night. Also, horrible. It's worse than most places in SB, and too small to boot. The dance floor is about 6 X 6, although they do have a pole, so that counts for something I suppose. The used to have girls dress up as mermaids, and swim in a tank behind the bar, and I must admit, that was pretty cool. But apparently, not "healthy' or something cause they had to shut it down As a sports bar, it is passable. They have a huge amount of television's here, and on Sunday's they have all the games going on, usually with a rather boisterous crowd...but I prefer Madison's personally... Two redeeming features: If you just want to have a few drinks, the outside patio, front or back, is pretty cool. I like out front so you can watch the people walk by. Secondly, the make your only bloody mary bar is a cool concept...but I'm no professional bartender...that's why they're there. but if you know exactly how you like...it's pretty sweet.
label: NEG

text: A small salon tucked unassumingly in the bottom of an apartment building, you'll have to keep your eyes peeled to spot Elevate. The stylists here are all super friendly and chatty, and happy to offer you coffee, tea, or water while you wait for your appointment. A fun and laid-back atmosphere while you get your hair done, and plenty of new gossip mags to go around. I love the hair products Elevate carries. Rusk is a favourite of mine, but other brands are available too, and they always have the newest products for you to try. I was sooo happy with my cut and colour here. Will be going back for sure!
label: POS

text: If you're in the mood for cheap wings and PBR, Manny Brown's is the place for you. Have fun putting up with the South Street crowd. It isn't expensive and the service tends to be quick, but don't expect much.
label: NEG

text: I've never had a bad time at Noche, well except for the time I opened the door to the bathroom and there were two girls in there and they slammed the door in my face and the bouncer who was waiting with me started laughing. Actually that was pretty funny so I guess I haven't had a bad time here. Noche is my shot place, it's a great spot to just start pounding them down with friends and get some pizza to soak up the alcohol. Many fun nights in the dark open room at Noche.

text: The staff on Second Street is so friendly, and truly a staple in the First Friday ballin'-on-a-budget lifestyle. The Rittenhouse location, not so much. They're delivery service is arbitrarily determined on how much you're spending. "15 dollars? No, you need to pick that up" was something that was actually said to me on the phone. The size and selection of the wraps is a bit better than the Pita Pit, but the taste and service dwarfs in comparison - not to mention delivery. As a result, I've taken my business there.

text: What a fantastic Experience!! It was our 1st trip to New Orleans and we really wanted to try something unique to New Orleans. We discovered this place with the help of Yelp and it was quite a find! The New Orleans sampler was incredible and served with a Cesar salad. The 5 layer Chocolate was a true experience, the BEST I have ever had!

text: Some of the best food I've ever eaten. Period. Great service, beautiful ambiance and amazing food. It's expensive so get over that fact before you go. Worth every penny in my opinion.

text: Club fit is a nice enough place but it wasn't for me. I'll start with the positives. They had a booster juice inside which was great for after workouts and... and... ??? Ya, that's about the only positive. I can't quite put my finger on why I don't like this place. It's not just the lack of equipment, I often found myself having to wait to get a machine or a weight and that slowed down my routine. It's also not the fact that people here are all so anti social, and I don't mean they need to talk or anything but they just look down right awkward. Everyone is so into themselves here, it's weird. On top of all that the service is bad. When I wanted to cancel my membership it was eerily similar to that one Friend's episode. You know the one. Where Chandler wants to quit his gym and then they send him to keep talking to different people who just don't let him quit and he ends up trying to cancel his bank account instead so the gym can't make withdrawals from it anymore. That's exactly how I felt. They told me to talk to some person, then they sent me to another, and that person tried to make me explain why I wanted to quit before they would let me. No offense to anyone but if I want to cancel that's my business and at the end of the day that's what this place is. It is a business, don't expect anything extra.
label: NEG

text: Have been in a couple times and really enjoyed the beer! The drafts change frequently and there's lots of interesting stuff to try in the bottles. Cool vibe, but small.

text: I really like this place but the food is not up to par. The idea and location is great. Mid-city needs a breakfast/lunch spot that's fresh and organic but this place is not it. This week there was only one item on the menu that was vegetarian and it wasn't very good. The juices are pulpy and are not made with organic fruit and veggies. The staff and the restaurant are awesome but the food is really lacking. I came home after eating lunch and was hungry an hour later because my sandwich was just blah. My husband ate a sandwich that was basically just bread, there was hardly anything on it. They need to really step it up.

text: I was in the mood for a burger and I thought it was time to try this place since I've walked by so many times the last few months and it looks busy. The service was good, the prices were right but the burger, while it was cooked well like I wanted, it so was dry it crumbled, not only that I'm fairly certain they cooked it previously and reheated it because it was not totally warm all the way through. If I wanted a rewarmed burger I would go to McDonalds.
label: NEG

text: They have a good collection of teas and tea utencils. However, the lady at the counter is not so nice. The store offers an array of tea, but nothing too exotic or special. Tea cups and tea pots are also over priced, and you can get them cheaper online. :) If you are dying to get a good quality tea drinks NOW, go for it. If you are looking for a place to get good loose tea and a good service, don't go.

text: The service was fine once we got to our table. But the food was a major disappointment. I had the fried chicken and it was extremely bland the food in general was completely forgetable. If you are trying to make up your mind where to go while in New Orleans definitely pass on this place.

text: If you need custom or factory wheels repaired or replaced, this is the place to go. They can fix bent, dinged, scuffed, dented, or even cracked rims and make them like new again. You can also buy new tires and wheels or have wheels painted too. The owner and all employees are very helpful and knowledgeable. Nu Wheel also offers precision CNC machining services.
label: POS

text: Oy vey, St. Louis. Surely we can do better than this. I'll echo what previous reviewers have said: yes, good service; yes, clean and spacious; yes, spare but lovely decor. Honestly, though, that's like telling someone that the jerk you're dating is worthwhile because he has a full set of teeth. Foodwise, this place simply doesn't cut it. Vietnamese food is all about flavors, and this is among the blandest food I've tasted. Their vermicelli bun with chicken (generally a healthy and delicious staple at a Vietnamese place) is topped with a toothy slab of near-unseasoned chicken breast rather than the savory strips the dish usually comes with. The egg rolls are greasy, uninspired lumps. The stir-fries are soggy. The fried tofu tastes like toilet paper. And -- most damning of all! -- there's nary a strong cocktail in the joint to wash away the sorrow of your dull, unappetizing meal. Get thee down to South Grand if you feel the need for good, cheap Vietnummies. Mama Pho, Lemongrass, and Pho Grand are all eagerly awaiting you with much, much better food than this.
label: NEG

text: I am far from a healthy person, I smoke, drink too much coffee, eat what I like, well you get the point... but when I hear words "smoothie" and "fantastic" at the same time, my interest is piqued.... I stopped by Bryn and Dane's... not sure what to expect... I was greeted very warmly and offered a quick explanation of what they are and what they do... Yes, it is a place if you want to be healthy.... and yes, the smoothies are fantastic!!! Also, I asked to try their coffee, so that I can have an alternative to Wawa and Seattle's Best... They had Columbian French Roast.... while not my favorite, it was good and the price is definitely right... Definitely recommend this place!!
label: POS

text: For a place that seems to be located out in the middle of nowhere, this place is a mecca. They have an excellent produce section, a decent selection of meats. There is a pharmacy and a Little Clinic. They also have free coffee for the adults and free cookies for the kids back in the bakery.

I was quite disappointed on the search for good chinese still and if anyone tells me they love Panda Express I may have to hit you because that to me is just as icky.

text: I've been a devotee of the King's falafel with feta cheese (and hot sauce) for more than 10 years. It's got a slightly different flavor than some of the other good falafel places in the city -- it's a little sharper than Mama's, for instance. Maybe more lemon is involved? Anyway, I love it. Always consistent, always delicious, and healthy for a cheap lunch in Center City (I'm pretty sure that the wraps are made with whole wheat). I also echo everyone else about the amazing value of this place -- I think they've only changed their prices once or twice since 1995. I really can't say enough good things. Go here for lunch!

text: This bbq place is amazing, it has a great down home feeling to it. It is a great mom and pop place with friendly people that are working there. The prices are very reasonable and just the feeling of being there is like my own mother's home. The brisket and pulled pork are to die for, they melt in your mouth like butter. The sides I had were Dad's worlds famous beans and those were great. The other side I had was the fresh made curly fries, they were great because they did not salt them. Overall the best place in tucson for real bbq.

text: I think this is location is par for the course with other Red Lobsters that I've been too. Really busy but not special at all and kinda a mess. I wouldn't have picked here by my bf was obsessed with the crabfest promotion they currently have. Our server John was nice and I felt for him because he said tonight was the fourth double shift in a row he had to work but he lagged on EVERYTHING. I ordered a strawberry margarita and it wasn't until after our salads came out that he brought it. Also, my boyfriend spilled his beer and we needed more napkins which we asked about and never got. Finally my dad just asked the greeter if we could get more and she gave us a huge stack. The biscuits are amazing as I remembered and John did great in bringing us more when we needed it. The margarita was pretty tasty too. The food was kinda bland, but then again I love seafood restaurants that do fresh seafood and have spoiled myself.

Terrible, terrible, terrible service. I mean, if you were not going to serve me, at least tell me CONGENIALLY that you are not serving any more.

text: One word comes to mind: squish. Do NOT wear anything other than the oldest shnarliest pair of shoes you own to this place. Chances are you're gonna want to toss them afterwards anyways. Pretty sure the "soil' (which is a stretch) is 90% duck droppings. -Families: the park on the South end of the lake is generally okay and tends to be less duck-poop ridden. Not much seating though, and is right on the road. So be vigilant with the kids. -Feed the ducks at your own risk. It can be fun....but once they know you have food it turns into bird poop bombing and feather mayhem. I'm serious, they're brutal. Might even disturb small children.... -Runners: It's an okay place to get your run on. But, like I mentioned earlier...old shoes. -Walkers: If you're not here for a serious aerobic workout or to feed the ducks, then just....don't come. Seriously, go the extra few miles to Idlewild. Sidenote: nothing like rotting bird carcasses and algae that looks like toddlers boogs to getcha in a good mood. Guh-ross.

text: Great atmosphere and old time feel. This place will transport you to a different time. The chocolate ice cream isn't great, you could taste the coco powder, but the Oreo ice cream was dense, creamy and delicious. It's great on a hot summer day, just beware of the weekends. We went at 5:30 hoping to miss the rush but they were totally backed up and it was over an hour wait for a shake. Will be back.

text: A pathetic hair cut for a huge price. Had an appointment after work at 6pm (the salon closes at 7). I think that was a big mistake as she seemed to be in a great hurry to finish up. When I took the appointment I informed the lady over the telephone that I have really thick hair and need some one experienced; so the lady receommended Maria who supposedly has 20 years of experience. Went for the appointment and told Maria that I want a style that would require less maintenance while it looked professional enough. She recommended emphasizing my wavy hair instead of ironing it. Sounded like a plan to me. Went for a wash and came back, she trimmed it by an inch or so even though Iwanted it shorter; she told me it wouldn't look nice, so I kept quite. She finished cutting it in under 15 minutes which must be a record for my hair and started blow drying it. Then she ironed it partly so now it looked like I had tried ironing my hair for the first time in my life.When I told her to make changes she told me to be happy with what I have as many people don't have hair! I don't really need to hear that. Can't wait for my hair to grow out of this. Actually had to come home and cut a lock of hair that she had missed!

text: If you are having difficulty shedding those pesky last five pounds or find it impossible to remember "portion control" try the Jet Rock Bar and Grill weight loss method! The pervasive presence of big screen television sets broadcasting sports will give you vertigo and the vague sense of nausea. Staff members will not give you eye contact or acknowledge you while you stand, patiently waiting to be seated... Then, when you decide to help yourself to a menu to peruse during your ridiculous wait, Sandra the Server will snatch said menus out of your hand and curtly show you to a table. Your veggie burger will be as dessicated as the dead beetle right behind your dust bunny infested station. When you politely mention that some "light house keeping" would be in order, Sandra the Server will retort, "That's my lunch." Verbatim. Sandra the Server informed me of her insectivore meal from across the room and couldn't be bothered to address my concern in any way. She didn't acknowledge the mess visually, much less get a bar towel or cleaning supplies to give it a quick wipe-down. The greens plated on the Goat Cheese Salad are wilted and no amount of "sunscreen" or filler could rehydrate them. If you love cheese, as I do, skip this dish altogether and spare yourself the greasy, golf ball sized gobs of chevre. Five stars, all the way. *eye roll*

text: My boyfriend and I come here every time we are in town. We always feel like "home" when we are here. Cute sushi place and the owner is super nice and friendly. So genuine and sweet! The sushi is really good and very affordable. The special dressing for the salad is YUMMY, Spider Roll, Short Ribs, Tempura Shrimp, etc...are lovely. I can go on (I always order A LOT, and Mama always makes us special rolls. SHE IS THE BEST !!!!!!). This is a great place for everyone. I give this place a 5 star all-around. I am a foodie, so I know what to expect when I walk into a place. This is a family owned restaurant and I definitely feel good when I leave. I love it here! BTW, there isn't any "reverse" asian racism. The owner is a sweet and helpful lady who sometimes works all by herself! And when she does have help, it's one other girl! So to see a one bad review on here is frivolous. People need to look at the bigger picture and stop being so insecure.

text: I read Gary C.'s review and was intrigued by his pancake review. Why aren't there any good pancake places around here? Restuarant is small and dated. Decor consists of old telepole poles, plastic plants, plastic tablecloths. I had the omelette special with spinach, onions, bacon and swiss. I could make better at home. Potatoes were baked and not greasy. Fruit cup was watery and tasteless. Guest had the pancakes. Although my coffee was refilled, Guest's tea was not. (They have Lipton BTW.) The waitress never came back to check on our beverages. Take the trip and go to Gilchrist's Offshore in Egg Harbor City instead.

text: This Urban Outfitters is on the way to the French Quarter so we stopped in to do a little shopping! The store is really big, and has a second level for their novelty type items. Also, its really clean and organized which I really liked, because the ones in Houston can sometimes turn in to a free for all with clothes everywhere. They had a really great sale going on in the front, with the women's clothes in the middle of the store, and the men's clothes in the back. I left with a pair of shoes for my boyfriend which were fairly inexpensive! Overall, fun store to get lost in!
label: POS

text: Went back to Swift Half, partly egged on by Craig LaBan's review in today's Inquirer. The Eagles were playing the Chiefs, so the bar was nicely filled with fans, many wearing number 7 Eagles jerseys (not for Vick, but old Garcia shirts). Loud but nice ambience. I ordered the soup special, Italian Wedding Soup, and the Fish and Chips. As for the half pints, only a couple of the beers on tap were available in that format (a very good Brooklyn Pumpkin Ale and a very smoky PBC porter). The service, as on previous visits, was friendly and efficient, the food was another matter. The soup, although of decent stock, featured large pasta shells that were so overcooked and mushy, I could not bring myself to eat on. As for the fish and chip, I had no recent memory of a worse rendition. Grotesquely thick (in some places over half-an-inch), and oozing oil, the darkly fried batter made it impossible to taste the fish inside (I scraped out some oil-soaked morsels). Alarmed by the piles left on the plate, the waitress inquired about the state of the food and I described it as above. This brought Amy, the efficient and competent manager to the table, expressing regret and taking the dish off my bill. Nice gesture, I thought. Except, when she came back, she informed me that the dish was served as customary (and typical of Ireland) and that LaBan got the same batter. Whatever. Leo Burdock's rendition in Dublin certainly did not look or taste anything like the Swift Half version. A real disappointment.
label: NEG

text: A hodge-podge menu No sense of identity Bad fake Asian food ______ It's not good, even by desert standards. It's also expensive, to boot. I'd rather eat "California" rolls from Safeway--they're cheaper and more authentic.
label: NEG

text: I dont think I can ever get sick of Great Basin! I eat there once a week, and order the same thing each time: Blackened Blue Cheese Chicken Sandwich and side of Beer Cheese Soup. Eachtime it is great! I've had the Sheppard's Pie too. It is the best that I have ever had. They make it with lamb, and I HATE lamb. Their artichoke dip is pretty mouthwatering too! As for their beers, I love them! Bitchin Berry is by far my favorite. It is the best berry beer I have ever tried (and I've tried atleast 10 different ones from other microbreweries). If that isn't on tap, the Nevada Gold is pretty good too! The customer service is alway good, and the owner is around at lunch times to make sure things are running smoothly. Their outdoor patio makes a nice place to chill for a casual lunch! Also, make sure to try "tightwad tuesdays." Most beers are only $2!
label: POS

text: They were reviewed in the Philadelphia Inquirer's Food section some months ago, so I called them and had them fax over a menu. My co-workers and I have ordered from them quite a bit since then. Personally, I go for the Heuser Hoagie, which has cotteghio, prosciutto, olive spread, sharp provolone, sopressata and imported hot carpaccio. The olive spread is made from unpitted green olives ('cause I bit on a pit once, I know ;-) ) and is an excellent substitute for oil or mayo. They have freshly made fries and real batter fried onion rings. Some of my co-workers like to get the side greens as actual sides and say that the spinach and broccoli rabe are very good. The Zig is another signature dish, a steak sandwich with mild provolone, sharp provolone, greens, and roasted peppers. My co-workers have raves for this. They do have daily specials, though one has to tack on an extra dollar if ordering the signature hoagie/steak sandwich. Also, their current menu is slightly outdated, so we have to add on an extra fifty cents per item, except for the sides. I am hoping they order new menus soon, as this is irritating to have to explain over and over again. Of course, if you eat in, this is not an issue. I've been to their place, and it's clean, with wooden floors and booths and diner car steel accents. You order from one window and pick up from the other and they set out pickles, hots, and other things for your sandwiches.
label: POS

text: Ok, so Raising Cane's is a local fast food chain. For fast food, this was surprising in a couple respects. 1. This place was cleaner than you can imagine - like, cleaner than any hospital I've ever been in. The bathrooms, the kitchen, dining area, even the parking lot - spotless. You could eat off of any floor in the place. Very surprising. 2. Decor was surprising, not fast food joint: Velvet elvis on the wall, as well as movie posters from cult classics ranging from easy rider, pulp fiction, to Anchorman. Funny. 3. Menu consisted of chicken fingers only. 3 or 4 finger meals or a handful on a bun. Sides were fries and/or slaw. Only one sauce choice unless you count ketchup. 4. The chicken was ok, not like KFC or Churches good, but ok. 5. Staff was really, really nice. No attitude which is so common in fast food joints. The cashier spied my military ID and gave me a discount without me asking or anything. All in all, I may go back if I'm hankering for fried chicken strips because its was a really nice, clean place, but they need a grilled option and 3-4 sauce choices at a minimum. A buffalo, Jerk, Thai or BBQ sauce would have bumped it up to a 5-star easily.

text: I really like King of Prussia. The Court was everything the Plaza was not -- clean, sunlight, high ceilings, bright gleaming white paint, and upscale shops -- a Bloomingdale's, for Christ's sake! This curious mismatch was one of the largest shopping areas in the US -- the largest in East, the third largest in the country, etc. But the day of the high Court lording over the lowly Plaza were numbered. The new Plaza is by itself one of the largest malls in the country. The new Plaza has everything -- abercrombie, Abercrombie & Fitch, American Eagle, Apple Store, Armani Exchange, Coach, Crate and Barrel, Diesel, Express, Forever 21, Gap, GUESS?, Hollister, J. Crew, Janie and Jack, Kenneth Cole, Lily Pulitzer, Lord & Taylor, Louis Vuitton, Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, Old Navy, Pac Sun, Puma, Sanrio, Sony Style, Starbucks, Tiffany & Co., Versace, and more -- and a lovely food court. text: The wildly varied responses to this place reflect one of two things: either people don't know what to expect from Texas BBQ, or the reviews are a result of a newly opened restaurant that's still working out its kinks. That said, I didn't experience any of the kinks--in fact, I commented on how impressive the service was, especially considering the place has been open for only 2 weeks. I didn't experience the kinks... nor, oddly enough, the BBQ. Because I don't eat meat (what?!). So what the hell kind o' business does a vegetarian have evaluating a BBQ joint? I walked away stuffed. So there. My boyfriend lived in west Texas for years, and was salivating when we saw the BBQ joint opening soon. I can make a meal out of side dishes, so I happily went along for the ride. They have vegan chili, which was tasty, and a baked mac & cheese that was quite delish as well (note: these, and the coleslaw are the only dishes that are truly vegetarian; the beans, mashed potatoes, german potato salad, collard greens are all made with meat and/or animal fat). Best part of the meal, though was the banana pudding (save room). BF had the pecan pie. mmmmmm. The atmosphere is inviting, and very well done--complete with movable walls that expand the restaurant when needed. The beer/wine/bourbon list is small but selective; the service was very attentive without being intrusive. I had a blast, and want to see this place succeed. I will definitely be back, if only to see the bf's smile as he indulges his west Texan cravings.

text: The Koreans in this country have an unshakeable reputation for running kick ass food markets. Stroll up and down the avenues in Manhattan in the spring and see the sidewalk in front of their stores awash with fresh cut flowers, salable decor, the very best kind and here a portent of the goodies to be found inside. Fruit and produce arranged in high and precise heaps, fresh fish imbedded up to their clear eyes in shaved ice, row after row of mysterious and wonderful foods from across the Pacific. The flowers, the fruit and produce and the fish seem to be the inviolate template on which Korean markets are built. At H Mart there is all of that and much more. A woman standing over a huge galvanized tub rythmatically stuffing house made chili sauce between the cabbage leaves for the store's stuffed kimchi, rows upon refrigerated rows of packaged beef, pork and poultry that seems almost too fresh, rows upon rows of packaged ready to eat tofu, pork, kimchi, fake crab, long beans, frogs legs, chicken feet, shrimp shu mai and countless other grab and go items. The bok choy, pea shoots, choi sum, eggplant, water spinach, daikon as well as western green grocer favorites iced and bright occupy almost a half acre of real estate. The fish department, continually being replenished with ice by a young man with a shovel, this night the displayed fish guarded by the groteque and massive head of a giant monkfish, and if there is an uglier denizon of the oceans, I don't think we have found it yet. What is most compelling is that the monkfish head was not for show. As the middle aged Japanese fish department manager explained, this is fine fare. Put it in a very large pot with vegetables and cook it a long time, set it in the middle of the table and pick him to death, so to speak. And beltfish. Isn't belt fish a trash fish? Perhaps he said but not when I fry it. Porgy, Spanish mackeral, croakers,squid, cuddle fish, eel, striper, sea urchin ad infinitum. Hungry? text: With a last name like mine, you'd probably never guess I'm Polish. But I am, on my mother's side. Thanks to my babcia and mamusia, I grew up on a steady diet of kielbasa, pierogies, golompki, borscht and bigos. So when my colleague told me about the New Wave Cafe, a Polish mom-and-pop joint in Port Richmond, I could hardly contain my excitement. "It was recommended by a friend of mine who knows his kielbasa," she said. After googling the place and reading a Philly Weekly review that deemed the food "like babcia used to make," I jumped at the chance to make the New Wave my first food group pick. As I drove into Port Richmond, I noted the Polish delis, bakeries and other family-owned businesses along the main drag, and I marveled at the Catholic church, which dwarfed them all. "This is gonna be great," I thought. "Some authentic Polish food in an authentic Polish restaurant in an authentic Polish neighborhood in Philadelphia." An unassuming little place on the corner of Alleghany, the New Wave resembles a bar more than a restaurant. Aside from the kitschy decor (which included neon wall paintings of various planets and a statue of an alien that appeared to be giving us the finger), I felt like I was in Poland as soon as I walked in. Four men sat at the bar chatting to the bartender in Polish, and a Polish newscast blared from the television in the corner. I was a bit concerned when I saw that there were only 3 or 4 tables that appeared to be for dining (drinking was obviously the primary purpose here), but my anxiety subsided as soon as I saw the authentic menu. We ordered some potato pancakes as an appetizer to share. I ordered the pierogies and borscht for my main course and some Polish beer (Okocim) to wash it all down. The Okocim was fabulous, no complaints there. But my disappointment set in as soon as I tasted the food. The potato pancakes had the right thickness and crispiness, but they needed more salt. I tried my friend's cucumber salad, which also needed more salt as well as some lemon and dill. My borscht was okay--for some reason it was lukewarm (there's nothing worse than lukewarm soup) and they forgot the sour cream. The pierogies were the most dissatisfying part of the meal. Granted, I shouldn't have ordered them fried (steamed is the traditional way), but there's really no excuse for how overdone and dry they were. Maybe that Philly Weekly review was outdated, or maybe it was just a bad night, I don't know. All I know is that our food wasn't fabulous. I appreciated the cultural experience and the opportunity to drink Polish beer, and I'd go back to Port Richmond for sure, but I'll be trying some other Polish mom-and-pop shops before I head back to the New Wave Cafe.

text: I could go on for days about how much I like McGillin's. I have been coming here since coming of (legal drinking) age, going on seven years, and it still love each visit as much as the last. I'll go through some of the things McGillin's has going for it. First, great pub fare. My personal staple is the R.B. McGillin - roast beef, au jus, kaiser roll, horseradish - must I say more? Plus, it's not a massive meal, so I save plenty of room for the great local microbrews they have on tap. This brings me to the second (should be first) reason why McGillin's is so great, they always have a large selection of microbrews on tap, and at great prices. You'll find at least one variety of all the locals, Yards, PBC, Dogfish, Troegs, Flying Fish, etc. No question you'll find something to your liking. Finally, you can't talk about McGillin's without talking atmosphere. This is a pub's pub. The history of the place is a draw in its own right, it's practically a museum. From the photos on the walls, to the exposed beams, fireplace, and dark stained wood, McGillian's is a place that will make you want to stay for a while, or maybe all day / night. Also in its repertoire, McGillin's has a popular karaoke night on (last I checked) Wednesday and Friday and other specials throughout the week. They also throw some popular holiday events. St. Patty's Day, of course, New Year's Day, and my favorite, Oktoberfest which coincides with the Mid-town Village Festival. I could go on and on. McGillin's is a great place for nearly any occasion. It's a great place to watch the Phillies, soccer (if you're into that), and other sports. It can get very crowded in the evenings on the weekend, and nearly any other time for that matter. You never know when a crowd could amass at this popular, historic bar. My favorite time to go is on a weekend afternoon, preferably Saturday for lunch and a few (or many) beers. It's a great way to start your day, and see where the wind takes you from there. I once found an extra life out the side-door alley. McGillin's has a special place in my heart, and if you are talking best pubs in Philly, McGillin's, in my opinion, sits atop that list.

text: Wow. Guys, I'm really excited about Niche. I'm from St. Louis, but I spent the last couple years in California--both northern and southern--and lucky enough to eat at some of the very best restaurants the state has to offer. I've been on vacation for the last few weeks, and I've been really missing Californian food. Until Niche. I took the tasting menu, since I like to put myself in the chef's hands when possible, but I'll comment on some other courses my dining companions had: 1. Tomato consommé. A small slice of beautiful heirloom tomato was served in a large bowl topped by a scoop of burrata sorbet and surrounded by a ring of basil oil. The waiter then poured crystal-clear tomato consommé into the bowl. A tomato in every spoonful! A magnificent soup. The sorbet was really lovely and interesting, with a hint of vanilla. What a great take on boring old caprese! Several tricky techniques used in this dish--very impressive. 2. Scallop. A well-seared dry scallop stood on a bed of lobster mushroom and sea beans, with corn puree elegantly plated on the side. The mushrooms and beans tasted like they might have been cooked in bacon fat and went marvelously with the scallop, which had a great crisp, clean flavor. Fresher seafood than I'm used to in St. Louis! Extra dish: Slow roasted pig's head. Wow wow wow. The layers went as follows: pig's head, foie gras, peach, pig's head, foie gras, peach, and so on. The pig's head meat had been packed into a torchon, sliced into wafers, and seared at high heat to give a nice crispy edge. This was rich, decadent, sweet, and *awesome*. 3. "Reuben" Hah! A take on the old-fashioned Reuben sandwich. This was a few rye gnocchi, cabbage tossed with pickled mustard seeds, and horseradish, all as separate components. The gnocchi had a really strong bitter rye flavor, and mustard seeds popped with flavor. Palette cleanser: grapefruit and basil sorbet. Crisp, clean, and tasting powerfully of its components. Nice. 4. Lamb. Served with rhubarb, hummus, and white chocolate. The flavors worked wonderfully together, and the lamb was done to perfection, but I was actually a little disappointed with the quality of the meat itself. It was rather chewy and tough, even though it was clearly served (correctly) rare. Maybe they just got a bad shipment. Nevertheless, the combination was creative. Extra dish: Pork belly and barbecue consommé Oh man. This wasn't part of the tasting menu, but I heard "barbecue consommé" and had to order it as a supplement. A cubic inch of wonderfully tender, crispy pork belly was served in a bowl of transparent orange barbecue consommé, topped with pickled peach and mustard greens. The soup tasted just like barbecue! The peach was nicely spiced to match the rest of the dish. This was really impressive and extremely creative. Win. 5. Coconut Kulfi This is an Indian dessert--I'd never had it before! As our waiter put it, "it's kind of like a mix between ice cream and fudge." Rich, but not overly sweet, and with a very hard consistency. This was served with passion fruit glazed pineapple and house-made granola. The crunch of the granola went wonderfully with the soft pineapple and hard kulfi, and the fruit brought sweetness to the kulfi. A very unique dessert. It was only $65 for those five courses! What a deal--this was better than many $100 meals I've had in San Francisco. We had a witty, attentive waiter and Chef Craft came out to chat with us, which was great. I've spent a lot of time in St. Louis trying to find a restaurant that stands up to Californian cuisine, and Niche is not only the first to succeed--it surpasses many of my favorite restaurants on the west coast. I have no hesitation in crowning it the best meal I've had in St. Louis. Congratulations, Chef Grant; you have a winner!

text: This was a very disappointing meal for a special occasion. I had family visiting me for my birthday and chose not to make a reservation at any restaurant to keep things flexible. We all felt disappointed in the food and that we had paid $25 for parking on South Street to avoid missing our reservation. We were not at all eager to try dessert even though it was my birthday. text: Not half bad! I have yet to find a better place in the Tampa area, but then again I haven't looked all that hard! So, I had the pulled pork and the ribs combo with baked beans and fries. Let's start with the sides: The fries were great and seemed to be fresh-cut (which are the best). The baked beans, though, seemed to have too much molasses in them (or I think it was molasses). Perfectly sweet and smoky, but a little too... molasses-ey. :-) The pulled pork was exactly how I wanted it to be! Moist and flavorful, lots of smokyness. The ribs were tender as ever, but seemed a little underwhelming to me... I like my ribs to have a good amount of rub and sauce on them and these just weren't that kind of rib. Still, though, the flavors were pretty good. One thing that this place is missing are desserts! It seems like they should really be serving some banana pudding or coconut cake with all this BBQ (or at least, those are the things I crave with it). All in all, though, definitely a place I'll be going back to often!

text: I stayed at the Silver Legacy 18-21SEP09 for the Reno Air Races. The hotel feels like a tired, but expensive, Motel-6. Rooms are small and poorly appointed (no coffee maker), beds are uncomforable, carpets and shower curtains old, A/C kind of functional, thin walls, etc., etc. There are MUCH better alternatives-- especially for $100+ per night. I did have a nice view... Reno looks great from 28 floors up. The casino is very smokey, but they do have single deck black jack and friendly dealers. The gym is just ok... reasonable, but not outstanding. Feels like a decent YMCA. I also went to see Bill Maher while I was there. Excellent performance, but the room is very large and one may as well watch him (or similar performers) on TV. Comedy is not the same if it's not close-up. The best feature is Sips... their in-house coffee bar. Excellent coffee and superb service.

text: I'm kind of disappointed in this place. I went here for a late lunch today and was not impressed at all. It was a bit warm out so I decided to dine indoors. I was one of only two tables seated inside. Yes it was bright inside with all the windows, but it was also kind of shadowy since they didn't have any interior lights turned on. It felt like they didn't want to be serving anyone in there at the time. They filled my water glass after a couple minutes, but didn't ask if I wanted anything else to drink. I had to flag the server down to ask for an iced tea. On to the menu. I had high hopes for one of the kebabs. I was torn between the Chicken Adana Kebab and the Iskander Kebab. Asking the waiter for an opinion on the two he highly recommended the Iskander, so I went with that. The menu describes it as "Slices of Turkish Gyro placed over cubes of pita bread and immersed in rich tomato sauce and topped with hot butter. Served with homemade yoghurt on the side". It was tasty, but swimming in oil and not much of the rich tomato sauce. The menu also stated that "All Kebabs served with Basmati Rice and Vegetables". They never showed up. Normally I would speak up about that, but I wasn't really craving them and thought perhaps they weren't included with lunch and it would be at a cheaper price. Upon getting my bill (which I also had to flag the server down to get), it wasn't discounted for no rice or veggies. Had it not been for the fact that I wasn't that hungry and that I'll be getting reimbursed for this meal from my work, I would have pitched a fit about not getting all the food that the menu stated I would get. Sitting in the shadows, no refill on my tea that I had to beg to get, not getting the rice and veggies promised with the dish, alright tasting, but nothing noteworthy food all for $22 equals the worst meal I've had while spending time here in Indy. Disappointing indeed.
label: NEG

text: I read so many wonderful reviews on this bridal salon, so this was the very first place I went to try on gowns. When I arrived the owner had me fill out a card and asked me a few questions around the types of gowns I was looking for. I am a curvy size 10 and I want a mermaid or fit-n-flare dress to show off my "assets!" As I started to show the owner/consultant pictures of gowns that I liked she told me that I would not be able to try ones like them in the shop on because my hips were too big and I couldn't fit any of her dresses. I felt so embarrassed, disrespected, and humiliated all at the same time. Side Note: I am not "fat" I just have hips, a round butt, and breast. No I am not a size 2 or 4 but the dresses that they had on the showroom floor were a size 10. I have been in other bridal salons where if the lady trying on the dress could not fit into the sample they would clip the back of it to her bra and other undergarments and I was not offered that service at all. Before even trying to see if I could fit into the style of dress that I was looking for she just shunned me away. It wasn't until I started tearing up that she realized that she offended me and could have taken a different approach to letting me know that the sample sizes they had in stock MAY not fit me. The least she could have done was appease me by letting me try one that I liked on even if it couldn't be zipped up. I just walked out and decided to try another place. If the owner had any type of customer service knowledge she would have called me on the phone number that I left on the card and apologize, and not try to scream "I'm sorry" as I walked out the door in tears! That same day I went to Elite Bridal off of Hwy 94 and found a dress that was a size 10, and the same style and designer as the dress that the owner of Wedding Gallery told me I couldn't try on. It's her businesses loss of $2500, not mine! So if you are a size 10 and don't want to be embarrassed in front of other customers, DO NOT STEP FOOT INTO THIS PLACE! I recommend that you go to Elite Bridal right down the street.
label: NEG

text: Hrmm. I must say my BBQ experiences in the south comes short yet again (first in Texas then here). Not sure whether I lack the palette to appreciate BBQ...but I highly doubt that. The location was full of tourists. But it was the closest to the hotel I was staying at and I didn't have a car. I had 3 meat combo: Brisket, Ribs, and Shoulder. I chose the Nashville BBQ sauce (figured that when you're in Nashville, gotta try things that have Nashville in the name). Good: -The all three kinds of meat were smoky. You could tell that these bad boys were sitting in those smoker for a long time. -Cole-slaws were good. Really top-notch. Wasn't creamy at all and really refreshing. Unfortunately that's where good ended... Not-so-good: -All three kinds of meat were really dry. I've had much better, juicy briskets elsewhere. The outside of the ribs were so dry and tough that for a second I thought that they might left the skin on. The pulled shoulder reminded me of Pork Sung (dried, shredded--taiwainese--pork in a jar) but less tasty. -They were smoky but they weren't flavorful. Is it snobbiness that prevents them from basting/mopping the meat with sauce or is it the will to please all types of taste that leaves the meat with no flavor? I don't understand it. Those who say that you don't need BBQ sauce are liars; or they must eat fries with no ketchup or salt. -The nashville sauce...I found it to be too vinegary. I had to go to Texas, which had good heat, but a (tiny) bit too sweet. -Beans. They were just mediocre. I don't know. Maybe I was expecting way too much. I was looking for, oh-my-goodness, yee-haw moment in the south for BBQ. And this place didn't come remotely close.
label: NEG

text: I would definitely have to agree with Byron J. on this one (we seem to frequent many of the same locations)... We've tried it on SEVERAL occasions. First of all, I know they make everything to order, but they are SLOW. This is kind of annoying when I just want to grab and go...SECOND, it is underwhelmingly decent but not a fantastic burger. When a place SPECIALIZES in one thing, I think it should be done PERFECT, every time, no exception. The one thing I do like about the burgers is the bacon. They do the bacon AWESOME. Everything else is just average, which is fairly disappointing considering it's ALL they do. I also think it's ironic that they BOAST about how fabulous they are on every wall. Too bad none of those are local. Maybe I'll check out a Five Guys in another city, but I would recommend Hardees over this joint and they are a LOT faster!
