text: Boucherie is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. Located in the little house on Jeannette, which was most recently home to Iris, it is small and intimate, yet not too formal. Due to its size, you will want to make reservations. Boucherie's menu features large and small plates. The menu changes monthly, but a few items remain constant. My favorite small plate is the blacked shrimp and grit cake with house made bacon vinaigrette. I also enjoy the grilled heart of romaine Caesar salad. Of the large plates, the scallops are always a star. The preparation changes monthly but this dish is a winner. Another great choice is the beef brisket with garlicky parmesan fries (a very generous portion and a bargain at $15). I crave this dish. My recommendation is to visit with a small group or at least one dining companion that is open to sharing, so that you can try many dishes. If you don't like sharing, you will be perfectly satisfied ordering one small and one large plate. Boucherie has a nice selection of beer and wine. Boucherie also serves creative, refreshing cocktails, which also seem to change seasonally. In the winter, they serve a fantastic version of hot buttered rum. Leave room for dessert! All of the choices are stellar: bacon brownie, Thai chili chess pie, or Krispy Kreme bread pudding. There is some debate about which dessert is best. My vote goes to the bacon brownie or bread pudding but you can decide for yourself. Boucherie is currently on vacation until September 7 but rest assured I will be back soon. (Note: Boucherie was closed for the month of August, when this review was written. It is open now.)

text: This has got to be one of my favorite treats from childhood! Having grown up in New Jersey, these were a summer staple among my friends and me. Basically, in terms of consistency, water ice is a cross between a slushy and a sorbet. It's not as sweet as sorbet either. It's different from say a hawaiian ice in that its not shaved ice with syrup on top - its made together then frozen and has a much smoother consistency. You have to try it! Their custard is also fantastic --- it's ultra creamy and rich, and in a gelati, it perfectly balances out the water ice. A gelati is a cup with custard on the bottom, water ice in the middle and more custard on top. My favorite is the vanilla custard with the root beer water ice. It's like a root beer float but better! I've also had the chocolate custard with banana water ice and that is great too. I really look forward to visiting the east coast in the summer and getting one of their gelatis. It's a very nice, cool treat! As far as this location, it is near a busy intersection but next to a secluded parking lot with some grass to sit on. They used to have a picnic table or two - not sure if that is still the case.

text: You hear everyone talk about how good New Orleans food is but you don't have a clue as to where to start looking for it once you get there? Ralph and Kacoos is your place to start. Why? Because you will use your experience here as the benchmark by which you judge every other culinary experience in the French Quarter and beyond. They have all of the classic dishes you've always wanted to try. I've had crawfish etoufee at half a dozen places in New Orleans and the best version of this classic dish is served here, with freshly made hush puppies of course served with some outrageously delicious dill sauce. Here is where you try alligator bites for the first time if you must, you'll find none fresher or better prepared. The Louisiana crabcakes are an experience in themselves especially if you're accustomed to the overly breaded and combined variety...you'll find these are made with lump crab that makes you appreciate each and every bite. As I may have mentioned in another review, it is my life's mission to find and spout about the world's best bread pudding. Famous Dave's in Chicago is my blue ribbon winner....but in New Orleans Ralph and Kacoos takes first prize, its amazing, served warm (as only it should be served) with a fantastic bourbon sauce. Now for the final reason I love Ralph and Kacoos aside from its off the beaten path location its cozy, yet contemporary library feel.....the crawfish etoufee. Long a favorite of mine, its just hard to find it made correctly with a thick roux, lots of crawfish and real rice (not that Uncle Ben's stuff)....here you'll find everything as it should be with a bonus of shrimp and crabmeat in your etoufee' as well. Pass those hush puppies because they were made to partner with the etoufee. You just can't order a steak or seafood that you won't enjoy here. Everything is made fresh, they make all of their own sauces with fresh herbs and seasonings. Yelp back after your visit so that I can reminesce!
label: POS

text: I loved it! .... It was a truly beautiful day .... rare in Arizona .... lol ...... we had just driven from the snow and were dressed rather warmly .... so nice to be back in Arizona ..... the 'take your time peaceful guided tour and then self guided tour' was about the only speed we could handle after many hours on the road. Our guide was very knowledgeable and very passionate about film, music and the history of the studio .... he was a pleasure to listen to and be guided by. Being a photography lover I was in seventh heaven .... so many great shots to be taken! We will definitely be back and will take advantage of the trail rides which take you through the 40 acre property .... as you would expect being a major filming destination there are some gorgeous backdrops to be seen. Even the street leading to Old Tucson Studios is quite breathtaking. The studios are still in operation and are even available for theme parties, group events, reunions and wedding receptions.

text: It had been a long weekend after going to Indianapolis for the F1 race. After a long weekend of racing, drinking and some minor sightseeing nothing could top off the weekend than having lunch at Shula's. I had heard many great things about Shula's over the years, and there was no better time to try it than now. Shula's raises their own cattle for their relatively small chain. The cattle are raised on the Graham Angus Farm, which is recognized as one of the top Angus farms in the country. In this way, they are able to have total control of their produce from birth to the slaughterhouse. Since the cattle are raised only for their restaurants, the beef is even more rare to find than prime beef. The 24 oz. Shula Cut Porterhouse is a sight to behold. With a great char on the outside, and a perfect medium rare center, the steak is pure bliss. The steak is dry aged, so very little juice runs out of the steak. The dry aging process also helps to develop the flavor of the beef while also breaking down connective tissue thereby making the steak more tender. The steak was so delicate that you could almost cut it with your fork. The beef flavor was intensified due to the dry aging process. As with most high end steak houses, everything is a la carte. Expensive, sort of. Compared to Morton's or Ruth's Chris, the steak at Shula's is much better and about the same price point. I would definitely go back to Shula's if I am in a city that has a Shula's.

text: L'Oca's open kitchen comes through time and again with consistently well-balanced and executed dishes. But more than just finding its established niche in fine cuisine-starved Fairmount, it fills a surprising void as a Northern Italian neighborhood bistro in a city replete with Southern Italian red sauce eateries. They've done a nice job in rehabbing a corner beer distributor space across from Eastern State Pen. with large windows that open out in summer and recessed and pendant lighting. The chef and his staff are committed to taking great care with their ingredients, from the deftly-handled salads to the richness of their game or pasta (half of which are homemade) preparations. On more than one occasion I've been blown away by the quiet perfection of their soups-- which are always simple, but manage to clarify the savory pleasure of a fresh young leek or humble beans in a minestrone. The owner Jack is always there, vigilantly supervising the service, which is pleasant in its tidy coordination of various servers looking after your needs. Most Philly BYOs fall off in quality after their initial year in business, but it's nice to see that in its commitment to standards, L'Oca manages to bilk the trend. What I've loved: valeriana and crescione/rughetta salads, gnocchetti armenville with sage butter, seasonal soups, saffron spaghetti with scallops and prosciutto, fresh pappardelle with goose ragu (only seasonal), and rabbit loin braised in milk. They now accept reservations.

Shredded chicken, yellow rice, peppers and onions, and topped with sweet plantains. Absolutely hit the spot! You can also get plantain chips, which are crunchy and wonderful. They also have a variety of sweet "shakes", and authentic Cuban soft drinks. Prices are moderate--my meal today ran me about $10, and that included a drink. You'll pay around $7 for sandwiches, $12 and up for entrees. The place isn't big and can get crowded right around lunchtime, but you can definitely get it to go! text: Like Eating Sushi in Tijuana (Disclaimer - We did not try the Shabu-Shabu, only sushi...) Weird title, I know, but this was what I was thinking the whole time I was there sitting at the sushi bar. The same kind of careless service, funky smells, and mediocre food you would expect in a Tijuana tourist restaurant catering to gringos, complete with mostly native Spanish-speaking staff. This may offend some people, but when I go to a sushi bar, I expect to see at least one Japanese-looking person behind the sushi bar. Call me overly traditional or a "sushi snob" but I had a really hard time believing that the guys making our sushi had any serious training other than watching someone else make sushi for a while. The usual "artfulness" of sushi making was completely missing. Watching them handle everything with bare hands and not washing between different operations was unsettling as well. The table tents describing the offerings were filthy, the sushi was slapped together hastily, and the service at the bar was gruff and unfriendly. I happen to speak Spanish (and am often confused for a native Mexican because of my accent), and when I tried conversing with one of the guys behind the counter in his native language (he had been carrying on a lengthy conversation in Spanish with his co-workers and the people next to us) he acted like he didn't understand me. I repeated myself three times in Spanish, then finally in English before he acknowledged my question and gave me a terse answer in heavily accented English. So much for my attempt to bridge the cultural divide... I will definitely not return, and I don't recommend that you try this place. Maybe their Montecito location is better, but other than one of the hostesses who smiled and was attentive, this place was a zero-star joint in my book.

It got worse after the flood in 2005, when most members were scattered, NOAC began charging everyones account when they (NOAC) were ready to open; regardless of whether members were back in New Orleans or not. They had collection agencies after people in Houston, they even harassed the widow of a dead member! After many frustrating dealings with management (Stacey must get a secret thrill reciting the contract rules and saying the word "no"), Bill (the owner) saw the error of his ways and did attempt to mend fences. Of course that will happen when a huge percentage of people who represent $$$ resist. Bill appears to have good intentions. Unfortunately they come at the expense of the members. The final straw for me: women's locker room renovations. I think renovations are fine, but you need to accommodate the women who use the facilities (and, ahem, PAY for them). Part of the locker room was sectioned off by a tarp. They installed temporary showers (after an outcry) and we women were told to "cover up" when walking through the workmen's pathway to use the sauna/steam area and on the way to the showers. Of course management said that they would do "something" for the "ladies". I guess you could say silence is something. This had become an unacceptable situation after a month of walking past workmen in a towel, over a muddy carpet. Not to mention the surprise (!) water shutdowns. This beautiful old club has become below par, and an embarrassment of its former self. There is a beauty in the old world patina of the building, however the rudeness and laziness of the staff, and the "we know better than you" attitude has gotten old too.There are a lot of other gyms in town, all LESS expensive, with newer equipment and better customer service.

text: I have canceled my subscription to the Arden even though I think much of its work is outstanding. My reason for canceling is because I find it hypocritical for the Arden to ask patrons, who have already paid for tickets, for money before and after each performance. As a patron of the arts I understand that many, if not all, theater organizations are in constant need for funding. The hypocritical part comes with the Arden's decision to consistently higher actress Sally Mercer, who although is quite competent and good in the roles that she plays, does voice over work for Swift-boat styled ads paid for by companies determined to mislead the public about Democratic candidates and policies. How one makes a living is not my business and I do not judge a person's political preferences, but anyone associated with the arts is well aware that Republican politicians and policies are often against funding for the arts in communities, in schools and in general. So why do I have to pay for a ticket to watch a play featuring an actress that uses her voice to denounce democratic candidates (who support arts funding in education, in communities and in general) and then be asked before and after each show to contribute more money before leaving the theater? Answer is I don't and that is why I have canceled and will not renew my subscription. Ms. Mercer's ads tend to be played in other markets I believe in an attempt to remain unnoticed here; however, one was recently played by ABC World News in a story about ads used to mislead the public about the health care bill, another was designed to paint a very ugly picture of candidate Deval Patrick, during his campaign for Governor of Massachusetts, and then there is the infamous "wolf" ad that ran nationally during the 2004 Bush vs. Kerry campaign that many journalists used in stories as an example of the fear mongering tactics used by Republicans in that campaign. My issue or review is not in conflict with Ms. Mercer's decision to earn money making those ads (even though I find them repugnant), but with the Arden's arrogance to work with an actress who uses her skills to denounce the very candidates and their policies that support the arts and then ask its audiences to provide more than the cost of their tickets to help keep the Arden running. It just feels wrong to me and I wanted to share my views. Thank you.

text: When studying for exams, I find that I always get painful knots in my shoulders. One day, it was painful enough that I couldn't continue studying (maybe it's postural, maybe it's because I have a short torso. whatever) so I called MassageLuxe (referred by a friend) and set up an appointment for the next day. I spoke with Jeremy and he was the nicest person ever - I also had the opportunity to meet him the next day and he was incredibly helpful and kind. Upon entering MassageLuxe, you are greeted by the front desk, which sits next to a falling water facade. After checking in, they whisk you away into the relaxation lounge where you are offered hot tea (in a variety of flavors) or water and essentially relax until your appointment. It can become a little awkward if there are other people there waiting too. Come appointment time, your therapist will whisk you away into a room and review your charts (like in a doctor's office) where they meticulously log what went down each session. If it's your first time, you'll fill out a form and can indicate trouble areas. The first therapist I had noted my incredible knots and suggested that I come back every 2 weeks to get them worked out (of course they would say that). I went back again in about 2 weeks and had a therapist named Tim. He also noted all the knots I had and after much reassurance, proceeded to really work those knots out (it was a deep tissue massage afterall!). I've been back every few weeks to have Tim keep the kinks out of my shoulder and back. He's great at what he does and is pretty comical. He'll listen to your stupid stories and laugh at the right time. Not to mention, he works the knots out!!! My shoulders no longer hurt anymore and I can study forever and ever. Plus I have a membership here now so I kind of have to go back every month. One HUGE Pro: - Late hours!!! They are open until 10 PM (last client at 9 PM) which is very convenient if you work during the day!

The risotto was pretty nice too, you can still taste the freshness of the vegetables and it was nice and cheesy/creamy with a hint of what I think was white wine. text: For a person with food allergies, it can be daunting when trying new places. The hubby is always willing to try new things with me, but his allergies can raise ugly eyebrows when we try places with Names to them. NOLA is not one of those places! Our first full night in New Orleans, I wanted to check off an Emeril restaurant and the Passport Around the World Pris Fix Menu drew me in. NOLA was spotlighting Vietnam, that was like a foghorn calling me home. We came in without reservations, and was seated immediately, upon being seated our waitstaff team introduced themselves and the lead waiter asked if we had any allergies or concerns he should be aware of. Hubby was charmed instantly! Coming from SF where dining is an art, no one has ever asked about allergies. I had the Passport Pris Fix which started with a Shrimp Springroll and grilled bok choy. The springroll could have easily been something family made with it's sweet tender pork, shrimp and veggie filling. Fried to golden perfection and served with a delicate garlic vinaigrette over the grilled bok choy. Hubby decided the Hickory-Roasted Duck with Whiskey-Caramel Glaze, Buttermilk Cornbread Pudding, Haricot Verts-Fire Roasted Corn Salad, Natural Jus sans Candied Pecans. The waiter didn't even bat an eye when we asked to not have nuts. He ensured the flavor will still be amazing with a missing ingredient. When the duck came out - seriously, it could have been a whole duck! Hubby says it was 2 legs and 2 thighs, but still the portion was out of control. The smoky flavor made the duck skin crispy and delightful, the duck meat was tender and soft to the bite - not overdone for the serving size. Hubby loved everything down to the fixing underneath the duck. I had the Lemongrass Grilled Chicken Breast over Jasmine rice with sugar snap peas and ginger black bean sauce. I'm not a big bean fan, but each component truly complimented each other to create a very New Orleans yet Vietnamese inspired meal. The chicken breast was moist and juicy, I loved the grilled flavor with the lemongrass and somehow found myself dipping the chicken in with the black bean ginger sauce. We finished with the coconut flan - amazing! Light, fluffy and soooo rich. Not a big flan fan, but I'm going to try making a coconut panna cotta inspired by this dish. The waiters were comical and very entertaining, you can see the cohesive team who is very proud of where they work. Knowledgeable in their menu and we were very pleased with everything. For two people - mind you, very decent portions - two entrees, one starter, two desserts and coffee, the meal was about $75 dollars. It's hubby's first time in the Crescent City and he loved that NOLA was a touch of the familiar but daring enough to be something he's never tried.

The pizzas are good - on a weeknight, it's very common for us to go grab an antipasto, a pizza, bottle of wine and call it a meal. The service is fantastic - I literally had one bad server like five years ago, and the manager remedied it IMMEDIATELY. text: I wish I had a better experience to report about Morris Refuge because I have heard nothing but good things about them. Unfortunately... My review deals primarily with something they are known for, and that is their spay and neuter voucher program. They advertise that for $40 (cats) or $60 (dogs) you can get a voucher good at a number of local veterinarians who will spay or neuter your cat, and the refuge will pay the difference. Now they do advertise that additional services not part of the routine surgery may be an extra charge. Examples they cite include vaccinations, blood tests, even the fixing of internal abnormalities. But here's the problem. All of the places I called wanted to charge a very hefty additional fee for anesthesia, the INJECTION of the anesthesia, and antibiotics. On what planet are these things not part of a routine surgery? Again, even the voucher itself says it covers "routine surgery." I even asked the vet offices I called point blank whether they considered these things PART of a routine surgery. One of them put it best when she said "Well..anesthetizing your pet for the procedure is not optional." So basically you're getting, IMHO, a mild to moderate discount on the entire procedure by buying one of these vouchers. I'm not even entirely sure how this benefits the refuge...I thought that this was probably a service they budgeted for, one of their main services to the community. But really it seems like if you're actually a person who has found himself in a seriously difficult financial situation, you shouldn't be relying on this as the affordable way to get your animal fixed. With a $60 fee plus a $60 fee for pain meds etc..., plus a this and that and so forth fee, you should look to be spending $150 or more total (including the cost of the voucher.)

text: Play is a great bar IF you have your expectations in check. You need to understand that this bar is an 18+ bar and as such - sometimes you'll see immaturity on display inside. Also, unlike most bars where there are chairs right up at the bar where you can sit, relax and have a drink - Play doesn't have a single chair sitting at the bar. There are some tables and places to sit - just not right at the bar. But, all that being said - if you like drag shows, friendly bartenders and great music from a live DJ - you'll love Play. They do charge a cover - anywhere from 5 dollars on up - depending on the night and the event. I have never been there when you didn't have to pay a cover and that gets on my nerves some times - because I'm an adult and I'm paying to drink - I shouldn't have to pay for the privilege to drink in your establishment. However, I digress. So, aside from the cover - the drinks aren't too expensive. However, I am used to paying 6 bucks for a drink at most other bars - so, paying that here doesn't bug me too much. If you want to get drinks quickly during the drag show - you can go to any one of the 3 bars in the dance area and get served quickly. Once the shows are over - go back into the showroom once the dance floor fills up. Play is basically divided in half. The show bar and the dance bar. There is also an outside patio area both upfront and out the back door where you can go to smoke if you so choose. The bathrooms are huge and very clear - however, being a gay bar the sex rules are a bit more relaxed. So, I frequently see women in the mens bathroom and vice-versa. The dance floor is incredible. It really is! I have had friends from New York and LA fly in to see me and most are just floored at how incredible this dance bar is - in the heart of Nashville none-the-less. At 11 and 1 on Friday and Saturday there is a drag show performed by some very talented drag queens. Occasionally Play will have a special guest visiting to perform - and sometimes they have porn stars or other people are visiting for some special event. If you want the most up-to-date information - its best to visit the website (Playdancebar.com) and they have a complete listing of all the events they have coming up. Most people in Nashville visit Tribe (which is next door) early in the evening and visit Play around 10:30 or 11 at night. So, this is a late night club for sure. So, to sum up: Play is a great dance bar - as long as you aren't expecting a quiet night sitting at a bar with soft music. Its a high energy dance club with LOTS of people on the weekend packed shoulder to shoulder. You'll get to see some of the best drag queens in Nashville (or anywhere for that matter). Drinks are reasonable and served up by friendly and handsome bartenders. Go, you'll have fun. Trust me!

After being told that no one in their right mind could start their night with a milkshake and keep on drinking, I immediately ordered the double espresso milkshake which rocked my world (and got me quite buzzed... win) I ordered chicken sliders which were a-mazing. I don't even know why I ordered them. I hate chicken burgers. Always so so dry. Not these. Yum I also ate part of my friends burgers, even though they didn't offer. The lamb burger almost caused me ordering envy. It was delicious, juicy, and huge! Next time...

text: It is a Saks and it is vastly less snooty than most - unfortunately its selection is less than most, as well. Went in and browsed for a bit, was greeted by two different salespersons during my time there and everyone was very friendly. While I did not buy anything, I would have if they'd had something uniquely New Orleans.
label: POS

text: Is it cliche to complain about how some auto mechanic ripped you off? This place pissed me off so bad that I will take it to the grave with me. Even sans the smug owner who talked about me in a hushed voice right in front of me, I feel like the level of ondescension I received from him when trying to ask about the 2200 dollars I paid him was only on par with the catch and release scam that seems all too common from reading other reviews. I took my car here to get it checked out as it was leaking oil. Upon inspection, I was told that I needed a new transmission for 2500 dollars. When I told him that I considered the car a loss and would rather not have work done to it, he informed me that I can pick up my broken car for 500 dollars as this was the cost of the mechanic having examined it. Now, the average cost of mechanic work is 80 dollars an hour. This insinuates that the mechanic had done roughly 6 hours of work on my car. 6 hours to remove a transmikssion from a car? Maybe he and 5 of his peers examined it for 15 minutes and rounded it up. But somehow I doubt it. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this place.
label: NEG

text: We wanted to do an antique ring so this is the place we looked, they have two locations. I liked the Clayton location better than the Olive, seemed to have more (at least for what we were looking for). Very helpful--the woman showed us everything we possible wanted to see. She gave good suggestions and we ended up coming back for one we'd noted. We were able to get the ring sized that day which made it more fun. I did notice with appraisals though they do tend to rate 1 level lower on diamonds than other places. I'd have an outside appraisal done in additional to theirs just for 2nd opinions/to be on the safe side. You do have 7 days to return.

text: OMG, Mexican food that will have you coming back. I had the Chicken Taco Salad... Ahh. So Good. Great presentation. The service is great. Priced affordable and all the beauty of a new restaurant.

text: I was not greeted upon entering the store. I would even go so far as to say that I was glared at like an intruder upon entering. One employee was building a display. The other employee never left her perch behind the register, even when I obviously needed help finding the circular needles I was looking for. (Here's a tip: If you are not going to have all sizes in one display, you might want to let customers know this by either putting up a sign or TALKING TO CUSTOMERS who stand there for a few minutes looking perplexed.) I had to ask for help and was treated like an annoyance. Most of the very beautiful needle holders (by Lantern Moon, I think) did not have prices marked. When I had to interrupt the personal conversation between the employees again to ask for the prices, I really felt like I was annoying them by wanting to spend my money there. Poor customer service aside, they do have a nice selection. I chose not to spend much money there because I thought about all of the yarn shops I have been to around the country and how some of them really struggle. I would rather give my money to a shop that appreciates my business and does not make me feel like a nuisance. I bought some yarn on clearance from Rosie's and decided that I would not be back.

text: I attended a music video shoot here a few years ago, which allowed me to sample the goods, get a sense of the place, and rub shoulders with some icons... Still, I think that this place lacks character on larger levels. For starters, it's in a galleria. That'd pass in KoP, but in Center City Philadelphia, it would make any date seem like "I'm 16 and going to Houlihan's" vibe. I thought that the music/ambiance (once inside) is cool, but less organic than say Ortlieb's or Chris'. Granted, this is a cut above in terms of quality/class, but it just feels plastic to me. I think this is where Philly's own Bridge & Tunnel crowd goes... I much prefer cozier, cheaper, and more appealing spots.

text: I just bought a combo from this place (lunch combo E), and I am appalled by the food here. My food was literally soaked in oil, I can understand a little oil for cooking purposes but not like this. The chicken balls were rock hard, and don't even get me started on the ginger beef.... it was sooo dry and hard, I wondered if this was yesterday's left overs. I am surprised the food was as dry as it was considering how much oil there was at the bottom of the container. Not fresh, poor quality. Never again.

text: enh, it was ok. I'd read about the speakeasy resurgence and was excited to try this entry into the competition. I wanted a place that wasn't tooo heavy on the theme, without the silly passwords and drama. But in retrospect, there wasn't *enough* going on in term of the theme here. It was definitely a Very Slick Bar. But I wanted more than that. Besides the retro cocktails (we didn't get the one with valerian--um, why would you want to fall asleep. I mean, I guess it's sort of a psychotropic, but not my thang...), it wasn't very Prohibition at all. Granted, it was a travel article that billed them as such, so maybe it's the writer of that article I should be disappointed with. Drinks were good but pricey. The ginger beer in the French Buck was not even kidding (spicy!!), and I don't think I'd personally want more than one of them in a sitting--or perhaps a lifetime. Best to know your retro drinks and order what you like rather than use the (limited) cocktail menu. Online they feature recession specials, but there is no menu for that readily available; so study it online before you go. The Husband got a sidecar; he is VERY particular about his sidecars (his Platonian sidecar is from the Starlight Lounge at the Sir Francis Drake in San Francisco), and he loved it. Anyway, maybe on another night or something, but this place was not what I wanted last night. As a side note, a group of trying too hard 20-something women came in at the end, wearing almost identical bubble-hem strapless mini-dresses and pumps (bachelorette party? probly not; just seems to be the sorority girl type that hangs around here), before we headed to dinner around 9. YAWN. I say again: enh. Conclusion: Just not my scene.

text: I came a couple of years ago and had a good meal, but I hadn't made it a point to get back. However lately, I had been hearing a lot of people buzzing about Little Fish again and I thought it would be worth a second trip. And MAN am I glad I went back! A friend and I went out for Sunday 5 Course Tasting meal which was a great choice and came highly recommended. The first and second course (Halibut with Truffled Mushrooms and a Pea Sauce & a Smoked Salmon with Cucumber dish) were good and above average respectively. Given that my friend has a soft spot both roasted beets and goat cheese, the 3rd course salad of said items was also well received at our table as well, although not groundbreaking. But nothing, and I mean NOTHING, compared with the "entree" course of Escolar with Creamed Corn and Zucchini. One word: Sublime. The fish was perfectly prepared and the accompaniments paired amazingly. People often talk about the best dish they have ever consumed...this is near the top of my list. Phenomenal. The dessert was the chocolate torte that others have yelped about as well. Tasty and would have paired beautifully with a glass of red wine, but we hadn't planned that well (note to self for next week!)

text: I moved downtown over a year ago, and I've been waiting anxiously for a full-service grocery store to open here. I'm happy to say that I'm thrilled with what we got. For this review, I won't take into account the demolition controversy and the small coffee shops and eateries that have closed because their business has been going to Culinaria instead. I'm strictly going to focus on what's in the store. I'm very pleased with Culinaria's stock. The produce is fresh, and there are enough varieties of staple garden goods to meet most people's needs. Moving to the frozen foods, Culinaria carries everything you'd expect -- pizzas, tv dinners, veggies, even those weird PB&J sandwiches without the crusts. Personally, I'm happy that they carry Kashi frozen meals at great prices. I do wish they'd carry Gardenburger varieties, though -- Morningstar doesn't do it for me. The refrigerated/dairy shelves meet my needs well enough. They don't carry my brand of yogurt (Dannon naturals), so I'll have to continue buying that at Dierberg's. There's plenty of shredded cheese and an ok selection of butter. Juices could be beefed up a bit more. Milk (white, chocolate, organic) is great, and there are plenty of dips and sour creams. Dry goods like rice, pasta, etc. are well priced and there are plenty of brands. I'm pleased with how many varieties of Nature's Valley granola bars Culinaria carries. Applesauce and apple juice often are on sale. As for the pet section, I wish Culinaria would carry more natural cat litters and foods. I'll still get most of my items at PetSmart. However, it's nice to have a store just a few blocks away where I can pick up litter or food if I haven't been to PS in a while. Moreover, even though it's not my preferred litter, Tidy Cats often is on sale at Culinaria for about $5 for the giant "Indoor Spaces" jug -- I definitely appreciate that. I haven't made much use yet of the health/medical or school supplies sections yet. I also can't speak about meat or seafood, as I don't eat those items. However, I do like the number of cheeses Culinaria has for the store's size. I also like the sandwiches I get from the deli. In the bakery, I ordered a cake for a coworker's birthday, and everyone in the office loved it. Even better, I walked in at 7 a.m. to pick it up on my way to the Metrolink station. For those doubters, yes, a scant few products have been marked up slightly to make up for this small store. However, most items are the same prices as "regular" Schnucks stores. Sales are frequent, and that's why Culinaria is my go-to store for salad items, Kashi frozen meals, frozen vegetables and granola bars. The checkout line is speedy, as it's set up like a banker's line. The cashiers are fast and friendly -- a bit chatty like cashiers at Trader Joe's. They encourage reusable bag use and don't bat an eye when I come in with three reusable bags and my shopping trolley. I love having a full-service grocery store just a few blocks away from my home and preferred Metrolink station!
label: POS

text: I was a regular at Lulu. The dim sum is not the best in St. Louis, but they have plenty of room, variety, fast food service, and fun characters carting dim sum to your table. Aside from not so great shu mai (go to Wonton King or Wei Hong for that), I had an especially bad time on my last visit. The snotty cashier tacked a mandatory gratuity on my bill. Because I usually tip more and I don't take it well when I'm told I have to pay something that is completely voluntary I refused, but the snarky cashier ran my card for the tip anyway without my authorization.. I should have called the cops, but I was in shock. I sent a letter to them via their website to complain about the situation and no one has responded. TIPS ARE DISCRETIONARY. You can add a tip to a check, but you can not force someone to pay it! That is the law. I prefer the food at Wonton King and will BOYCOTT Lulu because of their unfair business practices. I have since found out that this has happened to many people and that the tips don't even go to the staff. UNBELIEVABLE.

text: I have always dreaded going to the hair salon. I hated the phony atmosphere of most places and I really dreaded the small talk I would be forced to have with my stylist. Maybe I am unusually insecure, but I always felt intimidated in most salons. Then, one day a couple of years ago, I wandered into Andre's salon and I never looked back. Andre is warm and personable and made me feel at ease immediately. Right off the bat, we connected on a topic I care about--dogs--and I didn't feel uncomfortable at all. Oh, and the cut and color were fantastic! My highlights last longer than highlights I have received from any other salon. For the past year or so, Christopher has been styling my hair and I LOVE him to death. He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth and talented! My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it and, try as I might, I can never get it to look as good as he can. The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion! I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!). Also, back in the spring, I asked Andre if he would be interested in donating a gift for a charity 5K I was helping to organize. Being the wonderful person he is, Andre didn't hesitate and put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race! Andre has a good heart and that it what I love about going to his salon! I also love that clients can schedule appointments online through schedulicity! Great prices, great cuts, great color, great space, convenient scheduling options and, most importantly, great people--you will not regret choosing Andre for your next cut or color!

text: Hands down, Paul and Angelo in the deli make THE best hoagies I've ever had, and I've had a lot of hoagies. I am kind of a sucker for their old style italian hoagie, my favorite,, which is far from healthy with the loads of good tasty meats in there, but nothing quite compares to it and you've got to treat yourself once in a while. I've tried their roast beef, corned beef, turkey, ham+cheese, and really, they're all good. I like the store itself too, it kind of takes you back to a different time period (like the 50s... not that I was around yet in the 50s, but that's what I imagine it was like). However it's more of a place where I pick up a few things you might have forgotten on my regular food shopping trips, because it's a small market and the selection and prices can't really compete with the bigger supermarkets. But, they do carry Bassett's ice cream (a rare find at regular stores), which is the best ice cream ever (the only exception is homemade ice cream).

text: I stumbled upon this place with some coworkers when we were looking for lunch. text: So I bailed on work the other day, basically for lack of interest. I had slept horribly, had bad dreams, and I felt just yucky and tired. And HUNGRY! By the time I left my office around 11:00am and met up with my husband (I always seem to get "sick" on his days off) we both hadn't eaten yet and were starving. We also were trying to not spend too much dinero, so I suggested King Buffet. We both had lunch and sodas there, and with the nice tip we left, we got out of there spending like $22, which rocks. I mean, it's like $5 more than fast food. And way less nasty! So my favorite thing here is mos def the terriaki chicken sticks. I eat like, ten of them. That, and the sesame balls. Those things are freaking delish!!!! I also like that garlicy green bean dish, but I think they make it better at that other Chinese buffet on Plumb lane. When we go there, I eat like 2 plates full of those green beans. The selection here is kind of random and strange. They have super Asian seafood dishes, octopus and stuff that I won't eat because frankly I get a little scared about what that stuff might do inside my belly. Then they have Americanized Asian dishes like fried rice and egg rolls and sweet and sour chicken that mostly anyone will eat. And then they have french fries and chicken nuggets. Oh and they make these little sugar coated fried doughnut things. They are incredible! Seriously! Flakey and yummy and they melt in your mouth. The husband isn't much for sweets, but I practially mouth raped him with one of those fried doughnuts and next trip around the 'ffet, his plate was half filled with them. Their salad bar is also so random! It's like iceberg lettuce and nasty looking pasta salad, various canned fruit some of which I had no idea what it was but I still ate it, tapioca pudding and jello cubes. I did eat some pudding too, tapioca and banana mixed together. It was yummy. King Buffet is one of those places where you can't expect to want to eat EVERYTHING, and there will probably be some things that you shouldn't eat. But if you pick and choose you can fill up on delicious morsels of randomness. Oh and next time I need to go when I actually have money because I want to buy like 10 items from their display case. I want a lacy fan (for my daughters!) and a bamboo plant and some sparkley plastic jewelry. I love resturants that have gift shops and what not inside them!

text: My first impressions of Pod were mixed. I thought the atmosphere was kinda cool, but also trying too hard. Then I was seated at one of the tables on the main floor where felt like I was in some kind of weird, dimly lit futuristic high school cafeteria. My dining companion noted that she felt oddly exposed. That's pretty much where the mixed feelings ended, though, because from that point on, I have nothing but love. We ordered from the University City Dining Days prix fixe menu. For $30, I was able to choose an appetizer, an entree, and was served a "pastry chef's selection" for dessert. We were also offered $5 sake mojitos, which was a nice touch and a great compliment to all of the food. Since, like the Continental, food is served as it's prepared, my friend and I ordered together and shared everything. Food came out at a perfect, leisurely-but-not-too-slow pace, so we had time to enjoy and digest everything. Our waiter was totally friendly and attentive, which I have found to be unusual when ordering from prix fixe menus. As for the food: From the dim sum menu, we chose the shrimp dumplings and the vegetable maki. Each dumpling was stuffed with a whole piece of juicy shrimp and they were served with a side of lime-chili dipping sauce. Yum! The maki were also delicious, stuffed with avocado, cucumber and asparagus - and since everything is made to order, they had no problem leaving out the carrot to accommodate my food allergy. For the main course we chose the Sezchuan lamb chops and the miso glazed Chilean sea bass. The lamb chops were slightly overcooked (they were small and we ordered them medium-rare) but flavorful, and they were served atop a pile of sesame Shanghai noodles. We both agreed the noodles were kind of boring and unnecessary to the dish. They weren't bad, but we left most of them on the plate. The sea bass was the stand out dish of the night. The fish was cooked perfectly, and was buttery yet light, making us wish we had both ordered it because we could have eaten twice as much. It was served over mashed sweet potatoes, which seemed like it wouldn't go but turned out to be the perfect addition. Dessert ended up being a piece of pumpkin pie napoleon (layered ginger spice cake, cinnamon white chocolate mousse, crispy rice pastry and pumpkin custard) and a trio of sorbets (banana-passionfruit, blueberry and raspberry). The napoleon was delicious, and though the sorbets tasted really good, they were underwhelming next to the cake. The menu offered was a perfect introduction to Pod restaurant. I can't wait to go back, and my friend and I are even considering going again this week while they are still running the prix fixe!

text: If you have lots of money, special dietary needs, or need rare/high quality pre-packaged products, and don't care about the quality of store employees, then Whole Foods is just great. I don't fall into most of those categories. I'll shop at WF, these days, when they're the only option or when I'm looking for something that can't be found at any other local place, but I also expect it to put a dent in my wallet. Let's just do a run-down of my criticism: 1. Many products are expensive. Some because of their rarity, some because that's the standard price for that item in any store, others because they can charge way too much and still have someone pay. Example: Two normal-sized, in-season pears should NEVER cost $5+ (although, since Feders opened down the street, I've never had a reason to get produce from WF). There's just no excuse for most of their produce section's pricing, organic or not. 2. Employee quality is... inconsistent. I'll give them some credit--in the past year or so, it seems like most employees are decent (if not friendly) human beings. Additionally, the folks behind the bakery, meat, and fish counters have been excellent in all my interactions with them. The cashiers and other employees, though, tended to be a combination of the following: surly, rude, useless, helpful, knowledgeable, and/or friendly. That is, some would smile and proceed to tell you "Sorry, but I have no idea what X is," others might lead you to where you can find a particular item (although they wouldn't always be correct or find the actual item), and others would openly criticism or make fun of you for your purchases. Nothing makes me want to shop somewhere more than having a barely-employable ex-punk brat harass me for buying groceries at their store. 3. 365 Brand is... well, also inconsistent. Some items are about what you'd expect (although never better than what they're imitating), but some store brand items are just inedible. They don't give you any grief about returning items you hate, but it's still disappointing and wasteful. 4. What happened, bakery? Bread's easy (and fun) to bake for myself, but it's too hot to be worth it during the summer, so I started getting some WF fresh baked bread this past year. And it was good. Then, one day, tired and hungry after returning from a trip to New York, I grabbed a fresh loaf before going home for making a sandwich. And it wasn't fully baked. Chalking that up as a fluke, I tried their bakery bread again, a while later, and experienced the same problem. I've tried contacting management regarding the issue but never gotten a response and not found it pursue the issue, if the people running the store didn't care. 5. This is probably petty, but the whole naive "we're helping!" feel/message of the store is kind of annoying. It's really cool that they have battery and polypropylene (#5) recycling, but giving cashiers a fundraising quota for horribly misguided projects is bothersome and weirdly depressing. Edit: Since writing this review, they eliminated battery recycling, but they did further expand plastics recycling, so now you can take any recyclable plastic there. Which is pretty awesome. Employee quality also seems to have improved in the past year or so. I still can't comfortably give it a third star--there certainly are much better stores--but I have at least come to be okay with the occasional trip to this store.

text: Walking in to An American Place last Friday was like driving to work on Christmas morning. Where the heck is everyone??? It was 7 PM- prime dining time in St. Louis- and there was only one other two-top. When my husband asked the maitre d if he was expecting more diners, he just smiled awkwardly and said, "This is it." Weird. We chose a comfy upholstered banquette at the rear of the dining room to enjoy our meal- we had the pick of the litter. The restaurant is beautifully and luxuriously decorated- the type that makes you feel like you've entered the set of a 1950's Carey Grant movie. The only thing missing was some Sinatra music playing on the piano (which I'm pretty sure they had when I visited a few years back). Instead, there was some lounge music blaring from the restaurant speakers that was set on replay. Needless to say, we got to know this CD VERY well. The chef started us off with an amuse bouche of blue cheese panna cotta with crispy bacon and pears- light and delicious! We followed that with two cold glasses of Schlafly's Helles- a Munich-style lager that paired perfectly with a plate of pan-roasted sweetbreads. The sweetbreads were perfectly cooked and served with an Alsatian pasta called noques that was died with squid ink. Then began our tasting menu- cold smoked scallop paired with a fume blanc from Napa, braised pork belly with sauerkraut paired with an Alsatian style Riesling, sous-vide veal loin paired with a pinot noir from Sonoma, blue cheese cigar paired with a 20 yr-old tawny port, and chocolate mousse paired with orange muscat. Everything was perfectly executed and, for some courses, the wine pairings beautifully accentuated the food. With the exception of the maitre d pulling double duty as a sommelier (not very believable, I might add), the service was outstanding. Our waiter was attentive, but not overbearing, and very knowledgeable about the preparation of each course. But, how could we expect anything less when there's only 4 people to wait on in the entire restaurant? Bottom line- where are you St. Louis? You're missing out on some fantastic food at An American Place, which might not be around much longer with nights like last Friday. Let's give them a reason to bring back that live pianist so that their ambiance can be as delightful as their food.

I've had the yellowtail, and the sangrita sorbet was a light, tarty surprise with the fish. The forest mushroom huraches were very, very rich --- a mushroom lover's paradise. The tacos have a complex set of flavors, and the corn tortillas themselves have a fresh, corn-y taste. The whole grilled fish is also delicious, with grilled smoky flavor that doesn't overwhelm the fresh taste of the meat. I feel like you can't really go wrong with anything on the menu. Best of all, you don't feel weighed down. Just full. Out of the three Jose Garces restaurants I've been to (Amada, Chifa, and Distrito), I have to say this one is my favorite. The balance of flavors and textures is perfect --- the spices and sauces complements the meats and vegetables instead of overwhelming them. It's not "authentic" Mexican food in the traditional sense, but hey, that just means Garces has reinvented Mexican food so that it is light, complex, and refreshingly delicious.

I ordered the croque madame with frites and my husband had the pressed sandwich of cochon au lait with frites and an excellent hefeweizen. It's pretty hard to screw up what is essentially a ham and cheese sandwich with an egg on top--but this was absolutely incredible. The egg was perfectly cooked and I broke the yolk so the whole sandwich had the wonderful flavor of it. The ham was perfectly sweet and salty, and I'm not sure what they do with the bread to this sandwich but it was melt in your mouth delicious. The frites were perfectly cooked, and the service was impeccable. I will dream about this sandwich from afar, and if I'm ever in New Orleans again this will be the first place I visit.

text: UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP!!!!! I'm not a hard person to please. I don't complain a lot. I love food of all kinds, and eat well and often. BUT... I will say this was one of the worst meals I've ever had, and my companions agreed. I know Fiorella's has a lot of positive reviews on here, and they WERE well deserved. When I first ate at Fiorella's a few years ago, I had a pleasant experience. But Fiorella's of today is under new management as of their reopening about a month or so ago, and they are doing the name a disservice. The service was painfully bad. It took us about 7 minutes to even get menus and a drink order in, and 10 minutes to get our beer after we ordered it. When a second beer was ordered, it had to be ordered twice, and it still took about 7-10 minutes to get it after the 2nd request, at which point all she said was, "Sorry, I forgot." I don't know if it was her first time waiting tables, but even if it was, it was inexusable. Every aspect of it was bad, including her repeated efforts to slide dishes across the table, with the same result: shoving the tablecloth around and pushing flatwear onto the ground. I left the 2nd worse tip I've ever left (only 10%), and I don't feel bad about it. And as a veteran of the service industry (6 years of waiting tables, and 2 years of cocktailing), I have a lot of understanding and patience, and enough knowledge to know when it's the kitchen's fault, and when it's simply bad service. This fiasco was both, that's for sure. Then the food.... We started with fried pickles. And they were excellent, and are the reason I even felt comfortable giving them even the one star in this review. Seasoned well, piping hot, a large portion. YUM! We were encouraged. Then the entrees. My out of town guest got red beans and rice. The beans were a little firm, but the taste wasn't terrible. She added A LOT of hot sauce, but I don't know if it was because the dish was underseasoned, or if she's a hot sauce addict. My boyfriend (a chef) got fried porkchops, with sides of veges and mashed potatoes. He said the potatoes were good, but the veges... I took one look at them and said they looked like those frozen bags of mixed veges you get at the supermarket, overcooked (boiled, I think). He confirmed that they were, and barely touched them. His porkchops were horribly underseasoned, and he didn't understand why they didn't use the same batter on those that they had on the pickles. Said the meal would have been a lot better if they had. As it was, he said they were bland, and didn't even bother to fully eat them. I had the eggplant parmigan. And it was almost inedible. It was 2 very thin slices of panfried eggplant served over undercooked fettucini, and SMOTHERED with the worst tomato sauce I've ever had. I spent the first 2 minutes trying to scrape it off to the side. I'm pretty sure they opened a SYSCO can of "unseasoned tomato sauce" and just dumped it on top of the dish. There was a very small smattering of dried oregano and Parmesan over top. I ate the eggplant (which wasn't terrible, once I scraped off the horrific sauce), took a few bites of pasta, and gave up. I have NEVER in my life left a plate full of food. I ALWAYS take my leftovers... I love leftovers like nobody's business. Last night, I left a full plate of food. It was almost inedible. If I hadn't been so hungry, I wouldn't have eaten it at all. I don't think we were the only ones disappointed in our meals. As we sat at the outside table, someone leaving the restaurant stopped by and handed us a business card from the restaurant with "Good for one free entree" written on the back, dated that same day. He said he didn't want it and we could have it. I was excited at the time (it was pre-food arrival), but I won't ever use it, as I will never go back there. I'm going to give it to the next gutter punk that harrasses me for change. Maybe they'll like it. I guess that's my final statement on Fiorella's: I won't even eat their food if it's free. EDITED: Also, the bathroom was so disgusting I almost threw up. They JUST reopened after changing ownership. You'd think someone would have hosed down the bathrooms or something. But it was worse than the ones at dive bars across the street.
label: NEG

Therefore, expect to pay more than you should for the meal you receive... and do not expect any epiphanies of the palate. The drinks are also really nothing to write home about, and they are expensive enough when off special. At least the interior design isn't bad. It's fairly open and bright in the daytime. Also, I can't imagine you'd have much trouble getting a table either -- judging by the sheer lack of diners at happy hour during my visit. I would suggest this restaurant to the type of person that visits a new city for the first time and chooses to go to Applebee's. Mexican Post might be a safe deviation if they were craving "Mexican" food.
label: NEG

These were not just any potato skins...it was like two potatoes cut in half, slightly scooped out, and then toppings put on. Really good and probably horrible for my health. There is a website for The Grill and it urges you to check out the drink specials...but when you click "drink specials" you are taken to a wine list. Oops. We had no idea what was on special because of that and I was excited to hear that all Stoli flavors were on special and priced very well...not to mention preeeeeetty strong. I was feeling really good by the time we left. As per usual, I was disappointed to see a place with a full menu allowing patrons to light up cigarettes, so despite how great everything else was, The Grill loses a star for that. text: OK, I've read some of the reviews and I admit I have not had a salad from here yet, so I'll refrain from one star, but two is all you're going to get out of me. text: Because I tend to be overly optimistic, finding something to rate with only one star has been difficult for me. But really, I think the definition of a grocery store should include free parking, so no points awarded for that. It's hard to understand why I would give this store only one star when it has so much! For example, it DOES have cluttered and confusing aisles that narrow as you go down them. Because the Fresh Grocer is always full, you inevitably end up halfway down an aisle only to find another cart meeting you head on. And like driving in some tiny Philly alleys, you play a little bit of chicken with the other cart until one of you (usually me) ends up backing up the way you've come. The Fresh Grocer also has some of the most unfriendly, unhelpful staff in all of West Philly (which is saying quite a lot, actually). Oh, and it also does have ridiculous prices; never have I paid so much for so very little... If all that it has hasn't convinced you, the one thing that the Fresh Grocer DOES NOT have is fresh produce. I have never in my life seen such a sad collection of fruits and vegetables. text: Sorry Mama Lovers, but we were very disappointed with our lunch here. On our trip to New Orleans for New Years, we craved a burger on New Years Day. After searching our trusted Yelp for reviews and recommendations we decided to hike back into the French Quarter for Yo Mama's burgers. We arrived about 12:30pm, and went to sit upstairs. It was packed, but no one was standing waiting, and two seats open at the bar. We asked if we can just sit and the bartender smiled and said sure, but just be warned it is only me working right now, they'll be a wait. Waiting is understandable at any highly reviewed joint, so we parked ourselves at the bar. Looking around the place, then realized everyone must have just sat down, no one had food in front of them... like 20 some people... but I was tired and slightly hungover, and just wanted a coke and a good burger. After a few minutes we got our cokes and ordered the chili cheeseburger with mac n cheese. We heard a table behind us complain that they wanted a burger done rare, and she said "sorry, my cook is slammed and all burgers are done med-well right now." Which we then realized she didn't ask us, and ours would be well too... hmmmm we don't want med-well, but too late. 2 slow refills and 45 minutes later our burger came out. We were starving and dug in... but all it did was ease the hunger pains. The burger was charred on the outside, and had no distinct flavor whatsoever. The chili was blah (out of can) and just didn't taste that great overall. Mac n cheese was pretty good though, actually better than the burger. Stopped about 3/4 way through burger because I ran out of coke, and realized that I had not put any ketchup or mustard on my burger. Sat for about 5-10 minutes waiting to get her attention for a refill and condiments. Overall, not a good experience. It is sad when you can say you've had better burgers at places that aren't even known for burgers... And living in Chicago, we go out for burgers all the time, at various places, and are rarely disappointed. The only reason I give 2 stars than 1, is because of the bartender/waitress/bus person all in one behind the bar - she warned us with a smile and continued working a crowded hungry complaining room of people with a smile, by herself. I give her the extra star that she can wear like a badge. Note to Yo Mamas: You are located in the French Quarter, it is New Years Day, with the Sugar Bowl happening later that day... did you not realize that you would be busy? Why only one staff? And with such a limited menu, I think charred burgers isn't going to help you keep your reputation of the best burger in New Orleans. I would like to give you the benefit of the doubt, and hope that all your staff called in sick and you just tried to make due... but you did not satisfy our burger needs :(
label: NEG

text: A NEW ORLEANIAN SAYS: Don't waste your money. As a native New Orleanian / foodie (perhaps some redundancy there), I'd been raised believing Antoine's was the "creme de la creme" - a slight notch higher than Galatoire's and Arnaud's, in seniority but also quality. Intimidatingly expensive, but worth it. (Curiously, in retrospect, growing up no one I knew actually ever recommended I go.) So, bringing my gf in town for the holidays, I figured it was time to make the plunge. Wrong. **SLEAZY WAITER TRICKS, AND THE BILL FROM HELL Long-story short: Mediocre food. 2 people. Lunch. No alcohol. $108.00 What REALLY riles me up the most, leading to this one-star review (vs. 2 or maybe 3, because of its history), is the classic "sleazy waiter trick" that snuck under my radar because I was in just too good a mood, being with my gf. WAITER (casual, after taking order, on his way away from table): "Oh, you want some puff potatoes for the table." Waves hand casually over the table, like it's free. ME (guard down): "Yeah, sure, thanks." Upshot: $8.75 for these dry, flavorless potato husks. In college, I waited tables for a time at Arnaud's, one of the other 3 creole flagships, and this is a classic disreputable-waiter trick to pump up the bill when no alcohol is ordered. (I still wish we'd gone to Arnaud's, for the "old creole restaurant experience." Next time.) Tragically, I didn't check the itemization until after I'd left and already tipped a generous 22%. MAKE IT A MUSEUM The best part of the trip wasn't the ambience (Arnaud's has better); it was seeing the place, and saying: "Yes we went. And can tell others to avoid it." Like places on the Sunset Strip (think the Rainbow Room, still in tourist books for its place in hair-metal history), Antoine's lives on because of its place in history. As a museum, it probably wouldn't make as much moolah, but that's kind of what Antoine's is ... and where it belongs.
label: NEG

text: We went to Gemelli for our anniversary. It was really special. We live right around the corner, and apparently so does the chef! I almost didn't want to write a review, thinking, if we all write reviews like this we'll never be able to get a table. But we don't go out enough to keep them in business by ourselves, so we'll just have to plan in advance and make reservations. We went late-ish on a Tuesday and expected it to be empty, but it was full, and we had to wait a few minutes even though we had a reservation. It wasn't a big deal, but they were so nice about it that by the time we sat down we were in a great mood. We ordered the tasting menu, and that was a huge pleasure. They just kept coming by with these fabulous plates of food, and we didn't know what we were going to get. Sort of like combining a personal chef with a guardian angel. Everything was fantastic and there were some real surprises. If you asked me how the service was at about course 2, I would have said just fine. Very nice. The staff was working really hard. But as the other tables finished their dinners and the restaurant emptied out, the staff got more and more relaxed, and the service took on a very warm, personal quality that was unusual. They were clearly having a good time, and it was contagious. The kitchen is open and visible, so even the cooking seemed personal. I am being intentionally vague. I don't want to tell you what we ate, because the chef changes the tasting menu from night to night, and for all we know it could be from moment to moment. I don't even want to tell you specifics about the service, because we left with the feeling that we had gotten extra-special treatment. If we did, then I don't want you to be disappointed if you don't get it, because just the wonderful food and nice service is enough to be happy about. If they really treat everybody this well, then I'll let you be surprised like we were. To sum up: this is a great place for people who love good food, and who prefer neighborhood service and prices to the more snobby alternatives downtown.

text: I've been to the Caspian Grill several times now, and every time I wonder why I don't go more often. I'll say right up front that this is not really a place for vegetarians. There are plenty of vegetarian dishes, but from what my family and friends tell me, the kabob and rice is really the point of the whole experience. The really relevant thing is that the gentleman who runs the Caspian Grill is possibly the kindest person I have met since coming to Philadelphia, and he really cares about the food that he makes. Everything is made fresh, and he invents a lot of the recipes himself. Don't be scared off if you don't know a lot about Iranian food - I don't either. There's plenty of Greek, Indian, Arabic and, if you'll believe it, Mexican food to go around for those looking for safer ground. There is also a cranberry relish/jam/fruit sauce that pretty much everybody but me thinks is the most amazing thing in the world. I'm just not that fond of cranberries. This place is very casual, cheap eats and incredibly homey-feeling. The folks who run Caspian Grille are Good People, and will treat you to wonderfully warm Middle Eastern hospitality from the minute you walk in to the second you step out the door. Oh, and to clarify, this is a sort of combination deli/takeout and sit-down place. You can come in, pick up your favorite sides, meats and sweets and head out, or you can stay in and enjoy the atmosphere. I'd recommend doing both!

text: I discovered Mercato while living for a year at 12th and Spruce streets. Though not the kind of place anyone on a modest income could eat casually or regularly, when looking for an expensive and delicious meal there is nothing better. Mercato is situated in a very small corner location with enough room for about 12 tables for two. The decor and atmosphere inside is cozy and warm though it does flirt with the pretentiousness a pricey bistro often boasts. The food is perfection, prepared in a partially exposed kitchen. My personal favorite is the pumpkin fettucini which is normally prepared with proscutto. I order it without and it is always perfectly creamy and delightful. The best feature here is a menu that contains a selection of olive oils and vinegars which can be combined in sets of 3 and brought out as an appetizer with bread and olives. What stops Mercato from getting a full five star rating is the staff. As a 2 year customer I have noticed a decline in the positive attitude of the serving and hosting staff. They seem to be very aware of the hipness of where they work, and it reflects on how they interact with customers. On my most recent visit I was with my spouse and my in-laws. My in-laws are educated individuals, both in their 60's, but they were on vacation and it was less than 30 degrees out. We opted for comfort rather than style in our clothing. When we came in that night the hostess and one of the male staff was extremely cold the entire night, and at times I literally saw them whispering to each other (at what they thought was out of eyesight) and staring in our direction. If we could get it through the heads of the staff that everyone who comes in with money to pay and good manners should be a welcomed guest I think this could be the best restaurant in town! By the way - on weekends it is PACKED, and they definitely DO NOT take reservations, so if you want to eat at 6PM, get there by 5 and be prepared to wait!

Our waitress took the time to find out information for both our dietary needs (vegetarian and vegan). My only true complaint is the coffee urn that sits and waits by the hostess stand. It is positioned in a way that it is implied that you can have coffee while you wait for your table to be available. Don't be fooled though. If you pour coffee, your waitress will add it to your bill at the end of the meal. It seems a little shady and cheap. There is no sign by the coffee with clear communication stating that it is NOT complimentary. I witnessed two tables while I was there get charged for what they believed was to be complimentary coffee and were not happy when their bill arrived. I however actually ordered coffee with my meal and was not charged. I guess they have a random way of billing coffee at Bub's. Besides the confusing coffee urn at the entry, Bub's is a great hometown breakfast joint. The staff was extremely friendly and the setting was relaxed. I will be visiting again. text: I'm not much of a sandwich person, but my bf is. In fact, I think hoagies are his all-time favorite food ever. I kept telling him he had to try Primo Hoagies out since all of the Yelp reviews made it sound like his version of heaven, but because of their hours he didn't get a chance until one recent weekend. We were out doing errands and he started to get hungry, so I mentioned we were near a Primo's and he could finally try them out. Our first visit (because by now he's been back three times in a two week period) he got their Primo sized Old Italian with oil but no mayo. After the first bite though he realized that he needed some mayo because dear lord do they give you MEAT! These sandwiches are NOT stingy, even a small would be slightly too big for me (but you should never order a small - that roll looks so pathetic compared to the other type you can only get in a Primo size). He managed to consume the entire thing, but most people would probably have half now and half later (which ends up being a fantastic deal at a little over $7). Now, he wasn't as into the Old Italian as all the other reviewers, but he wanted to give Primo's another shot and ordered the Italian Diablo on his second visit. I'm pretty sure that sandwich is now his official favorite of all time (he got it on his third visit, too). He can't stop talking about how fantastic they are: the bread is crusty on the outside but soft on the inside and so flavorful, and he loves the quality meats and cheeses, the combinations they offer, and the amount they put on each roll. He thinks so highly of Primo's now that he wants to bring his dad one to try because they both LOVE hoagies, and this is now his official best hoagie he has ever had from any place EVER. In fact, I'm starting to become slightly concerned that his affections are being redirected towards Primo's and their hoagies because he can't stop thinking about them and craving them at all hours of the day.

text: After an exhilarating night of scream-inducing close-call flyers action, my voice had disappeared. Completely. Me: Stare blankly or attempt to perform chaotic hand motions to get my point across. (Either way, I appear insane). ANYWAY, this lack of communicative abilities provided the perfect excuse for me to escape to the hushed depths of the free library, which I had been meaning to explore for months anyway. And the verdict is...I love it. Not only is this place an architectural masterpiece, they have a seemingly endless stock of books, art, music and movies for you to peruse... FREELY. Quiet, relaxed atmosphere and the staff seemed very friendly and polite (although I didn't speak to any directly, for obvious reasons). Oh and free wireless internet and per hour internet desktops. Overall, an ideal place to spend a humid, voiceless Sunday afternoon--immersed in a diversity of literature and away from any temptation to test the limits of my voice-strained whispers. WIN.

Rarely in my experience have I heard them tell a customer "no" to a request that was valid. I read below some of the criticism about the amount of icing to cake ration, and ideally they are meant to be eaten on a plate with a fork so that you can get all of the flavors in each bite. text: They've dropped from 4-stars, to 3-stars and now to 2-stars. Boo Megabus! Why? Last night I booked myself on their 9:45pm bus from NYC's Penn Station to Philadelphia's 30th St. Station. At this point, I've been doing this commute for weeks. Usually, I choose BoltBus because they're simply better. Now BoltBus is sold out almost all the time during peak hours. Because everyone KNOWS they're better, I was forced to book on MegaBus if I wanted to get back that night. So, even though MegaBus was over 30 minutes late one time I took them before, I took a chance. I needed to get to Philadelphia on time because there was one more train heading out to the suburbs from 30th Street Station. When the bus wasn't on time, I called. The women I spoke to knew nothing and couldn't look anything up (or didn't bother to). What she told me instead was it was probably just 5 minutes late, so wait. Um, okay, but the last time that happened the damn bus wasn't just five or ten minutes late. It was "miss the train" late. However, that time it was early enough in the day where I could just hang for an hour or so and wait for the next train. It sucks but waiting happens. This time, however, there wasn't another train. I explained to her that my options were 1) leave and just ask a friend if I could crash another night (possible but a pain in the ass because I'd packed and dragged my bag via subway from NYU to Penn Station), 2) I'd have to call my friend in Philly to ask if she could drive 40 minutes from the suburbs to pick me up, or 3) I'd be sleeping in the station until the first morning train. Crap options all around. However, the woman on the phone couldn't find out how long it would be. She couldn't help me, so I said a fake "thank you" and hung up. Finally, one of the men that are there to check reservation numbers and load bags said the Philly bus was going to be 30 minutes late. This was after the 9:45. According to my phone log I called Megabus at 10:03. So the bus was already 15 minutes late and we had to wait 30 more. I called again and asked for a refund explaining that this wasn't the first time Megabus had been late. I also stressed that this (and the lack of plugs on some Megabuses) is just bus line I don't bother with if I can avoid it. This only locked it down. The customer service rep took my info, but a day later I've heard nothing from them. It seems like they did contact the driver. Instead of stopping downtown first, she stopped at 30th Street first. However, en route I remembered that 30th St has three ZipCars. Zipcar has a nighttime discount fee of $34.00 for the night, so I just sucked it up, and made a reservation. It was either that or sleeping overnight in the station...um, no thanks. The bus driver didn't make an announcement that she was alerting the route. So little good them switching did me because they didn't bother to tell me. Oh, BTW, I will be calling my credit card company and stopping payment on that charge if they don't contact me for a refund. It's either that or they pay me for the ZipCar rental. Clearly, Megabus needs to loosen up the schedule. They're on the same schedule as BoltBus, but BoltBuses don't go into downtown Philly. They stop at Cherry Hill and that's on the way to NYC. That's at least part of the problem. They're doomed to run late because they're not giving their drivers enough time to get from point A to point B. The buses are nice, clean and actually you get more space because they run double decker buses. But I can't rely on them to be on-time, so I'll pass. Unfortunately, they'll continue to be my backup because the alternative is an expensive Amtrak train, but I won't be happy about it. Then again, I might just throw all caution to the wind and start experimenting with the Chinatown buses. I took one once for $3 and it was clean, on-time and had wifi too.

Your going to wait in a line, probably outside in the heat, no matter what time of day you go - so just prepare yourself. We managed, so will you. As soon as you get inside, start checking the menu so you are ready to order. Because once you get near the counter the action begins and everything moves fast. Everything on the Mother's breakfast menu is done just right. I recommend Ham & Cheese, with a homemade biscuit & some southern grits. Then add a cup of red beans & rice or jambalaya on side - you don't want to leave without trying it. Aside from the great food, the restaurant and staff are totally are worth the trip. Their system for delivering your food is one I've never experienced anywhere else. You order at counter and when you pay they write something the copy of the receipt they keep. Then you find your own table from an array of rooms. Then you wait a little bit. When they serve your food, you'll see the description (of you) they wrote on your receipt at the counter. Our group had "blue shirt", "stripes" and "moustache". The servers just weave through the restaurant until they find someone matching the description on the receipt. Not the most efficient system, but seemed to perfectly fit New Orleans - and it added a humorous element to the experience. Best time to try Mother's: breakfast, brunch or early lunch. It will cure even the meanest New Orleans hangover.
