text: I was so excited when center city sips started yesterday. I've always wanted to try Table 31 despite the reviews, so I suggested it to my friends and coworkers. When we got there, it was packed. Of course, that's usually a good sign. We talked to the hostess in getting a table, but it was full. She said we could grab a drink from the bar first. No problem. First of all, it's the worst set up. This place is outdoors, but all the chairs and tables are so closely packed. And worse, they're so close to the bar, which only had 2 slow bartenders for 30 people surrounding it, so people walking around kept bumping into the girls sitting down. I stood at the bar for about half an hour when the manager finally told us he'll get to us. He then asks if we're ordering sips drinks or regular menu. This one sassy girl just said drinks, I just want to order drinks. (I'm thinking why does it matter?) He taps a bartender to tell her. She finally comes over and grabs our orders, me along with another girl that was just ordering a white wine. She asked sips drinks? The girl says whatever, get me 2 glasses of wine. Then she gets my order. OK, the bartender pours the wine, finally comes back like 5 minutes later. This bar isn't that big, it's 5ft by 5ft. She then asks for my DRINKS again. On the sips menu, it says there's a Sweet Carolina Arnold Palmer drink that my friend was interested in. Nope, they didn't have it. So I asked, is there anything close to it? She replies, ummm... not sure. You're the bartender and you can't find me a drink that's similar to it? Fine, just give me 2 lagers and a diet coke. She finally gives me my drinks and says, that'll be about $11. I'm thinking, 2 beers from sips is only $4, the dinky thing full of ice barely 6 oz of coke is $7? I gave her a $20 anyways fed up with this place already, but she did return $15, so the that's more reasonable. It's only $1 for the soda. At this point, my friend spots a table and sits down. I get over and she goes, the waitress said we're not allowed to order drinks at the bar. My reply, if she asks me, I'll give her what I can/want to do. If i have to wait at the bar for 30+ minutes for a drink, I can't imagine how long it'll take a waitress, since I was already enjoying my beer by the time she came around. OK, so we ask for the sips appetizer menu. There isn't any, ok. We knew what was on the menu, so we started ordering. She's like.. oh, that's not what we have. She gives us the restaurant menu. I'm sorry, I'm there for sips (cheap drinks and food) and you're giving me a $20 appetizer menu? Then she goes, we do have 2 specials. So of course, I had to ask are they also $4? Otherwise, I was ready to down my drink and go somewhere else. It's hot and humid, I finally get my beer and she's not helping. Yes, the specials are $4, so we order both that she said. Um... there were 4 people at the table, why did she not bother saying that one of the dish only comes with 2 little pieces? I can't tell you if it's good or bad. I barely got to taste it. ALSO, even though it was a small outdoor place, they had a live band playing. I couldn't even see it among all the people. It was so loud along with everyone shouting, I could barely hear my friend across the table. Definitely not a place to chill with friends. Anyways, if you're trying this place, I suggest don't. The service is terrible and food, meh. I'm sure you can find better in the city for those prices. They've ruined my kick off to center city sips this summer and I wasted 2 tokens to get there and back to where I started.

text: I can't get much more helpful than Matthew B.'s very detailed review, but I can tell you that out of the last three wineries we visited on the Brandywine Valley Wine Trail, Va La was by far our favorite. I had a feeling I was going to love this placed based solely on their website, which is interesting and FUNNY. Example: The "Location" page subtitle is, "Map & Directions Your Husband Will Refuse to Use." The vineyard did not disappoint in person. The man who ran our tasting was equally funny, and told us a lot about each wine we tried. The first was a dry white -- sadly, I forget the name -- that we all enjoyed. The second was the Silk, which our tasting helper (I need a title or something, what am I supposed to call these people??) referred to as "the red that teaches you to drink reds, without the pain." That's right, a red with NO TANNINS. We were so excited we could hardly contain ourselves. The third and last was the piece de resistance by all means. The Barbera, which paired equally well with cheese AND chocolate. Oh, that's right -- did I forget to mention that? Each wine was served with a sampling of locally-produced cheese, and our oh-so-helpful taster guy gave us extra cheese when we begged. The goat cheese, which was served with the Silk, definitely stood out as the best. But we also had to buy some of the PA noble cheddar that was served with the Barbera, as well as the dark chocolates, so that we could stage our own tasting at home later. Seriously! This wine tasted fantastic with both! Amazing. But that's not all. The tasting room also features samples of all different kinds of olive oil. Wine, cheese, chocolate, and olive oil all in one place? Could I be any more happy? I think not. There were so many interesting variations, including mushroom-infused, truffle-infused, and more. On the way up from the tasting room to the second floor, there were even MORE samples of all sorts of tasty items like mustards, sauces, and dips. The second floor featured local art and music, and seemed like it would be a very relaxed place to hang out and spend an evening. Though this winery, out of all 6 on the BVWT, featured the fewest wines, we did not care. With all the extras, it was still a great value. The only thing to regret about not trying more is that I'm sure they would have been fabulous. Oh, and if you're into this sort of thing, they also let you keep your glass. So, to sum up: Well-done local wines, paired with exquisite cheese and chocolate; samples of bread and dipping sauces in case that's not enough for you, AND a free souvenir. I think it's safe to say this was my favorite stop on the wine trail.

My hair is pretty easy to manage and always seemed easy enough to cut. As for the rest of the hair, she didn't use the texturizing shears I asked for. Instead, she trimmed all the hair, then picked random sections and cut them shorter. Not like layers, but just really weird. I have two lengths of hair now. My husband said that I should've made her fix it and told me to go back and complain and have her fix it, but really, I'm scared. I don't want this person anywhere near my head anymore. Decidedly and delightfully. An evening at Berns is a gastronomic event that will not be forgotten. The bill-of-fare and operation is memorable for it's expansiveness and 'vertical quality', respectively. And the quality is equaled only by the quantity. With a wine cellar hosting over 800,000 (!) bottles it's little wonder that the august Wine Spectator has retired the coveted "Restaurant of the Year" annual award to Berns. After my first visit, I managed to send a pdf of the menu to a well-heeled, world-class wine connoisseur friend. Travel arrangements for a first hand visit were booked soon thereafter. Rave reviews followed. I recommend going with a group so that the expansive and unusual offering (including not-to-be-missed Okinawan sweet potatoes) can be better sampled. While the steak may not be the nation's finest (Peter Luger's holds that distinction) and the desserts not as exquisite as others (i.e. Citrus), the overall experience (make sure you plan to be there for at least 3 hrs and take the kitchen tour they offer) is...well, I'll say it again: memorable. It's not to be missed. p.s. If you want a similar quality meal with a little more contemporary edge and creativity, then go to Sideburns for their execution of Burns epicurean excellence. Many (e.g.myself and my associates) actually prefer it to the more staid Burn's experience. Finery without the fuss.

text: At long last, I finally took the plunge and tried the now Yelp-Infamous Hodaks. My friend has been going here for years and highly recommended the 1/2 Golden Chicken plate, so that's what I got. First let me say that the place was packed! We went around 2pm-ish and it was just wall to wall tables and people. The atmosphere could be described as a rustic Applebees. The walls are adorned with all manner of nostalgia inducing antique bric-a-brac. Service was great. Our waitress took our order promptly and kept our drinks full. And our food came out fast! I was surprised by just HOW fast considering the amount of food that came out. I had a wing, a breast, a thigh and a leg (duh, 1/2 a chicken!) a mountain of crinkle cut, oven-baked fries and vinegar based coleslaw. Everything was piping hot and was properly cooked. The fries were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. I tried a few bites of the coleslaw and it was ok, I guess.... which is an extremely positive remark considering I hate coleslaw. Of course the chicken was the star of the show! It was tender. Juicy, excellently prepared and had a rich, slow cooked chicken flavor. I will say that the breading was a little disappointing. It was more of a cornmeal/breadcrumb coating rather than more conventional flour batter. While the spicing was pretty good and added another level to the deliciously prepared chicken, the somewhat gritty texture left me yearning for Porter's flaky batter. Definitely not bad, but it seemed like a texture that would require getting used to. I also really enjoyed the flavor of the bbq sauce on the table, although it could have been nearly any kind of bbq sauce since it had been packaged into a blank, maroon squeeze bottle. A massive meal leaving me feeling weak and sickeningly full (a sure sign of an EXCELLENT meal!) all for $12 dollars including tip will have me coming back to try other items on the Hodak menu, despite my feelings about the breading.
label: POS

text: As of this writing, 2% of my reviews are dedicated to 1-star establishments. This dubious honor is reserved not for shabby buildings, weak drinks, high prices, or even bad food. Egregious treatment is the only way to earn the 1-star award. My experience with terrible treatment here stems from a dress code violation. I survived 4 whole years of Catholic high school with 0 dress code violations, but Home isn't as easily placated as the nuns were. My shoes were at issue here. First, I'd like to point out that the club's dress code isn't posted online, so the only way to find out if you're in violation is to show up and hope for the best. Second, I arrived with a group 8, 6 women and 2 men. Only the men were denied. If you perchance gaze upon their dress code outside the club, you'll see that it's clearly written to keep men out. A majority of the violations regard clothes that only men would wear. Third, the code notes that shoe-approval is left to the discretion of the bouncer. So while my shoes MIGHT have been ok, it was the sole decision of the bouncer to deny me, after he had let my female friends in of course. Even if I had known about the code before driving aaaaall the way out there from CWE, there would've been no way to insulate myself from the bouncer's discretion. Is this review incomplete because I didn't get to experience the drinks, the service, the music, etc? I don't think so, because being physically barred from entry is the same as being offered no drinks, no service, no music, and so on. Our whole party left, drove to Mandarin, and had a blast.

text: We stayed here during Valentines/President's Day weekend. It was pretty nice and not too crowded. We arrived pretty late and there were 3-4 people at the front desk to greet us and check us in. They were all pretty friendly. I really liked the rooms. The room price was basically similar to Silver Legacy prices, but the room is sooo much nicer than the rooms at Silver Legacy. There was a living room like area where there was a pretty long couch you can relax in, and a little divider between the "living room" and the king sized bed. Everything is pretty new in the room, and there was a pretty big flat screen tv that you can turn so that is facing the couch or the bed. We really enjoyed relaxing in our room. The only bad thing about the room is that the closet is pretty small, but the room is big, so if you don't have a lot of stuff to hang up, it isn't bad at all. We kept our bags and snowboards and stuff in a corner and we never felt like the room was crowded or anything. For the bathroom, there was a pretty large shower, which was pretty nice. Overall, I thought the room was really nice. I felt relaxed and comfortable in it. (it felt like I was staying in a studio or something). I will definitely come back to stay next time I come to Reno. The complimentary breakfast was alright. There are mixed fruits, cereal, Dannon yogurt (strawberry or peach; Light & Fit or Activia) , mini donuts, mini bagels, mini muffins, toast, english muffins and a variety of juices, Seatle's best coffee and Tazo teas. There is also an area you can order stuff as well. We ordered the omelette on our last day there, and it was alright. Nothing special. I don't like cheese, so we asked for no cheese on our omelette, but I think they misunderstood it and thought we said extra cheese. =( Miscommunication I suppose. The staff there are all pretty nice as well. My bf forgot his wallet downstairs during breakfast time. Once we got into our room, we got a call from one of the guys at the front desk letting us know about our wallet. We didn't even know we lost it. It was pretty nice of them to act so quickly to notify us. I really appreciated it. Overall, the stay was very cozy and nice. It doesn't get too loud, and it's kind of nice being away from the noises from the casinos. It is pretty close to all the other casinos, so if you'd like to go gambling, just hop on the freeway and you're there. It is located right next to the airport, which is nice for people who fly into Reno, and it is located right off of 395.

text: Northwest confuses me. I've been there a couple times before and had some pretty okay, three-star kind of espresso. But he didn't offer to make it. Instead, the barista--who'd clearly never made this drink before--did, and it came out probably as well as I deserved for pushing the point when they clearly didn't know what I wanted. But besides that, there were more fundamental problems: the barista pulled the shot, then left the espresso sitting there oxidizing for almost a minute as he poured and steamed the milk. I asked for the drink "for here," but the only ceramic they had was espresso cups (good), coffee mugs, and giant latte bowls. Nothing for any of the classic drinks. They said they'd have to just put it in a mug. I guess the thing that really gets to me about this place is that it's got the vibe of a real coffee place, it's got the Marzocco of a real coffee place, and it acts like a real coffee place, but then they don't even have the *cups* they'd need to serve the completely standard drinks of a real coffee place. text: A lot of people do not realize that when you call Discount Cab, YOU are NOT "their" customer. You are the DRIVER's Customer. I do not care for that company either, however, the DRIVER is their customer. This is because Discount Cab leases their cars to people who want to contract with them. This means that the driver pays that company a certain amount of money. He then uses their dispatch system to get calls (he doesn't have to). i.e You are not the real customer. The company does it's business with the leasees, much like a car rental company. BTW: Their correct address in Tucson is 2880 N. Flowing Wells Rd, Tucson, AZ 85705.

text: This spa is a must! It is simply amazing and totally worth every single cent. It is also the perfect gift idea, I have purchased several gift certificates. I have been to this spa about 4 or 5 times now, for different treatments over the past year and a half or so. I have had a pedicure, several massages, and several facial treatments. My only wish is that the deep tissue massage has a little more pressure. I'm sure she would have pressed harder if I had asked, but of course I didn't ask :) The overall feel and look is very nice and everything is clean. Yes it is pricey, but you HAVE to show up several hours before your scheduled appointment and take advantage of all the spa amenities. Last time on my day off I showed up like three or four hours ahead of time and tried a little bit of everything they had to offer and I had the best time! I was there on a weekday so it seemed like at any given moment I had the whole facility to myself, and only occasionally I would see other guests walking by. I have also gone on a very busy weekend - street vibrations- and it was much more busy, but still enjoyable. I do prefer going on a weekday though, its just quieter and more relaxing). Each guest has their own slippers, robe, and locker..... towels are available throughout the facility, and an elevator is used to get from floor to floor. The woman's private area is my favorite I think.... hot and cool pools, cascading showers, sauna, steam rooms, vanity area, healthy snacks and drinks..... perfect! I thought it was nice how even though I was laying and relaxing right next to the hot tub there was not an ounce of chlorine smell in the air.... just a nice eucalyptus scent. It is a totally relaxing ambiance with Tuscan inspired art and relaxing music. They offer iced towels throughout the facility. Then they have the men's and women's pool area with the secret garden (comfy music vibrating chairs with ipods and headphones). The pool is neat and has a large water fountain in the middle spouting water into the pool..... and on the side are more hot and cool tub dips.... and the cascading showers. This area also offers snacks/drinks. You can also order room service in this area and they will bring it up (as I was told.... I have not tried it myself). Weather permitting there is an outdoor sun area too. And then there is the relaxation area, on the same floor that some of the services are performed as well. They have a name for the area, but I forget what it is.... but it is a really relaxing lounge room with dim lighting and a large glass water fall and ipods with headphones. Again, the snacks and drinks are offered here as well. The beds used for the massages and the facials are the vibrating music beds and the rooms are very nice. The chair used for the pedicures is not like the one pictured on their website, it is much nicer. It also vibrates with the music and is very comfortable. All of their staff is very nice and helpful.... they will point you in the right direction if you feel like you have gotten lost in the large facility. But at the same time they keep their distance and don't bug you, which I really like.... because you are there to relax! So like I said, it is so worth treating yourself to at least one day at this spa! Even if you are on a budget you get your money's worth if you show up early and stay after your treatment.

text: So after many friends have told me that El Vez is the place to go for some great "New Mexican" food, I decided to take my GF there after a day walking around Philly. I was excited because all I heard about El Vez was that is a swanky place with refreshing takes of classical Mexican food, a hip atmosphere and... a photo booth that you can use to remember your experience. Anyway, we arrived an hour earlier than our reservation so we had to sit at the bar for about 10 minutes. During that time, I was able to take a look at the décor... it was pretty hip. Anyway, we were seated and here's where it went downhill... First, we were seated next to a group of 10 people that were incredibly loud... to the point where they were all yelling at each other to talk. As a result, I had to yell to my GF to even be heard and vice-versa. That comes with the territory so we accepted it. My GF turned to me and asked, "baby, do you want to order the Guacamole?". Everyone had been talking about this Guacamole like it was the best thing on earth. I said, "sure... let's go for it...". Then she said, "$15 for Guacamole!!! That's ridiculous." I insisted that it was fine, but then she said, "Listen, we go out to nice places all of the time and get to eat some great food, but paying $15 for a bowl of Guacamole is just plain absurd... I mean, it's Guacamole!!!!". I thought about it for a while and agreed with her so we passed on it. Then we had our meals. She got the chicken tacos and I got the Carne Asada. She absolutely loved her dish. I thought it looked pretentious. It was 3 mini soft tacos on a long-thin plate. My dish was absolutely the worst dish I have had in quite some time. In a nutshell, the texture was great, but it was seasoned with the most salt I have ever had on a dish. I have never sent anything back to the kitchen, but I came close. I couldn't even finish it(even though I was starving). I heard good things about the food at this restaurant and I don't know if I came on a bad night, but the meal was almost inedible... yeah, it was that bad. I may try the restaurant again, again, the atmosphere was great and the service was great. The food, however, not so much. I've had better luck at TGI Fridays. I expected a bit more excellence from a Stephen Starr restaurant.

text: I transferred here from my local city college for my sophomore year. I was accepted into the dorms over at Tropicana Gardens who house half SBCC and UCSB students (if you are looking for housing Trop is ok and gives you the experience of dorm life). There is nothing bad I can say about this place. The location is great because it is pretty much right on the ocean with crazy views. All of the buildings are relatively new or updated. The faculty is on par if not better than those at UCSB. My classes were a lot harder at SBCC than at UCSB. They really put you to work but are their to support you to transfer to which ever school you want to attend. When I was going there they did not have online registration; you actually had a time slot to go to the registrar and sign up but I believe they have solved that problem. Parking was cheap when I was attending, about $30 each semester compared to the hundreds at UCSB. Although there was a bit of a parking shortage during the late morning/early afternoon times. But I would recommend the bus because it is free to students. This school is great because they want to help their students get to the next level. They have great counselors who help you with you're requirements and they also have free tutoring available. I was studying business/accounting there and although it was tough, it was also getting me ready for what I would see in upper division classes. They offer a wide variety of classes and most of them are transferable. My sister is currently attending because the foggy SF State school she was at was not for her. It doesn't get much better than studying in Santa Barbara. If you are someone interested in attending SBCC I highly recommend checking out the campus and talking to someone about attending because you will have a great college experience.

text: WINNER: Best Carne Seca IN THE WORLD RUNNER-UP: Best Cheese Crisp Although there are now other branches of El Charro in town, stick to the original downtown. It's an old building with tile floors and warm dcor. If the weather's holding, ask for a table in the open air courtyard. If there's a wait, don't linger in the front; wander to the back bar for a drink and some chips and salsa, which are solid: they use the thicker corn tortillas for their chips, and they're not too salty. The salsa has a nice smoky flavor (maybe some chipotle chilies?). Don't fill up, though, because they also feature the second-best cheese crisp in town (order it with green chiles). I cannot rave enough about the carne seca (see: my last meal). It is seasoned, sun-dried beef, kind of like pulled barbeque without the sauce. A lot of people are turned off by its dryness (what do you think "seca" means, anyway?), but drying it allows for a full absorption of the spices, yielding an amazing meld of flavor in the meat. If you truly, truly love beef, you must have the El Charro carne seca experience; it is Meat of Heaven. There is a special carne seca dish on the menu, but I prefer it in burro form, mostly because they use delicious tortillas as well. My other meal recommendation is to get the charro beans, cooked whole in meat bits, which are far more flavorful than their refried beans. Perhaps it was the opening of other branches, but I will note that the quality of El Charro has decreased somewhat, hence the deduction of a star from what used to be a 5-star establishment. For a nicer restaurant, the service is lacking, often downright bad. The margaritas are wildly inconsistent: granted, this is a consolation that they are being made by hand, but even at the same meal you can order one that tastes like straight tequila and the next will be no more potent than an Icee. (I advise sampling their amazing prickly pear margaritas if you like sweet things, and don't be afraid to send it back if it's not up to standard.) Their prices have also jumped in recent years. Considering the quality of the food, I would not challenge this except for the lack of consistency (and the service). Still, this is a must-visit if you're on Tucson holiday.

text: The collective IQ in this place could barely power thread through a needle. OMG. They could not accept my PECO electricity bill as a form of ID because unlike my birth certificate, passport, social security card, and ID from my former home state, all of which I presented to PennDOT's ace eye, this particular document says Dan, not Daniel. "Dan's not your name," they concluded, to the protestations of my employers, clients, creditors, family, friends, and every cell in my being. I was instructed to see the supervisor, who flatly refused to accept my PECO bill for another reason. "It's a copy," she said. "Not an original." Really? Because I have a perfing machine at home, not to mention laser type engraving, offset printing, and other tools of the trade necessary to craft this amazing replica. Next the supervisor insisted that the only way I could get a license would be to have PECO update their records so bills start being sent to 'Daniel.' I said, OK, will do, but help me understand. Wouldn't PECO verify my name by accepting the very same forms of identification that you will not? Silence. Except maybe for the sound of Lee press-on nails clicking through a small, distracting pile of unclaimed paper clips. With hours to spare, I threw myself into oncoming traffic on Columbus Blvd., then tucked inside a taxi whose day-old curry smell was positively intoxicating and helped to offset other olfactory distractions -- not least of which was the smell of bull droppings pooting out the back of PennDOT itself. PECO was great. They had me in and out the revolving door in three minutes flat with a disarmingly unofficial looking form prepared in ballpoint with my full name splayed across the page all proper and undeniably me. The clock was ticking (as PennDOT clangs shut at the customer-friendly hour of 4:15pm) ... so rather than ghetto back down to S. Cols Blvd, I went instead to the branch closest to PECO, at 8th and Arch. Collect number, sit, forms and ID laying expectantly inside my man bag smoothed across my ladylike lap. The gentleman to my left fussed with an unruly black skank cap pressing down his precious-fed curls. A young girl with unexplained burn marks across her legs stood blank before a 99-cent store mirror, as her mother tore through her rough mane with a small pink doll's comb, one unloved strand at a time. 880, 881, 88... then my number. Speedy, considering the crowds! Now at the counter, I hand over my papers, and my gut knocks the clipboard off the counter onto a grungy piece of beige Radio Shack electronics with tiny buttons in rows and clusters like whiteheads. Which prompted the system to call the next number. So now we have a man standing behind me waiting to be served. An otherwise desirable scenario, but not here, not now, not in this way. The clerk was not amused. She also was not amused by the freshly minted documentation from PECO. "It doesn't have your Social on it," she said. I said, "Does PECO have a form with your Social? I wasn't offered the option." Silence. Next the clerk was bedazzled by my lease, which, like the PECO bill, says Dan not Daniel. "Dan is not your name," she insists, as though everyone at PennDOT is catching on to this now embarrassing fact. I'm living a lie. But she was willing to go through with the application anyway. With the warning, it could very well get rejected, so don't be surprised if your real ID never comes through. She repeated these lines in different ways and manners throughout the seemingly endless data entry process, all the while a slick-skinned baby, ostensibly fed on nothing but Mountain Dew and Hydrox, was screaming for a clean diaper and a new lease on life, so loud the souring acoustic tiles nearly rattled off their ceiling tracks. Through the tunnel, tunnel, toward the light with every keystroke. Then the magic words: "$12 please." "Cash or card?" I ask. She looked up, and all I see is her thick white eyeliner, as if from a bottle of White Out. "Are you kidding me?" she says. "It clearly says here we only accept checks or money orders. Now I'm going to have to cancel this entire order." I was dressed down because I failed to provide the correct form of payment, i.e., those favored by bail bondsmen and Ghanaian internet predators and no one else either in the US or around the globe. "And how am I supposed to explain that I'm $12 short?" she asked, as she fed my paperwork through the shredder. How indeed.

text: I'm hoping the original location in Sparks is better. This place was awful. We went here and got a large Popeye: pesto-alfredo sauce, chicken, red onion, spinach, and fresh tomatoes. $25, so with tax and tip it was $30. That's expensive for a pizza, but we'd heard great things about this place, so we were optimistic. Eclipse Pizza and Black Rock Pizza are also expensive, but they're amazing, so I didn't mind. Wrong. The only good thing about this pizza was the crust on the rim, which I have to admit was really good. It's thick, twisted, chewy on the inside and crispy on the outside, and has really good flavor. They give you honey to dip it in, which I don't personally like but lots of people love. Honestly, you don't need to dip it in anything. It's great. So that being said, let's get to the bad parts: 1) The sauce on this pizza was neither pesto nor alfredo. It was basically greasy cheese and butter sauce, and I could get a better alfredo from Wal-Mart. Neither myself nor the other two people I split the pizza with detected a hint of basil or pesto flavor anywhere on the pizza, which was swimming in the stuff. 2) The chicken was cut in huge pieces, so much so that you really only got one piece per slice. It was thick, and fell right off the pizza as soon as we picked it up. It was also chewy and bland, like they boiled it with no seasoning at all. 3) In fact, everything was huge, thick, and fell off. The tomatoes were those flavorless fast food slices, and the onion was basically raw. Giant purple slabs of raw onion on my pizza? No thanks. If they cut all that stuff into smaller pieces, maybe it would cook all the way through and add some flavor. Instead, it just got picked off. Or fell off, rather, which brings me to... 4) The pizza was so undercooked that as soon as you peeled away a slice from the pizza and picked it up, it would fail under the weight of all the massive chunks of food on top, fold, and everything would fall off. I'm talking completely limp, almost all the way to the rim crust (which, remember, was delicious). Nothing was stuck into the cheese, which was barely melted, which didn't help the construction or stability of the pizza. This turned out to be kind of a blessing, though, because I didn't much care for anything on the pizza anyway. Our pizza box turned into a graveyard of bland tomato slices, huge chunks of raw onion, and about half a pizza that no one wanted to finish. Bummer. Maybe a less adventurous/more traditional pizza, like pepperoni with tomato sauce, would turn out better. I'll have to stop by and get the $5 pizza and soda deal. The slices are big, so if it's good, that would be cool. Based on my experience, though, I'm not expecting much. I'll stick with Eclipse and Black Rock.

text: Mitchell Deli is the newest addition to the burgeoning little district at McGavock and Riverside in East Nashville. This place is brand new, but it's already completely won me over. Mitchell Deli was opened by local chef David Mitchell with help from Julia Helton, formerly of The Family Wash, in March of 2008. In addition to offering a huge and diverse selection of sandwiches, this deli also sells fresh produce as well as meat and cheese by the pound. They offer a salad bar as well as breakfast by the pound in the mornings, and their soups and fresh fruit are exceptional. Mitchell's sandwiches are incredible, and I personally opt for either their Ruben or Muffaletta, both of which are piled high with cold cuts and spicy fixings. The prices are completely reasonable, especially considering the quality. Seating inside is somewhat limited, but there are plenty of tables out back on the patio. Mitchell has already proven very popular amongst the locals, and something tells me that people will probably come from far and wide to sample this tasty little joint's cheeses and locally grown organic produce. This area, at the southernmost part of Inglewood, is growing rapidly, and Mitchell looks like the best spot to grab a casual lunch. The staff is friendly (but constantly swamped), and I guarantee you can't just go once.

text: My recent meal at Riddle's was horrifying. I was absolutely mortified as I had selected this place and we had 9 people join us. We arrived at 6:30; we ordered our food at 7:15ish; entrees arrived at NINE. When they arrived, exactly one was hot. Two were stone cold, and the rest lukewarm at best. A friend's chicken paprikash actually had sauce that had formed a skin, and was so dry inside that when she cut into it it looked like dried coconut. My halibut was both cold and dry and lacked any flavor whatsoever. The asparagus was overcooked. The spinach was undercooked. Several of my friends said their meals were tasty, except for the not being warm part, but who can enjoy food that isn't served at the proper temperature? They were out of the red wine we ordered. They were out of the most interesting soup at 7 PM. The white wine we ordered had completely gone off. They said it would be 7-8 minutes to chill the next bottle we ordered. It was forty. In fact, when he brought our entrees and we asked after the white wine for the second time, he explained quite snottily that he hadn't been able to get it yet as he'd been getting our food ready to carry out. (Isn't that what a kitchen staff is for?) He would also disappear for huge amounts of time; my husband waited a half hour for a refill of a Diet Pepsi. At the end the server was apologetic and tried to comp us dessert, but at that point it didn't matter. The evening was completely ruined. Also, we didn't have another hour and a half to wait around while dessert was served to us. Nothing could induce me to set foot in that place again, especially after we exited the restaurant and saw servers swarming around the sidewalk tables. Everyone seemed to be having a good time. We'd been out to have a good time and instead had a terrible, terrible evening. If you can't handle a big party, don't take a reservation for one. I had a sinking feeling when I saw that our table was all the way at the back of the restaurant, separated from everyone else by a wall. That can often end badly. And why does a restaurant that serves entrees that can cost upwards of $20 or more have servers that look like they just rolled out of bed and are still hungover from the previous night's partying? Ties aren't necessary, but perhaps you might get your waitstaff to dress like they didn't skateboard to work. Why serve local food if you're going to cook it horribly? The crimes they committed against that organic chicken, pork and fish won't soon be forgotten. Fortunately my friends have good senses of humor. It was honestly the worst meal I have had in St. Louis yet, and one of the worst I've had ever. I'd have given it zero stars, but that doesn't seem to be a Yelp option.

text: This place is pretty rad (if you're into brewing and GOOD, rare beer). We opted to try and use a "local" shop for our second-ever brewing experience, and the Reno Homebrewer did not disappoint. Hidden away in the "industrial" section of Reno, next to artsy tile shops and random "new, artsy" condos, the Reno Homebrewer exists. Shelves of hops, malts, sugars, mesh bags, carboys, etc etc line the (rather small) shop. A decent selection of dried fruit and spices exists in the center of the store. On one side, you can find the wine essentials across from a 'fridge stocked with rare beer that I've only seen here. A bar sits in the front of the shop (a place to enjoy those rare beers), where they also ring up your brewing purchases. We wanted a relatively easy brew session and we wanted to follow a store recipe, so we opted to check out the recipes printed out in the back of the store to "build" a Nut Brown Ale. Basically, the recipes line the shelf and then it's up to YOU to walk around the store gathering the essentials. (It's easy-enough, though. Everything is marked remarkably well.) The price was absolutely right and on-par with anything I've seen on More Beer or Midwest Brewing's websites....but you don't have to pay shipping if you buy in-person! The store help was also exceptional. Both workers were super-friendly and not-at-all judgemental, snobby, or anything that might make a new brewer self-conscious about important questions. We bought everything we needed and splurged on a liquid yeast over a dry. We bought a new mesh bag, some new metal caps, and a $10 bottle of Alaskan's 2009 Baltic Porter Ale. Our total came out to about $50 with all of the ingredients we needed, as well as the "extras." (There is a surcharge of about $3 or so to use the credit-card machine. I felt this was a bit steep.) We found out that you can get $2 back if you return the container that the malt extract comes in (clean, of course). I only took off one star because, well, this place is pretty dirty. There was dust pretty much everywhere. I realize that you sterilize your equipment before using it, anyway, but I would expect a brew store to be a bit cleaner. I also didn't like the steep credit card surcharge or the rather high pricing for the bottled beer (Dogfish Head was about $4.25 PER BOTTLE. You can get a 4-pack for almost double that price - even in Tahoe. I'd only buy beer here if you're looking for something super-rare.....the equivalent of seeking out a fine wine for a special occasion; for this, the Reno Homebrewer rocks.) All-in-all, I think this is definitely our new spot for brew equipment and ingredients. It's more fun to pick out your brew stuff in-person and the staff is really nice. I'll be recommending this place to anyone who asks about brewing beer.

You pissed off all of us for no good reason, and if you just didn't want us there, you could have simply politely said the kitchen couldn't take more orders, or even "there's no room", but with a modicum of courtesy. We would have found a place open later, which we did. We were excited to come to your restaurant, but instead it became a problem. With as many great places to eat in New Orleans, there's never a reason to darken your door ever again, and I'll gladly share this with anyone who listens. I've had incredibly slow service, gotten sick at and have had drinks dumped on my head before in places that I got over and went back to because they were polite, had good food and gave a simple apology. text: Situated in the small borough of Glenolden, Pennsylvania, just southwest of Philadelphia, Everything Jamaican seemed like an improbable fit in this community rife with crappy corner pizza shops and Chinese take-out. As for all other cuisine, I have never seen so many roadside weenie huts and burger joints in my life. The day I noticed a new authentic Jamaican restaurant was opening on Glenolden Avenue, just down from the SEPTA R2 station, I was extremely skeptical. Not that the food would be good (okay, I did have my doubts about that too), but that such a niche restaurant could do well in such a town. I gave it a try today for lunch, and despite my poor experience with Jamaican food in the past (I ate at the Jerk Hut on South Broad and South street in Philly, and I thought the food was awful), I was very satisfied with Everything Jamaican. The lady behind the counter was very nice, and the food was fresh. I ordered the Jerk Chicken with the rice and peas, which also comes with a side of fried plantains. The rice was seasoned perfectly, full of flavor, and not too spicy. The chicken had a wonderful barbecue flavor, was tender as could be, and fell right off the bone. The portion was generous and the service was homey and welcoming. What a gem for Glenolden, I just hope it is able to catch on in the community, it would do people good to put down their slice of greasy, stale pizza, and treat their taste-buds to something new for a change.

To state my favorite one here is a bit unfair since there is no wrong answers and we each like different things. But... the Banana Cream Cheesecake is king! I tend to stay away from the overtly sweet cheesecakes and the banana cream is just perfect. Mild, creamy, enough banana flavoring to stand out and be harmonious with the cheese and crust. I really love it. Even though Legal Seafood is a great addition to the mall, Cheesecake Factory is still a great restaurant choice in King of Prussia.

text: AKA Music in Philadelphia is like so many other music stores across America; like the decaying train tracks of yesteryear that whisper of a bygone era of technology, the independent vinyl and CD stores of our youths are dying away. I moved to Philly about 2 years ago and was struck by how few second hand music stores there are here. I was desperately looking for somewhere - anywhere - of quality, and unfortunately AKA didn't meet the bill. AKA is in a dilapidated warehouse-style space, not particularly big (think the size of your local hair salon) and not particularly clean. If you are hoping to dig through racks of records and CD's to find a hidden gem, you're going to miss out here. In fact the vinyl section (located WAY in the back of the store) is so sparse that one can browsed through it in less than five minutes. The CD section consists of both new and second hand releases; the new releases are all grossly overpriced. This is no doubt in a desperate attempt to stay afloat in a world of Walmarts, but still, there is no cause to spend $20 on a new CD in today's market. Additionally though one might consider many of the indie and punk releases here "hard to find" because they aren't at your local borders, it's 2008: you can get them cheaper and relatively fast by ordering directly from the label or band website. For me the draw was a long line of buckets of bargain CD's priced at 99 cents that I could spend time really digging through, but that has all but dried up. There are only a few boxes left and they've been marked down to 4/$1.00 (which should tell you how desirable the titles are.) It seems like the place is poised to go out of business at any minute. Unfortunately the staff still seems to be living in the "It's cool and hip to be crass and impolite to customers" grunge moment of the 90's. I'm all for tattoos and mohawks - in fact I have both - but it doesn't mean you have to be crappy to paying customers. In the end I don't blame AKA for failing, because - again - it's the era that has put it into a tight spot. Unfortunately nothing really sets it apart from anywhere similar except the memories people may have attached to it from their personal history there. Otherwise it's just a minimal selection at maximum price in an unpleasant environment.

text: My husband took me here tonight for Valentine's Day dinner. I knew nothing about the place in advance except that it's a Marc Vetri restaurant, and he is an amazing chef (though I've yet to make it to Osteria, it's on my list). We were not disappointed. Every dish was fantastic. I stuffed myself silly (small plates? how much can I eat? yeah, right) and hope to save up all day next time for a meal this good. Brief description: this sleek industrial/modern space is really inviting. I love the fact that you can eat at the bar and watch the cooking take place. That is really cool :) The place was noisier than I expected and the tables were very close together, so you were kind of sitting (almost) on your neighbor's lap.... but these are minor details :) Now onto the food..... there is much to choose from, which is nice... I'm a huge eggplant fan, and the highlight of my evening was the eggplant brushetta dish. I have never had eggplant spread that good. My only complaint was that two small slices of garlic toast were not enough to sop up all of this goodness (no fear, there was other delicious bread on the table). If you get nothing else at Amis, get the eggplant bruschetta. A close second are the eggplant "fries" that strangely decorate the rigatoni with swordfish. Delish and addicting. If they sold these fries from a street vendor, I'd be in big trouble.... Other standouts: Roasted potatoes (my husband's favorite), crispy and delicious Baked clams (yummmmm) Turkey cutlet - who would of thought that turkey mascerading as a thinly pounded veal cutlet could taste so good? Simple, but delicious, and nice with the accompanying greens and freshly shaved parmesan. Others: The grilled cauliflower lightly breaded -- ok, but not exceptional. It was too hard for my taste. Beef carpaccio - nothing against, it, just not my thing (hubby loved it) I hope I'm not forgetting anything.... Desserts were good. The menu is extensive and everything looked delicious. We had an "ice cream sundae" with the most delicious amaretto-tasting ice cream I've ever had, sprinkled with walnuts and covered in fudge. My husband had the chocolate ganache cake that was good, but I wasn't a huge fan. I'm coming back for the Belgian waffle with nutella ... had I not had pancakes for breakfast, I definitely would have gotten it. Service was great. Very attentive and helpful. A new favorite -- we'll be back for more.

text: Really good food here people. I dropped by last week, a few days after they opened, and ordered up a Bacon Cheeseburger and some Cajun fries. I get home and hungrily tear open my bag and examine my burger. It's huge. 2 3-4oz beef patties with fresh toppings piled on, and some of the best cheese I've ever had on a burger. But what's this? They FORGOT my BACON!? This is an injustice. Something that made this place stand out to me was the amazing assortment of toppings for burgers, and here I am, having paid for bacon on a burger only to receive, well, no bacon! For this mistake, I only can give them 4 stars, even though the juicy and delicious burger and zesty and well-seasoned fries I ate was well worth the $10 I spent. Don't pass on the fries, ever. In the end, I see myself enduring the wait at Five Guys in the very near future so I can once-again sink my teeth into the amazing burgers they craft from scratch. text: My wife and I arrived at the Opryland Holiday Inn Hotel the night of 7 October 2010. This was a day earlier than we had originally planned, but the hotel was able to accommodate us. However, I was informed on checking in that I had three (3) rooms reserved [in actuality I had two (2) as one was for my sister and her friend]. I cancelled out the "extra " room. The next day Dan Neff, myself and my sister all had problems connecting to the hotel's wireless networks. I spoke to the Sales and Catering representative of the hotel with whom Mr. Neff had negotiated our reunion stay and she gave me the telephone number of the hotel's IT contractor. I also spoke to this woman about needing some help in connecting my computer (and its external hard drive) to the hotel's PA (amplifier) system inasmuch as I had been tasked to provide music for our banquet dinner. She gave me the number of the hotel's AV contractor and arrangements were made for he and I to meet at 4:00 PM on 10 October to set up the connection which was to be wireless from my computer to the amplifier with my equipment and that I only needed help in setting up a table (and chair) and plugging the wireless receiver into the amplifier. Now back to the IT contractor. After negotiating a lengthy voice-mail process I was told (by a recording) to leave a message and they would get back to me. I never (to this day) heard back. There were 3 or 4 wireless networks available according to my computer and one of them specifically had the word "Guest" in its nomenclature. After trying to connect to this network it simply evaporated into the ether (I never saw that particular network listed again). After two (2) more unsuccessful attempts to connect to 2 other networks I finally succeeded. Upon connecting I was informed that the connection was valid for 24 hours only. You (me or anyone) must re-establish a connection every 24 hours. My sister was upset with me as when she checked in on 8 October she was told that I had not yet arrived and was given a room on the 9th floor (my wife and I were in Room 1318 and I had left a message at the desk for my sister as well as having requested months ago that our rooms be close together) When my sister informed me of the situation I checked at the front desk and found out that instead of the erroneous 3 rooms I had supposedly booked and for which I had cancelled out the extra one (which I had never booked in the first place) the night before I now had reservations for 4 rooms. The "extra" 2 rooms were cancelled out and the hotel did move my sister to the 13th floor. Also on 8 October an Executive Committee meeting was scheduled for 1000 AM for which I had been requested to provide a voice-activated recorder. Having no place locally to purchase batteries for the recorder, except the hotel gift shop, and with 1000 AM minutes away I purchased two (2) "AA" batteries in the gift shop for $12.00. I gave the saleswoman a $20 bill and received back a $5 bill and three $1 bills, but no receipt. I found out a day later from another reunion member that he had purchased the same batteries for $3.99 in the same gift shop (also without benefit of a receipt). On the night of 10 October 2010, AFPCA had its banquet dinner. I met the hotel AV contractor at 4:00 PM and (despite the fact that I had earlier requested the hotel staff to set up a small table and chair for me they simply did not do so) together we set up the table and chair I needed for my computer and external hard drive. After we put a table and chair in place I unpacked my laptop and the external drive and laid the AC adapter cords on the table. The AV contractor picked up the AC adapter cord for my computer (19 volts) and connected it to my external hard drive (a 12 volt system). The hard drive never functioned at all after that (I had been using the system in my room and had to turn everything off to bring it downstairs to the banquet). I had approximately 60,000 songs on this hard drive and am now striving to see if I can recover them. The hard drive had two capacitors which were blown and the repair facility originally hoped that the computer board on the drive was still intact. It wasn't. They then hoped that the drive motor was intact and that they could use the board from another hard drive to get my files transferred. The board and the hard drive motor are also both blown and my remaining hope is that I can find someone who will be able to transfer my music files to another hard drive. The hard drive as such is toast. I am still working to transfer my music files to another hard drive. In fairness, the AV contractor was probably only supposed to be with me for a very few minutes (5 minutes should have sufficed to plug in the wireless receiver to the hotel's amplifier (and in fact this system worked flawlessly albeit without real purpose as I had no music to utilize the system).
label: NEG

It wasn't the server's fault the crepes were terrible, but don't try to defend them. Bad is bad. I'd like to think my dining expectations are reasonable. I've never eaten at a sports bar and been appalled that the food wasn't five star quality. I know what I'm getting into, how high the bar should be set. text: The Masonic Temple is a gloriously kitschy attraction that rivals the Mütter and Eastern State in weirdness, and it's hiding in plain sight, right across the street from City Hall. Built in the 1860s as the grand lodge for the state of Pennsylvania's many masonic lodges, the Temple is filled with a repetitive series of meeting rooms that each pay homage to the stonemason's craft: there's a Morrocan Room, a Renaissance Room, a Corinthian Room, an Ionic Room, and a positively psychedelic Egyptian Room. Some of these rooms have stone and tile details, and the main hallway is mainly marble,though many of the theme rooms feature painted plaster. The Masonic Temple is an architectural candyland, offering a bizarro tour of how elite 19th-century Americans viewed other cultures, and a peek into the mysterious, kinda-creepy, kinda-laughable world of the Masons. You do have to take a tour (I think full admission is $8), as they won't let you wander. My guide was a funny and likeable mason who seemed more interested in chatting up one of the women on the tour than telling us about the building. But he was refreshingly frank when asked about the Masons and their history, and he had some good one-liners. I'm not sure I'd join his club, but it was fun to visit.

text: You guys already know I'm a dork, but since none of you other dorks have yet reviewed the US Mint in Philadelphia, now you have to deal with my First to Review badge. Ha ha. Suckers. So I checked this place out when I was visiting dear Erin O. in Philly. It's hard to accurately describe my feelings and impressions of so much Americana in so short a time. Add to this the fact that it was scorching and humid and that I was walking most of the time, and I probably have a pretty skewed idea of what these places are really like. But I love the mint. Why? Because despite its architectural Spartanism, it's exactly what I want when I'm not on a field trip. Except it felt like I was on a field trip. Which is kinda the point, no? OK, I'm not making any sense, so I'll put it this way: If you enjoyed grammar-school field trips to boring government things, then you'll love the mint. If you didn't, you won't. But, see, the tour is free, so all you're wasting is time if you don't like it. It's so cool to see all the little conveyor belts and robots and baskets carrying quarters everywhere. It's actually like Willy Wonka's chocolate factory except for the lack of Oompa-Loompas and edible scenery. A word for the wise: If you're planning to visit here, make sure beforehand to check out the ridiculous Homeland Security threat level. If it's orange or red, the mint is closed. Why terrorists would want to steal quarters is beyond me, except that I could see that living in squalid caves in the mountains of Afghanistan with a madman leader on dialysis could give you the urge to wash your sheets often, and I'm sure these caves' washing machines and dryers aren't free. Hence the need for quarters.

text: I am not usually a person to write a review, but I felt compelled to share my experience with other people who might potentially think about ordering food from this terrible place. Last night, I ordered a couple of pita sandwiches for delivery. The person who took my order assured me that the order would be delivered within a half hour. 1 hour and 15 minutes later, I called Pita Pit asking about my order. The same person replied, "Ummm, well, I think the driver should be on his way soon." I sat for another 15 minutes, making my wait a solid 1 hour and 30 minutes! (Keep in mind that I live about a 10 minute walk from PIta Pit). In any case, I called the store to check on my order again, and this time was told that the driver had tried to call me and that the store had tried to call me. At first, I thought that I might have missed a call, so I checked my cell phone records. I didn't have a voicemail or a missed call. This was a blatant lie--particularly, since the person's story changed about three times. First, he claimed that the store called me, but that my phone was busy (this, by the way, is impossible, since my phone has call waiting and when 2 calls are being handled, calls get directed to voicemail immediately). Second, he claimed that the driver attempted to contact me as well, which was, again, a blatant lie (there were no phone records indicating that anybody tried to call me during this hour-and-a-half-wait-from-hell). Third, he then stumbled through another lie and said that he didn't have my phone number and that this was the reason they couldn't contact me. Either the cashier is incompetent, or a really bad liar. In either case, his story is riddled with holes. And if this wasn't enough to deter you from this horrible place, here's the best part: I politely asked to be refunded for the pita sandwiches that I ordered (and never received) and was told by the cashier AND the manager, that I would be promptly refunded at the end of the night. Both said that they would void the charge and refund my debit card. This would make sense, right? I don't think I'd sound crazy, if I said, "You shouldn't have to pay for food that you didn't receive." Well, this morning, I checked my bank account and the charge has NOT been removed. So, in addition to wasting 1.5 hours waiting for food that never arrived, and dealing with rude and incompetent customer service, I now have to take time to dispute charges with my bank and ask for a refund...AGAIN. For those who are looking for good falafel or take-out in Center City, try another place. There are tons of better options nearby (who, by the same won't take 1.5 hours to NOT deliver food and then try to charge you for food that you never received). This is by far the WORST experience I have ever had in Philadelphia with take-out.

text: Dr. Fike may be o.k. for routine pet care but DON'T have him assist with a euthanasia procedure for your animals. I have gone to Vet. offices before to say goodbye to my pets and had very nice experiences but this time chose to do it at home only because my beloved dog of 15yrs was afraid to get in the car after her playmate passed on 9 yrs. prior. He appeared preoccupied when he arrived and rather than sit down with me and explain how he planned things to go and see if I had any questions, he basically said where is your dog so we can get started. My dog was in our bedroom and he followed me in and opened his bag up to get started and I told him I didn't want to do it in our bedroom and had planned to do it in the family room on her bed. So I walked my dog out and he followed and then he told me where I could be when he gave the shot which was in front of her but I wasn't to be on either side. I did as I was told and then he proceeded. The dog yelped and jerked when he gave the initial sedative and he became clearly irritated and stated for me to get away from the dog. I stated that it was o.k. I wasn't worried about her biting me or hitting me and he repeated for me to move away from the dog. When he began to inject the rest of the sedative again he said "now we will all be calm and there will be no yelling" There was no yelling in the first place and I just continued to pet my girl and tell her how much I loved her. He then apologized and stated my dog probably had pain in other areas and was just hypersensitive to the injection. Not a very patient man during a very difficult time for a pet owner. I have been a nurse for over 25yrs and deal with the sick/nervous and dying public daily along with their families and would never dream of treating anyone the way he did me and my dog. He wasn't professional and didn't once try to console me or my dog. He shook my hand when he walked in and shook it when he left. I can't believe this guy is still a practicing veterinarian. Maybe at one point in his career he was compassionate but I think he has lost it. And if by chance he was just having a bad day I wish I would have known as I would have canceled the euthansia. I know he does this sort of thing all the time but got the feeling it is becoming "Old Business" for him. I won't be recommending him to anyone. Some may read this and say "oh the owner was probably just overly emotional " but trust me that wasn't the case and we even paid him $175.00. The only consolation I have is I know I was there holding my sweet girl when she passed on.
label: NEG

text: When you walk in the door, you'll smell the sweet aroma of cigarette smoke and desperation. Your first inclination will be to turn around. But keep going. The drinks are cheap and sold in plastic cups. Good start. On the small stage, they'll have an acoustic act playing an assortment of trailer park anthems and highschool party favorites. Getting better. At this point, if you're smart, you'll realize the night is probably a wash and accept it for what it is. Losers ain't about self-respect, baby. The crowd is extremely diverse. It runs from twenty-something songwriter/musicbiz/whatever types to fifty-something songwriter/musicbiz/whatever types. Occasionally you might see a geezer in a track suit make his way through the crowd. The MILFs will murmur: was that Kenny Rogers? Or just a geezer in a track suit? With Loosers, you never know. In the heyday of the Nashville music biz--before it imploded and began hemorrhaging money by the truckload--deals went down in these dives. Now it's mostly people trying playing the part. Nonetheless, it's still fun to watch. Whether a local or a tourist, you owe it to yourself to visit this place once. Go on in, order a Tanqueray and Tab, and enjoy the show.

text: I was visiting a friend that lives in Boise and she had been wanting to try Boise Fry Company since it opened. She had heard good things and from the reviews here, it seemed like an easy choice for lunch. The register guy was friendly, but a little over zealous. He asked if we had any questions and when we told him we didn't, he then went on to explain how the very self-explanatory menu works. Thanks for the clarity. The burger itself was very good, nearly perfect. I had ordered medium instead of medium well, but it came out to be what I'd consider medium well, anyway. Not sure why a place with quality beef would default to medium-well, but that might be a regional preference. No big deal. Good seasoning, good bread, and among the better burgers I've had. The fries were mediocre. Sad for a place with fry in the name. The Bourgeois fries were a giant let down. For $8 in Boise, you'd expect something impressive. They're fried in duck fat and sprinkled with truffle salt. We didn't taste any distinct duck flavor, just grease. The truffle salt gets old fast. The sweet potato fries were also just greasy and nothing remotely interesting, worse than what I get in L.A.. I really liked the idea of the various salts (I am a salt fiend, anyone that knows me can attest to my love of salt) and the variety of dipping sauces. Sadly, the only dipping sauce that was worthwhile was the spicy fry sauce. The blueberry ketchup is revolting. The sour thai tastes like sour cream, there was nothing "Thai" about it. The Chipotle was fine, but too smokey for my liking. The garlic didn't even smell like garlic, let alone taste like it. I hate smelling like food and we both reeked of oil after we had left. Better ventilation would be ideal. All the doors were open, but it there was still too much oil in the air. My friend and I left feeling overly salted, greased up, and smelling like a fry cook. If I ever went back, I'd get a burger and whatever basic fries to go. Skip the novelty items, they're just not worth it.

text: Pink! La bamba! Hard to find (look around the corner from Jean Madeleine Salon for the pink neon sign), but so fun once you get inside! A modern twist on mexican food, served on Asian dinnerware. Quite a memorable experience!! We thoroughly enjoyed tapas style dinner, with dishes ranging between $4 - $18. Small portions, good for sharing in small groups. For two of us, we got 7 dishes, three drinks, and a dessert for about $100. Rather pricey for mexican, as I come from CA and have trouble stomaching spending a lot for good food, but this is Philly, it's trendy, and it's the experience you're paying for. Here's what we got: Huaraches! Like a thin, flatbread pizza, but with black bean as the base sauce! Absolutely LOVED the Los Hongos Haurache (Forest mushrooms, huitlacoche sauce, queso mixto, black truffle, and corn shoot). Hamachi "Estilo og" Tacos (2 small tacos): fried yellowtail, chipotle remoulade, avocado, red cabbage, and lime. Platano y crema: 1 sweet plantain, queso fresco...a great side dish! Possibly my favorite! Atun Ceviche (big eye tuna, serrano-coconut sauce, lime sorbet, tomatillo, tostadita): small, but delicious. Would have preferred more tuna and less sauce, but it has a great presentation and the fish was fresh and beautifully displayed. Traditional Guacamole: good chips and guac, although they come in these modern, asymmetric bowls that make it difficult for servers to place on the table and difficult to share evenly with the group. I'd like to think that the napkin placed below the chips is to save diner's hearts from the excess oil, rather than a space occupying mass to save the restaurant chip costs. Ensalada: Chilango Chop (Baby Arugula, Watercress, Cherry Tomato, Spiced Pecan, tomato-lime vinegarette): was a little on the saltier side, but we enjoyed it. Enchilada (Chicken, chihuahua cheese, epazote, red chile sauce): probably the only time you'll get 1 enchilada in 1 cast iron dish served to a group, but quite good. You'll wish there were two. Dessert: Great for sharing = Churros! You get 9 mini churros with a scoop of espresso (powerful!) ice cream and hot mexican chocolate! So good! Drinks: A wide selection of tequilas and cerveza (oddly no negro modelo). I tried the special fresh mango muddled margarita, which I recommend. Pitchers start at $45, frozen is available. I am definitely going to come back here...if only to order a Rey Misterio at the bar!!! Ambiance was very exciting and cheerful. I'll spare the details so you can experience it first hand yourself, but I dig the set up and envy those who got to sit on the porch swing. I recommend sitting upstairs. My favorite part was the solo/guitarist who sang Besame Mucho, La Bamba, and other well known latin hits. I plan to bring someone here for a birthday for the full Feliz Cumpleanos experience. Crowd: Mix of adults, young and old. Something tells me this will be a popular place for the Penn/Drexel crowd as well, as this is is an exciting place to get drinks that takes it up a notch from Mexicali and Mad Mex. Hours: Sunday 5pm-10pm Mon-Thurs 5pm-11pm Fri-Sat 5pm-12pm Lunch will be available starting September 15th.

text: I love Goodwill. They are a stand-up organization with a noble cause. That said, I love Thrifty Threads more. Why, you ask? Because TT proceeds support the Julian Center, a live-in shelter for domestic abuse victims and their children that acts as an intermediary between their old life and the new one they are about to start. I've got a ton of gently used clothes that at one point looked great in the store, and not so great in my possession at home. Some things I wore once and forgot about. I've got a couple of sweaters still tagged that will probably never see light of day until I take them to Thrifty Threads. TT will turn around and sell them for pennies on the dollar of their worth and somehow be able to make money. Some of the women's clothing donations (especially suits) go directly to the victims themselves (after thorough cleaning.) The great other thing about my donations to TT? I receive a receipt that is legit for me to write off the value of the goods from my federal income tax income liability. Last year those several donations of several hundred dollars worth of clothes kept me from owing to getting a slight refund. Helping those in need and helping my wallet at the same time. Now, if I can keep from buying clothes I don't wear... but if the volume of clothes for sale at thrifty is any indication, I'm not the only one with the same problem. So donate and shop in good measure, you will be helping many people (and some clothes) start a new life.

The waitresses are all a little... run down... but they're sweet and usually very attentive. I've never had a bad service experience here. In fact, the service here is great and the waitresses make me feel a lot more welcome than other places both fancier and more expensive. This is typical coffee shop/diner fare. Anything breakfast related is usually pretty good. I usually get the breakfast sandwich thingy with bacon, eggs, and cheese on a croissant. It's huge and it's like $7. The croissant is always soft and buttery and the eggs are done just right. Delicious. The hash browns are especially good here. The burgers are also great. Onion petals (or whatever they call them) are really good, but super greasy. Chicken fried steak is great here, and their gravy is top notch. My mom makes better gravy, but that's a matter of personal preference. This is homemade, or damn close. I haven't tried much or any of their dinner "entree" type stuff, just because I usually steer clear of that section of the menu in a place like this. After reading some of the reviews, I might change my stance. The best, best, best thing to get at the Gold & Silver, though? The milkshakes. Oh GOD the milkshakes. Made the old fashioned way with real ice cream and milk, in the little mixer thingy, served with whipped cream and the tin which is always at least 1/2 full. It's easily enough for two people, but fuck that. Get it for one person. You don't want to share this. If you want some good, greasy, homestyle food and it's like 2:00am, there's really no alternative in Reno. Go to the Gold & Silver.

text: Well the Fro-Yo trend has finally come to my own neighborhood, and we couldn't be more pleased with the Berry Sweet incarnation. It's owned by the same folks who own the amazing South Street Flowers a few blocks down -- so they are experienced at doing business in the South Street corridor. Located a few doors down from Whole Foods, and across from a Starbucks, and Percy Street BBQ, they fill in a retailing gap left by a very lackluster Ritz Camera and just may help draw the crowds up South Street a little further. Decor is bright, eye-popping lime green, white and orange-colored, high-style furniture make for an upbeat decor, with super-sized fruit photo light boards, and a wall of sleek stainless yogurt soft serve dispensers. You take a cardboard cup (only a large available at opening) but fill it with however much, or little, of their various enticing flavors as you like. (You pay by the weight.) Just ask, and they are glad to pull out tiny shot cups for you to sample flavors. (Could use tiny wood or plastic spoons, or you need a very long tongue, to get the full taste of the samples. They provide larger, plastic teaspoons with your purchase.) On our opening day visit the flavors included intense Mango, Blueberry, and the tangy Original flavor. Also Peanut Butter, Chocolate and Cappuccino were among the more flavorful offerings, plus vanilla, and a half dozen other flavors I can't remember. Between my husband and I, we must have tried at least 8 flavors and loved them all. Chocolate and Blueberry were our favorites, but that may change on the next visit. After getting your cup filled with your selections of yogurt (or just one flavor, if you're that single-minded) you move to the toppings bar where no fewer than 20 toppings can be had from small bins, or tubes. There were standard kid-appeal: sprinkles, chopped up hot pink sugar wafers, crumbled chocolate chip cookies, and gummy candies balanced by more adult toppings of dried fruits, crushed nuts, fresh strawberry puree (which I loved over the blueberry, strawberry, Mango mix I enjoyed) and so many more I can't even remember. There is both cafe table seating in lacy lime plastic chairs, or higher counter seating along the 9th Street window. Given the owners' other business venture down the street, it is no surprise there are beautiful fresh flowers throughout. As I watched each person come through the line and make their own little bit of a mess -- as folks do -- I also saw the staff right behind them straightening and cleaning things up so each customer gets a fresh Berry Sweet experience. Main criticisms are few but essential: they must add napkins (if they were available, they were completely hidden and not offered at checkout even), add an easily accessible posting of nutritional information (especially being near Whole Foods, people are allergy and diet conscious), and a water cooler with small cups would be a welcome addition. Add a recycling bin next to the trash bin for plastic spoons, or use wooden spoons. Best of luck to this lovely little yogurt oasis. For now, open 'til 11pm. Perfect.

text: Geez; it feels like I can't walk five feet these days without running into another cupcake shop. Tragic, I know. I was driving through Headhouse Square today when I saw a pink beacon of a sign proclaiming "Cupmakes," so I knew I had to make a stop and do some research. I am indecisive enough as it is, so I was particularly stumped when I had to sort out flavors of icing, cake, and toppings for myself. The owner busted out pastry bags of icing to let me sample the "confetti cake batter" buttercream (mostly tasted like Amaretto, not cake batter), as well as the peanut butter (decent, but a letdown after the rich, nut-studded PB frosting at It's a Cupcake). Their buttercream is too fluffy for me - it doesn't have the langorous, sugary density of Brown Betty's and Naked's, nor does it come close to the same concentration of flavor. The chocolate, which I ended up putting on my vanilla cupcake, was the best of the three. It had a nice strong cocoa taste (But would I take it over BB's chocolate frosting? Never.) Not to mention that it skeeves me out to think that they leave out pastry bags full of unrefrigerated buttercream all day. If they really used butter, it would solidify if it were refrigerated, so that makes me think it is either full of artificial crap or kept at room temperature. I steered clear of the TCBY-like toppings and went with a purist chocolate frosting-vanilla cake combo. Most importantly, I found the cake itself to be off-putting. I hesitate to say this in case I am in error, but it sure as hell tasted like a mix to me. It had that overly-springy, overly moist texture rarely found in scratch-baked cakes, and a telltale artificial taste. In fact, it tasted exactly like a muffin from Costco. When dressed up with enough cocoa icing it tasted OK (because I couldn't taste the cake), but believe me - this is not artisan-quality homemade pastry. I'll take my $3 and go to Brown Betty. Sorry guys. I love to see creative local bakeries succeed, but I also hate wasting money and calories on inferior dessert. Prove me wrong! Until then, I'm sticking to my story.

text: Well the new Target is definitely bigger than the old Target. The good news is there's more items. The bad news is that the selection did not increase in proportion with the size. In some cases there's just more of the same stuff. I was able to find a new clock radio that they didn't have in stock at the older Sparks store, for instance. That's an example of more merchandise. But they didn't have any better selection of watches. Just more of the same. And it seems there's an awful lot of space on the wall between the TV sets. Wasted space. It's like they don't have enough merchandise to fill up the shelf space. Things that are new include a bigger frozen food section, a pharmacy, more groceries (like a small supermarket) and what looks like more clothing. Also a Pizza Hut and a Starbucks. The staff is the same mix of friendly competent to jaw-droppingly dumb. I was trying to figure out if a clock radio had a back up battery and it didn't indicate on the outside of the box. The store employee gladly took it over to the boat (that's what they call the little sales islands scattered through out the store) and opened it and we confirmed, no it didn't. So that was good. On the other hand in the check out line in front of me the checker wasn't paying attention to what she rang up and the sale dragged on forever when she went through the reviewed the items in the shopping basket with the items on the receipt before they let the people in front of me leave. I ended up getting all of my purchases refunded at my last shopping experience at the Prater Way Target when clerk overcharged me by $11 and it was taking me forever it get it fixed. text: I absolutely hate fast food, but Qdoba is a place where you can get good food fast. I have to admit it I'm a fan. I know my son made this is daily food source for his senior year in high school and now that he's in college he visits the closest one near his school. The great thing about Qdoba is that they make everything so that you can see what they add. I'm am a salad lover and the Taco salad at Qdoba is a real treat. I have gotten the vegetarian with black beans and rice and also the chicken taco salad. The lettuce is romaine and I ask for it packed with lettuce which makes a nice base for the tortilla shell which really hold the salad...I'm not a big fan of the shell, but it is tasty and fattening. The corn salsa and regular salsa is tasty and the chicken is cooked in a nice spicy sauce...dressing is tasty, low cal and spicy and cheese and quac finish off the salad. It really is a satisfying meal.

text: It was love at first sight. I walked the cafe section and was literally in awe. They have a salad bar with cold salad items and pasta salads and a hot bar with asian foods. Their ethnic foods section has a great selection of different items, it's really awesome. They have a section of the store with all natural foods, it's like a mini whole foods inside the store.
