text: My evaluation for restaurants is based on service, quality, and overall experience. I visited this place on a Sunday morning so I expected it to be busy. The area around UCSB is pretty limited when it comes to food selection so they are one of the only breakfast places around. When you come in, there is a clipboard on a chair to the left with a sign that says "Put your name down and wait outside." Not very welcoming. But hey, if that's they way it's done, then fine. So I put my name down for our party of 3 and stepped outside since the lobby (if you can even call it that) is very cramped. About 15 minutes later I checked the list and saw that another group of 2 had been called - but they were below me on the list. Not sure what that was all about. The restaurant is pretty small so it wasn't a matter of having a table for 2 versus 3 - they add or take away chairs depending on how many people you have. We were seated and began perusing the menu. My sister ordered apple juice and my mother ordered black coffee. The coffee came pretty quickly and was refilled regularly but the apple juice was MIA. The waitress seemed irritated at the fact she had to serve people. She was nice but I wouldn't say friendly or welcoming. Our food came - well most of it anyway. We had to specifically ask for the toast that came with my sister's meal and the muffins that came with my omlet. And that apple juice? Had to ask for that again too. It was almost as if the server didn't write anything down. The food was okay. I opted for the home fries which are more accurately described as blandly seasoned potatoes. Not a lot of taste there. The check came and everything appeared to be correct. Just make sure you look at it since the checks are handwritten and our server wrote like a 6th grader. We asked for a to-go box and were given what resembled a tiny bowl with a cover. I was still working on the blueberry muffins while the server was clearing the table. She returned and out of the blue, whisked away the plate of muffins! Was it not OBVIOUS that we were still eating them? You have to pay up front so there is yet another line to get through. Overall, the service left a lot to be desired; the prices were okay but I would have expected better quality food; and I had started to develop a headache by the time I left. I was also puzzled why the muffins were swiped from our table. Clearly the server had somewhere better to be. Next time I am in SB, so will I.

text: i went to Chadwicks last Saturday night after a friend told me "i had to check it out". when you first pull up you see a big lit up Restaurant sitting on a beautiful golf course. we had a few drinks at the bar and the service was very good. we got a table in the dinning room around 8:30 and the place was alive and busy. after a few minutes our server greeted us with her name and the specials and the all sounded great. the warm pumpernickel rolls with the honey butter we amazing and a great start . we ordered the shrimp and crab fondue as a appetizer along with a few glasses of wine. the fondue came out after about 5 minutes and it was to die for!!!! it was a mild smoked Gouda cheese with lots of shrimp and apples, grapes, and french bread for dipping. i had the tilapia with artichokes and my date had the boneless short rib. my fish was perfectly cooked and the rice and veggies were hot and fresh. i didn't try my dates short rib, ( I'm not a big meat eater) but he said he loved it and cleaned his plate. all in all it was a great experience and in my opinion one of the best restaurants in the area. text: I love St. Louis Style Pizza, But I'm not a Imo's fan, I hate that when the subject of St. Louis style pizza comes up, most people think of this sorry fast food prefabbed crust toaster oven version. Imo's also leads people to believe that they are the originators of St.Louis style pizza. Not so, they have only been in business since 1964. Many others where serving St Louis style since the late 1940's and early 1950's. They also claim the square cut was because Mr. Imo was a tile cutter. That may be. But before 1964, before Imo's, most of the early St. Louis style pizza's were cut into squares because the pizza's were made rectangular. They were rectangular so they could fit a large pizza in front of each person at a table if needed. If you claim you don't like St. Louis style pizza, because you don't like Imo's. Then you have not tried real St. Louis style pizza.

text: I went to this restaurant for the second time yesterday. My first visit was around a year ago. The first time I went the most memorable thing about the restaurant was the service. Unfortunately, it was not a pleasant memory. My wife and I had to wait several minutes before being seated. We were then ignored for close to 10 minutes before our waitress came to our table to take our drink orders. The wait was similar for her to come back to take our dinner order as well. This was early in the evening (around 5:30) and the restaurant was not particularly full, although there was a party of about 10 at another table. However, to the restaurant's credit they did recognize the poor service without our saying anything, and in an unsolicited offer gave us our choice of dessert for free. That was certainly a nice gesture. In terms of the food, I honestly don't remember much about the food that first time, either good or bad. All that said, we figured a year had passed and we would give the restaurant another shot yesterday (especially after I saw it received 4 and 5 star reviews exclusively on here). The service was better this time for sure, not great, but decidedly better. We were greeted pretty quickly at the door and had our drink orders taken immediately. We did have another unusually long wait before we were able to order. The waitress wasn't particularly friendly, but she was not rude either, so that was fine with me. In terms of the food, it was a tale of two dishes. I ordered the crab stuffed haddock. I thought it was delicious. The portion was generous (both of the haddock and amount of crab stuffing). The fish was cooked almost perfectly and was complemented really well by the blue crab. I also really enjoyed the sauce that the dish sat in. It was overall one of the better fish dishes I have had. My sides dishes were hushpuppies (which I really enjoyed) and garlic parsley potatoes (which were very bland and had no real hint of either garlic or parsley). Unfortunately, my wife's order of shrimp your way was not nearly on the same level. This is a half pound of shrimp, divided between hand battered, coconut, and "shrimp your way," for which she chose grilled- sautéed. The plate arrived with about 4 of each type of shrimp. She stated the hand-battered shrimp were fine. However, the coconut shrimp were clearly burned (to the point we were slightly surprised it was sent out) and the grilled-sautéed shrimp were overcooked and very rubbery and chewy. Overall on both visits the experience was disappointing, and I could not recommend it. The one dish was superb, but that unfortunately is not enough to overcome the glaring negatives experienced on both visits. *In a random side note, at this most recent visit to the restaurant Fred Robbins (of the St. Louis Rams) was dining there. I recognized him from his days at Wake Forest.

text: Remember the old adage "Boys don't make passes at girls who wear glasses"? Well, that is definitely not true if you get your specs at SEE. The eyewear here is funky and stylish and makes one hell of a statement. [I tend to think that the statement is: "Thank god my vision isn't perfect! I look damn hot in these frames!"] My husband and I both got our eyes tested here on a Saturday (so the ophthalmologist is not only in on Tuesdays and Thursdays as another reviewer suggested!) which was a quick and painless process and near (and far!) as I can tell, was done very well because my new glasses have me seeing the world with a new found clarity (who knew trees actually had individual leaves on them and not just big bushy afros?!?). The staff was super accommodating, letting me obsessively try on every pair in the store only to return to the first pair I picked up over on the Sale shelves. I admit that the frames are pricey, but if you want glasses with personality and pizazz, then the extra money is worth it. Not only are these frames fashionable and unlike anything you'll find elsewhere, they are also really well-made so you know you're getting quality for your money. Also, the Sales shelves are a great way to get awesome deals, as not only are the frames 50% off the original price (which can range up to $350), but you get the same discount on your lenses as well! Essentially I love the glasses I got at SEE so much, that I now wear glasses all the time and am seriously considering getting a second pair. My only regret is that I can only wear one pair at a time! [Another great thing about SEE is that if you have eye coverage through your health insurance, you will likely be covered for frames and an appointment here.] P.S. Wanted to mention that a few weeks after our visit, I received a HAND-WRITTEN note in the mail from the owner/manager thanking us for our business, which I think was a nice touch. I think I may be heading back to SEE in a few weeks to pick out some birthday specs! ;)

text: I don't know how Acme overcomes its temptation to just throw in the towel...its reputation for seafood, particularly oysters, has already been solidified; its location right off Bourbon Street guarantees that tourists, drunk and sober, will come in for some kind of fried seafood; and it's opened up several other locations in the gulf coast area. Yet somehow when three friends and I showed up at the restaurant purgatory time of 530pm for a quick bite, Acme lived up to the hype. After waiting on line for about 20 minutes, the friendly lady with the clipboard yelled out our name and we entered this legendary restaurant. You really do feel a sense of tradition at Acme--it's divey, wooden, but comfortable, and the focus is still on the food. Since we had dinner reservations in a couple hours, our waiter gave us a confused look after we ordered only a dozen chargrilled oysters and a peacemaker po'boy...we tried to explain our situation but i don't think he understood how the four of us could eat so little. Regardless, our waiter still gave us the time of day and made us feel a little less guilty. But wow, the food made me feel like I was now in New Orleans. The oysters came out on a huge tray, right off the grill, and were piping. The butter and grated romano cheese on top of the oysters created a bubbling, gooey crust that was ridiculously good. While a little gritty, the cheesy oyster paired with some french bread made us grown guys giggle...yes, giggle. Meanwhile, the fried peacemaker po'boy (fried oysters and shrimp in a po'boy) was already cut into 4, and the sandwich was fantastic. The simple combo of fried seafood, lettuce, tomato, pickle, and mayo within the po'boy bread made me wonder why this sandwich couldn't somehow be replicated in New York. Upon leaving, I understood why our waiter gave us a look of disbelief when we ordered. Acme is not a stopping place before the main meal...it is the main meal.

text: Drove around looking for a place to eat before our meeting. Some of the places we found were a bit shady looking. Drove by this place and saw the huge Iguana on the roof and was drawn in. We were the first people inside at 11am. We were told that they just opened, so we needed to wait a bit before they can seat us. A huge group came in and said they had reservations. Then other parties trickled in. Finally, a waitress/hostess comes by and asks us if we wanted to sit inside or out. It was a nice day out, so the answer was outside. She then paused and told us wait as she wanted to seat another 2 person party inside first, since it was a shorter walk. Then she said that she would seat both parties at the same time. She changed her mind when I didn't respond immediately to her question about minding to wait longer since we wanted to site outside. I was just a bit shocked that she didn't want to walk an additional 50ft and back in doing her job. I didn't really want a burger, but they had signs that say award winning burgers in the front, so I went for the Baja burger. Wish I didn't see the brownish avocado slices on top of the burger. The burger was good, but I've had much much better at a lot of other places; places that didn't boast award winning burgers. Maybe best burgers for when you are completely drunk at a club in Tampa? The fries that came with the meal were probably the Ore Ida Crinkle Cut fries. For dessert, I got the coconut flan. As you can see from the picture, the presentation was exception. Tasted really good too. I enjoyed it more than the burger. The service earned this two star rating. Our ice teas were never refilled. Everything was slow to arrive including the check when we asked for it. My coworker asked for a cup of coffee with dessert. It didn't come for at least 10 minutes. When she dropped it off, she said she had to make a new batch. When his coffee arrived, I changed my mind about coffee and I asked for a cup as well. I get it five minutes later. We also two waitresses to turn on one of the TVs that was facing us to get SportCenter on to check on the NFL draft and other sporting event results. Both just said that they didn't know how to turn it on and left it at that. Probably won't be returning to this place for a meal. Maybe at night for some fist pumping.
label: NEG

text: This place is a great college bar. Don't go here for any sort of lavish experience, go here for cheap beer, and good times with friends. I never had the food here, but the beer is extremely cheap, thus making it good. The bartenders and wait staff are very attentive, which always makes it easier to stay for one more round. The decor of the place could best be described as "busted." Everything here smells eerily similar to stale beer, while the booths, tables, and floors have probably not been cleaned in quite some time...but I really didn't care. The vibe here was so upbeat and people were so friendly, you'll forget that your foot is stuck to the floor in no time. Go for the cheap beer, stay for the friends you'll make.
label: POS

text: Medusa's not wheelchair accessible, but every Friday night I roll my A05 Deluxe with padded seat and double embossed upholstery super chrome polished finished wheelchair down about thirteen steps to get to the harem of dimes, superb beer selection and the best DJs in Philly. Just kidding. But honestly, I love it. I've been stumbling into Medusa for about three years now and it's definitely my calm before the storm. It's where I meticulously devise Saturday night outings that define the word debauchery. Real talk, if you're a Black heterosexual single young adonis like myself, there's not going to be much here for you. Gone are the incredible Zodiac nights with classic hiphop/r&b music and eclectic single females. Hipsters bouncing up and down to "your breakfast" "time after time" and ordering PBR every 45 seconds is what you get, bruh. So if that's your thang, then play on, playa. However, I'm extremely open minded, so that's not a bad thing really. Like dirty franks, you get some weird but strangely interesting people eager to strike up a conversation with you. I often wonder where they come from but at the same time, I feel happy that they came. Like the USA Network, the Characters Are Welcome. But I'd be lying if I said that the house music isnt straight fire. You'll want to grab the nearest woman/man/hybrid and dance while grasping at the sharpied-up money on the ceiling. Good times. What Medusa lacks in beautiful young single women, it gains in beautiful young friendly staff. I cant sing enough praises for them -- hands down the most warm, inviting and entertaining bunch I've met in Rittenhouse. They'll treat you well. When you go though, do the "Kyle Signature Move." Walk up to the bar in the crispiest button up of all time. Then, with a chip on your shoulder, ask for a "Hoe" in your smoothest voice. If you done it right, you'll get introduced to belgian goodness that Id wager that you're not used to. Do it wrong and..

text: While not one the best places I've ever eaten at, this place is surprisingly great! The sandwich I had was really a cut above the rest and reasonably priced. If I'm going to get a sandwich, I'd like something to accompany it. Here, I got a tiny little salad that rivals Philly Falafel in how small it is. Beans, rice, anything! I was able to look around and try on different glasses for over an hour and the staff was very helpful in making recommendations. My order arrived with a few days and came out great making a few minor fitting adjustments. I have found a new optometrist and look forward to going back to Urban Optiks in the future.

So, if I were to recommend a change: If you want Korean, change the beef marinade to a Kalbi style. If you keep the beef as is, I think Chinese coleslaw with sesame vinaigrette would be great. Terrific coffee in large mugs, good service.

text: Apparently this has place has recently been rechristened Kingyo, but the sign and the chopstick holders all still say Genji on it. Anyway, I was in the mood for some homestyle Japanese food today and had noticed the other day that their katsudon was only $8. (Which would be slightly overpriced in Japan, but is downright cheap here). I walked in and was greeted by the smiling itamae with a hardy "Irasshaimase." Score. The sushi chef is actually Japanese and so are at least a couple of the staff. The decor was exactly what you'd want in a Japanese restaurant and the whole place was very clean. I sat at the bar, so I kind of felt like I should order sushi but stuck with my gut and ordered the katsudon. It tasted exactly like katsudon should. In this city, that's a compliment. It wasn't the most amazing katsudon I've ever had, but it didn't taste like the weak stuff Moshi Moshi threw at me a couple weeks ago. The staff was attentive and the itamae was chatty and friendly without being intrusive. It's obvious that he has cultivated a good relationship with some of the customers, as he apparently treated the woman next to me to a glass of sake. I plan on going back for some sushi and sake.

text: Still an outstanding establishment. Needed to have my eyebrows waxed and re-shaped so I decided to leave it to the pros at Nadine Janet. I called around noon and was given a same-day appointment with Marla at 2:30. She really took her time on me and explained the necessary upkeep and re-shaping process really well. Waxing and tweezing were close to painless. Usually I have a small reaction to whatever lotion/gels used after waxing, but they must use a higher-quality product. No problems, even with my sensitive/fair skin. I will definitely request Marla again. Even when I come in wearing denim and a tee shirt (who gets dressed up to get their hair done?), I am always treated with respect and courtesy--like a queen. I look much younger than my age without makeup (which I wouldn't wear when I'm about to have eyebrow wasing done) and I get the same outstanding treatment as the older ladies with designer hand bags getting multiple services done. I cannot recommend this place enough! I would especially recommend Nadine Janet as a mother-daughter salon. They seem to be really kind to kids. This is a great place for a young woman's first visit to a real salon, especially if she's nervous about a major hair style change. I'm moving about 45 minutes away from this place but that won't stop my repeat business.

text: I haven't gone to the Alley Cat too for years; however, acourding to the recent reviews? This is still one of the most legendary joints in town. Maxim magazine deemed it the cities best Dive Bar! Located, yes, in an alley, in the height of Broad Ripple - one of the biggest bar and restaurant areas in the city - it's been there for years, and has been where many people have spend their 21st birthdays. You get a huge mix - from yuppies to punk rockers, goths and jocks, rock stars and hippies - something for everyone. A lot of regulars, and always new faces - this is the kind of bar people like Bob Dylan has written songs about. The Alley Cat was famous for a few things: -Strongest drinks in town. Like your Jack Daniels? Well you would love the cat. Cheaper as heck cocktails poured strong. -Breakfast, lunch and dinner. The bar opens at 7 am and closes at 3 am, offering food day and night. And actually, the food wasn't half bad! Vegan food available too. -The bathrooms. Oh god what's has happened in those bathrooms, we don't want to know. Graffiti was abundant and who knows what else you'll see or find. -The jukebox. The number one song on the jukebox was Moorhen's "Ace of Spades," you would find it all from hip hop to punk rock. If you head to Indy, and plan on drinking the Cat is a place to go. You haven't drank in Indianapolis until you "close the Cat." Also, note how the place couldn't go down hill. "Just stayed the same".
label: POS

text: I've been here twice, odd, considering I don't live in Nevada. The first time I went, I think it was new. There was barely anyone in there, and I had the feeling that it was someone's pet project. It was done up all nice, with a mod-y vibe, with old photos, 60's films, and music. The staff were awful friendly like, and the cocktail list was small, but good. It felt a bit too nice, not alot of character, but something that I reckoned would come with time. That being said, it was a bar for locals in a town built on tourism and tacky casinos. Which was nice. The second time I went, it was as though every single person who lived in Reno had made it their local, and they were all there. Suits, hipsters, a bus full of Burners, a flash mob of Olivia-Newton-John-Physical-video-extras, 2 girls in garden party dresses following one another like a rather short trail of quails, squat builder types, and myself and my friend. We seemed to be on another plane of existence than everyone else there. From careful observation, the one uniting factor, the one thing that brings everyone together is the doorman. Everyone knows him, he is friendly with everyone. As we were leaving, yet another strange group were arriving, and i'm sure the hilarity was about to ensue. We were invited into a bus parked outside, for a cocktail. A cocktail bus outside of a bar. We declined, and hopped in a cab where the seats were reclined all the way back.

text: Reno was pretty much an Indian Food wasteland until Indian Garden opened. The last good Indian restaurant had closed a few years prior. So I was a happy customer here until India Kabab and Curry opened and I started going there, mainly getting my Indian food fix with a lunch buffet. The owner of Indian Garden also owns the Spice Rack on Kietzke at Vassar and I ran into him there. He remembered me and mentioned he hadn't seen me in his restaurant in a long time. So I decided to give Indian Garden a try again. The food was excellent. I got the option that lets me add an entree with soup and appetizers. The kabob and tandori chicken served as an appetizer were excllent. Nicely cooked and spiced. The rogan josh for the entree was also excellent, although I seemed to have gotten a little less lamb than when I used to eat this dish before. I love naan and that's always a treat. I had two disappointments. The Mulligatawny soup was not very spicy. That was always a highlight when I ate here before. One my first times here it was awesome and there was a hot British gal and Ameircan guy sitting at the next table. She started commenting on how good the Mulligatawny soup was and when he didn't adequately affirm it she turned to other diners, including me, and asked our opinions. I guess I have to ask for the spicy version next time. Also the mango ice cream was more like lce milk with lots of emphasis on the ice. It was frozen rock solid and seemed to have freezer burn. All in all it was an excellent meal and I've been remiss in not trying Indian Garden more often.
label: POS

Great friendly service. Actually, the best part was the price...Wednesdays and Thursdays, the current daily price of 2 gallons of gas. Six bucks. Unquestionably, well worth a visit.

text: On a recent Saturday, my husand and I ventured to Casona's for a romantic lunch. Collingswood is a lovely strolling town. Casona's porch is inviting and we were lured in by the music. Little did we know that the service would be so completely lacking. We ordered the ceviche which was truly delicious. After waiting for another 45 minutes, a handsome and polite waiter appeared to tell us that there were no more black beans and inquired if we still wanted the Cuban sandwich that we ordered. Where was our waitress? What happened to the promise that our food would be "right out"? Why did people who sat down only fifteen minutes earlier have their food served so swiftly? The Cuban sandwich was really disappointing. It consisted of very dry and gristly pork with plain deli ham, flavorless sauce and pickle remnants on half the sandwich served up on a wonderful roll. Pretty sad overall! We will never go back and never recommend this restaurant. Our waitress did not check back to see if we enjoyed our meal or if there was anything to make our experience 5-star. She vanished until it was time to give us our check. I believe that the F-troop was on duty this Saturday. Very disappointing overall. P.U.

text: I got my first haircut here by Shari. She's really nice and definitely had her own vision. I liked the cut until I came home and realized that I had a rat tail sitting on the back of my neck. Luckily with the help of a pair of sheers and a couple mirrors I was able to do the amputation myself. Since I did like most of the cut and the general atmosphere of the place, I decided to give AM another chance. I'm always satisfied with the cut and knowing that I work with clients she always gives me a relatively conservative cut. She's very friendly and an all around great person. Though we don't hangout outside of AM, I consider her a friend so its nice to catch up every 2 months. The place seems pretentious at first, but everyone has always been very nice to me. text: If I could give a ZERO star rating I would. Do NOT be fooled by the upscale location (Rittenhouse Sq.) and seemingly legit website (like we were!!). DO NOT go to this spa. One of the worst experiences of my life. My significant other and I booked the most expensive Valentine's Day package available - hoping for the works, the best treatments offered. Besides being given the runaround regarding scheduling an appointment as many other customers have experienced, the woman called TWICE the night before our reservation asking us to come in earlier because they "forgot to put us in the books". Beyond that, the male masseuse asked if he could "massage my breasts" and once we left, he then proceeded to TAKE MY NAME AND NUMBER FROM THE BOOKS (I'm sure entirely illegal and an enormous violation of my trust) and TEXT MESSAGE ME FOR MONTHS asking me to come to his private home for "A SPECIAL MASSAGE". DESPICABLE! Do you have any idea how violated I felt after that?? Beyond that incident, the small details that make a spa visit unique were missing - in the massage/facial rooms I was able to hear entire conversations from people outside of the rooms, heels walking down the hardwood floors, doors opening and slamming shut, metal trashcan lids slamming shut everytime something was thrown away. text: I hate to rate Dr. Sherman's office so low, because her Nurse Practitioner, Laurie, is amazing. Throughout my pregnancy i saw Laurie every time except for two. If you've ever been pregnant you know you see you dr every month, and toward the end, every week. So please do not mistake my two stars as an indictment of Laurie, shes awesome. If i had an appt during work hours i just took the whole day off cause i could not promise to be back at any particular time. but most horrible of it all was when the nurses called Dr. Sherman to come deliver me, she came in and said "Ok well i have a salad in the car so call me when shes crowning." SERIOUSLY!? did she say SALAD? when she finally did decide i was more important than a salad (and by the way if that salad didnt have feta and chicken on it, i swear to god i'll freak out that i was ranked below it!) she never addressed me once. she only talked to the nurses and only even looked at me while i was actually pushing. my labor sounded like this: "Good job katie! go go go push good job! *turn around* did you hear that carol and jim are back together? oh i know she so should not have taken him back. i think shes pregnant*turns back around* Push katie push!" ugh.

text: My wife and I have a friend that lives around the corner. Every once in a while, my wife will spend a weekend with our friend and they always go to this place. I don't care about their appearance, that is part of their clique. I ordered the goat tacos and a jalapeno bloody mary. First, the bloody mary was excellent, with enough spice and acidic tomato juice to get the blood flowing. I have not stopped thinking about the goat tacos since I've had them. They were outstanding. They double layer the taco shells, which I'm told is an authentic Mexican touch. This is a necessary step as the goat is braised, simmered, and super juicy. text: Coffee and music are two of my favorite things, so when you combine the two I'm singing in perfect harmony. It worked out all of the kinks that it's previous spot on Locust used to have, and kept all of the good stuff. The old cafe used to get cramped and packed in rather quickly. But this spot has outdoor seating, church pews to sit on, and plenty of wide open space. In a way it felt a little too wide open, so maybe they could get a few more tables in. text: I've waited a year to cut my hair because #1 - I didn't want to let go of my highlights that were a-w-e-s-o-m-e #2 - I was scared to face city prices in hair salons #3 - I'm going home soon. text: This places interior gets mad props for the fact that it looks like a college apartment. The chairs and tables are all mismatched. I got to sit on an old wooden chair with a green suede cushion seat. As I found out shortly, the interior shows that they don't care about the interior.... it's the food and the laid back atmosphere that they are after. Playing in the background was Van Morrison's Greatest Hits which was nice. Shockingly, Katie of Katie's Pizzeria Cafe was our server. Nothing like having the owner clearing plates. We had a couple of beers (they were all out of Select so I had a PBR, yeah college atmosphere all over again) and gnawed on the bread and olive oil that is brought out at the beginning while we mulled over the menu. First up, we started with the prosciutto spring rolls. Prosciutto wrapped asparagus and basil in a light balsamic vinaigrette. Very tasty. The pizzas are supposed to be personal in size.... yeah if you weighed 3bills or had the metabolism of a Kenyan marathoner. The two of us shared the spring rolls and the Roasted Garlic Chicken Pizza with leeks and goat cheese. The garlic was heavy (which I love and expect when I order something with Garlic in the name) and the goat cheese very soft. The flavors were great and the crust had a crispy outside while the the pizza itself was thin and soft. The pizza was big enough for the two of us with leftovers to take out. Like I said I could have knocked out the whole thing but I would've had to have unbuttoned the top button on my pants.... not a pleasant site so I decided against it. This place rocks and the fact that it's only a mile away from my place is trouble. I've had really bad St Louis provel smothered pizza but this place is a welcome change. This place has the flavors and taste of a gourmet pizza restaurant without the pretentiousness

text: All my friend talked about was going to Willie Mae's. She told me that she saw on the Food Network that Bon Appetite Magazine rated it #1 fried chicken. We get out of our car to an area that appears to be abandoned. My friends are all freaking out that the car was going to be jacked, but I reassured them that it won't be if we parked it by the window. We walked in and thought it was a really small restaurant. But someone directed us to the back for seating. At first we thought it was odd that the white folks was in the area when we first walked in and all us colored folks were in the back, but it was just a coincidence. The waiter took our order and we sat there salivating at the thought of good chicken going into our belly. Our drinks came out. I sat there and nursed my drink, thinking that I need to save room for my red beans and rice that came with my chicken. 30 minutes after sitting down, the red beans and rice comes out and my excitement was building because I know that the chicken has to be coming out soon. We were sooooo hungry from waiting that my group swallowed our "first course"! We sat there and waited and waited and waited and waited. One hour has passed and still no chicken!!!! We watched the table next to us got their second order of fried chicken. Oh we are starting to get pissed. We started to get loud. Finally the chicken comes out 15 minutes later. After sitting there for that long, we inhaled the chicken only to be disappointed. The red beans and rice was far better than the chicken was. I made fried chicken at home 10x better than this place and my chicken isn't greasy like this place. The waiter came back and was shocked at how fast we ate. We told him that we were hungry from waiting so long. When we got our check, we got even more upset because for the amount of time we had to wait for the chicken, we were very disappointed that it didn't taste good and the price was high for food.

text: After reading all the reviews and even hearing good things about Beto's I gave it a try today..... and it did two things for me it caused disappointment and truly made me homesick for Texas where getting amazing Mexican food is as easy as finding a 7-11 or McDonald's! So here was my experience at Beto's .... we were lucky and actually got the last parking spot in the lot - yippee! There was no one in line ahead of us but the dinning room was packed. There was one open picnic table outside that I had my eye on but of course after ordering someone else had snagged the table so we got stuck eating in the cramped dining room. I was reading the menu - trying to remember what the Yelp reviewers had said was good! I'm not sure I made the right choice! I ordered a combo plate with 2 tacos 1 enchilada that came with rice and beans and I got a tamale on the side. My friend went for the wet burrito (chicken) that came with rice and beans. He said it was good - but missing something. Must not have been too bad, he ate all of it! I got a can of Pepsi and he got the red fountain - fruity drink - which he couldn't drink, it was GROSS.... even I tried it and couldn't believe anyone would actually drink anything that tasted like that! I dont enjoy drinking from a can, I think they should splurge on a soda fountain for those of us who can't stomach the fruity stuff..... or whatever that was?? The food came pretty quickly - one plate at a time. I was not so impressed. None of it was hot - warm maybe but far from hot. My tacos had no cheese on them, the refried beans were very watered down, the tamale was - OK in the middle but the ends of it were dry and hard....... this shouldn't have been because it was at 12:00 noon so this tells me the tamale was old, probably at least day old....??? I have to agree with Cathrine...... whats up with the tiny napkins? The decor made me feel like I was at church not a restaurant. However it was a clean church so I did like that! They bused the tables quickly another plus. By the time we were leaving the place was almost vacant. I might work up the courage to go back one more time and try something different in hopes of finding what everyone else is so excited over, but my quest for great Mexican food is not over I've yet to find it in Nevada! The cost was $20.00 for two people to have lunch - for me that's not that great of a deal - but then again I'm used to being in Texas where you have amazing all you can eat Mexican buffets for less then $6.... oh how I miss Texas! ** they accept debit cards now! UPDATE..... http://acorn.rgj.com/rails/inspections/rgj_showbyrestaurant/163 so now we know why the tamales arent fresh.... read the review of the health inspector. I suggest reading on this site before YELPING on how great an establishment really is. I'm learning what restaurants are clean and dirty and VERY shocked!!! WOW

text: MY ABSOLUTE, HANDS-DOWN, FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN THE ENTIRE WORLD. BEST SUSHI EVER, EVER. How are there only 16 reviews on this place?! EVERYONE I ever take here fall in love. I grew up in St. Louis and this restaurant has been a staple in my life for years, and even now after moving North & traveling a lot. Every time I come home to visit, I ALWAYS make at least one visit to this restaurant. I have to. It's the best for so many reasons. The fish here is so fresh; the rice is perfectly seasoned with the right texture. You may not be a connoisseur but you can tell. Immediately. Non-sushi people change their opinion about sushi once they try GREAT sushi here. Everything is good. If you have to ask for my favorites: 1st and foremost, you have to get the SPICY TUNA ROLL. Yes, I know. Spicy tuna, woo hoo. Doesn't' sound special right? You couldn't be more wrong. They take the freshest red tuna and blend/mix it w/ the most perfect combinations of green onion, tempura flakes, and probably other fantastic things I can't make out but the roll will just melt in your mouth while your stomach screams with satisfaction. My second fav is the spicy crab roll (or get it as a hand roll). For appetizers, you must get the CRAB RANGOON. It's not your typical Chinese pocket of deep-fried goodness--- somehow they took something already yummy and found a way to actually improve it! They come out looking like eggrolls filled with the yummy, crab-infused cheese that come with a perfect match of sweet and slightly spicy sauce. A must. Also, go for the HOUSE SALAD. The presentation is beautiful and they make their own miso dressing that is to die for. So fresh and light. People always see me eating it and ask what it is. Do it. Oh this is getting long but there is so much to say! Other yums are the flash fried spinach app (the leaves melt in your mouth. literally!); the peppercorn sea bass, the yellow curry anything (any meat/seafood you like), and the scallop dishes. This is a family owned business, owned by a woman who can be summed up as a truly beautiful person. She treats you like family, she treats all of her employees as family (and a lot of them are), and in turn, the entire restaurant becomes your family. There are many regulars. Once you go, you can easily see why. This restaurant is a great destination for everything: dates, family dinners, girlfriend get-togethers, business lunches, all of it. The decor is tasteful and surprising given it's strip mall location. Do not let this facade fool you. You are in for a treat. Come as you are. The atmosphere is as casual as you want to make it or as formal as you want to get. Go now. Have a Lychee martini for me since I'm far away and tell everyone I said hello. You won't be sorry. This is my favorite place to eat--- and I eat a lot. I think it will become yours too. :)
label: POS

text: In short: It's a top-notch spot. If you've been following my reviews, you may know that I'm on a quest to eat at and review every Mexican restaurant in Norristown. Taqueria Mexico Lindo was the second place on my list, and it did not disappoint. Like most of the Mexican eateries in Norristown, it's small and spartan, but the food makes up for the decor. Service is friendly, but ranges from tolerant to very friendly depending on the day and the business. English is not widely spoken, but the staff knows enough to get by if your Spanish is not up to task. The tacos are top-notch, as are the enchiladas, which are my personal favorite and are easily the best enchiladas I've ever had, anywhere. My one gripe would be that the menu is somewhat limited. While they have a very wide range of meats to choose from for your tacos or whatnot, the actual menu items themselves are quite limited. For example, they do not serve burritos, which is quite unusual for the common Mexican eatery. But what they do serve, they do very well. Prices are average for the area, $2 for a taco, $6 for a larger meal (torta, enchilada plate, etc). Recommended.

text: Let me preface my review by saying that I like well-salted foods, and that we like sausage pizza. We started with a small order of the baked wings based on one of the reviews here. Eaten solo, they were hot, crispy, salty, and rosemary-y. Crispy like they might as well have been deep fried. I wasn't into them. Eaten with the onions, they were pretty good, though. So if you don't like thick caramelized onions, you should know that the wings were really better with them. We had the large, 1/2 broccoli rabe + sausage, and 1/2 sausage + meatballs + sweet peppers + ricotta. Salty, salty, salty. I normally eat 3-4 pieces and I toyed with stopping after 1.5, but I finished it. The meats just blended together into saltiness and the oily salty broccoli was no break for the mouth; might as well have been another meat! The sausage had no defining spice, and the meatballs were just sortof balls of mashed meat. Again, no defining spice other than overwhelming salt. We like much more sauce (there was basically a thin reddish smear that added no tomato flavor), and even though DH loves ricotta, he thought it added to the saltiness. The pizza was covered in toppings, which usually is a good thing, but it was just torture to eat all of it. I did like the crust, which was just chewy enough and not cracker-thin, but it was hard to get the flavor of the big black char bubbles out of your mouth once you ate one. We kept comparing it (each of us, in our heads) to the delicious Peace a Pizza Battuto we ordered last week (Pesto, mozzarella cheese, fennel sausage, plum tomatoes and basil) that we housed. I'll go there in the future and we will not be back to Anthony's. As a finale, DH and I and our 4 y.o. were all in the bathroom within 30 minutes of arriving home. We both still feel salty bloated sick.

text: If you are looking to get a sick deal on any exercise equipment...this is the best place to go. I know that people don't always like to buy used, but sometimes, it's merited. They get a good deal on the slightly older stuff, and so, you get a really good deal on the stuff. It's really a win win situation. Obviously, there are some pitfalls to shopping like this. For example, some of these pieces have taken a few hits. The equipment has been used by hundreds of people over a course of time, and so, it is not in the best shape. However, that does not mean that it's at the end of its life. I suggest really looking at the equipment. Give it a test run, and then see how you feel about it when all is said and done. Don't be afraid to ask questions about where the machine might have come from either. Trust me, you will be glad you did. text: I was recently in New Orleans with my boyfriend, my sister, my brother-in-law, and my sister's boss, and her boss said we HAD to go here because it was so awesome. I had a good time during our visit, which was on a Thursday afternoon, but came to the conclusion that he's looking for different things in his bar hopping experience than I am. The draw for him? 3 for 1 drinks. I suppose that works well if you have a high alcohol tolerance, but I don't. I did not sample the triple-shot-vodka-lemonade that he recommended (not a big lemonade fan), but everyone else seemed to like them. A waitress came around at some point with test tubes containing various shots while we were on the back patio. The kamikazes my sister and I got were quite tasty, but we didn't get the memo about having to take the test tube from the mouth of the waitress. I assume the men in our party quite enjoyed this show. I just felt vaguely awkward, but it's all good. At some point we went inside because we thought there was karaoke occurring. However, they were just playing some karaoke favorites and occasionally having people sing over parts of them. We could never figure out where the DJ and the microphone were. There were very few people on the dance floor while we were there, but I expect it gets bumpin' during the evening hours. So, overall, not my scene. I hope this review doesn't make me seem like too much of a crotchety old person.

text: A friend introduced me to San Diego style Fish Tacos almost 15 years ago now and I absolutely FELL IN LOVE with them. Since I'm from Ohio, finding the same taste as a San Diego FINS or WAHOO or any number of other places out there has been quite a difficult task. Anytime I visit a city I search online for any place in that city that might serve Fish Tacos and give them a try. Well, I must say, the moment I tasted the Fish Tacos from BAJA BURRITO in Nashville, I knew I had found the exact taste I was looking for. They are as EXACT as anything in San Diego, and eating them was just amazing. It's like San Diego was literally transplanted into the heart of County Music... how wild is that. Not only were the fish tacos just incredible, but the whole experience was an A+ all the way around. I loved the atmosphere. The chips were simply perfect. The guacamole was as good as I've ever had. My wife had a burrito and just loved it. And the staff were very very friendly and helpful. What a great, great experience all the way around. They were working on a large outdoor patio in the back, which I can only imagine is perfect on summer nights. Besides reagge playing, there isn't much of an ambiance. We saw three ants crawling on the counter when we were paying. So why go to a place with basic service and little atmosphere? It's the food. I had the jerk chicken, and it was the most amazingly flavored piece of meat I've had in recent memory. My friends also seemed to enjoy their dishes. The side of plantains I ordered perfectly complimented my meal. Honestly, I would recommend this place for takeout, especially if you can't eat outside. The good tastes good enough to overcome what the restaurant lacks otherwise.

text: I just moved to the Philly area recently and didn't know which body shop to turn to when my car was damaged. I took my car in, Dominic looked at the damage to my car and the estimate from the other guys insurance company and straight up told me, that if they only did the work on the estimate my car would be two different shades of silver when I got it back, because the insurance wasn't going to pay for paint blending or a new fender. So he told me he would request a supplement from them and fight them for me and just give me a call when everything was done. But me being the worry-wort I am, and with the bad luck I tend to have, my car sat in the shop for 8 days because the lady that was supposed to do the supplement "said" she called and "someone" from the shop told her the car wasn't there, which totally wasn't true. When she did finally come out to look at the supplement she would not agree to have the insurance pay for some things still no matter how hard Dominic fought for me (because she was very RUDE person who is probably a very unhappy in life). So Dominic did the little work she wouldn't pay for anyway free of charge so my car would be restored to it's prior condition! :D Needless to say, dealing with the insurance company and getting into a wreck is always a nightmarish experience, but Nigro's made it so easy, simple, and took care of everything. They even have a good connection with Avis, and had the insurance company pay to put me in a luxury rental car for the duration of my car being in the shop! I would definitely recommend Nigro's Auto Body to anyone who gets into a wreck, wants their car to look brand new when they get it back (they even vacuumed and washed the car!!), and don't want to deal with the headache of fighting insurance companies.

I've had the Chicken Tikka Masala, the Chicken Dumpakht (my favorite), and the Chicken Vindaloo (amazing!), all of which were delicious. Their garlic naan is good and very garlicky, although sometimes I think it's a little on the doughy side. My boyfriend has made naan before and I think it was as good, if not better, than the naan that I had here. If you eat too much doughy naan, it's easy to fill up pretty quickly. Twice when we went there, we were given free Firni (rice pudding) and Gulab Jamon (fried cheese ball with honey sauce). Delicious. text: It's no secret that I generally haven't been as fond of the La Colombe coffeehouses as I am of the free trade one's in Philly. But then I as I walked in further, I noticed that it was La Colombe self serve, a la WaWa or 711, meaning that if you're ambitious enough as you might be at Wawa, you can mix and match your own caffeinated coffee concoction. Only for extra measure you can add on that extra shot of espresso. Difference Maker #1! But sometimes when your at a coffeehouse you want to say screw coffee, espresso, etc., and get something slightly different. So far, again unless it's Cafe Ole, most La Colombe coffeehouses have been somewhat limited on those options. Yet Euphoria hooks up some pretty awesome bubble teas and smoothies. Difference Maker #2! On it's own Euphoria didn't have the greatest outdoor seating, but it's part of the Piazza so not a problem. and The Piazza attributed to it having free wireless minus a problematic connection. and meanwhile the indoor area was pretty solid in it's own right, and hooked some a great variety. While the Piazza is by far the best outdoor location to accompany a La Colombe coffeehouse, I can't really credit Euphoria for it. And there are plenty of La Colombe house s that deliver a similar indoor vibe. So while it's not quite a difference maker on that category, it is beyond solid! and thatgains Euphoria another euphoric fan!

text: I have tried, for YEARS, to understand why I have put up with the service at this establishment. I can no longer tolerate it. text: I've eaten Vietnamese my entire life and I think I know what a good bowl of pho is. I've eaten at almost all of the Vietnamese restaurants in Nashville, including Miss Saigon and Kien Giang, and Pho Yen Hoa has a better bowl of pho. The pho at Pho Yen Hoa was well-portioned (small bowls of pho are insulting to me). The broth was flavorful, had substance, and not overly sweet (a common finding in too many bad pho restaurants). The noodles were firm and not overcooked and soft, and the meat was good quality, including the tripe. The pho was also accompanied by all the proper herbs, spices and sauces. Although it lacks ambiance as compared to its competitors, I go where the good pho is and not where I can look at fake bamboo and hear trickling water from a fountain. We're fortunate to have many other good Vietnamese restaurants in the area, such as Kien Giang and Miss Saigon (the former being better, I think). (I would probably give these restaurants 3 stars.) But, if I'm going for pho, I'm going to Pho Yen Hoa. Now, only if we could get some good Chinese in here.

text: In brief: very good food but pricey with small portions. If not BYO, would get 3 stars. You MUST get the calamari if you go. In detail: Very small, homey interior where Gail used to be. Wanting to get the best bang for my buck, went for the four course tasting at $39 (seemingly a pretty good deal since some of the courses are $20-25 alone). However, the portions, though delicious, were tiny. Was definitely not full by the end of the meal. One more gripe before the good stuff: before the meal they gave us breadsticks instead of actual bread. No free bread equals an automatic minus one star in my book. The good stuff: tuna ceviche -- citrusy, sweet, tangy and tender. Calamari -- BEST I've ever had. Crusted in cornmeal and nice and crispy with a little Asian flair going on somehow. Would gladly have eaten it for four courses. Grilled scallops with mashed potatoes and asparagus -- traditional, tasty, only got 3 scallops. Some kind of chocolate ganache cake was good but a bit heavy. The tres leches was scrumptious. Needs free bread and bigger portions for five stars.

text: Yes, Charleston's is a chain restaurant, but I have to say I'm a fan and have been for a long time. 10+ years ago I had a brief server stint at the Carmel / Westfield location for a few months and it was a good experience. Occasionally its good to see how a proper kitchen runs from the inside out and have some peace of mind that there aren't any "Waiting" shenanigans happening in the back. :) The menu selection here is pretty diverse - you can get some outstanding salads, fresh fish (grilled, blackened) and vegetable medleys, a filet and baked potato or chicken fingers and fries. Honestly, I've never had anything here I didn't like. The food is of very good quality, its prepared well and the service is usually on it. If you want to stick to the basics for a quick work lunch, get the soup and salad. It's $10 so not cheap, but it will fill you up and the baked potato soup alone is worth the money - it's the best! Chunky, thick and rich and topped off with just the right amount of cheese, bacon and scallions...Yummmmm! Chicken finger lovers, you are in luck! The fingers here aren't the flat, compressed, burnt ones - you'll get a huge platter of beautifully voluptuous fingers, all white meat, lightly battered and golden brown - incredibly tender and juicy inside! Pair those and the fries with a side of honey mustard and you are in heaven! And if you can eat it all, I'll be surprised. I haven't had a filet here in a while, but I do know the last time I had one I was impressed. It had great flavor and was done perfectly. The atmosphere here is nice. text: A restaurant this delicious and diplomatically priced would otherwise deserve five stars. AS gets one half star subtracted for way-too-salty greens (one of five sides) and one half star for the waitress' terrible attitude. We went here on a Monday evening as it was a family member's birthday and we didn't want to stick dad with the full bill from a seven-person dinner at any other of Besh's restaurants. So, we ended up here. They were doing some construction on the street, and if they had not been, the entrance would have been not only welcoming, but impressive. Boutique hotel-style cushy seats lined the outside porch, facing a two-story, lit-up trellis. Very pretty and ideal for smokers. Apart from two industry workers having a drink, we were the only diners at AS that night. The restaurant itself had more ambiance than a regular diner, though it was, obviously, less cozy than August or Domenica. For drinks, I had the Big Mamou, which was made with a peach puree, Bacardi light, and soda. I like "authentically" fruity drinks, made with fresh fruit and not too sweet, and this was just what I wanted. The only thing is that I expected MORE than what I received for the $9.50 price tag. Lots of beer and wine available, and if you enjoy cocktails, the list of specialties is staggering, though they really need to make a separate menu explaining the contents. Husband had the bibb salad (tasty), I started with the collard greens, which were WAY too salty. I like things on the salty side, and I couldnt' even get halfway through them, which was tragic because you could tell that the spices were otherwise on-point. It was, sadly, as fragrant as it was salty. IT WAS INCREDIBLY SALTY. Canned shrimp with remoulade (adorable presentation) was next for the table, and though slightly salty, it was flavorful and unexpected. Baby had the grilled cheese with fries, which I might even go back and order for myself, as it would hit that "grilled cheese spot" on the mark. I've found that great cheese equals great grilled cheese, and that sandwich was definitely not made with Kraft Singles. I ordered the crispy buster crab with jalapeno cheese grits, which was to-DIE-for. The only suggestion I would make would be to serve it with more grits and less crab, because the grits were so great WITH the crab, but the ratio was off and I ran out of grits about halfway through the crab. The cheese grits were just what a person would want from cheese grits; crispy on the top and gooey throughout. I had a few bites of mint pattie for dessert and, again, a great dish with off proportions. The cookies were ROCK hard and nearly impossible to break into pieces, even when hammered with a steak knife. The mint chocolate chip ice cream was heaven on earth, and I would have done more ice cream with just ONE of the rock solid cookies. Also, our waiter, though authentic-looking with her hairnet, was awfully cold for us being the ONLY customers in the place. She never smiled or even said hello. Like lots of new restaurants in NOLA, the waitstaff seem to be the worst representation of the growing pains... Ultimately, because of the FOOD, the decent prices, and not feeling like cultural rejects for dining at a Besh restaurant with our 18 month old in tow, we will definitely be back to American Sector.

text: Whenever I come back to PA to visit my family, my mom and I go out for tea. Our most recent spot was SpecialTea. We tend to stick to the traditional full English afternoon tea: tea sandwiches, a pot of tea, scones with clotted cream or lemon curd & mini pastries. The sandwiches were tasty and light with just the right amount of filling. The scones were fresh and really flavorful. The tea was just about perfect and the pastries/chocolates were a wonderful way to end our lunch. The decor is light and sunny. Before you enter the main dining room, there is a tiny shop where you can buy your own jar of clotted cream or lemon curd. They also sell their homemade scones and you'd be a fool to pass one up. If you are new to tea or just want to try something different, you will enjoy this spot.
label: POS

text: I have worked in the restaurant industry for years. What I experienced at this place is something I have a hard time wrapping my brain around. My friends and I had taken a daytrip to New Hope and were checking out restaurant menus before deciding on where to have dinner. The MD intercepted us as we were heading down the walkway toward the front door. After sizing us up, he asked if he could help us. We told him we'd like to see a menu. He told us that "this place is expensive" and that there were other places to eat nearby. We were dressed presentably, but apparently, this man did not wish to serve the likes of us. I could not believe his audactiy. Apparently, our money is not as good as others, and as angry as his statement made me, I'm glad he turned us away because it prevented us from supporting him.

text: My wife and I stopped in here about 3 weeks ago and had an amazing visit. I had the pulled pork sandwich which was towering with delicious pork. My wife ordered the chicken which was also a ton of meat. We didn't realize how much meat we'd be getting when we ordered so we also got sides. I had the scalloped potatoes and slaw and both were great. The slaw is made without mayonnaise and is excellent on top of the pork sandwich. The staff was fantastic to us. They had a fresh batch of mac & cheese come out of the oven so rather than throwing out the previous batch, they brought us full size sides of it for free (it was good too!). They're really friendly people and were soon told about their newest dessert experiment - white cupcakes with a cream cheese/nutella icing. They smeared the icing on the still-warm cupcakes and gave my wife and I each a free one to sample. Holy sonuva... they were awesome. Needless to say, we walked out of there bursting at the seams from all the delicious food laid in front of us. I'm sure we'll be making another trip there again soon.

Wish it was garlic butter instead, but it wasn't the worst I have ever had. Overall, it was a great meal for a reasonable price. I also had a ton of leftovers. I will go back again soon.

text: Usually when the fam drags me to a festival 5 or 6 times a year to look at wild flowers or nick knack patty whack craft type stuff I have to wade through the b.s. to find the handful of food and beverage booths. Not in this case. It's AAALLLLL about the food. We went to Baton Rouge to visit our youngest at LSU and catch a football game on Saturday. A buddy of mine told me that the Oak Street PoBoy Festival was the following Sunday and suggested that we check it out if we had time. Sunday morning with some encouragement the wife and youngest agreed to appease me and we arrived at the festival as it opened at 11:00 a.m. The first hour or so the crowd was pretty thin and we were able to either walk right up or wait in a small line for whatever we wanted. By the time we left about 1:30 the place was slammed. There were probably fifty or so restaurants from all over New O that had booths and offered Po Boys, soups, desserts, or something awesome. Our favorites were the Roast Beef from Parkway Bakery and the corn n crab bisque from can't remember. We will be back but we will time it so we can stay in New O after the festival and so we can stay longer and drink. (had to drive back to Baton Rouge after).

text: I just stumbled upon this park while cruising around the Santa Barbara shore. It looked like it had a great view of the Marina, so I stopped by. Unlike just about all parks along the shore in Los Angeles/Orange County, you don't have to pay to park! No meters or outrageous fees! Just park and enjoy the beauty of the park! I walked around to the edges of the park and the vistas were great. It was a beautiful pre-noon morning. You can see the whole Marina and then some. I stood there and soaked in the sights. I watched the boats moving around, divers diving into the kelp beds, some dude paddle surfing, people playing on the shore, just a very serene setting. As I explored the park some more I came across a staircase going down to the water. I walked down and it was sort of High Tide, so I didn't walk too far along the shore. I took a few pics as I dodged the water rolling up the sand. I walked back to my car and really took notice of how clean the park was. No graffiti, green grass and restrooms that didn't look like you'd get mugged or raped in. Just a nice park to hangout, jog, walk your dog or have a picnic. A good place to come and enjoy the beauty of Santa Barbara.
label: POS

text: After having lived in Phoenix for three years, the lack of real Mexican food in the Northeast represents a frequent frustration. Moctezuma, however, is the real deal indeed. With Latin music blaring (don't worry, not too loudly) from a large television and servers as comfortable speaking Spanish as English, one knows from the start that his or her Moctezuma meal will be well prepared. The dining area is clean, bright and comfortable. Right upon sitting down a large basket of chips is brought to your table along with a choice of two different salsas. Unlike at some Mexican restaurants, there is no charge for a chip refill. My sister and I both had the enchiladas verdes, which she recommended from a prior visit, and I was not disappointed. The enchiladas were well constructed in delicious tortillas with plentiful, well seasoned pulled chicken. While the rice accompanying one's meal can often be lackluster at some Mexican restaurants, this rice was lleno de sabor (full of flavor). For the portion sizes, meals were a great value and I would not hesitate to return.
label: POS

text: Wandering through chinatown this evening in search of someplace new with decent AC, we decided to give Penang a try, it was early in the evening- they weren't terribly busy and we were greeted and seated near the window almost immediately. It was my first time eating Malaysian food, but quickly got the idea that they enjoyed meat (chicken, beef, pork) in most of their dishes. My boyfriend and I, only eating seafood & veggie food, started off with the Satay Tofu - Crispy fried tofu with cucumber, bean sprouts and a peanut sauce. This was delicious and looking back, perhaps the highlight of our meal, The dish was unique- the fried tofu was perfectly cooked, the veggies fresh . For main dishes we chose the mango shrimp and mee siam (vermicelli noodles with shrimp & tofu). The vermicelli dish was our favorite here- we enjoyed the spicyness but agreed that it could have been even spicier. The presentation of the mango shrimp in two halves of a mango was different, and this dish went well with the coconut rice we also ordered. The dish itself was supposed to be a mix of spice and sweet, but ended up being mostly sweet with nothing to counteract the sweetness (i.e. spice). It was delicious, however felt more like a dessert than a main dish. Overall, we enjoyed our meal, and will return in the future. Hopefully next time they will be more confident that spicy food won't scare us away!

text: Let me say, I love sweets. I love candy, cake, anything with sugar. And cupcakes are the best. They back a little bit of childhood. However, this place is like cupcakes on steriods. BAD STERIODS. Let's talk about why these things are awful. 1. Their cupcakes are simply a delivery system for icing. It's towered inches off the top of the cupcake. While icing is tasty, it is not the focal point of a desert. It's piled on! Less is more, people! 2. The cupcake is stuffed. "What do you mean by stuffed?," you ask? If means that not only is there three inches of icing towering on top, but the middle of every cupcake is filled with teeth-achingly sweet goo. Most are whipped cream, like it's a freaking Ho-Ho or something! There is very little cake in this cupcake. 3. There is so much going on in these cupcakes. The first time I went I got a "Bee Sting". The cake (what there was of it!) was vanilla, honey, and lemon flavored. The filling was a sickeningly sweet filling of lemon, with a tower of lemom cream cheese icing, and some tart lemon candy stuff on top. See what I mean? There is just too much going on there! It hurt my teeth it was so sweet, and my stomach hurt afterwards. 4. The staff is pretty snotty. I've been twice, and I wasn't happy with my service either time. Bottom line, if you like to eat raw lard and sugar from a tub, you'll love this place. But if you like a little cake with your icing, try somewhere else. Stop by The Cupcakery in the CWE. Cheaper, and better cupcakes. And you won't even lose a tooth!

text: I was out in Indy for business...all the locals said St. Elmos was a must for a Seattle guy like me. Apparently Peyton Manning who is like a god around Indy goes to St Elmos after every home game. After hearing all the hoopla I decided I would ante-up the corporate card to spend the $60+ per head for the dining experience. I started with a caprese salad. The salad had a decent balsamic dressing and the tomatoes were of great quality. My only gripe with the salad would be that it was over dressed...making the salad soggy and visually unappealing. Next up the sides. I chose the bean soup and veggies. I'm not a huge fan of bean soup but I guess it was ok. I feel like you could probably get something on par in a canned product from Progresso. As for the veggies, they were pretty standard. Nothing bad, nothing great about them. Now for the main course...the steak. I had the 14 oz New York cut ordered medium rare. The quality of the meat seemed to be fine and the center temp was was also ok. Where it falls apart for me is the seasoning and char. The meat was bland and did not have that nice char that really sets off a steak in my mind. If I was served a steak like this at The Keg or Black Angus I would be ok with it but at a premier steak house I expect a lot more. I might give St Elmos another try if someone twists my arm but I will definitely check out many other Indy restaurants first.
label: NEG

text: First off, I have to say that I'm not a big supporter of chain restaurants. I would much prefer patronizing a locally owned place. But, that said, PF Chang's does a damn good job with their restaurants. This was probably my 6th or 7th time eating here and each experience is about the same. That's a great thing! This visit had a few good points that made me want to write up a review. First of all, I went in with my dad for lunch on a Friday. It was decently busy and we were seated quickly. Service as usual was nice and quick. Our server was exceptional on a few fronts. Very conversational without being trite or fake, and knew just when to stop in and not interrupt conversation. I told her I was torn between ordering the Singapore Street Noodles or the Canton Chicken and Mushroom Noodles. She quickly suggested the Street Noodles. And of course, my dad ordered lettuce wraps and sweet and sour pork. Side note- this place exists and is successful because of those lettuce wraps. But that's a whole other discussion. Wraps were as good as always. Drinks were refilled without asking. When I started on the noodles I remarked that they weren't what I expected. Didn't care for the flavor much. A little too much curry, a little too bitter with vinegar. For me at least they didn't hit the spot. I still ate my fill, picking out the shrimp and chicken pieces. When our server (I need to start writing their names down....a cute petite brunette with curly hair) asked how lunch was I told her that I wouldn't order it again, just not for me. She asked if she could get something else started for me but I declined. After we were finished, she offered to buy dessert. I again refused since it wasn't their fault but she insisted. I told her to bring whatever she suggested. Moments later she delivered a shotglass of double chocolate mousse with two spoons. A nice gesture, especially since there really was no fault on their part. Go visit, order lettuce wraps and tell your friends.
label: POS

text: For a small-town local service shop, Newtown Bicycle has consistently disappointed. It has the worst customer service of any small-owned store I've been to. There is never anyone on the floor or behind the counter when you come in, the store doesn't open until 11am, and the owner has never expressed any interest in his customers. He seems more annoyed that you've come in than interested in offering service. I went in to buy a 12" inner tube for my stroller and hoped he would offer to fix the tire, something that takes 5-10 minutes. The store was empty when I got there. He sold me the tire, reluctantly, and when I asked if he would be able to fix the tire, he said no, I could do it myself. No apology, no "I'm sorry I'm swamped with work but would be happy to otherwise." I once went here to buy bikes for my older kids but given the owner's incredibly indifferent manner and absolute lack of interest in getting my business, I went to Firehouse Cycles in Yardley instead, where I had a wonderful experience. And Firehouse Cycles happily fixes stroller tires, too. Newtown bicycles needs to take some lessons in customer service. I have no idea how it's stayed in business so long.

text: Agave was a great, fun, place to be seen when it first opened. The food was decent--all tapas which was fine--and drinks were pretty nice. The mango mojito is fabulous. They do specialize in tequila though, which, as a rule I stay away from--but I've heard from friends that it is a pretty decent selection. The last few times I've been though has been a huge disappointment. The service has not been great--it was super crowded on a Friday night, and they wouldn't even take names at the door. It was pretty much everyone hovering over tables like vultures, trying to grab one as soon as anyone got up. That only made the diner's experience that much more stressful! Also it's pretty loud--especially on a Thursday, Friday, or Saturday night, it's not ideal if you are looking to make conversation with your friends/date. This said, it's not really a destination place for dinner anyway. Agave has actually taken some food choices OFF of the menu, rather than adding anything! They no longer have the lobster quesadilla which I personally thought was the best. The guacamole is pretty tasty though, as is their homemade salsa--spicy though watch out! It's a pretty small place, but if the weather is nice, they do have a good patio. Plan on using the valet--they block off most of the parking lot for that anyway, and trust me there is not really any other parking around there! If you are looking for a place to just unwind with a shot of tequila and some chips and salsa, this is your place. Crowd is upper 20's/30's, mainly professionals. Good people watching!
label: NEG

text: In order to truly appreciate this place, you need to eat there for dinner. Unfortunately, most of their business seems to be the lunch buffet. For me, I think the lunch buffet is just fine. text: I went to Oceanaire after a friend suggested it and the experience was absolutely top notch. You will not find better service anywhere. Our server, Bill, was very knowledgeable, helpful, and friendly, and was easily one of the best servers I've ever had. text: This small, almost nook of a restaurant pride themselves on preparing full gourmet meals - emphasizing local fresh meats and produce. And the tiny interior has been very carefully designed as a marriage of homey intimacy with upscale dining. The decor signals romantic casual dining, but draws a dress-for-dinner crowd (there is no jacket requirement). If only the food were as piquant as the setting. The menu is undoubtedly gourmet. It changes on a daily basis to reflect the chef's recent shopping. Bravo. But what does not change is the penchant of the chef to destroy his preparations with salt. I had the saltiest rissotto in memory here. And therein lies the fundamental problem with this romantic BYOB; the basic ideas are truly of-the-moment, but the finish lacks, well, finish. A creative chef has no room to mask technical deficiencies, and seasoning is what is unmasked at Pumpkin. The ingredients and the recipes promise far more than what is being delivered. Not all dishes are deserving of this somewhat harsh criticism, but gourmet fare cannot afford to be hit or miss, especially at prices rivaling even stalwart local gourmet cuisine. The waitstaff is entirely average at best, giving a somewhat affected performance that actually interferes with rather than embellishes the dining experience. Being aloof about the food is unjustified, and spilling water on me and my food is simply unacceptable. The menu is priced aggressively high, with a seating running easily into the $40-$50 range (including and depending on the wine(s) you bring). But then, that also increases the odds that your dinner companions at other tables, who will be sitting on your elbows, if not in your ear, share your values for a dining experience. I would not discourage spending an evening at Pumpkin - it is a bright spot in what seems to be a neighborhood renaissance. And the basic ideas that are being nurtured in this fresh genuinely gourmet restaurant may yet blossom. But for now, this is a night of adventure, rather than a regular visit.

text: Where do I start? Every once and while my fellow Yelpers and I disagree . For the most part I've found the reviews reliable - so much so that my team has learned to use yelp as a resource and that's how they picked up on the Stockyard for a group dinner That said, I could not disagree more strongly with the other reviews on this one. The Stockyard is a classic case of a restaurant surviving purely on its historic reputation. We had a large group - so let me begin at the beginning... While I expect a high-end steakhouse to be pricey - I also expect to "get what you pay for". The wine list was not a good start. The wines I recognized were priced 4-6X retail. When we have a significant size group I try to target wines in the 50-80$ range. Thats a real challenge at the stockyard. Precious few decent wines in this range. We went with a Malbec that I know sells for about $20 a bottle retail - $80. Also got a white -- which was a bit more reasonably priced - $65 and surprisingly good. We did the "seafood" appetizer - again, family style due to group size. I was surprised that they didn't cut the fried lobster tails into bite size portions a bit awkward to share. No real complaints here, but it wasn't superb either. At this point i am still thinking "expensive but average steakhouse". But then we got to the main course - and the hustle. Our main waiter launched into a description of the available entrees to the group, including - much to my dismay the description of limited number of American "kobe" filets. In a group this size, I'd want a heads up that he was offering $90 filets BEFORE people start to order. This was followed by an offer to each table (unknown to me) of a 2lb lobster add-on for each. He later claimed he asked first on this - but he did not come to me and i was clearly acting in the capacity of host. Talk about cranking up the bill... All of this - while disconcerting and annoying - is still somewhat "forgivable" when you get a really outstanding meal and service. Nothing could be further from the truth. To a man (or woman) our group was disappointed in the quality and preparation of the entrees - including the kobe which was described as bland and a bit chewy. My porterhouse was undercooked, non-prime beef and clearly not the size stipulated on the menu. I am no steakhouse novice. I know what to expect and this was clearly far below my expectation at a third of the price -- I could have gotten better at Outback. Based on conversation, I was clearly not alone in this opinion. Additionally, a number of people had to wait extended time for entrees while others ate. Lobsters - while large, should have been pre-cracked so inexperienced diners wouldn't struggle so much (and not overcooked). Overall, our price per person was outrageous, the food average, and the approach to draining our pockets insulting. If you want a good meal in Nashville look to the west end near Vanderbilt. Some great places... but Stockyard is the kind of place that makes "overrated" seem like a compliment.
