We also ordered some chips and salsa which was totally unremarkable - chips and the salsa, I suspect, can be found at the local Gordons Food Service. The environment was tragic. The choices of materials used, the total FAILURE to properly manage sound makes this environment extremely uncomfortable. As we placed our order, we could barely hear the person and she could barely hear us. The ultra industrial ceilings, the TVs blaring, and only 35 people added enough noise into the space that it was near impossible to even have a conversation. Oh! The SWEET relief when we stepped outside to walk to our car. We just sat in our car for a minute just to take a deep breath. I can only imagine what this place sounds like when it is raining outside... I suspect that the owner of this restaurant has high hopes to create several of these "joints" around the Indianapolis area and maybe even offer franchise opportunities. But, right now this place is a total miss with their own goals outlined on their website.... "The company's success will be directly linked to great customer service, generous portions of quality food, affordable pricing and an ability to create an atmosphere that is enjoyable, relaxing, clean and ultimately unforgettable." "Great customer service": If they were "working the tables", they would have known about the problems with our food (which is really shocking for a newly opened restaurant - they usually hit the tables multiple times with multiple people... but not here!) "Generous portions": Yep generous for a 200-pound man, coming in from a hard days work. "Affordable pricing": Nope "Atmosphere that is enjoyable, relaxing": Nope, nope, nope! Not even close,... it would have been more relaxing in the middle of a rodeo. "Ultimately unforgettable": yep, but not in the way that they hope. This place is lacking in a real professional touch. Its felt with the choices of materials, their selection of a very poor location and the lack of understanding of guest comfort and the failure to assure that guests are satisfied with their meal and experience.

Oysters were simply gritty and not fresh. Asked the server when they had their oysters delivered and he said 'this morning.' It was either a blatant lie or whoever inspects their deliveries before signing off from the seafood purveyor is incompetent. It is pretty easy to tell you got bad oysters & refuse receipt of an inferior product. Yeah, they will be some harsh words but it is part of the restaurant business. My bet is that the oysters were delivered sometime earlier that week and they improperly stored them in plastic/water in their walk-in. What irked me though was that they were so gritty. Out of the dozen oysters I got, 7 were notably gritty. Even if you get shellfish which aren't the freshest or have been around for a few days, any seafood place should adequately clean them. Yeah you sometimes have to really scrub and spend a fair amount of time cleaning shellfish to get the grit out of them. Hell might take you to scrub them 3x or 4x with clean water to really get them sufficiently cleaned. Did my share when I lived in Boston & worked at a place that had a raw bar. Just takes time and effort. This clearly wasn't done here. The capper though was just how indifferent the manager was when we told him about the oysters. Didn't expect anything like a refund, just an acknowledgment and an apology. Nope. Prices at this place are reasonable for raw oysters. It isn't the $2-$3/oyster at some high-end places for more exotic oysters. Just need to take the time to make sure they clean their oysters thoroughly and get rid of product that has been in the walk-in more than 4-5 days. Hell, just bread those old oysters with a beer batter and fry them up. Even if I lived around this neighborhood, this wouldn't be a place I would come to for the raw bar again. Tangy, sweet and a little spicy it was a real winner. Sure a bit out of place in New Orleans but good food is good food. I read that others has poor service, but when I went it was pretty busy and I had good service. The only thing that was awkward was figuring out who exactly was my server. text: Preface: I LOVE the local philly music scene. Ever since the GSP went the way of the purple buffalo, I've felt a little displaced. Orphaned by the music scene and desperately in search of a new venue to catch my favorite local bands. How is it that Doc's wound up with the honor? I've been to this bar plenty of times, but to go from such a great set up at the Grape to this makes me so sad. The sound quality is decent and the staff upstairs is always cool, but as a venue, Doc's is pretty lacking. It's tough to actually SEE whoever is playing, unless you're right up front and center. The atmosphere is also really strange. I've been to so many local shows and even though there's a decent amount of crowd changeout on a 3+ band lineup, plenty of people tend to stick around to catch the other bands elsewhere. That's always been one of my favorite parts about the scene: your chances of catching an amazing band you've never even heard of is so greatly increased just by going out to see a band you've already been following. Unfortunately, at Doc's, that's just not the case. It can get so claustrophobic upstairs that people seem to be chomping at the bit to get the eff out of there after the band they came to see is done. And it doesn't help that the other bands themselves don't even stick around. How can anyone expect a local music scene to thrive in such an environment where there's very little support? I feel like the set up of Doc's has lended itself to that air. I mean, maybe they're like the unwanting godparents who suddenly found themselves with this task of taking care of all of the fans and bands that have been left by the wayside after the death of GSP, but I just wish there was something better! I know they do what they can, but I'd rather catch a show somewhere else. Sorry Doc's, nothing personal!

This store within the West Edmonton Mall was busy and as far as I could tell, there were no Contagious Canucks writhing in the aisles. What I did find was a neat electronics section, lots of interesting office supplies and nick knacks, some sun screen that contained a non-FDA approved ingredient, and some nonprescription items that couldn't be obtained in the US in an over-the-counter form. And yes I brought them back across the border and have lived to tell this story. Unfortunately, I didn't think of including Cuban Cigars/Rum or even Poutine while working undercover as Rosebud - International Man of Mystery.
label: POS

text: I will say the service was not very friendly (it was like slow time late on a Friday afternoon, too! What the heck?), but I loved the selection of the market, and the Muffaletta was delicious. I am tempted to question when it was made, since it was good-to-go by the time I got there, but since it tasted fresh and wasn't at all soggy, I guess I shouldn't complain. GO! Get yourself a sandwich, stroll off Decatur to get away from the (in my case, other) tourists and have lunch by Jackson Square, take in some culture!

First off, when hiring staff...make sure they are at least educated enough to work a damn register AND converse in English without having to repeat yourself 9 TIMES. Second, if you are going to make a sandwich called a "grinder" (something i've only found here in AZ) Go easy on the oil....nobody likes a soggy sandwich! Third......AGAIN TUCSON AGAIN!! PLEASE STOP TELLING ME THAT THE FROZEN DRINKS ARE OUT OF THIS WORLD! All that I experienced out of the stuff is that it was sugar water and ice. No Thank You, I've got Kool-Aid at home.

text: The first thing that stuck out to me was the name. It sums up the coffeehouse's purpose perfectly - to caffeinate all those who seek a tune up in the morning. Better than a Starbucks in my opinion, the setting is trendy and you have many different options as to food and beverages. They have everything from a "Market Street Machiato" to "Jolt Chewing Gum". Great place to people watch and/or surf the web using their free wi-fi service!
label: POS

text: Do yourself a favor and go to Blue Mercury. I was a little hesitant at first because the prices are steep, but at the end of the day, the level of knowledge, service and general vibe (and of course the AMAZING aromas that permeate!) make the experience and the price points worth it. Blue Mercury is in a lovely old house on Walnut and is filled to the brim with the best face/body products around. I like to go and get my make up done when I'm buying something... you leave feeling fabulous! The staff is very warm and helpful and they will not point you in the wrong direction. Unlike other reviewers, I found them to be the perfect ratio of standoffish and helpful.
label: POS

text: Monday nite's are Industry nite!!! $2 drafts, mostly microbrew. Mike the bartender is a great dude. Tell him Mike said hi!

text: ok. so i wanted pizza. and i have had rusty's before, and it was good. sure, they have expensive ingredients, thus a pricier pizza. But what happened to me this rainy night in january is unforgivable. My roommates agreed to order a thin crust pizza, which i felt i would get more for my money with a personal pan pizza than a few slices of cheese and cracker pizza. Horribly, my personal pizza was about $8 and i got the equivalent of 2 thin slices. My roommates just mocked me as i sat there eating my sorry slices. I'm not sure whether they had made me a thin crust personal or not, i didnt see the receipt. In the end, irony reared its ugly head...i felt totally ripped off and my roommates offered me a slice because they had filled up. One is the loneliest number.

text: 1 star because this restaurant is racist. (I'm asian) My boyfriend made reservations for us at 6 PM for our 3 year anniversary dinner. The atmosphere was very romantic and perfect for the occasion. We were seated upstairs in a cozy corner, and were the first people seated in the area. The waitress came to give us menus and take our drink order. After a few minutes, another party got seated a few tables from us, a family of 5, white. Our drinks came, but our waitress quickly walked away to tend to the other table that had just arrived. The other table got their drinks, bread, and ordered their entrees before we got bread or ordered our meals. Huh?? I thought maybe they were good friends or the waitress just wasn't thinking straight or something, but I got really irritated when they received their food and desserts BEFORE us, and paid and left the restaurant before us! A family of 5, who got to the restaurant at least 10 minutes after us was able to order, eat, pay, and leave the restaurant before we were even able to pay?? It's not that they were rude or hostile, just a major lack of attention. We were the first table to be seated in the upstairs area, and when we left, there were only 2 or 3 other tables, so it was definitely not a busy evening for them. I don't remember what the food was like. I think many would agree that bad service overshadows good food any day. Bad service may be tolerated for outstandingly delicious food, but I had an overall bad experience from this place, so the food must not have been spectacular. Maybe it was just the waitress that evening, but she definitely ruined our special evening. I would not dish out another $100 for that kind of experience.
label: NEG

And John's Roast Pork is no exception. Geno, Pats, and the other Delaware Ave joint are not in the same league. The only reason for the 4 stars is that John is never open... I do grocery shopping in that area and for the past 2 years have not seen it open.

Some in our party were disappointed that the 'spicy' stuff wasn't hot -- so I'd suggest that you make it clear to the waitstaff if you want your dishes spicy/hot/not toned down.

text: probably the best hotel in Reno... i'd say this rating is really a 3.5ish. check-in was pretty simple, as was finding our room, but the place is sort of a maze. The room itself was quiet, great view of the mountains, very clean and the bathroom was awesome! (we stayed in the tuscany suites) perfect tub for a bubble bath! :) bed was super comfy. the decor was a bit 'over the top' ie: too many chairs, very large wall art, etc. but it was a nice room overall. we had the 'Stay Lazy' package which meant a 2 pm checkout, $25 credit for the mini bar, and $50 room service credit. we spent a little time in the arcade, which was fun, but the arcade 'system' w/ a card was DUMB! there is a machine to get tokens but only 13 of the games actually TAKE tokens anymore!? wtf?! we had a roll and some oysters at 'oceano' - roll was blah, oysters were fine.(our server was great) but it was the actually restaurant we couldn't deal with...neon visual simulant overload...OYE... its very similar to the rest of the Peppermill Casino - Neon Hell. We went across the street to Ruby River for steak, which was delicious. We ordered room service the night before, so breakfast would be delivered at 10 am. it was on time, all the food was hot, and actually very good. we had the 'privacy please' sign hung on the door, and didn't have any issues w/ maids interrupting. we checked out at about 1:30 on the TV. we decided to double check the charges at the desk, and good think we did because the room service credit had accidentally been charged, but they removed it and apologized. overall, a good experience, we were happy. getting $75 in credit and an extra couple hours to be lazy in the room made the $140 pricetag decent. It's Reno, not Vegas. ;)
label: POS

text: What is it with this neighborhood and ethnic food that's different from everywhere else in the world? The palak paneer is awfully GREEN, like they didn't boil it quite long enough or something. And the tikka masala is awfully CREAMY, like too creamy. I dunno. Anyways every time they drop off a menu with a coupon I order some and they drop it off after and hour and the world is well.

text: DO NOT GO TO NORTHSIDE- They treat customers rudely and refuse to stand by their work (or lack of it.) In July of 2008 I asked them to replace an inner sole. However, they lost my shoes; every time I'd go to check on them and show them the ticket, they'd say they still couldn't locate them. I was always polite, said don't worry about it, keep trying. Finally, two weeks ago (beg. of Dec.) they found the shoes; I was delighted, until I realized that after all this time, the work hadn't been done (!) I was still polite, still courteous, but I suggested to the lady (the repair guy was out) that it might be a nice gesture for them to do the work and not charge me, since they had kept me waiting for almost six months. The lady completely refused, saying "no way is he going to do that. just take the shoes and go." I was dumbfounded: six months they can't find my shoes, and they refuse to do ANYTHING AT ALL to try to make it up to me?! I said fine, but be assured that I will tell everyone I know about the kind of service I got here. Yesterday, Dec. 22, I decided to go back and see if we could work it out. When I went in I made a point of shaking the guy's hand, being very courteous. I said look, this is what happened. I waited months and months and the work wasn't even done. What do you suggest you can do to compensate me for this? He interrupted me repeatedly and refused to do anything. He accused me of not having the ticket, which was a lie; I had shown the ticket every single time I had gone in. If I hadn't, they wouldn't even have looked, since their policy is that if you lose the ticket, you don't even get your shoes back. He wouldn't even listen to me. "I don't want customers like you! Take the shoes and go. I don't care what you do!" I was just dumbfounded.... All I can say is: DO NOT GO TO NORTHSIDE. I work in a very public job and I will make sure that as many people as possible avoid going there.
label: NEG

text: Very nice place with great service. We made our reservations using the OpenTable app for the iPhone and it worked perfectly. We were seated immediately and with a great attitude from the host. The service was great and the server seemed to always be there when we needed her. The food was well prepared (to order) and tasty. I had the Steak Frites, which is a sirloin with fries, and wasn't disappointed. My wife had the Lobster Ravioli which was good but I don't like that they give you two ravioli that are 6 inches across. I'd prefer the more conventional size. It's a nice place. I'd go again.

Dressing was very sweet. My companion had the pasta tutto mare. HUGE bowl of pasta with mostly "seafood stix." I had the veal piccata. The veal was overcooked and difficult to cut and the breading was soggy due to the "flavorless watery sauce." Must have been the same sauce used on Fred's chicken spedini. The best thing was the side dish of pasta. With a bill that was $50 for two, we won't be back. There are better Italian restaurants in St. Louis.

text: It ain't bad, but if you've had Chipotle, this place is a serious disappointment. Everything inside of it is a ridiculous clone of Chipotle, from the interior decor to the layout of the food to the actual food itself. Problem is that it doesn't taste half as good as Chipotle and it's not as fresh. When it's not busy be prepared for room temperature meat. Tasteless white rice like you're in a Chinese restaurant. Nothing is seasoned exceptionally well and the salsas are watery. Roll that up in your burrito and smoke it. Do yourself a favor - get in a cab, spend 5 bucks, and go to 39th and Walnut and eat at the new Chipotle. It's the real deal for all you Philadelphians that have never experienced it. By the way, Qdoba is crap too so don't even think about eating there.

text: We went to Cafe Pontalba for the white chocolate bread pudding, and decided to have lunch while we were there. We shared the gumbo, red beans and rice, jambalaya, and BBQ shrimp. All of it was really good, and their jambalaya was the best we had during our stay. Sharing was great, so we actually still had room for the bread pudding. Yum! If we had stayed longer, we would have gone back for another meal, and probably would have ordered the same things. Our waiter was on the non-chalant side, but prompt with everything. The whole place seemed very clean. All of the external walls are windows, so if you can, get a table by one, so you can people watch, and keep an eye on all of the goings-on in the square.

text: I must say that i believe that I have been to almost all the coffee shops in town here, large and small. I had to meet someone in town and they suggested Bibo's. Never having heard of this place I was excited for new coffee place to try. The Sunday AM I went, (extremely early at 6am) I was floored by the sheer number of people in line!!! After a bit of a wait just for a drip coffee I finally was handed my hot beverage. I will say now that the wait was well worth it! For regular drip coffee I was amazed by great it was!! Not burnt not stale, almost perfect (darn near impossible to find "fresh" coffee anyplace) I sat there for at least 3 hours and the coffee just kept on pouring! Person after person after person, non stop for those 3 hours poured in the store and enjoyed the beverages they were made. The ambiance of the shop is very pleasant as well! Very comfortable sofas in the back and the regular tables were large enough for me to spread out and do some work on without having my papers drop off the side. I did hear that they also have oustide sitting but I didn't find that out until later. Over all I was very happy with my experience here and will be visiting as often as I can!!
label: POS

text: I went to Batch last week for the first time. I shared cupcakes with my mom and took some back to my co-workers. The cupcakes were very tasty. The selection was pretty good as well and I think the price was very reasonable. I've gotten cupcakes at similar bakeries in other cities and Batch's prices were much lower. I've seen them ranging up to $4 or $5 each! Batch's were about $2/each with the day old cupcakes for $.75! I would like to see a larger selection, however, for a bakery like this in a town this size it was pretty good. Overall, you go to a place like this for a treat that you don't want to make yourself, and Batch is perfect for that!
label: POS

text: Wont go back again. Do not order the Parmesan Crusted Chicken. It is flattened skinnier than a pancake, so it was more of a overcooked chicken tender than a chicken breast. The entire meal was cold. The sun dried tomatoes were like potato chips and the sauce was like jelly. The meal took 35 minutes to arrive. When the waitress found out about the cold food, she offered to take it back for a new meal. I didn't want to wait another 35 minutes for a meal, while my party finished theirs. The manager took off the price of the meal, but I feel he should have comped us the entire meal for the whole party, as the cold food ruined it for all. This will be the last visit for us.

text: This place is very hit or miss. I've been there 6 or 7 times, and each time, the service and dining experience is either really good or terrible. There is a really buff dominican waiter who is very sweet and helpful. He took time to find out exact ingredients for foods to make sure someone like myself with a gluten allergy can eat. He's also very friendly and clearly makes an effort to make sure everything is perfect. Unfortunately, nobody else in Mixto shows the same quality of service - not even the manager! Recently, when we went there, we had to ask four servers, the hostess, and the manager ONE question regarding one of the plates, and everyone responded with, "i don't know." When we finally asked if anyone would mind asking the chef, they rolled their eyes and said that the chef was too busy to answer questions. While I really like some of their dishes a lot, I would never recommend this place to anyone who has food allergies.
label: NEG

text: I am a fan of El Camino. Quite often you can find me there on a Friday night after a show. They have a pretty good selection of food there and the portions are healthy. (Although I could always use a bit more Mac and Cheese.) The service isn't always spot on... they don't always have enough people on staff on busy nights. However they have recently placed TV's in the back room so... there is something to watch. I'm looking foward to the late Phillies games next year. The staff is friendly and recognize us when we stroll in. In the past they've had some rude staff, but it looks like they've all been let go. Now...whenever there is a slight problem, they strive pretty hard to fix it. If you haven't gone there... check it out. And Rachel W. is correct, they do have great Margaritas.
label: POS

text: What this place lacks in "ambiance" it makes up in an expansive menu and affordable prices. Not a place to take a date to impress, but good for a big family dinner, which is why we came. Most things, including combination plates, were below $10. In addition to your usual Mexican staples (tacos, enchiladas, burritos, etc), there is also a pretty large seafood selection and other specialties. I had the Mole Enchiladas, which were great- with just a hint of chocolate and sweetness. My boyfriend had the seafood soup which was huge and full of calamari, crab legs, fish, and more. Everyone else in our party were satisfied with their entrees as well. The only things that were lacking were some of the basics: rice a little dry and refried beans looked canned. There were also a lot of drink options, such as Michelada-- which is like a Mexican bloody mary that substitutes beer for the vodka. I was skeptical but my boyfriend enjoyed it. The service was friendly and prompt. Overall, a good meal.
label: POS

text: Slightly better than it's almost identical cousin Landshark's (I don't know if the same people own these places, but if I'm not sure what would be worse? That the same person opened two almost identical bars or that there are two different people that would think this is an OK concept?) OK, Rock Lobster is bigger, has more seating/standing room, and an outdoor back area that most people don't realize exists. Those are it's merits over Landshark's. Other than that, it's the same tired music, the same creepy guys, the same d-bags and the same occasionally ghetto atmosphere. Although at this bar the bi-level dance floor gives you a chance to scope out a ton of really drunk people fighting over who gets to dance on the top platform and who has to stay below. The drink situation is a little better and Landshark's because there are more bartenders and more beer carts. But that is a limited consolation. I really hate the type of bar concept...Leave it out.

text: Try to imagine that I used to drive from LA to Santa Barbara, just to have dinner at Holdren's. Picture it. Summer time. Sunset time. Grab a table on their mini patio, by the heat lamp. A glass of sauvignon blanc and you're ready for the best Sunday combo. Great food, wine and people-watching. Personal favorite: coconut shrimps, OMG don't get me started on the coconut shrimps, a pure delicacy, artichoke dip, grilled halibut and OF COURSE: the mud pie! I have no shame admitting that I took a picture of their mudpie and had it as my screensaver for several weeks. Holdren's is the perfect place for a quick get-away if you're not from the Santa Barbara area. I dont recommend it as much for lunch but definitely on my MUST-list for dinner.
label: POS

text: To paraphrase Lloyd Bentsen, "Lumiere, I've been to the Bellagio. The Bellagio is a friend of mine. You Lumiere, are no Bellagio." OK, maybe it's not a fair comparison. But you know, Lumiere had some potential, especially compared to its nearly competition. But... Damn! I've inhaled my fair share of cancer sticks, but this place does get wicked smokey. Not to mention it gets really crowded. Maybe more casinos in the area will spread out the population. Yeah right. The dealers here have that wonderful robotic I-am-only-here-to-deal attitude. No humor. No recommendations in tough spots. (Guess what? No tips). And finally, the gatekeepers/ID checkers. They used to be nice and friendly. As of late, if you're even slightly wee bit buzzed, you're going to get grief from them. WTF? Doesn't that automatically make me a VIP player? I'm guessing that some moron came in, got wasted, lost a ton, and managed to threaten them with a lawsuit if they didn't get their money back. The only pros are they have some decent slots and some decent cheap blackjack tables. Beyond that, my recommendation is to save your pennies, buy a deck of cards, some chips, and invite some friends over for casino night. It will be cheaper, more fun, and bound to get a better review.
label: NEG

text: The creme brulee is an amazing vanilla, coffee, and pistachio concoction. It is incredibly rich and creamy, yet light and airy at the same time. The dinner is simply the precursor to this remarkable dessert. The food is quite delectable, too, and I am a fan of the sea scallops (lovely truffle sauce), short ribs (so flavorful and tender) and the lobster mac and cheese (although Zephyr in Cambridge has a better one), along with the calamari appetizer (light and crispy with a slightly spicy and zesty dressing). But honestly, the dessert trumps all. Service is okay but nothing to rave about. Plus, it's in a shopping center so parking is easy. The happy hour is weekdays from 5-7 pm and they have a selection of appetizers, including sliders and the calamari for only $5. You can't beat that.
label: POS

text: The beer line-up is usually a great mix of styles and breweries and it certainly is fun to also read about the "on-deck" selections waiting for pouring should a keg kick while you are there. As for food, the fantastic Charcuterie Board is always a winner, with morcilla, La Quercia prosciutto, and a fine house-made rabbit terrine, as is the Short Rib Sandwich, slow braised meat resplendent on a brioche bun (the excellent, well-informed and kind waitstaff will agree to split it for you - a good idea if you also want to eat all of the generous charcuterie board). Some other food selections are less successful, the prime culprit is a flatbread margherita that made me pine for store bought frozen pies. The atmosphere is convivial and fun, if loud and crowded most of the time - sure signs of a very successful bar.
label: POS

text: Went to dinner with my dad/sister, excited for some Italian food (we generally go out and eat Chinese...I know cliche!). Came here hearing how good it was. Got here, the ambiance is nice, everyone seems to be having a good time (but quiet). Get seated, and looked over the menu. There isn't a wide selection, but it's fine for a small type place. I ordered the mussels for an app, and the branzino for entree - I'm not usually a seafood eater, but my sister was saying how good branzino is, as she had it twice this week! I said, sure! She knows I don't like fish, but said I should give it a shot. The mussels were underwhelming. It unshelled and in a tomato soup like base. Again, I'm not a seafood guru, but I've eaten mussels before where I enjoyed them, this I just ate like it was cereal. Warm, tomato soup cereal where the corn flakes are mussels. The branzino came out - pretty good portion, I got 2 filets, 3 slices of potato, and some spinach. The spinach was awesome, if I had a plate of that I would've been happy. The potatoes were ok, tasted like a potato. The branzino tasted like nothing - maybe that's what it is supposed to taste like? Not sure, but it felt like I was eating fish without any flavor. Not being a fish fan, I guess that's ok...but what am I paying for? My dad/sister got the 3 course - (2 choices of app, 2 choices of entree, full dessert menu) for $30, which isn't bad - it's like restaurant week here (but only Tues-Thurs). I didn't have their salad/entree, but ate some of the tiramisu. Ok, I ate it all. But it was good. Looks diff than your average tiramisu, but still tasted good. A bit stronger on the kahlua flavor, but I was definitely ok with that. The service was professional. Not friendly, not mean, professional. Overall, it was an ok time. I wish I got the pasta, but no regrets. I can't say I'll give this place another shot unless someone else mentions to go there. It is a byob, so that's good. Maybe getting wasted will make it yummier. In summation, meh, I've experienced better. I also do not think this place is $$, it is $$$. Each app runs $8-9, entree runs $19-$27. For 3 people, 2 prix fixe, 1 app/entree costs $100+, fyi.
label: NEG

text: I almost feel silly writing a review for Audrey Claire because it is silly good. Upon sitting down, I was whisked away to a metropolitan street side. We definitely over ordered..... quite serendipitous. I think the best plate (that's probably very consistent) is the appetizer sampler. It is a cornucopia of delicious veggies... all of the ones that are hit/miss with certain individual: asparagus, beets, brussel sprouts, artichokes, pickles, sweet potatoes. It's amazing, because somehow, everyone gets a little more of their favorite. The flatbread pizza was out of this world. We did the pear/gorgonzola combo. I think the force de resistance for the evening was the tile fish with lentils and israeli couscous and sundried tomatoes. I'm getting fuller just thinking about my meal here last night. Our waiter was very knowledgeable, but I think he definitely knew better than to recommend so many courses for 3 girls.

text: After all of the reviews that have been floating around, I decided to go and see what all of the hoopla was about. The unsophisticated decor is a hodge podge of Asian colors and textures. The vibe is colorful, but clumsy like a dorm room (Asian influence on a dollar store budget). They attempted the open kitchen concept, but I thought their execution of it was a failure in that it looked sloppy and the cook was generally pissed off and throwing things around in plain view. The Chinese flicks projected on the wall didn't really work either. The projection was too high up and there was no sound or close caption. The food was the real disappointment. I understand that when food is defined as fusion, it allows the chef some latitude. But, I feel you can't call a dish by it's name without having essential elements in the dish. For example, Pad Thai without rice noodles or peanuts (at least some kind of nut) and/or a spicy nut sauce isn't Pad Thai. Their Pad Thai was a tiny portion for $12. It had flat, soggy, extra wide egg noodles (yuk) and a salty soy/sirachi sauce that was bad. The meat in the dish was the only good thing about it. The waitress told us that the sushi pieces would be large and they were not. In fact, they were teeny, (the price wasn't). The potstickers, that came highly recommended by the waitress were floating in a rice vinegar soy sauce that was too heavy on the vinegar. The root vegetable fries were cold, but probably the only tasty thing we ordered,. However, the dipping sauces were just okay. Overall, the service was slow and we were not impressed. It might be a good place to stop for drinks, but the food fails.
label: NEG

text: I live a few blocks from the old CWE location so it made me sad when Chez Leon decided to move, but then I had not been there for dinner since this time last year so it's probably my fault. On Saturday we gave the new Clayton location a try. We called midweek for a reservation and the earliest they had was 8:30. Mary gets too hungry for dinner at 8, but she managed. When we arrived the first words out of the valet's mouth asked us if we had a reservation because there was a 2 hour wait -- so word to the wise, if you really want to have dinner at Chez Leon don't go without a reservation. The place was packed. We intentionally arrived early assuming that they would then want to seat us early (which normally drives me crazy because I want a drink or two in the bar), but that wasn't happening, so we were forced to have drinks in the bar - my favorite way to begin a civilized dinner out. The new place has a roomier bar area even though the bar itself is shorter. There being no room at the bar, we sat in a couple chairs across from the bar and someone came to take our drink orders nearly as soon as we sat down. The bar tab was seamlessly transferred to our dinner check without a word being mentioned. While the old place actually looked and felt like a Parisian café, the new place has almost a theatrical look. The walls are painted slate black and perfectly lite to highlight the candles on the table and set a great modern atmosphere for classic French food. The menu is nearly the same as before including the prix fixe for $40 (with upcharges on a few of the higher end plats principaux). The food is as excellent as before. I had the diver scallops in an incredible sauce that I couldn't keep my bread out of. Chez Leon has my favorite dinner salad in town - salade lyonnaise. I'm not a big dinner salad person but any dinner salad that has real think bacon chunks and a poached egg is heaven on a salad plate. Say what you want about the French, their belief that an egg on anything makes it better -- a belief they have exported to the world -- has made me a Francophile for life. I finished with the duck l'orange which was very good (I ordered the duck medium. The chef prefers medium rare, but I just can't do. I wish I could, but I can't. Steak sure, but not duck or any other bird for that matter). Mary is a farm girl at heart so after having the best escargots in town (which I would have gotten if the scallops weren't on the menu sucking every drop of garlicy butter out with bread) ordered the calves liver with bacon and onion reduction (I think on the onions - the liver is also served with a mustard sauce instead -- but let's be honest, no one says "no" to bacon anything) and finished with the cheese plate in lieu of desert. There was enough cheese for both of us. I need to learn more about cheeses. The bottom line is that the new modern looking Chez Leon hasn't lost a step on the food which is as excellent as ever and a great value for fine dining French cuisine. If you haven't been, you're missing out. Why not 5 stars? Little things. Our waiter didn't bring out our food (pet peeve), and the guy who did placed both the appetizers and entrees before the wrong person (reason why it's a pet peeve)-- apparently because our server gave the wrong cues (fork/knife placement, etc). Had to ask twice for more bread for Mary's escargot. Finally, My duck could have been a little warmer and I wish the skin was crispier. These are little things, but the difference between 4 and 5 stars at a fine dinning restaurant is all about the details -- even on a very busy night. One final word: You're not a rock star. When you go to a fine dining restaurant -- look nice (and not "good jeans" nice). The dinner may not be a big deal for you, but there will be people at the restaurant who have been saving up for that dinner to celebrate an important event in their life. Out of respect for them dress like the place is as special as they believe it to be.
label: POS

text: My boyfriend and I chose City Tap as the place to celebrate our three year anniversary--and I kid you not, we could not have chosen better! This gave us the opportunity to try many of the beers they had on tap--did I mention there were 60 of them?! Although I love a good beer, this was a wine kind of night for me so I stuck to Chardonnay. The weather was perfect so we spent a good part of our night on the roof deck terrace. We had initially made a reservation for 7:30 but because of the impromptu happy hour party we didn't sit down til close to 9pm. The staff were very accommodating and let us know that whenever we decided we were ready to sit, there would be a table waiting for us. When it came time to eat, we were seated at a table inside their lovely dining room. The architecture and atmosphere set the tone for a truly fantastic evening. Although we were celebrating a special occasion we weren't looking to spend an arm and a leg--this was the perfect "$$$" moderately priced menu and you truly got what you paid for. I had the chicken--which was juicy, tender, and DELICIOUS (6/5 Stars). He had the salmon and was equally impressed. I think we honestly didn't have two words to say other than "mmm" after the food arrived. It was just too good for words. I read several sour reviews before making this reservation--but I couldn't possibly disagree more! Overall A+!

text: Today was my first visit, and boy have I been missing out! There are so many positive things about Sugar Philly Truck: First, the dessert is amazing. I had the molten chocolate cake, which was fresh out of the oven. It was warm, moist and had the perfect amount of chocolate (not too heavy). The sauce was vanilla-y goodness, but the cake would have been plenty moist without the sauce, which is really impressive. Second, I love that they make the dessert right there in the truck. In my experience, dessert items from trucks are often made elsewhere and then sold from the truck. Not the case here! When I asked for a recommendation, the guy working there (unfortunately I didn't catch his name) pointed me to the molten cake because it had just been made. Talk about freshness! Third, the guy working there was so nice and friendly. I could tell he was really passionate about his desserts and sharing them with customers. Plus, he also just seems like a fun guy to be around. And finally, I adore the design of the truck - it's impossible to look at and not be happy. Plus, it's eco-friendly! It runs on natural gas and the utensils they use are made of cornstarch. A happy, eco-friendly truck, quality desserts AND great, friendly service? What a gem!

text: This restaurant's niche is it bills itself as a fine dining establishment that serves massive portions. What most people realize in going here is that you're basically paying for almost two platters worth of food on one plate and that the size of the appetizers and entrees is reflected in the cost. Seven Stars Inn holds an unflattering distinction as being the 2nd worst dining experience I have ever had in my life (#1 is held by a TGI Fridays). Sadly, the unbelievably bad experience had nothing to do with the food, which for the most part was pretty good, and had EVERYTHING to do with our server and the host. Just thinking about the dinner our party had here makes me angry. I should qualify this review by stating that the dining experience I'm writing about happened a while ago - before I learned about the existence of Yelp. Normally I wouldn't bother writing a review so long after the fact, but the story is so incredible and this restaurant so badly ruined what was supposed to be a special evening out (retirement celebration) that it still brings back memories for everyone that was in our dinner party. Our waitress gave our party of 8 the worst service I have ever witnessed at a "fine dining" restaurant. To start things off her demeanor was a tad cold, at least towards our table. Throughout the evening various things occurred that irked us about the service we were receiving, including receiving some drinking glasses that had large chips at the rim where you put your lips (EEK). However, nothing compares to the lack of attentiveness she gave our party. We watched during the 2+ hours we were here while she zipped around to other tables of diners refilling drinks, clearing plates, checking in to see if everything was ok. All things she was REPEATEDLY negligent in doing for our table. Not too long into our dining experience a number of us were getting annoyed at the lack of service we were receiving and we are NOT a demanding bunch. So I decided to go have a talk with the host. The host was a middle aged gentleman who sat on a stool by a podium and resembled Jesse Ventura with glasses. I told him what had happened thus far and he said that he would take care of it. About 45 minutes after my first visit to the host it was clear that nothing had changed. Our plates were not being cleared, our drinks were not being refilled, more rolls and butter were not being brought out, and all while we watched our waitress serve other tables in an efficient manner. We attempted on several occasions throughout the night to get her attention as she was walking nearby coming from other tables and unbelievably most of the time she wouldn't even look our way. On at least one ocassion she looked right at us as several of us were gesturing to get here attention and she just kept right on walking. We were dumbfouded. It was as if we were lepers. I paid my second visit to the host almost 2 hours into our dinner. Once again we had been sitting with empty dinner plates and empty drink glasses for roughly a 1/2 hour and the waitress was still ignoring our table. On this visit to the host he seemed less interested in what I was telling him and the way he responded didn't inspire confidence that anything was going to be done. A short while after my second complaint to the host the waitress finally visited our table and cleared our plates - I think this was just coincidence. She once again disappeared and now we were left sitting with no offer for coffee or a dessert menu. After 2 discreet complaints by me to the host regarding our waitress's chronic inattentiveness (among a few other things), it was clear that nothing had changed. After sitting idle for another 15 minutes we collectivley decided to just give up and end the evening early by getting the check because we didn't feel like waiting another 1/2 hour for dessert. As we walked through the foyer I paid my 3rd and final visit to the host. I told him that I wanted him to know that we got tired of waiting for our server and were so disappointed with our service that we decided to skip dessert and just leave. I also mentioned to him that my comments to him had changed nothing and that our waitress had been ignoring us all evening. His reply to me was a flippant, "we'll make it up to you next time." I was so flabbergasted at his response to me that I just walked away. My thought and what I should have said to him was "Oh really? How are you going to do that, by giving us the service we should have received tonight on our next visit?", but I was left speechless by his response. So this is the type of service you can expect from a $400 night out at a restaurant that bills itself as fine dining!?! As someone who eats out often I realize that any restaurant can have an off night but that wasn't the case here. This was blissful ignorance, lack of courtesy and blatant disregard for the customer. No one in our party of 8 has ever gone to this restaurant since.
label: NEG

text: I have now been to Green Eggs twice, two weekends in a row, and while there are some things I LOVE about this place, I can't quite give it 5 stars due to some deficiencies. As others have stated, it does get crowded, but neither time did we have to wait too long-- maybe around 15 minutes. And yes, it is cheaper than Sabrina's with similar quality (and much closer to my house, which is a bonus). The first time I went, I was with two friends who were visiting from out of town. They were wowed by the low prices, as was I. One of them got the Belgian waffle with fruit, which she liked, and the other got the creme brulee French toast, which she raved about, before-- I am sure-- slipping into an insulin coma on the drive back to DC. We all loved the brown sugar cubes they gave us with our coffee. I don't usually sweeten my coffee, but that is a nice touch. The coffee was excellent as well. The spinach and chorizo omelet was slightly disappointing, since it didn't have a lot of either thing in it, but overall, the plate was good, much aided by the rosemary potatoes (slammin'!) and the LeBus multi-grain toast (one of my favorite breads ever!). One of my friends got an order of bacon, which was thick cut and delightful. On the second trip, I ordered the three eggs with chorizo, which turned out to be a much better choice, since it had two decent-sized patties on it. I don't know where they get it, but it's not that overly spicy/greasy red kind. It's really delicately spiced and awesome! As for the service, we didn't have anything extremely bad happen either time, but my boyfriend had a weird encounter with the server when he asked if he could get The Kitchen Sink with rosemary instead of signature potatoes, which contain onions. She said, "I don't know" instead of "let me find out, " and my boyfriend and I got the impression that she was expecting to just put the order in and then we would have to wait until the plate came out to find out if there were any potatoes in the dish at all. text: Come on, people, show PHL some love! This place has improved exponentially over the years. I've seen it grow over my three and half decades of life. As a child, my dad was an airline pilot, so I got to explore the place, way back when security was quite different. I knew the place well, yet it always seemed, for what seemed like nearly 20 years, to be in a constant state of construction. But now, construction is complete, and thanks to the terrible state of our nation's airlines, it's a good thing. Delays and cancellations are inevitable, and not due to the airport itself. So PHL has entertainment! First, they have a great rule that all vendors and stores must sell items and food at the current 'street rate' in the Delaware Valley. So no overpriced food unless it is overpriced everywhere. You won't get gouged just because you are in the airport. A beer won't cost $10--hooray! There are rocking chairs in which to sit. The food court is clean and has local chains like Bassetts, not just McDonalds. There are souvenir shops to keep you occupied while the rain delays your trip. The concourse has an entire shopping mall to satisfy our need to shop and consume. Best of all, there is art! Pick up a map and tour the terminals. (You don't have to stay in your airline's terminal, you know.) Get some exercise in, and check out the exhibitions. I am always impressed by their curator's choices. Exciting local art mixed with some folks from far away. In March 2008, there was art made from the old trees from Logan Square that had reached the end of their life cycle. An earlier exhibit of felted sculpture was so gorgeous I called a friend to tell her to learn more about the artist. (Did I mention the wifi so that you could even Google the artist right there if you had a laptop?) You can catch a train right to Center City from Bag Claim. (Though don't get me started on SEPTA's removal of ticket machines. Grr) There are TVs everywhere to entertain you. There's even a spa for massages, pedicures, and facials! So complain if you will. But I think that most complaints are the result of the sad state of our airlines and air travel in general, not the airport. PHL does a great job of making it a little less miserable.

text: I'm surprised the reviews of Hotel Oceana are so bad. I thought the place was kinda cute. The boyfriend and I recently stayed two nights at Hotel Oceana. Overall, our experience was good. They have several buildings on the property and some rooms are better/larger/quieter than others. Here's a run down of the good parts and the bummers. The Good Stuff- 1. Location. It is right across the street from the ocean and only a few blocks from Stearn's Wharf and lots of restaurants and shopping on State Street. We couldn't have asked for a better location. 2. Staff. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We complained after our first night there (more in a minute on that) and the guy at the desk was accommodating and not only gave us a different room but a better room. 3. Rooms. Really comfy beds, very clean rooms. 4. Breakfast. Yes, it's your standard fare but it was tasty. Their pastries were much better quality than at most hotel breakfasts, the fruit was fresh and they had real dishes and silverware which was a nice touch. The Bummers 1. The Noise. The first room they gave us was on the first floor and the walls were paper thin. We heard everything upstairs and next door. And I do mean everything. Apparently several people found the hotel to be quite "romantic," if you catch my drift. We did not sleep much that first night. But when we complained, the hotel gave us a very nice room in a part of the place that was empty. 2. Parking. $10/day kinda sucks. It's much less than other cities in CA, but still. 3. Lack of vending machines. We looked around for a soda machine but couldn't find one. When we asked at the front desk they told us that was what the mini-bar is for. Lame. So when you visit Hotel Oceana make sure to ask for a quiet room on the top floor and bring your own soda if you don't want to pay mini-bar prices. Besides that, it's a great place. I'd go back.

text: Ate here on a Monday night, and I am still in awe of the food. I nibbled my leftovers all day despite the fact that they were so spicy... Han Dynasty is the best sichuan food I have ever had in a restaurant --and this includes all of the Philly Chinatown Sichuan spots as well as the big ones in midtown Manhattan. I own both of the fuschia dunlop cookbooks and this place is serving very authentic food. we had dan dan noodles, wontons in chili oil, and cold pork belly slices in chili oil for appetizers and the dry hot pot with chicken, the chicken in the chili oil with peppers and celery/cabbage, and the triple fried beef with peppers. I liked the fact that they offered a choice of light or dark meat for the chicken, since the dark meat has way more flavor. All of the food was very flavorful and you could tell that everything was fresh. And, this place doesn't mess around with the spice. you like it hot? you order it hot and you get it hot! Despite the large amounts of "Ma La" flavor, you could still taste the ingredients and you couldn't stop eating despite the sweat on your lips and brow. It's a byo, but the owner was kind enough to provide us with a lindemans peche lambic to try with the food. the sweet fruit taste of the beer paired really well with the hot food. Han also set us up with an order of fried chinese sausages and garlic slices. These paired really well with the Kenzinger and Newbold IPAs we brought to drink. I am sure I will eat at this place many times in the future, I am always on a quest for real sichuan food that truly provides the heat, and this place has that in spades. Probably the only bummer is the fact that with the prime olde city location parking may be a bit of a hassle on weekends-- but it is very close to the market st el stop so no biggie. The word is already spreading on this place so, if you have been on a quest for really authentic, top quality sichuan-style food in philly, you need to go here ASAP.

text: This was the first Greek food I've had since eating in Greece last Summer. The ambiance leaves something to be desired, which is the only reason I'm not breaking out star number five. Noisy space, fluorescent lighting (thank god I have attractive friends), and uncomfortable chairs were a bummer. But we're here because we like eating, right? So all that other stuff is okay. Eating with a group of six was nice, because we got to order a whole bunch of stuff as appetizers. Tzatziki was awesome and gone in a matter of minutes. The hummus was good, I thought (though it was def heavy on the tahini and lighter on the lemon than when I make it), pita was delish, and the calamari and greek salad were both excellent. The service was really good, and attentive, too. For dinner, most of us ordered fish. Actually I think we all did. Several of us ordered the special, which was Dorado grilled with lemon and garlic, with a side of spinach and rice pilaf. Our most gregarious guest ordered the whole fish, filleted it himself, then proclaimed loudly that he would eat Fishy's eyeball, then followed-through. No one seemed to notice this but me, oddly. Anyway, a couple others had the salmon (greek-style) with olives, feta, asparagus and tomato I think... Also quite good. Everything was just really fresh and cooked simply, which is easier said than done sometimes. Some ordered dessert, some ordered Greek coffees, and others of us simply had more wine to bring things full-circle. By the time we were finished - prob around 10:30 - the whole place was empty, and they had turned the Greek music up significantly... Which I think is sorta like the equivalent of the dance club putting on really whiny Country music (Read: LEAVE), so the Winos, Fish-Eye-Eater, et al. took the hint and called it a night.

text: I spent six years of my life in Santa Barbara. It will always be my heart's home. I became interested in Eastern Religious beliefs at UCSB and subsequently found Vedanta. The small, serene temple sits on 45 acres of land in the hills of Montecito overlooking the ocean. Run by a a convent of seven nuns, activities include daily worship, meditation and vesper services. The best time to attend the evening vesper services is during daylight savings time when you can quietly observe the sunset. There's a rock not far from the steps outside. I used to sit there after the service in in the "otherworldy" silence that envelops the place and reflect. The following detail on the vespers service comes from their website. I couldn't do it justice, so I thought I'd add it. It is a quiet time, a time for reflection and meditation at the close of the day. During the ritual, five items, representing the subtle elements that form the universe, are offered back to the Lord. The ritual symbolizes the multiplicity of the world being dissolved into oneness. It is an act of surrender to God, an act of the soul's return to its Source. After a brief meditation, the worshiper begins the arati by lighting wicks in a special holder. These wicks are made of cotton dipped in melted ghee (clarified butter). The lights symbolize the light of Brahman (the Godhead). They also symbolize fire, one of the five elements that comprise the universe. The worshiper pours consecrated water three times over the handle of the arati holder as salutations are offered to the fire that is Brahman. Pouring the water three times is believed to aid the worshiper's commitment to the act, thereby enhancing the effect. The worshiper rings the bell continuously with the left hand, symbolizing the mystic sound OM, which eternally reverberates throughout the universe. With the right hand, the worshiper waves the light clockwise before the pictures of Ramakrishna, Jesus and Buddha, thus offering fire back to the Lord. The worshiper then kneels down and passes the right hand over the light and then over the head. By doing this, the worshiper is purified by the light of Brahman and takes the darshan (blessings) of the Lord. This act also signifies the desire for illumination, or for realization of the soul's oneness with God. The worshiper then pours water over the hand as an act of purification before the next, and each subsequent, offering is begun. The second offering is water, which is contained in a conch shell. Water is another element comprising the universe. The conch is waved in a circular motion before the holy pictures, and is then poured into an offering bowl. The third offering is a cloth, which symbolizes the element space. Cloth covers the body as space envelops all creation. The fourth offering is a flower, symbolizing the element earth. The last of the offerings is the chamara (a fan made of yak tail), which symbolizes the element air as it is gracefully waved before the holy pictures. Three songs accompany the vesper service: Khandana Bhaba Bandhana, a Bengali song to Sri Ramakrishna written by Swami Vivekananda; Om Hring Ritang, a Sanskrit hymn to Sri Ramakrishna written by Swami Vivekananda; and Sarva Mangala Mangalye, a Sanskrit hymn to the Divine Mother. The singing is often acccompanied by a harmonium (an Indian hand-held organ), a tampura (an Indian string instrument), tabla (Indian drums) and cymbals. It's truly calming.
